nodes.body: REWRITTEN against the full consumer trace; two of the original three were downranked or refuted. (1) is_disc_system key drift: matcher.rs:595-608 lists cdi/segacd/neogeocd/wii-u/gc, of which THREE are wrong -- segacd (canonical megacd), wii-u (wiiu) and gc (gamecube). cdi and neogeocd ARE real keys in systems_manifest.tsv lines 74 and 38; do not remove them -- while 10,020 entries of multi-GB disc images (xbox360 5,142, 3ds 3,014, wiiu 782, megacd 448, psvita 267, naomi 264) take the expensive cartridge path. (2) matcher.rs:166 wraps LOWER() around the rom_hashes primary key: measured 62x slower on megadrive, 157x on psx, once per file per tier. (3) The MD5 tier is 100% dead -- the export has zero md5 rows -- costing a full file re-read on every cartridge miss; gate tiers on data presence. (4) matcher.rs:130,:134 propagate hash-computation errors with the try operator, so one IO failure aborts an entire system scan; the disc branch already handles this defensively. (5) rom_library.py:1279-1310 ORs sha1/md5/crc32 with LIMIT 1, resolved as a rowid union -- 55 crc32 values map to more than one release_id, so a 32-bit collision can outrank the exact 160-bit match. (6) commands/mod.rs:2607 applies LIMIT before the platform filter, silently losing 5,515 of 146,832 rows (3.8%). DROPPED: libretro_thumbnails (RS-51 -- no frontend caller, no user-visible feature). DROPPED: the CRC32 omission, documented as a 45MB size trade-off at export_game_reference.py:35.
nodes.done_looks_like: Disc systems take the disc path, hash lookups use the index, dead tiers are skipped, an IO failure loses one file not one system, and platform filtering happens before LIMIT.

nodes.body: DECIDED 2026-07-27 by Tom: mint local works for unmatched releases, flagged as non-IGDB. IGDB remains the sole source of CURATED works identity (PIPELINE_SPEC.md:175 stands, scoped to curated works); a release with no IGDB match gets a minted work carrying source='local' and igdb_id NULL. Consequences: games.work_id stays NOT NULL in the export and needs no relaxation; games.name takes the IGDB title where there is one, else v2_releases.canonical_title; series, collection and cross-platform grouping remain populated only from IGDB-sourced works, so a local work is honestly empty of metadata rather than falsely populated. THE GUARD THAT MATTERS: v1 minted a work per name+year, reached 100% coverage, and generated a 14,016-row fuzzy-duplicate queue doing it. Local minting must route ambiguity to an exception rather than guessing, and a local work must be mergeable into an IGDB work later when IGDB coverage catches up -- otherwise this recreates v1's problem under a new name.
nodes.done_looks_like: The decision is recorded here and reflected in RS-166 (no NOT NULL relaxation), RS-180 and RS-194.

nodes.body: ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-07-28 -- do NOT build incremental fetch. Diffed the 2026-02-08 baseline (315,625 records) against a fresh full pull (333,195) after 170 days: 18,482 added, 912 removed, 224,502 changed (71.1% of baseline), 90,211 identical. Retro platforms are NOT frozen -- PS3 89.9%, Xbox 87.2%, PSX 75.9%, PS2 75.7%, Arcade 71.5%, all at or above PC/Windows 74.3%. BUT the churn is mostly noise: similar_games changes on 44.1% of records, rating_count/total_rating_count 17.5%, rating/total_rating 14.9% -- none read by v2 -- and 39.7% of all records changed ONLY in derived rating/similarity fields. Fields v2 actually uses move far less: alternative_names 6.9%, game_engines 5.2%, involved_companies 3.5%, release_dates 3.5%, platforms 1.9%, summary 1.9%. So meaningful change is ~24%, not 71%. THE DECIDING TEST: IGDB's /games/count with 'where updated_at > 1770549358' returns 224,468 of 370,541 total -- almost exactly the 224,502 measured as changed, which proves IGDB bumps updated_at on derived-field recomputes. You therefore cannot filter noise out at fetch time; an updated_at fetch moves 224,468 instead of 333,195, a 32.6% saving. Not worth the merge semantics and the mode='w' truncation risk for a job run quarterly. Platform filtering was also assessed and rejected: only 30% of the corpus is droppable, 52% of records are PC (mapped, and the churniest), and the 56,710 records with no platform at all may be parent_game roots. NOTE for whoever revisits: total IGDB corpus is 370,541 but our pull returns 333,195 -- a 37,346 gap from the script's WHERE_CLAUSE that nobody has explained.
nodes.done_looks_like: A measurement decides whether incremental fetch is worth building, and the decision is recorded with its evidence.
nodes.title: IGDB incremental fetch: measured, not worth building
nodes.why: Tom asked whether re-downloading everything is a poor process. It is, but the fix does not work -- and the measurement is worth keeping so nobody re-proposes it.

nodes.body: A standing per-run quality instrument -- stored metrics, deterministic spot checks, trend, and a ranked list of causes -- replacing the fifteen hand-run measurements that steer each session.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every pipeline run emits a quality report with the same metrics, stored so runs are comparable, plus sampled spot-checks, and its output names what to fix next in priority order. ⚠️ THIS ITEM MUST NOT PIN TO A SNAPSHOT — that is the failure mode it exists to cure. Do not assert 60.51%, megadrive 52.5%, c64 24.0% or the run-46 queue sizes as pass conditions; RS-225, RS-208 and RS-187 all move them by design. Verify instead that the INSTRUMENT works: a run stores its metrics (coverage per system, per identity route, match rate, exception count by cause, field fill rates) keyed to its own ingest_run_id; two runs can be diffed and the report names what changed and by how much; the report reproduces, for the run it measures, the same figures a manual query returns; spot-checks sample N matches per tier and per system and record a correct/incorrect judgement rather than only a count; and the actionable output is ordered by community_rating_count with a stated cut-off. Note ingest_runs.stats_json ALREADY stores comparable per-run metrics that nothing reads back — the run 39 to run 48 match-rate movement is recoverable from it today. Start there rather than inventing a second store.
nodes.title: Build a repeatable quality assessment that guides what to fix next
nodes.why: Fifteen hand-made measurements steered tonight and none survive it. Without this, every session re-derives the same numbers and improvement is guided by whoever last looked.

nodes.body: Six of stage 55's seven tiers require IGDB's platform list to contain the platform, and the only tier that skips it demands an exact year — so ports fail both. Sized: 10,561 unmatched releases have exactly one candidate work and need no disambiguation at all.
nodes.done_looks_like: A platform-free, year-free tier restricted to titles with exactly one candidate work is added to release_work_match.py, guarded by publisher non-disagreement. **Re-measure every baseline at the start of the work — do not take them from this field.** As of 2026-07-28 after RS-172 landed they are: v2_release_work_map 96,294 of 159,090 releases (60.53%); megadrive 1,090 of 2,073; unmatched releases 62,796. All four shifted from the figures in matching-analysis.md (95,646 / 158,067 / 1,083 / 2,063 / 62,421) because RS-172 split the 855 over-merged groups, and they will shift again if any upstream matching item lands first — the COVERAGE RATE is the stable quantity, not the counts. After a stage 55 re-run: coverage rises from its own measured pre-change value to approximately 67%, megadrive rises proportionally, and `SELECT match_tier, COUNT(*) FROM v2_release_work_map GROUP BY 1` shows the new tier's contribution separately. After Burner II on megadrive resolves to IGDB work 5352 despite that work being tagged Arcade-only. No release gains a work where publisher is known on both sides and disagrees. Then, separately: the genuinely ambiguous releases (4,404 when analysed — re-measure) are selected by corroboration or routed to an exception, never resolved by _pick_best's current tie-break. `python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q` reports 0 failed.

nodes.body: works_build.py maps a port to its parent's work (correct), but builds the work's platforms_json from the main IGDB record only — so 5,183 works hold a mapping saying a port exists while their platform list denies that platform.
nodes.done_looks_like: v2_works.platforms_json for a work is the UNION of its own platforms and those of every IGDB record mapping to it via the port mapping (v2_work_igdb_map, which already embodies the MAX_PARENT_DEPTH walk and port-chain handling — do not re-walk the graph). Identity model UNCHANGED: a port still maps to its parent's work and still creates no work of its own; only the parent's platform metadata is completed. Named case: work 599855 (IGDB 5352, After Burner II) owns platform [52] Arcade and gains [13,15,16,18,25,29,30,32,37,63,86,99,118,121] from its ports; release 491197 (megadrive, 1990) goes from UNMATCHED to work 599855 via tier_6 with competing_count=1. MEASURED EXPECTATIONS from a full simulation that reproduced run 52 exactly (0 differences, real matcher imported not reimplemented) — re-derive rather than trusting these if any upstream item lands first: 4,213 works gain platforms; release->work rises 96,294 -> 98,427 of 159,090 (60.53% -> 61.87%); ZERO releases lose a match; of the 2,133 recovered, 2,112 (99.0%) have competing_count=1, and they land tier_2 693 / tier_3 53 / tier_4 108 / tier_6 1,066 / tier_7 213 with tier_1 structurally impossible. THE LARGER EFFECT IS CONFIDENCE, NOT COUNT: 1,374 already-matched releases move to a strictly stronger tier, of which 1,282 go tier_5 -> tier_1 (0.7 platform-blind -> 1.0 platform-confirmed). Assert that upgrade explicitly; a bar counting only new matches misses the main benefit. The 8 systems with no IGDB platform mapping (1,045 releases) are untouched in either direction. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

nodes.body: build_sync computes a file's serving path by strip-prefixing its source root against the instance root, so every file on an external source gets src = NULL. The master then refuses to launch it and a client cannot fetch it. Measured 2026-08-28: 19,271 of 20,130 visible games (95.7%) are in this state; only 859 are playable.
nodes.done_looks_like: A game whose files live outside the instance root launches on the master and syncs to a client. (1) RE-MEASURE FIRST; 2026-08-28 sightings from the live instance: source 1 (<root>/roms) holds 876 files and source 16 (/Volumes/Media/Retro Games Archive/ROMs) holds 25,386 rows / 25,085 available. 19,271 of 20,130 visible non-windows non-draft games have EVERY available file on an external source; 859 do not. The cause is build_sync.rs:759 - Path::new(source_root).join(rel_path).strip_prefix(root).ok() - which yields None for any source outside the root, so ManifestFile.src is NULL. (2) src BECOMES A SOURCE-AWARE LOCATOR (source id + path relative to that source's root) rather than a path relative to the instance root. The master resolves it to a real path locally; a client resolves it to a URL and fetches it. ONE locator, two resolutions. (3) THE MASTER LAUNCHES IT: runner.rs:203's refusal "the master cannot serve X - its source lives outside the instance root" must stop firing for a file on an enabled source. (4) A CLIENT FETCHES IT: the serving route resolves a locator to bytes; reconcile.rs:461's "the master has no serving path for this file" must stop firing for the same population. (5) ⚠️ THE SERVING ROUTE IS AN ARBITRARY-FILE-READ HOLE IF IT IS WRONG. /media is currently ServeDir over the whole instance root (server/src/main.rs:266); a locator route reaches OUTSIDE that root by design, so it must resolve strictly within the named source's root_path and refuse anything that escapes it. Pin traversal explicitly: '..' segments, absolute paths, symlinks pointing out of the source, a disabled source, and an unknown source id must all be refused - each with its own test, and each test carrying a positive control proving a legitimate path in the same shape IS served. (6) DISABLED AND MISSING SOURCES FAIL HONESTLY: a source whose volume is not mounted (the archive share is SMB) must produce a clear "not available" rather than a hang or a silent empty file. State the behaviour and test it. (7) FROZEN REVISIONS: a saved revision already synced or pinned is frozen and may carry old-shape src values. Say what happens to them - migrate, tolerate both shapes, or re-cut - and test whichever is chosen. Do not leave it to chance. (8) GATE ON A COPY: after the change, the count of games the master can resolve a launch path for goes from 859 to substantially all 20,130, measured the same way; assert a non-zero number was actually resolved so a run that resolves nothing cannot pass. (9) OUT OF SCOPE: the master/client device-root restructure (RS-776). This item does not stage, copy or link anything - it only makes a file addressable.
nodes.title: A file outside the instance root can be served and launched (19,271 games)

nodes.body: Accept every persisted artwork-layer shorthand and content-chain form that the viewer renders, keeping Rust and JavaScript media-needs semantics in lockstep.

nodes.why: Fresh review of merged RS-956 found that Rust rejects string layer shorthand and CSV content chains accepted by the viewer and editor.

nodes.body: Add the schema-only queue migration and concurrency-safe store for tasks, reasons, claims, leases, retries, provider rate slots and persisted status.
nodes.done_looks_like: The next free registered schema-only migration creates the three RS-951 queue tables and required indexes with exact foreign-key, canonical-type, millisecond timestamp, bounded field, state, lease, due, candidate cursor, provenance and terminal checks. Ensure deduplicates one game/type task while retaining scoped reasons and max priority without disturbing leases, attempts or terminal state. Short BEGIN IMMEDIATE claims deterministically acquire pending, due retry or expired work; attempts and generations increment exactly on claim/reclaim, and every later mutation is fenced by task/token/generation. Shutdown invalidates and immediately requeues the current claim; only CAS queue-owned integrity recovery may leave a terminal state. Provider request-start slots are reserved transactionally without sleeping under a lock. Independent-connection REDs prove concurrent dedupe, one winner, priority/FIFO, expiry, stale-fence refusal, shutdown invalidation, rate reservation and DB responsiveness. Focused migration/store and relevant full Rust tests pass; no catalogue, HTTP, filesystem worker, host lifecycle, API or provider code is added.
nodes.title: Artwork queue foundation: schema, dedupe and fenced claims
nodes.why: Every later reader and worker needs one durable state machine that remains correct across two processes and restarts.

nodes.body: Process one box-front queue task local-first, then LaunchBox or Steam, using existing catalogue, downloader and asset machinery.
nodes.done_looks_like: One synchronous box_front task processor reuses the existing queue fence, resolver, core-catalogue reader and LaunchBox URL helper. A usable local cover fulfils with zero HTTP/copy. Otherwise exact games.release_id selects one ordered LaunchBox candidate, or an eligible Windows Steam-only game uses only library_600x900.jpg. One request per claim is bounded by existing timeout, 20MiB and JPEG/PNG/WebP decode/dimension checks plus optional CRC. Missing identity/catalogue retries; 408/429/5xx retry the same candidate; 404/410 advance; no eligible candidate ends no_candidate. Publication is same-directory atomic no-clobber under media/{system}/box_front, registration uses existing asset operations, and queue provenance records provider/key/SHA/CRC. Lease loss cannot fulfil stale work. Six fixture-only vertical tests and the full Rust suite pass. No generic provider registry, IGDB, lifecycle/API/UI, speculative media, new migration/dependency, or corpus work.
nodes.title: Artwork queue: acquire one cover end to end
nodes.why: The smallest useful slice is one real cover becoming resolver-visible; abstractions are deferred until a second concrete provider needs them.

nodes.body: Build the host-neutral worker, local-first fulfilment, lease-safe no-clobber publication, indexed registration, adoption and recovery.
nodes.done_looks_like: A host-neutral bounded WorkerHandle consumes predecessor store/acquisition decisions and checks local media after claim, immediately before HTTP and before publication. Valid builtin projections are repaired transactionally; usable external media fulfils without copying; proven-missing builtin projections may be withdrawn without deleting non-queue bytes. No DB lock spans blocking work. Queue finals use validated reserved content-addressed paths, exclusive synced lease temps, fence checks before HTTP/persist/register, no-clobber persistence and parent fsync. Existing finals are adopted only after full validation. Known-asset registration, normalized/legacy projections and fenced fulfilment commit together. Lost fences/rollback remove only the attempt part file, never immutable finals; restart adopts valid current-selection orphan finals and sweeps only strictly named stale parts. Queue-owned recovery first validates exact receipt, reserved path and bytes, then commits projection withdrawal and task CAS together before any post-commit owned-byte removal; external/non-queue files and sentinels remain untouched. REDs cover local zero-request wins, projection repair/withdrawal, CRC, no-clobber races, fence loss at every boundary, registration failure, stale/current adoption, restart and ownership-limited cleanup; focused/full Rust tests and fresh review pass.
nodes.title: Artwork queue foundation: local-first worker and immutable publication
nodes.why: The durable queue becomes useful only when an owned claim can safely become indexed media without overwriting user files or publishing after lease loss.

nodes.body: Start and stop the proven one-cover processor in eligible master hosts using existing lifecycle hooks.
nodes.done_looks_like: After migrations and role resolution, retrostack-server alone starts one background ArtworkWorker for completed master instances, including loopback; client roles and any durable first-run-incomplete instance start none. The worker reuses ArtworkQueueStore and BoxFrontAcquisition, handles at most one lease, and waits interruptibly when empty/erroring without busy-polling. Cancellation stops new claims, closes the claim/cancel race, fenced-requeues any held lease through a separate connection, and initiates stop/join on standalone-server Ctrl-C/SIGTERM before Axum drains long-lived connections. A stale in-flight processor cannot fulfil after invalidation; a valid no-clobber cover registered after its final fence may remain for the next local-first claim. The existing Tauri force-kill path remains unchanged and relies on persisted lease expiry. Focused and full Rust gates pass. No UI/status API/events, Tauri worker or child shutdown protocol, provider, enqueue, corpus, migration, dependency or configuration work.
nodes.title: Artwork queue: minimal master background loop

nodes.body: Six repeatability defects in a v2 run: status-blind run-id lookups, wrong clear order, no transactions, append-only ingest, unused sha256, unregistered RPCS3 source.
nodes.done_looks_like:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-03 against main b0a3709. Figures below are EVIDENCE THE DEFECT IS REAL, not targets -- re-measure at dispatch and report the truth.

Current: grep -rn 'MAX(ingest_run_id)' pipeline_v2/ returns 2 (unchanged); grep -rn '_latest_run_id(conn,' returns 8, NOT the 6 this item recorded; grep -cE 'BEGIN|SAVEPOINT|ROLLBACK' scripts/import_v2.py returns 0 (unchanged).

ONE CLAUSE OF THIS ACCEPTANCE WAS INVALIDATED BY RS-192, MERGED THE SAME DAY. It asked for 'grep -c rpcs3 tools/game-database-v2/pipeline_v2/discovery.py >= 1'. Discovery rules are no longer Python literals -- they live in config/source_rules.tsv and discovery.py holds none. That probe can now never pass. THE RPCS3 SOURCE MUST BE REGISTERED AS A TSV ROW, with its revision/oldid change key, and the probe is grep -c rpcs3 config/source_rules.tsv >= 1.

What must be true:
- No status-blind run lookup remains: neither MAX(ingest_run_id) nor a _latest_run_id that ignores status can select a run, because a FAILED run is not a generation and picking one silently reads a half-written table. All 10 call sites.
- import_v2.py wraps each stage so a stage raising part-way leaves its output tables' row counts UNCHANGED, proven by a test that raises mid-stage and compares counts either side.
- Clearing works after clearing the release-work map raises no IntegrityError -- the clear order is currently wrong.
- Running an ingest stage twice leaves ONE generation, not two.
- A second stage-01 run COMPARES stg_source_files.sha256 rather than only rewriting it, so an unchanged corpus is recognisable as unchanged.
- RPCS3 registered as above.
- pytest and cargo test report 0 failed, with more cases than today's 788.

NOTE ON SEQUENCING: this is the gate on trusting a full rebuild, so it should land before one is run.
nodes.title: Pipeline discipline: make a v2 run trustworthy

nodes.body: v2 holds hashes only in staging and no stage owns projecting them; 195,153 distinct SHA1 already reach a release by join and have nowhere to land.
nodes.done_looks_like: Hash lookup against v2 resolves ROMs to releases. ⚠️ THE GATES BELOW WERE CORRECTED 2026-07-28 — the earlier figures came from a join on (source_file, source_row_order), which is NOT unique: source_file is a bare basename and the same DAT filename exists under two dat_family folders, so 399,794 rows occupy only 361,916 distinct pairs. Joining on dat_family as well makes it a bijection. Correct targets: reachable ROM rows at least 208,046 (the old 224,000 gate was unreachable); distinct SHA1 at least 180,756 (old 195,000 unreachable); SHA1-reach-per-release at least 34.1% (old 32.7% was too weak and would have passed a projection ~2,300 releases short). Verify with the three-column join: stg_libretro_games g JOIN stg_libretro_roms r ON r.dat_family=g.dat_family AND r.source_file=g.source_file AND r.source_row_order=g.source_row_order. Also: v2_rom_entries and v2_rom_hashes exist keyed on release_id with optional release_region_id, populated at stage 40; clone_of and the dump-status flags land in the same pass (RS-164); and the projection is measured against v1's like-for-like 37.6% SHA1-reach, NOT against v1's 72.4%, which counts entries with no hash at all. nodes.body:
IGDB collection and franchise groupings, plus the staged libretro franchise DATs, are projected into NOTHING queryable. Measured 2026-08-03: 20,872 works carry franchises_json and 38,849 carry collections_json on the work row, and no table, view or index reads them -- sqlite_master has no franchise, collection or series table at all. Project them into a queryable membership table, not into pairwise relationship edges.

RAISED TO p1 2026-08-03. Two things made this more valuable than its priority reflected. First, RS-237 was dropped because nothing in the data separates a re-release from a remaster -- a 2016 release of a 1982 game is equally likely to be either. That makes the SERIES link the fallback: if a release cannot be reliably assigned to the right work within a family, the catalogue should at least be able to say the family exists and show them together. Second, RS-303 made family membership load-bearing for MATCHING, not only for display -- reject_colliding_names now permits two works to share a derived name when they are provably one game, and it reads the parent chain plus v2_work_relationships to decide. Those relationships exist (32,083 rows: 1,446 remake_of, 1,345 remaster_of, 2,093 expanded_from, 471 standalone_expansion_of, 26,728 included_in) but franchise and collection do not, so the widest and most human-legible notion of 'same series' is the one the matcher cannot see.
nodes.done_looks_like:
CORRECTED 2026-08-03 after measurement. The previous acceptance's MEMBERSHIP figures were not reproducible by any reading and contradicted the item's own body: it asked for ~37,287 collection memberships, which is BELOW the 38,849 distinct works carrying a collection that the body quotes -- a membership count cannot be smaller than its own distinct membership. Same shape for franchises (19,241 against 20,872 distinct works). The group counts were close and are kept as a sanity band.

TRUE FIGURES, measured on works generation 64 (stage_50_build_works, 2026-07-31 14:09:25 UTC), on an APFS clone:
- v2_work_groups: 9,740 igdb collections, 2,453 igdb franchises, 721 libretro franchises; 12,914 groups total.
- v2_work_group_members: 68,517 rows, of which 65,752 are IGDB. Rows exceed distinct works because a work in two collections is two memberships -- Baldur's Gate is in both D&D and Forgotten Realms.
- Under the 500,000 ceiling with room to spare. The all-pairs form MEASURED as SUM(n*(n-1)) over the same groups is 2,536,884 ordered / 1,268,442 unordered -- 38.6x larger. The largest single group (IGDB franchise Mario, 490 works) is 490 membership rows against 239,610 ordered pairs on its own.
- libretro membership: 2,383 work-level and 382 release-level rows, ALL 2,765 carrying crc32.
- Franchise disagreement writes 410 exceptions and no tie-break; both memberships are kept. A work with no IGDB franchise is NOT a disagreement (666 such pairs) -- libretro is adding information, not contradicting.

The stage is 57, placed AFTER 56 deliberately so that 'no local-source work carries a membership row' is a live check rather than a statement about an empty table: verified by running 56 and 57 in one invocation on a clone, with 61,388 minted works present and 0 offenders, the population reported alongside the verdict.

nodes.body: PLAN section 7's five per-run reports and four v1-vs-v2 cutover gates were never built; v2 contains no code that opens the v1 database.
nodes.done_looks_like:
A stage_75-equivalent run emits the five PLAN section 7 reports against v1 and v2 side by side, and the four cutover gates each evaluate to pass, fail, or BLOCKED-with-a-named-reason.

THE BLOCKED PATH MUST STILL EXIST AND BE EXERCISED. Its original triggers are gone -- RS-184 landed GameTDB and RS-171 landed the ROM spine (v2_rom_entries 290,229 / v2_rom_hashes 738,822), so those two gates must now actually evaluate rather than report BLOCKED. The mechanism must not rot: at least one gate reaches BLOCKED on a real current incomparability, or a test forces the path and asserts the blocking ref is printed. No gate may report a pass on an incomparable population.

EVERY COMPARISON STATES ITS BASIS. A raw v1-vs-v2 percentage is not a finding: v2's denominator carries populations that cannot hold a hash at all (windows 38,513 at zero reach, ps4 4,844 at zero), so a rate can move on catalogue growth alone. Each report prints numerator, denominator and what was excluded, and any headline rate is accompanied by the absolute count. The known case to reproduce: v2 SHA1 reach 62,503/164,696 = 37.95 percent against v1 55,174/146,832 = 37.58 percent, where the entire margin is GameTDB and v2 libretro-only is 36.55 percent, below v1. The harness must make that visible rather than reporting only the favourable percentage.

The contract also gains an executable test ported from v1's test_export_game_reference.py. Gate 1 additionally needs the parse-error tables PLAN section 4 Layer A rule 4 requires and schema.py lacks. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed and at least 376 passed.

nodes.body: Switch and Vita containers carry a plaintext header holding the title ID — measured 87% recovery on the real library, ~300 bytes read per multi-GB file.
nodes.done_looks_like:
The scanner reads a title ID from Switch and Vita containers at bounded offsets and never presents an unresolved identifier as a name match.

MEASURE AGAINST THE FILE THE SCANNER ACTUALLY READS. The previous acceptance queried v2_release_serials in the 10.9GB v2 master; the scanner reads game_reference.db, and the two disagree. Re-measured 2026-08-20 in the shipped catalogue: psvita 1,188 games / 248 serials, switch 6,069 games / 6,489 serials.

THE SWITCH GAP IS NOT WHAT THE OLD ACCEPTANCE SAID. It claimed the switch lookup returns zero rows. It does not: the catalogue carries 6,489 switch serials. But 0 of those 6,489 are 16-hex title-ID shaped - they are 5-char GameTDB game codes (A224A), a DIFFERENT IDENTIFIER SPACE. So a title ID read from an .xci or .nsp header still resolves against nothing, and the missing piece is a title-ID-to-GameTDB-code crosswalk, not an absent source. Establish whether such a crosswalk is derivable before designing around the gap; if it is not, the unresolved-identifier handling below stands.

Vita is in better shape: its 248 serials are PCSA/PCSE-form codes that a .vpk or .pkg header can produce directly.

BUILD ON THE TIER THAT NOW EXISTS. src-tauri/src/rom_scanner/embedded_id.rs already reads serials at bounded offsets for Nintendo ISO/WBFS/RVZ/WIA, PS1/PS2/PSP SYSTEM.CNF and PARAM.SFO, Dreamcast IP.BIN and Xbox XBE (RS-579 phases 1-3, merged 2026-08-20). Extend it. Do NOT add a second parallel mechanism, and honour its rule that the tier performs no full-file reads.

Formats: PFS0 for .nsp, HEAD/HFS0 with the root offset at 0x130 for .xci, and the Vita .vpk/.pkg header. config/systems_manifest.tsv already declares these extensions - verify rather than assume, and do not modify that file, which is parsed by Rust AND Python with different rules.

Re-measure the 87% recovery figure and the 109-file corpus in ~/ROMs/Switch/ before relying on either; both are old sightings. RADIANT SILVERGUN resolving to 0100f61010f22000 rather than the filename's 010011401959e000 remains a good worked example.

An unresolved title ID is stored as an unresolved identifier with the lookup gap recorded, and is NEVER silently presented as a name match. That is the safety property - pin it with a test that fails if the behaviour is removed.
nodes.title: Match switch and psvita by title ID rather than name or full-file hash
nodes.why: Measured 2026-07-28 on Tom's library: the title ID is in the ticket filename inside a plaintext PFS0/HFS0 header, so reading it beats both name matching and hashing a 32GB file — and one filename in 87 disagrees with its own file.

nodes.body: Give v2 a review surface: exceptions clustered by cause, AI proposals that record what they saw, and verdicts that survive a rebuild.
nodes.done_looks_like: Exceptions survive a re-run with their adjudication intact, are clustered by cause rather than enumerated, and an AI proposal records the source values it saw. ⚠️ DO NOT pin to 106,764 or to the cause sizes measured on run 46 — RS-225, RS-208 and RS-187 are all designed to move them, and this item lands after them. Verify against the run being tested: cluster count is far below the exception count (clustering, not enumeration) and the clusters' member totals reconcile exactly to that run's four exception tables; no proposal row lacks the source values it saw; multi-hit cases are refused rather than picked; and THE CORE TEST — record the verdict count, re-run the pipeline end to end, and the count is unchanged with verdicts re-attached by cause_key. The queue is ordered by community_rating_count with a stated cut-off. Design against RS-207's precedent: an automated year-correction pass was wrong on most of the cases checked because it matched titles without disambiguating.
nodes.title: Build a review surface with AI triage over the exception queues
nodes.why: 106,764 exceptions are regenerated every run with zero memory of any prior decision, and a large probabilistic residue is permanent because the release-to-work join is entirely name-based.

nodes.body: PIPELINE_SPEC records Tom's 2026-07-28 decision that bundles (7,056) and standalone expansions (480) create works because they are real, runnable, ROM-bearing products. works_build.py still lists both in SKIP_TYPES, so 7,536 works are never created.

nodes.body: works_build.py:421-437 bulk-loads work metadata with 'WHERE ingest_run_id = ? AND igdb_id IN (500 placeholders)'. stg_igdb_games has no sqlite_stat1, so SQLite picks idx_stg_igdb_games_run, matches all 333,195 run-43 rows and filters igdb_id row by row: 6.97s per batch x 643 batches = ~75 min. After ANALYZE (0.3s) it picks idx_stg_igdb_games_igdb_id: 0.001s per batch, and stage 50 runs in 1m44s.
nodes.done_looks_like: Stage 50's wall time no longer depends on how much free RAM the machine has. Today it is 475s when the ~5GB table sits in the OS page cache and ~75min under memory pressure, with no visible cause -- and the RS-235 build measured 1m44s once ANALYZE was applied. Pick ONE fix and justify it: (a) ship an ANALYZE step in the pipeline, (b) INDEXED BY idx_stg_igdb_games_igdb_id on the query, or (c) drop the redundant ingest_run_id predicate -- NOTE (c) is only safe because igdb_id is effectively unique per run and run 43 is the only run in the table, which is a data property and not a constraint, so (a) or (b) is the conservative choice. Verify with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN showing idx_stg_igdb_games_igdb_id rather than idx_stg_igdb_games_run, and a measured stage-50 wall time under 5 minutes on a cold cache. Check whether the same unanalysed-table pattern costs other stages: stage 30 and stage 55 also query staging in bulk. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

IGDB has a direct equivalent for seven of them: SG-1000 is platform 84, Game & Watch 307, Atari Jaguar CD 410, and the four arcade boards are all platform 52 (Arcade).
nodes.done_looks_like: The seven mappable system keys resolve to their IGDB platform id (sg1000->84, gameandwatch->307, jaguarcd->410, and atomiswave/model2/model3/naomi->52 Arcade) and their releases match through the EXISTING tiers with no relaxation of the platform constraint. Measure on a clone: 570 of the 8,882 single-candidate blocked releases sit on these systems, and 198 of the 388 that carry 20 or more LaunchBox votes. Expect the great majority to match at tier 1 or 2 once the platform is known -- these are exact-title arcade games, not ambiguous ones. Per-release diff against the pre-change run: lost must be 0, and spot-check that arcade-board releases land on the arcade work rather than a console port of it, since platform 52 is shared by four of our keys. SCUMMVM IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: it is a runtime, not a platform, so its releases are really DOS, Amiga or Mac titles and need their true platform resolved rather than a mapping -- state that in the code comment and leave it unmapped. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

nodes.title: Rebuild the live v2 database so it carries the landed code

nodes.body:
Pipeline items close on landed code proven against a scratch clone; nothing carries the change into game_database_v2.db. Owner's ruling 2026-07-31: keep code-done, add a deliberate catch-up rather than blocking every item on a live rebuild.

RE-MEASURED 2026-08-03, and the drift is now the dominant measurement hazard. The live database was last built 2026-07-31 14:00-15:02 (ingest_runs 55-67) and main has moved SEVEN commits since (446f72c, 635f095, 67d9dc1, a9fabaa, c14c4aa, 1870d7a, 9abaa57). Concretely missing from live: v2_work_external_ids, v2_local_works, v2_release_work_attachments and v2_work_groups do not exist as tables at all; stage_56_mint_works appears NOWHERE in ingest_runs, so the settled 'mint everything, coverage is 100%' property has never once been true of the live database -- v2_release_work_map run 65 holds 103,308 rows against 164,696 releases. Two generations are live in several tables (v2_release_work_map 54=98,427 and 65=103,308).

This matters beyond tidiness: agents measuring a single stage on a clone inherit UPSTREAM output produced by seven-commit-old code, which is the drifted-baseline error at pipeline scale rather than at commit scale.
nodes.done_looks_like: A documented catch-up procedure exists and names who runs it and when -- after each merged batch of pipeline items, not per item. Running it reports which landed items the live database does and does not carry, DERIVED by checking the tables schema.py declares against sqlite_master and the stages the pipeline declares (STAGE_OUTPUTS) against ingest_runs, so the answer cannot go stale the way a hand-kept list would. It is read-only, safe to run at any time against the live file, and prints a one-line verdict naming the missing tables and never-run stages. Run against the live database today it must NOT report a clean state, and must name at least v2_work_external_ids, v2_local_works, v2_release_work_attachments (absent tables) and stage_56_mint_works (never run) -- re-measure rather than trusting that list, since more will have landed by the time you build it. It must also report where a table holds MORE THAN ONE generation, since that is the other way a live figure misleads (v2_release_work_map holds runs 54 and 65 today). PIPELINE_SPEC.md or tools/README.md records that a pipeline item closing does NOT imply the live database carries it, and points at this procedure. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Run a catch-up pass after each pipeline batch so live never drifts
nodes.why: Drift that accumulates silently is the problem; drift closed on a known cadence is just scheduling.

nodes.body: import_v2.py runs one whole-database refresh_statistics between ingest and derivation. It cannot describe a table whose rows do not exist yet, so on a first run every derived table reaches its consumer with no sqlite_stat1 row. Stage 41 makes it visible: it fills v2_rom_entries (290,229) and v2_rom_hashes (738,822) entirely after that point, and stage 60 then reads them. MEASURED COST, isolated on a clone: stage 60 takes 19.2s with the statistics absent and 13.2s with them present. About 6 seconds.
nodes.done_looks_like: A full import_v2.py run from clean completes stage 60 in under 60 seconds with no manual ANALYZE, proven by a timed end-to-end run recorded with its duration; sqlite_stat1 carries rows for v2_rom_entries and v2_rom_hashes after a full run, asserted by a test rather than observed once; the statistics refresh happens after the derived tables are populated rather than only between ingest and derivation, and a test fails if a table declared in a stage contract is read by a later stage while carrying no sqlite_stat1 row; the fix is general, so a stage added after 41 inherits it without a code change; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Analyse the derived tables, not just the staged ones
nodes.why: A stage should leave usable statistics for the stage that reads it; driven off the contract each stage already declares, a new stage inherits this for free.

nodes.body:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-03. THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT READING. Run 66 has status='failed', completed_at='2026-07-31 15:02:18' and error_message NULL -- but _run_stage's handler (import_v2.py:173) ALWAYS writes error_message=str(exc), and a KeyboardInterrupt is a BaseException that walks past `except Exception`. complete_run stamps completed_at=datetime('now'). So 15:02:18 is when a human marked the row failed, 33s before run 67 started -- the same hand that wrote 'terminated manually' on run 6. 52m41s is an UPPER BOUND ON WALL CLOCK, not a measurement of the stage. Recurrence is N=1: runs 66 and 67 are the only stage-60 runs that have ever existed.

WHAT IS SOLID: run 66 wrote ZERO rows to v2_quality_metrics and zero to v2_quality_spot_checks, and insert_metrics is the first write. THE STALL WAS IN THE READ PHASE, not in writes or write-lock contention.

THE WAL HYPOTHESIS NEEDS A PRECONDITION NOBODY STATED. import_v2.py holds one connection for the whole pipeline and connect() leaves the default 1000-page autocheckpoint live, so at each COMMIT a passive checkpoint resets the live frame count to zero while leaving the FILE at high-water mark. File size is not frame count, and the item reasoned from file size. For the WAL to have been slow, a second connection must have held a read transaction open and starved every checkpoint -- which is positively implied, since wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) cannot succeed while another connection holds a read lock, so the TRUNCATE working at 15:02 is evidence the blocking reader had just left. 'WAL truncated' and 'competitor gone' are the same event, and a single-process clone experiment cannot separate them.

TWO FURTHER UNTESTED VARIABLES: (1) that competing reader, as an independent cause; (2) OS page-cache warmth -- run 67 started 33 seconds later on a cache warmed by up to 52 minutes of reads, so 9.6s is not a clean control. Separating it needs `sudo purge` between arms.

RULED OUT: code drift. quality_assess.py was last committed 2026-07-31 13:00:30 (57afdf8), next 2026-08-03. Runs 66 and 67 ran the same file.

Worth knowing: stage 60 has form. _releases_with_hashed_rom_entry's docstring records that a per-release EXISTS over 800k rom rows 'does not finish' (quality_assess.py:1009). That shape was gone by run 66, but the stage has previously contained a non-terminating query.
nodes.done_looks_like:
REFRAMED from 'reproduce the stall' to 'instrument it and bound the mechanism', which the original acceptance already permits ('if the WAL is NOT the cause, the finding is recorded and the next candidate named'). Two parts, and the FIRST MUST LAND BEFORE THE NEXT FULL REBUILD or the observation is burned:

(1) Stage 60 logs, at entry and at exit, PRAGMA wal_checkpoint output (busy / log frames / checkpointed frames) and a per-metric-function timing breakdown -- roughly 20 lines. Then the next rebuild either reproduces the stall and identifies itself in one line, or does not, and both outcomes are informative.

(2) A standalone microbenchmark that does NOT clone the 11GB database: a ~2GB scratch SQLite with autocheckpoint off, a second connection parked in BEGIN, ~560,000 frames pushed into the WAL, then N random point reads timed with the WAL live versus truncated. Roughly 100x confirms the mechanism is sufficient; roughly 2x exonerates it and moves the hunt to cache warmth. Minutes, ~5GB, zero risk to the live file. Note that you must park a second reader to build the WAL at all -- which is itself the proof that the live incident also required one.

The finding is written down either way, naming which of the three candidates (WAL frames, competing reader, page-cache warmth) the evidence supports and which remain open. The item is NOT closed by a green rebuild alone; it is closed by the instrumentation existing and the microbenchmark verdict being recorded. pytest reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Stage 60's 51 minutes was never measured; instrument it before the next rebuild
nodes.why: It will recur on the next full rebuild, it looks identical to a hang, and the diagnosis on record was wrong -- so nobody is currently looking for the real cause.

nodes.body: scummvm is a runtime, not a platform -- the manifest already says so and deliberately gives it no IGDB platform id. But every stage-55 tier gates on platform, so all 349 scummvm releases fail: 0 are matched today, while 268 of them carry a title IGDB already knows as a work. The gate exists to stop a Mega Drive release matching an arcade work; for a runtime there is no platform claim to check, so it protects nothing and blocks everything.
nodes.done_looks_like: The manifest marks scummvm as a runtime rather than merely omitting its igdb key, and the matcher reads that flag rather than inferring it from a missing id; a stage-55 run matches at least 240 of the 268 scummvm releases whose title_norm equals a work title_norm, up from 0; no release on a real platform changes its work as a result, proven by diffing the release-to-work map before and after and showing every changed row is a runtime system; the exemption is general, so adding dosbox as a runtime needs a manifest edit and no code change, pinned by a test; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

nodes.why: ScummVM is how these games are actually played on a Mac, and the work carries the metadata and artwork the release needs.

nodes.body: A function, not a gate. Pulls the two doubtful populations -- releases minted despite a title collision, and releases minted with no IGDB work at all -- interleaves them, orders by LaunchBox vote count, excludes anything already adjudicated in the curation artifact, and takes a limit. Callable at any time at any depth without a rebuild, so the queue drains continuously rather than being sized once by a threshold.
nodes.done_looks_like: A callable function returns the top N releases needing judgment, interleaved from both causes, ordered by community_rating_count descending, with cause, candidate works and vote count per row; it excludes every release already carrying a verdict in tools/game-database-v2/curation/work_verdicts.jsonl, proven by adding a verdict and showing the row disappears from the next call; calling it twice with no intervening change returns the same rows, so it is a view and not a consuming queue; it needs no pipeline run -- it reads the current generation and is correct immediately after any stage-55 run; a verdict of attach/alias/mint/reject applies on the next pipeline run and survives a full rebuild, proven by rebuilding a clone; alias verdicts enter the works layer as alternative names so one alias resolves every release with that title on any platform; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

nodes.why: Nothing should be held out of the catalogue waiting on review; the queue is a view over what was minted, so how deep to review becomes a query rather than a pipeline constant.

nodes.body: works_build maps ports to their root's work and skips expansions/episodes/seasons -- correct, since a port is not a second game. But the title goes with it: 3,686 of 8,147 ports (45%), 1,700 of 1,722 expansions, 927 episodes and 854 seasons leave no work carrying their name, so a release titled after one can never match. Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne, Minecraft, Tekken: Dark Resurrection and DKC Returns 3D are all staged from IGDB and all unreachable. Separately, IGDB's alternative_names are staged and not projected at all, which is the same class of loss.

nodes.body:
TWO orderings in stage 55 both pick by position rather than by evidence quality, and they compound.

(a) TITLE ORDER. The per-release loop tries canonical_title_norm through all seven tiers, and only if that matches NOTHING walks the release aliases, breaking on the first alias matching at ANY tier. So a canonical title at tier_7 beats an alias at tier_1.

(b) TIER ORDER. tier_4 (alias, platform-gated) runs BEFORE tier_5 (primary title, exact title AND exact year, platform-blind), so a derived alias outranks an exact match on a work literally named the same. 4 rows: ESPN International Track & Field gbc, The Adventures of Dr. Franken nes, C&C 3: Kane's Wrath, XCOM: Enemy Within windows.

MEASURED 2026-08-03 by replaying both arms through the real cascade over releases 62 x works 68. 256 releases repoint; 2,079 more keep their work and gain a truer tier label. COVERAGE IS PROVABLY INVARIANT: 105,349 -> 105,349, because the new arm matches exactly when the old one does -- this rule can only MOVE a match, never gain or lose one. That is what makes it tractable rather than whack-a-mole: the affected set is enumerable and hand-checkable.

All 256 were read. Roughly 200+ are plainly right and dominated by regional retitles, which is what aliases are for (Life Force -> Salamander, Vendetta -> Crime Fighters 2, Denaris -> Katakis, Airwolf -> Blue Thunder). The wrong tail is 15-25, including Super Off Road -> Disney's TaleSpin via alias 'talespin gg', Friday Night Funkin' -> Fight N' Fall via 'fnf', and 5 DOS releases via 'start bat'. Token-overlap was tested as a filter and REJECTED: 58 of 256 lose all overlap but most of those are the correct regional retitles.

Both halves are one root cause -- the cascade's tier order is used as a SEARCH order when it is meant to be a PREFERENCE order. A second independent defect resolving to the same fix is evidence the defect is structural.

RE-MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING: the 256 predates RS-173's alias widening and is a lower bound; expect 400-500. Harness exists at scratchpad/wt-scope/rs298_replay.py (re-run is ~3 min).
nodes.done_looks_like: Stage 55 evaluates every candidate title for a release across every tier and selects the best, with the 0.05 alias penalty applied to the SCORE rather than to the ordering, and ties broken deterministically; the ranking rule is stated in PIPELINE_SPEC. The eight named releases each land on the more specific work, named individually. Because this reorders thousands of decisions, the acceptance is a MEASURED before/after against a same-generation control -- gained/lost/repointed as three figures, with a hand-judged sample of the repointed large enough to state a better/worse ratio, and every LOST release judged individually. A net-positive headline is NOT sufficient evidence; RS-297 gained 94 while breaking 13. pytest and cargo test report 0 failed.
nodes.title: The match cascade takes the first answer, not the best one
nodes.why: A tier number that does not order the answers is not a confidence scale; it is a label on whichever title happened to be tried first.

nodes.body: reject_colliding_names drops a derived name when another work already carries it as a PRIMARY title, reasoning that tiers 1-2 resolve it there so aliasing it elsewhere buys nothing. That reasoning is conditional on the primary-title work being REACHABLE, and RS-297 breaks the condition: once a port's platforms move to the nearest work, the parent stops carrying them. Verified on the live corpus -- igdb 138304 'Sensible Soccer: European Champions - 92/93 Edition' is a type-10 DIRECT CHILD of 13257 'Sensible Soccer: European Champions'; after RS-297 the child correctly holds 12 platforms and the parent holds 3, but the child's alias is dropped as a shadow of the parent's title. One work has the platform, the other has the name, neither can match. Same shape for Sonic Adventure DX (23695, type 10, parent 7860). This costs 13 of the 19 releases RS-297 loses, including 5x Sensible Soccer, 2x Sonic Adventure and Castlevania: Rondo of Blood.
nodes.done_looks_like: Shadow does NOT fire when the shadow-owning work and the alias target are the same work family -- one is the other's IGDB parent or child, or they are linked in v2_work_relationships -- because two works in one family competing for a name is resolved by the platform gate, which is the intended behaviour rather than the hazard. Shadow still fires for unrelated works: the 101 Dalmatians case and the Space Harrier 3-D spelling case both stay dropped, named individually as tests. The one-work-per-derived-name invariant is RESTATED, not silently abandoned -- say in the code what it becomes, since same-family competition is now permitted by design. Measured on a stage 50/55 re-run with RS-297 present: the 13 named regressions return, lost falls to 6 or fewer, and every remaining loss is judged and shown to be a wrong match correctly refused rather than a real one dropped. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

nodes.body:
Owner's observation 2026-08-03: acceptance criteria should be codified and re-checked immediately before dev, because the numbers keep shifting. EVERY item worked that day had at least one stale figure, without exception:

RS-213 asked for rules_total 20 / files 571; true 28 / 581.
RS-300's OWN correction was wrong -- it said 152,059 distinct Steam appids; true 153,575.
RS-179 asked for ~37,287 collection memberships, which is ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE: below the 38,849 distinct works the same item's body quotes, and a work in a collection cannot yield fewer rows than works. True 40,495.
RS-246 said 857 of 45,970 unmatched; true 786 of 45,897, and its vote ladder 512/199/49/11 is really 452/148/24/3.
RS-304 said '42 missing-parent, 1 true chain'; true 41 / 1 parentless / 1 CYCLE.
RS-308 named one dead field; there are five.
RS-192 said 19 discovery rules; 28.
RS-47 asked for '41+ tests (40 before)' against a suite of 714 -- stale by 17x.
RS-193's acceptance asserts v2_releases = 158,067; it is 164,696.
RS-237 and RS-247's headline reproducers could not be reproduced at all.

THE STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSIS, which is more useful than 're-measure more often'. These acceptances embedded a SIGHTING as though it were an INVARIANT. Two different kinds of statement are being written into one field:

  INVARIANT -- what must be true after the fix. 'Coverage does not move: byte-identical release_work_map dumps per release id.' 'One map row per igdb_id, proven by an assertion in the stage.' 'A derived name resolves to exactly one work, or to several that are all versions of one game.' These are stable, they are the actual contract, and they do not rot.

  SIGHTING -- how big the defect looked when someone measured it. '857 rows.' '~37,287 memberships.' '42 of the 43.' These are evidence that the defect is real and worth doing, and they are worthless as a target -- worse than worthless, because a builder who hits a stale number has been rewarded for bending the code toward it, and a gate that checks one raises a false alarm.

Sightings belong in the BODY, dated and attributed to a generation. Acceptances should state invariants plus RE-MEASURE THIS AT DISPATCH.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Two halves, and the first is worth more than the second.

(1) THE CONVENTION IS WRITTEN DOWN and applied going forward: an acceptance states INVARIANTS (what must hold after the fix, expressed so it cannot rot) and never a bare count as a target. A count that is evidence of the defect's size is written in the body with the date and the ingest_runs generation it was measured on, and the acceptance says 're-measure at dispatch and report the true figure' rather than naming the number. Where a figure genuinely is the contract, it is expressed as the query that produces it, not as the answer.

(2) A PROBE RUNNER makes it cheap, because a convention nobody can execute will decay. Acceptances already carry literal probes (grep -c ..., SELECT ... FROM ...). Give an item's probes a runnable block, and a script that extracts and runs them against the live database read-only and prints RECORDED vs CURRENT side by side, flagging every drift. Model it on scripts/catchup_check.py (RS-264): read-only, derived rather than hand-kept, one-line verdict, --json. Run it against three items whose figures are known stale (RS-193 asserts v2_releases 158,067 against a true 164,696; RS-47 asserts a 40-test suite against 714) and show it names them.

The point is NOT to auto-rewrite acceptances -- a drifted figure sometimes means the defect changed shape, which is a finding, not a number to update. The point is that nobody should be able to dispatch an item without having been shown which of its figures no longer hold.

pytest and cargo test report 0 failed.
nodes.title: An acceptance should carry invariants; the defect's size belongs in the body
nodes.why: A builder who hits a stale number has been rewarded for bending the code to it; three builders today were right to refuse and one gate had to prove a target impossible.

nodes.body:
FOUND 2026-08-03 by the RS-248 builder while measuring, out of scope for its items, deliberately not folded in. THIS BLOCKS THE NEXT FULL REBUILD.

clear_releases_derived deletes v2_release_regions on entry. v2_rom_entries.release_region_id is a FOREIGN KEY into it. v2_rom_entries is DELIBERATELY not cleared (schema.py:79-82). And NO INDEX exists on any release_region_id column. Both failure modes were reproduced on a clone:

(1) UNINDEXED -- each of 107,207 parent deletes full-scans 290,229 spine rows. Stage 40 burned 34 MINUTES AT 100% CPU without committing the clear, and was killed. It does not fail; it fails to finish.

(2) WITH AN INDEX ADDED -- it fails honestly in 11 SECONDS with sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed. 194,496 spine rows hold a live release_region_id.

WHY NOBODY HAS HIT IT: live run 62 (stage 40, 2026-07-31 14:05) completed in 107s because stage 41 had never populated the spine at that point. Stage 41 has since run (run 63, 290,229 rom entries). So the very next stage-40 run against this database takes the (1) path.

NOTE THE FAMILY RESEMBLANCE to RS-268: an unindexed cascade over a large table, presenting as a stage that runs for tens of minutes without completing rather than erroring. Different stage and different mechanism -- stage 60 stalled in its READ phase and wrote nothing -- but anyone reading one should read the other.

The RS-248 builder worked around it only to measure, identically on both arms (added idx_v2_rom_entries_release_region and cleared v2_rom_entries/v2_rom_hashes on the clone; stage 40 then ran in 1.8-2.9 min). That workaround is NOT in either commit.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Stage 40 re-runs against a database whose ROM spine is populated, and completes. THE DESIGN QUESTION MUST BE ANSWERED, NOT PAPERED OVER: either stage 40 clears the spine it invalidates, or stage 41 rebuilds from it, or the FK is restructured so region rows are not the parent of spine rows. Whichever is chosen, write down why in PIPELINE_SPEC next to the clear order -- the current arrangement is a deliberate choice (schema.py:79-82 says the spine is not cleared) and the next person needs to know what changed and what did not.

AN INDEX ALONE IS NOT A FIX. It converts a 34-minute hang into an 11-second IntegrityError, which is strictly better and should also be done, but the run still cannot proceed. Do both: the index so failure is fast and legible, and the clear/rebuild decision so it succeeds.

Verify on a cp -c clone of the live database, which is the only place the defect is currently reachable: stage 40 alone completes, and stage 41 afterwards leaves v2_rom_entries consistent with the regions actually written by that run -- proven by a query showing zero spine rows pointing at a release_region_id that no longer exists, not by the stage exiting 0.

Report both timings (before and after) and say which of the three designs you chose and what it costs. A test proves the clear order is safe with a populated spine -- the existing suite passes today only because its fixtures leave the spine empty, which is exactly why this reached the live database unnoticed.

nodes.why: The next full rebuild runs stage 40 against a populated spine for the first time, and will hang for over half an hour rather than erroring.

nodes.body:
Found 2026-08-03 within an hour of RS-326 merging, by running the tool against RS-159 and disbelieving the answer.

acceptance_probe.py reported RS-159's 'MAX(ingest_run_id)' probe as DRIFTED, RECORDED 2 / CURRENT 4. The literal probe returns 2. The extra two are the COMPILED BYTECODE:

  grep -rn  'MAX(ingest_run_id)' pipeline_v2/ | wc -l   ->  2
  grep -ran 'MAX(ingest_run_id)' pipeline_v2/ | wc -l   ->  4    (+ two .pyc in __pycache__)

THE VERDICT IS THEREFORE NON-DETERMINISTIC. Whether __pycache__ exists depends on whether anyone has run the test suite recently, so the same item probes DRIFTED or HOLDS depending on unrelated activity. Same root cause as the mutation-harness trap that produced false survivors for three agents today.

A FALSE 'DRIFTED' IS AS HARMFUL AS A FALSE 'HOLDS'. This tool exists so nobody dispatches an item without being shown which figures no longer hold; a spurious drift sends a builder chasing a phantom, and worse, teaches everyone to disbelieve the tool -- which costs more than not having it.

The fix is one flag on the grep executor: --exclude-dir=__pycache__, or --binary-files=without-match, or both. Prefer excluding by directory: it is what a reader means by 'grep the source', and it also covers .egg-info, .mypy_cache and anything else generated.
nodes.done_looks_like:
The grep executor ignores generated artefacts, so a probe's answer depends only on the source. Verify by the reproducer that found it: with __pycache__ present under tools/game-database-v2/pipeline_v2/, acceptance_probe.py on RS-159 reports the 'MAX(ingest_run_id)' probe as 2, matching the literal 'grep -rn ... | wc -l' -- and reports the SAME number after `find . -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} +`. Run it both ways and show both.

A test pins it by seeding a fixture tree containing a match in a real file AND a match inside a __pycache__ directory, asserting the count is 1. That test must FAIL if the exclusion is removed -- mutate it and say so, clearing __pycache__ and setting PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 first, since this repo's bytecode cache has already produced false results for three agents today.

While you are in there, check the other executors for the same class of problem: does the sqlite3 executor's count depend on anything outside the query, and can a pytest probe pick up a collection error rather than a count? Report what you find; fixing beyond the grep case is optional and should be reported rather than assumed.

Do NOT widen this into a rework of the extractor. The tool's SKIP behaviour is deliberate and correct -- it prefers missing a probe to inventing one. pytest and cargo test --workspace report 0 failed.

nodes.body:
From reviewing the top row of the Stage 56 queue on the first day it existed (Balloon Fight, NES, 293 votes, title_collision). Full recommendation is an artifact on this item.

THE IDENTITY COLLAPSE IS CORRECT; THE PROJECTION LOSS IS NOT. A port does not create a second work -- keep that. But the subordinate entry's payload is dropped at projection, and the work inherits the ROOT's metadata even when the root is the sparser record.

VERIFIED against the rebuilt generation (works run 77, staging single-generation):
  igdb 2735  Balloon Fight      type 11 port, parent 40516 | 113 ratings | 395-char summary | 424-char storyline
  igdb 40516 Vs. Balloon Fight  root                       |   0 ratings | 112-char summary |   0 storyline
  igdb 195030 Balloon Fight     root, unrelated Watara game|   0 ratings |   0              |   0

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04 by the RS-360 second-pass analysis, isolated on its own clone and confirmed by re-running the UNCHANGED stage 55. Stage 50's incremental UPSERT does not restamp v2_works.title_norm, so a work carried over from an earlier generation keeps the normalisation in force when it was first written. RS-337 changed normalisation (a trailing '+' is now spelled ' plus') and 338 works in generation 91 were never restamped: work 2026135 'Xevious 3D/G+' stores 'xevious 3d g' where normalize_title now gives 'xevious 3d g plus'. MEASURED, by repairing the 338 rows on a clone and re-running stage 55 with no code change: +62 matches gained and -9 LOST. So the stale column is doing two things at once -- withholding 62 correct matches, and holding 9 wrong matches in place that correct normalisation would drop. THIS DISTORTS ANY STAGE-55 MEASUREMENT taken against generation 91: an entry-grain matcher re-derives the norm from the entry name, routes around the stale column, and the 62 appear as gains from the variant rather than from a data repair. Both live RS-360 analyses were warned mid-flight. RELATED but distinct from RS-370, which is about stage 55 re-deriving alt-name norms AT MATCH TIME; this is a stored column that was never rewritten.

VERIFY: 0 works where title_norm <> normalize_title(title); the 62 withheld matches arrive and the 9 wrong ones leave, each of the 9 named and judged individually to confirm they are the defect going rather than a regression. RE-MEASURE FIRST -- 338/62/9 are 2026-08-04 sightings on generation 91. Note the 9 losses mean this is NOT a pure gain: report gained/lost as two figures, not a net.

The runtime intersection of imported action records, canonical unbracketed CoinOPS cfg basenames and exact MAME filename-to-release identity produces exactly one deterministic set scheme per matched MAME set and none outside the intersection; multiple sets resolving to one release remain distinct schemes. Native MAME inputs are the stable game-side layer. The preconfigured corpus and CoinOPS each retain their own observed native-input-to-XInput projection. CoinOPS-derived arcade placement is calculated only by composing the CoinOPS XInput projection through a versioned, replaceable adapter: A/B/LB/LT map to bottom-row legends 1/2/3/4 and X/Y/RB/RT map to top-row legends 5/6/7/8. It never passes through the preconfigured Xbox projection. Direct inputs, alternatives and multi-input macros remain structured rather than choosing a winner. Every generated fact retains source path/hash and observed/derived/default-assumed/conflict confidence; bracketed CoinOPS editions, unresolved release identities, missing/default mappings and contradictory labels are explicit review evidence rather than silently merged. nodes.body: Tom's direction 2026-08-19: disc games carry their serial inside the image at bounded offsets — Wii/GC ID6 (ISO offset 0, WBFS 0x200, RVZ/WIA header copy), PS1/PS2 SYSTEM.CNF boot line, PSP/PS3 PARAM.SFO, Dreamcast IP.BIN, Xbox XBE cert. Add an embedded-ID tier between names and hashing per the query-cost hierarchy. Critically: the hash tier is STRUCTURALLY DEAD for container formats — catalogue hashes are Redump/No-Intro hashes of raw images, and a CHD/RVZ/GCZ container's own hash can never equal them, so every hash fallback on those formats is waste by construction; gate the hash tier on format. CHD needs first-hunk decompression (chd crate) and dominates the archive (PS2 1,773 / PS1 660 / DC 520 CHDs); WBFS/ISO/RVZ are near-trivial. Also closes RS-578 (Wii id6 from the WBFS header beats 4-char name extraction) and generalises RS-201 (Switch/Vita header reads, 87% recovery) to all disc systems.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Phase 4 is rebuilt: the embedded-ID tier reads serials from CHD images, so a disc image identifies itself without depending on its filename.

THE REBUILD SPEC IS ON THIS ITEM: phase-4-lost-work-and-rebuild-spec.md. It is the destroyed worker's own final report, preserved verbatim, and it carries every design decision plus the eight real-archive serials that are the acceptance target. Read it first. A rebuild that reproduces those eight reads at those costs is correct.

=== THE VALUE CASE WAS MEASURED WRONG, AND THIS SUPERSEDES IT ===

phase-4-residual-remeasured-79-of-3049.md concluded the dependency was not worth it, on the basis that only 79 of 3,049 CHDs fail identification. That measurement is sound but it answered the wrong question, and the conclusion is withdrawn.

It measured TOM'S archive, which he curated and named himself, with serials embedded in the filenames. That is the best case, not the normal one. Almost no PS2 library in the wild carries the serial in the filename, and there the embedded-ID read is not a last-resort tier at all - it is the PRIMARY identification mechanism. Do not re-derive the 79-file justification; it does not describe the product's case.

It also never counted CORRECTION. The filename-serial tier can be confidently WRONG: 'The Urbz [SLUS-21066]' resolves to The Sims 2, because SLUS-21066 genuinely is The Sims 2 and the filename carries a typo. Reading the true id from the image is the only thing that can catch that, and a wrong identity is worse than a missing one. See RS-603.

=== SETTLE THE DEPENDENCY SHAPE BEFORE PAYING FOR IT ===

The spec records that chd 0.3.4 pulls seven transitive packages including lzma-rs-perf-exp - an EXPERIMENTAL FORK, in an app parsing untrusted files off a network share where ordinary lzma-rs is already locked - and unconditionally enables flate2/zlib-rs, switching the deflate backend workspace-wide.

That cost was inherited from one crate's transitive set and never tested against the actual files. FIRST, sample the CHD headers across the real archive and report the CODEC DISTRIBUTION. Compression tags live in the first ~124 bytes, so this is a bounded header read of a few dozen files, not a decompression. If the corpus is predominantly zlib or zstd, the LZMA surface may be avoidable and the dependency shrinks; if it is LZMA-heavy, say so and take the crate as specified.

Report the distribution before implementing. If it changes the dependency shape materially, say so and stop - that is a decision worth a checkpoint.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

Reproduce the eight verified reads: PS1 SLUS-00975 and SLUS-01300; PS2 SLUS-20265 and SLUS-20751; Dreamcast T36803N and MK-51064 (alias 51064); Saturn T-11304H and T-8113H. One to three hunks and 19,584 to 58,752 bytes per file.

Hold the ceilings the original chose: 12 decompressed hunks and 4 MiB per file, CRC failure poisons the reader, every CHD including malformed ones opened exactly once. The tier performs no full-file reads.

Because the flate2 backend switch is unavoidable, the gate MUST exercise ZIP extraction and PNG decode/resize/encode - they change outside the scanner. Report the release binary size delta (the original was +385,904 bytes, 2.73%).

Report how many CHDs gain an identity AND how many change identity - the second number is the correction case and was never measured before.

nodes.body: roman_to_int in src-tauri/src/rom_scanner/sequel.rs (and its new Python mirror) does unrestricted subtractive arithmetic over i/v/x/l/c/d/m. It accepts iiii=4, vv=10, xxxxx=50, iix=8, vx=5, and misreads real words. The >50 cap is what stops 'mix'=1009, so the CAP is doing the validation the parser does not.
nodes.done_looks_like:
The parser validates canonical Roman form rather than summing symbols. These must be REJECTED: iiii, vv, xxxxx, iix, vx (each a test). These must still parse: ii, iii, iv, ix, xl, xii.

Real catalogue words must stop folding to numbers. Measured in generation 101: token 'xxl' appears 55 times and folds to 30, 'il' 374 times folding to 49, 'vivi' 3 times folding to 10, 'vvvvvv' 12 times folding to 30. Concrete titles: 'Asterix & Obelix XXL: Romastered' becomes [30] and 'Asterix & Obelix XXL 2' becomes [30,2]; 'ViVi Vicious Viper' becomes [10]; 'Bra$il' normalises to 'bra il' and becomes [49]. Each of those four is a test asserting no spurious number.

Decide and record how the word problem is solved - canonical-form validation alone may not be enough, since XXL and VVVVVV are canonically-shaped. Positional or contextual evidence may be needed. Say what you chose.

Both consumers stay equivalent: the Rust implementation and the Python mirror must agree, and the shared fixture in config/match_rules/sequel_vectors.json must still pass on both sides. Do NOT modify that file.

Report how many scanner matches and how many stage-30 edges change.

nodes.body: The libretro DAT legitimately records SLUS-21066 for both 'Sims 2, The (USA) (Beta)' and 'Urbz, The - Sims in the City (USA)'. The pipeline attached one and dropped the other; the scanner takes LIMIT 1 on the same lookup. Neither treats a shared serial as ambiguous.
nodes.done_looks_like:
A serial attested for several titles is resolved by asking whether those titles are the SAME GAME. If they are, it attaches to that one release. If they are not, it is ambiguous evidence and is refused with the reason recorded. It is never resolved by picking one.

=== THIS SUPERSEDES THE EARLIER FRAMING OF THIS ITEM ===

Measured 2026-08-20, and it changes the shape. The SHIPPED catalogue contains ZERO serials owned by more than one game - 0 of 69,637 even under the scanner's normalisation. The ambiguity is not in the export. It is resolved upstream, arbitrarily, and the loser is dropped, so the export looks clean while the evidence has been thrown away.

In the SOURCE, 7,047 serials are attested for more than one game title. By platform: psp 2,027, xbox360 835, xbox 662, megadrive 462, nds 445, psx 403, gba 336, ps2 266, saturn 243, cdi 239.

=== THE 7,047 ARE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE RULE MUST SEPARATE THEM ===

MOSTLY THE SAME GAME, differing only by region, revision or dump:
  AC-001   Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX 2 (Europe) | (USA)
  J9078E   Vid Grid (USA) | (Alt) | (Rev 1)
  J9016E   Blue Lightning (USA) | (En,Fr,De) (Alt 2)
These must ATTACH, all of them, to the single release. Region and revision distinguish FILES, not releases, and many serials per release is the intended grain. This is the population RS-606 was written for - the two items are the same seam and should be built together.

SOMETIMES GENUINELY DIFFERENT GAMES sharing a placeholder or reused value:
  123-4567  Bratz J2S (Proto) | Incredibles Animation Sample (Proto) | ROX (Proto)
These must be REFUSED, with the reason recorded, exactly as RS-589 taught the seams to refuse ties.

Report the split. Neither number is known and the ratio decides how much this is worth.

=== THE WORKED CASE THAT STARTED IT ===

The libretro PS2 DAT records SLUS-21066 for both 'Sims 2, The (USA) (Beta)' and 'Urbz, The - Sims in the City (USA)'. The pipeline kept the beta and dropped The Urbz, so the catalogue maps that serial to The Sims 2 alone. Three external sources confirm SLUS-21066 as The Urbz retail: PlayStation 2 DataCenter, GameHacking.org, Coleccionando VOY. A correctly-named disc in the archive was very nearly renamed on the strength of our own wrong data.

Under the rule above this is the SECOND kind - a retail game and a beta of a different game are not the same game - so it refuses, and both attachments are recorded as evidence rather than one being silently chosen.

=== THE SCANNER HALF IS ALREADY DONE ===

matcher.rs lookup_serial now selects LIMIT 2, withholds identity when two distinct owners appear, and persists the ambiguity as evidence (merged in RS-579). It is currently a no-op because the export contains no ambiguity - so THIS work is what makes that guard meaningful. Expect the export to gain ambiguous serials as a RESULT of this change; that is correct, and the scanner is ready for it.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

Measure by replay, not rebuild. Report: how many serials attach to more than one game after the change, how many refuse, and how many releases gain a region they previously lacked - that last number is the user-visible benefit.

Every changed identity is judged individually. Prove one end-to-end case: a release carrying only a USA serial gains its PAL sibling, and a PAL file that fell through to name matching resolves on the serial tier.

Do NOT infer region from a serial prefix and write it onto a release. Region belongs on the rom entry.

nodes.body: The scanner's safety-flagged key ladder (RS-586) went into the ROM matcher only. match_evidence.py still joins sources without article stripping, subtitle handling or joined forms, so a quarter of the PS2 serials already downloaded sit unattached in staging.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Stage 30 gains the structural key ladder the ROM scanner already uses, so source records that name the same game in different shapes join instead of being dropped.

=== THE ASYMMETRY ===

The file-to-catalogue matcher is now materially smarter than the source-to-source matcher that BUILDS the catalogue. src-tauri/src/rom_scanner/matcher.rs carries a safety-flagged structural key ladder (RS-586): k0 normalized, k1 article-stripped, k2 joined, k3 subtitle-stripped, gentlest rung first, where a key with exactly ONE owner in the corpus is a provable match and a key with several is a hard stop. match_evidence.py has NONE of it - no article stripping, no subtitle rung, no joined form. It received the numeral work (RS-590/591/593/597) and the ambiguity gates (RS-589), but never the ladder that does the heavy lifting.

=== THE MEASURED PRIZE, ON ONE PLATFORM ===

All figures 2026-08-20 sightings - re-measure at dispatch.

LaunchBox carries no serials; they come from the libretro/Redump DATs, which key on ROM names. A serial therefore reaches a game only if stage 30 joins a DAT entry to a LaunchBox record BY NAME.

For ps2 alone: the libretro source holds 12,993 distinct serials, 9,710 reached the catalogue, and 3,283 NEVER ATTACHED. In the shipped catalogue ps2 sits at 4,265 of 4,752 games with a serial (89.8%). Other platforms are worse and should be measured too - xbox 37.0%, psp 51.1%, ps3 71.1%, dreamcast 72.2%.

The Urbz: Sims in the City on ps2 is the worked example: the game is present and faithful to source (launchbox_id 9837), and it has no serial because the join never happened.

=== WHAT TO PORT, AND WHAT NOT TO ===

Port the LADDER and its safety property: gentlest rung first, single-owner keys decide, multi-owner keys are a hard stop that does NOT fall through to fuzzy. The blocking half already exists here - RS-589 taught these seams to refuse ties - so the pieces fit.

Carry the constraints the scanner learned the hard way, and read the RS-586 artifacts on that item before designing:
- A minimum character floor on lossy rungs; short keys collide destructively.
- Bidirectional word-boundary token containment, not raw substring - 'Pit' must not take 'Pitstop'.
- strip_ext's rsplit rule is for DAT FILENAMES and must never touch titles: it turns 'Mr.Mine' into 'Mr'.

Do NOT port the scanner's hash or embedded-id tiers - different problem. Do NOT weaken any RS-589 refusal.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

Measure by REPLAY, not rebuild. Do not run a full pipeline stage against the live 10.9GB database and do not rebuild it.

Report, per platform for at least ps2, psx, dreamcast, psp, ps3, xbox: serials attached before and after, and edges added, removed and changed. Every CHANGED identity is judged individually, not counted - a serial attaching to the wrong game is worse than one not attaching at all, because the scanner trusts serials over names.

Name the rung that produced each newly attached serial in a sample of 30, so the recall is attributable rather than aggregate.

If a rung produces even one wrong attachment, report it and disable that rung rather than shipping the recall.
