nodes.body: Roughly 1,114 unattached ps2 serials name titles whose release already carries a serial for another region. Region lives on the rom entry, so many serials per release is the intended grain - and without them a non-US disc never resolves on the serial tier at all.
nodes.done_looks_like:
A regional release resolves to its game. Where a source serial names a title that unambiguously identifies one catalogue release, it attaches to that release even when the release already carries serials for other regions.

=== WHY THIS IS CORRECT, NOT REDUNDANT ===

The identity model settles it: REGION LIVES ON THE ROM ENTRY, NOT THE RELEASE. A release is work x platform; region and revision distinguish FILES. So many serials per release is the intended grain, not duplication - the shipped catalogue already does it deliberately, with 28 serials on Metal Gear Solid 3: Subsistence and 17 on Gran Turismo 4 (ps2, 2026-08-20).

The practical consequence is the point of the item: if only the USA serial is attached, a PAL disc does not resolve by serial at all and falls back to name matching. Cross-linking the regional serials is what lets a European or Japanese disc identify itself.

=== THE POPULATION, AND WHY IT IS MECHANICAL ===

Region is a parenthetical tag in Redump/No-Intro DAT names and each regional release carries its own serial, so the evidence is in the source data rather than inferred:

  SCCS-40001  Ape Escape 2 (China)
  SCES-50885  Ape Escape 2 (Europe)
  SCES-51102  Ape Escape 2 (France)

Sighting 2026-08-20, ps2 only: of 3,458 unattached serials, roughly 1,114 name a title whose catalogue release ALREADY carries at least one serial. RE-MEASURE, and measure the other platforms too - the ps2 figure was computed with a crude normaliser and an independent review produced a different framing of the same gap (1,246 raw spellings collapsing onto already-shipped serials by serial-string normalisation). Establish which measure is the right one and say so; they are counting different things and only one of them is this item's population.

=== THE RULE ===

Attach only where the title identifies exactly ONE release on that platform. Where the normalised title owns several releases, REFUSE and record why - the seams already behave this way (RS-589) and this must not become the exception. Do not let a region tag itself decide identity; it distinguishes files, not games.

Do NOT infer a region from a serial prefix and write it onto the release. Region belongs on the rom entry.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

Measure by replay, not rebuild. Report per platform: serials attached before and after, and how many releases gained a region they previously lacked - that second number is the user-visible benefit and the first is not.

Every changed identity is judged individually. A regional serial attaching to the WRONG game is worse than one not attaching, because the scanner trusts serials over names.

Prove the benefit end to end on at least one worked case: a release that today carries only a USA serial gains its PAL sibling, and a PAL file that previously fell through to name matching now resolves on the serial tier.
nodes.title: Cross-link regional serials so a PAL or Japanese disc can identify itself
nodes.why: Same seam as RS-603, measured 2026-08-20: the 7,047 source serials attested for several titles ARE the regional-variant population, so the attach-or-refuse rule and the regional cross-link are one piece of work. Build under RS-603; this item holds the regional acceptance.

nodes.body: A scan reports files_matched but not HOW. Rejection reasons (id absent from catalogue, id ambiguous, catalogue has no game_external_ids table) are only in evidence_json. Invariants: (1) the counts partition the PC candidates -- every candidate falls in exactly one identity outcome, and the outcome counts sum to the PC files scanned less deferred; (2) a row whose identity came from a store id is not stored with a classifier claiming a name match; (3) adding a new pc.* classifier cannot silently drop files out of the library -- the eligibility test does not enumerate classifier names; (4) the counts survive the transport as typed fields, not prose; (5) cargo test reports 0 failed.

nodes.body: v2_release_field_values accepts exactly three source types -- launchbox_game, libretro_game, gametdb_game. There is no curated/manual source, so a hand-entered field value is destroyed by the next rebuild. Durable curation exists for MATCHING decisions (v2_verdict_evaluations, the *_exceptions tables, replayed each generation, refined by RS-388) but not for field values. Needs: a curated source type at highest precedence, a stable key surviving release-id reassignment, replay per generation, and RS-388's needed/satisfied_upstream/stale classification so a hand value upstream has since fixed is reported rather than blindly reapplied.
nodes.title: Curated field values must survive a rebuild
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-22 intends a long-running agent session to fill metadata gaps by hand -- co-op type for non-arcade games, years for popular titles. Without this the work cannot be kept, so it blocks the enrichment programme rather than being part of it.

nodes.body: Create a separate Stage 58 carrier for release-grain canonical metadata assembled from exact release, matched-entry, matched-work, local-mint, and verdict-attachment evidence.
nodes.done_looks_like: Stage 58 produces a complete, reproducible synthesis generation. Invariants: (1) Stage 58 is registered after Stage 57 and before Stage 60; (2) exactly one synthesis header exists for every release in the selected current release generation, including map, local-mint and verdict-attachment routes; (3) the header pins release, works, release-work-map, local-mint and IGDB staging generations; (4) synthesized fields live in a separate carrier with generalized source reference, value kind, confidence, alternatives and provenance rather than overloading the Stage 40 candidate foreign key; (5) an exact-platform IGDB entry is preferred over work fallback; (6) a failed rebuild exposes no partial generation and leaves the previous successful generation readable; (7) current-generation Stage 40 field rows for LaunchBox, libretro and GameTDB are unchanged byte-for-byte; (8) display readers accept distinct release and synthesis generations; (9) stage, pin and full pipeline tests report 0 failed.
nodes.title: Stage 58: generation-pinned canonical metadata synthesis
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-22: LaunchBox covers 7% of 2024 PC games and 40% of the modern PC games it does have carry no genre. IGDB is the only source that can fill either gap, and today it cannot reach the merge layer at all.

nodes.title: Stage 58: canonical genres from all sources
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-22: 28.7% of LaunchBox-known Windows games have no genre at all, and the IGDB theme axis is the only source for whole categories the catalogue currently cannot express.

nodes.body: Map board observations to All ages, 7+, 13+, 17+, unrated, or unknown using the strictest valid age floor and preserved provenance.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every selected release has one valid age-band state. Invariants: (1) all 56 reviewed map rows are classified and tested; the current sighting is 41 rated, 8 unresolved, 3 explicit not-rated, 2 board identifiers, 1 pending and 1 advisory and is re-measured; (2) board identifiers are not observations; unresolved, pending and advisory values produce unknown; (3) only an explicit not-rated board result produces unrated; (4) rated evidence uses the maximum mapped age floor across boards before banding, never an average or preferred board; (5) raw source values and mapping decisions survive in provenance; (6) RS-644 remains excluded and unresolved IGDB IDs are not guessed; (7) coverage is re-measured and focused/full pipeline tests report 0 failed.
nodes.title: Stage 58: canonical age bands
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-22: a household filter needs young-kids / in-between / adult, and board labels are jargon outside their home market. ESRB 'Mature' means 17+, not adults-only, which is a different label again.

nodes.body: Synthesize separate nullable user and critic score/count pairs on a 0–10 scale with atomic evidence pairs and deterministic count weighting.
nodes.done_looks_like: Stage 58 emits user_rating, user_rating_count, critic_rating, and critic_rating_count under one reproducible formula. Invariants: (1) LaunchBox raw 0–5 user scores are multiplied by 2; IGDB rating/rating_count are user evidence divided by 10 from 0–100; IGDB aggregated_rating/aggregated_rating_count are critic evidence divided by 10; total_rating is excluded; (2) score/count pairs are atomic and contribute only when the score is finite and in source range and the count is an integer greater than zero; (3) each audience uses sum(normalized_score × count) / sum(count) and summed counts, with Decimal constructed from canonical source text, two fractional places, and ROUND_HALF_UP; (4) duplicate rows for one semantic source entity collapse once when identical and reject that entity when conflicting; (5) user and critic ballots never mix; (6) no evidence emits a NULL/NULL pair, never zero; (7) inputs, rejected pairs, deduplication and arithmetic survive in deterministic provenance; (8) the four fields are added to the Stage-58 policy surface while Stage-40 community_rating fields remain unchanged evidence; (9) quality_tier, Stage 70 and the schema-8 export contract remain RS-155/RS-651 scope; focused and full pipeline tests report zero failures.
nodes.title: Stage 58: user and critic ratings
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-22: LaunchBox has breadth with almost no depth (108,098 rated, half on 1-4 votes) and IGDB has depth on a narrow set (24,180 rated, averaging 42 votes). Using both is the only way to get either.

nodes.body: Represent local multiplayer, turn mode, split-screen, and explicit local co-op as independent tri-state facts with separate player maxima.
nodes.done_looks_like: The Stage-58 canonical policy surface carries local_multiplayer, max_local_players, local_turn_mode, split_screen, local_coop, and max_local_coop_players; players_min and the legacy generic player/co-op fields are not members of that canonical policy surface. Invariants: (1) booleans are true/false/NULL and missing or conflicting evidence is NULL, never false; turn mode is simultaneous, alternating, mixed, or NULL; maxima are positive integers or NULL; (2) exact GameTDB local_players and local_players_multi_cart plus mapped MAME PlayMode may establish local multiplayer and local maxima; GameTDB counts are accepted only at 1–32, any valid >1 votes true, and false requires all present valid counts to equal 1; per-entity, within-source, and cross-source maximum disagreements are sticky conflicts yielding NULL; MAME alone establishes turn mode and never co-op; (3) detailed IGDB evidence is read only from exact-platform objects on the header selected exact entry; work fallback, sibling and wrong-platform objects are excluded; (4) source inspection proved LaunchBox Cooperative preserves explicit true/false, so both values are usable local-co-op evidence and disagreement with exact-platform IGDB becomes NULL; (5) split-screen or local-co-op true entails local-multiplayer true, while false values do not imply no multiplayer; (6) co-op maxima require an exact-platform IGDB object with offlinecoop=true; zero, out-of-range or false/missing-associated maxima are rejected; (7) genre never supplies player/co-op evidence; (8) all contributing, rejected and conflicting evidence survives in deterministic provenance; (9) Stage-40 exact 18-field copy remains untouched and RS-651 owns export/backend changes; coverage/conflicts are remeasured and focused/full pipeline tests report zero failures.
nodes.title: Stage 58: local multiplayer and co-op facts
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-22 asked for one-player-to-four-co-op filtering. The trustworthy IGDB data reaches only 5.7% of releases, but MAME already holds the simultaneous-versus-alternate distinction on disk, unused.

nodes.body: A generated retrostack.txt per ROM folder with one [section] per game keyed on the file stem, plus optional hand-written <game>.txt files that override it key by key. Plain 'key = value', # comments, unquoted values. Keys: name (optional matching title), exe (relative path, may be in a subdirectory), store ids (steam, gog, epic, microsoft, itch...), ignore. RetroStack generates only the folder file and never writes to it again once a human has edited it.

Restores the right answer for MSU folders and weakens nothing else - a docs folder's README.md has no same-stem ROM beside it. Tom has MSU folders in his real library (megadrive-msu, 55 game dirs).

nodes.done_looks_like: refresh_source_folders returns on_disk per row (a type change plus python3 scripts/regen_dispatch.py and lib.rs registration, both transports green including the dispatch coverage test), RomSourcesModal stops hardcoding on_disk: true, and the Game sources window renders the 'Folder not found on disk - its files are kept, marked unavailable' tag for a mapped folder that has been removed. Pinned by a test that kills BOTH mutations - a folder that is present must NOT be flagged and a removed one MUST be - so a fix that never flags anything fails. Proven headlessly with a screenshot of the window in that state, against a fixture where the folder is deleted after mapping; the screenshot asserts a state-distinctive string, not the fixture's name (RS-695 REVIEW 3 F2). cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast reports 0 failed with the hash beside the totals, npm run build clean.
nodes.title: Return on_disk from refresh_source_folders so the window can flag a missing folder
nodes.why: Found 2026-08-27 during RS-695's fix pass while trying to photograph that state. Needs a return-type change plus regen_dispatch, which is leaf-2 shaped rather than a blocker fix, so it was surfaced rather than folded in. The wizard reaches the state, so the affordance is not wholly absent.

nodes.body: Read original eXo launch/config records from the installed external catalogue pack, preserve their source semantics, and compile minimal provenance-backed DOSBox Pure outputs without copying the corpus into mutable instance storage.
nodes.done_looks_like: A version-gated Rust reader queries the installed eXo launch-reference tables and returns collection/game identity, expected entrypoint, source runtime, raw ordered config/script statements, dependencies, shared-asset requirements and provenance without adding bulk corpus rows to retrostack.db; the parser preserves unknown lines and normalizes mounts, media, startup, hardware, timing and audio semantics; the compiler changes instance/device paths and emits only necessary libretro options, with every non-path adaptation linked to source text, a stable reason code, evidence and equivalence classification; unknown or ambiguous syntax fails closed; focused fixtures prove mounted-root reconstruction, lowercase IMGMOUNT cdrom passthrough and source-selectable sound branches without the former uppercase harness mutation; unchanged pack input and device capabilities produce byte-identical compiled outputs and stable identities that the collection manifest can reference; source records remain unchanged, and reconcile/provision/launch behavior stays in RS-738.
nodes.title: Pure integration — consume the eXo reference pack and compile audited profiles
nodes.why: The exact-config proof showed that catalogue-pack data should remain immutable reference truth; RetroStack should compile device-specific paths and genuine Pure adaptations without creating a second configuration database.

nodes.body: Match DOS ZIPs to exact eXo recipes or a deterministic generic fallback, then deliver the unchanged ZIP plus config where safe or one materialised .dosz where required.
nodes.done_looks_like: The product-v2 DOS scanner performs exact archive-SHA lookup against a version-gated installed eXo launch-reference pack and validates the recipe against a bounded ZIP inventory; unknown valid ZIPs use the documented RUN.BAT, unique root BAT, then unique root executable fallback without title guessing; traversal, collisions, ambiguity, specialist recipes and recipe mismatches remain typed findings; reconcile chooses the least-invasive safe delivery form—unchanged ZIP plus same-stem external config for reproducible copy-all recipes, or one atomically materialised .dosz for strip-prefix and bounded mount/boot exceptions—without modifying or retaining a duplicate of the source; translated configs preserve exact source commands and media order while changing only frontend/layout boundaries; the runner selects DOSBox Pure with outside config for direct delivery and inside config for .dosz; missing or incompatible packs degrade safely, reruns are stable, automated fixtures cover matching, fallback, both delivery forms, path/media/boot transforms, failure cleanup and source immutability, relevant Rust regressions pass, and approved real-content probes show no leaked RetroArch processes.
nodes.title: Recognise and materialise DOS archives for DOSBox Pure
nodes.why: An identified DOS archive is not launchable until RetroStack proves that its expected RUN.BAT or executable is present; arbitrary non-eXo ZIPs still deserve a reproducible fallback without hidden game-specific expertise.

nodes.body: Measured 2026-08-27: the expanded staging tree is about 22 GB, but launch-relevant XML/BAT/CONF/MAP/PS1/CFG/TXT is about 84 MB; ingest that text into a compact, reconstructable SQLite model and carry its normalized launch tables through the existing catalogue-pack contract.
nodes.done_looks_like: A resumable offline importer hashes only the authoritative source ZIP containers plus ingested text documents, reads the locally acquired XML/config/script/runtime-map corpus, and writes a compact versioned SQLite reference database without embedding game, VHD, media, emulator, BIOS, ROM or SoundFont bytes; every current source identity row reconciles to exactly one game/reference outcome or an explicit duplicate/unmatched/ambiguous refusal, and every ingested document remains losslessly reconstructable from deduplicated blobs; ordered config options and script statements, expected entrypoints, original runtime, dependencies, shared-prerequisite identities and provenance are queryable, while exact-document, config-key-shape and script-command-shape families expose common templates and per-game overrides; re-measured collection totals and input-byte/database-byte compaction are reported rather than fixed to recorded sightings; unchanged inputs produce byte-identical canonical exports and equivalent SQLite query results; deterministic pipeline stages carry the normalized records into the established base/per-system catalogue-pack mechanism with Python/Rust contract parity, schema/read/merge tests, PRAGMA integrity_check = ok and zero unaccounted launch-relevant statements.
nodes.title: Build the versioned eXo launch-reference pack from the complete source corpus
nodes.why: RetroStack needs compact, reproducible eXo launch knowledge outside the mutable instance database: original ZIP hashes establish provenance, while deduplicated source text and parsed patterns replace a distributable filesystem snapshot.

nodes.body: Recognise RetroStack.app/.exe as one of our own top-level entries so validate_target accepts the folder the app sits in; default first-run's root to that folder instead of asking; refuse it when the app is in /Applications, Downloads or the Desktop and ask there instead; drop the empty builds/ folder from the instance tree.
nodes.done_looks_like: A fresh RetroStack.app copied into an empty folder and opened creates its instance IN THAT FOLDER with no location question. (1) OWN_TOP_LEVEL recognises the app itself (RetroStack.app on macOS, RetroStack.exe on Windows) so validate_target accepts a folder whose only occupant is the app - pinned by a test that today REFUSES that folder, so the red is real. (2) First run resolves its root to the executable's containing folder (the folder holding RetroStack.app, never inside the bundle - an app update replaces the bundle and would destroy an instance kept inside it; assert the resolved root is the .app's PARENT). (3) GUARDED: when that folder is /Applications, ~/Downloads or ~/Desktop it must NOT be used - the wizard asks instead, with a message saying why. Each of the three paths pinned separately, and mutating the guard away must go red. (4) builds/ is gone from OWN_TOP_LEVEL and from the created tree; nothing else references paths.builds() on the first-run path. (5) Second launch from the same folder resolves via the existing sentinel walk with no pointer file written - assert no per-user pointer is created. cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 0 failed with the hash beside the totals; npm run build clean.
nodes.title: The app's own folder is the instance: stop asking where
nodes.why: Tom, 2026-08-27: 'I think we just assume it's the same folder that the application is in. If it's already looking for a config inside that folder, then we're splitting our approaches.' The sentinel walk already resolves an instance beside the app, so asking where is a second approach to the same thing. This is what makes extract-and-run work, and it is the whole of the zip flow minus the zip.

nodes.body: If you skip the catalogue at first run there is no way back: matching is skipped entirely without it and nothing in the interface can supply one. Add a locate-a-file control to the Game sources window's existing catalogue section, reusing the wizard's picker and its validation.
nodes.done_looks_like: With an instance that has NO catalogue, the Game sources window's existing catalogue section offers a locate-a-file control; picking a valid game_reference.db copies it into <root>/retrostack/ and the previously-unmatched files become matched. (1) The command reuses first_run's validate_local_catalogue - the SAME quick-check and five prepared queries - so a truncated, corrupt or wrong-schema file is refused with the same message the wizard gives; pinned by a test per refusal, not just the happy path. (2) After a successful install the unmatched rows are re-matched (the existing rematch path, which only revisits status='unmatched' and never churns a good match) - assert an unmatched row becomes matched and an already-matched row is untouched. (3) The control is ABSENT when a catalogue is already present: replacing one is out of scope because it can re-point identities users already hold in rom_files.release_id - assert it does not render in that state. (4) Reachable over both transports (regen_dispatch run, dispatch coverage green). (5) The window does not error and the control's own state is proven by a headless screenshot asserting a state-distinctive string. cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast 0 failed with the hash; npm run build clean.
nodes.title: Supply the game catalogue after first run
nodes.why: Tom, 2026-08-27, describing the onboarding flow he wants. The wizard already collects a catalogue path and it works end to end; the gap is that it is offered once and never again. Scoped to supplying one when there is NONE - replacing an existing catalogue is a bigger decision because it can re-point identities users already hold in rom_files.release_id.

nodes.body: Console files already carry a filename-derived region (megadrive: USA 1315, Japan 433, Europe 311, World 126, 43 null). Arcade files carry none, because MAME's per-set Region is staged and not exported. Export it and use it when tagging arcade files. Region must remain nullable - 15,424 MAME sets have none.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every ROM the app can know a region for carries one, and the arcade half is no longer blank. (1) MAME's per-set Region reaches the shipped catalogue (staged today as json_extract(extras_json,'$.Region') on stg_mame_entries: North America 27,381, none 15,424, Japan 2,518, World 813, Europe 704, Germany 440 - re-measure, sightings). ⚠️ This adds a COLUMN, so it is schema 9: catalogue_schema.rs MAX_SUPPORTED_CATALOGUE_SCHEMA_VERSION is 8 and check_supported() HARD-REFUSES anything above it before a scan writes any identity. Bumping the exporter without bumping the Rust ceiling bricks scanning outright. The ceiling, an app rebuild and a redeploy are part of THIS item, and the item is not done until a built app reads the new catalogue. (2) A scanned MAME/arcade file gets that region on its rom_files row, keyed off THE MATCHED CATALOGUE RELEASE, not off the arcade classifier: classify_arcade is gated to system_key == 'neogeo' (scanner.rs), so Tom's ~19,924 matching mame files never go through it and a rule keyed on it would be unreachable. A scanned console file keeps the filename-derived region it already gets from parse_region_from_filename (matcher.rs) - do NOT rebuild console tagging, it works (megadrive today: USA 1,315, Japan 433, Europe 311, World 126, 43 null - re-measure, sightings). (3) NULL IS A FIRST-CLASS ANSWER, not a gap: 15,424 MAME sets have no region and 43 megadrive files have none. Pin a test that a null-region file is still scanned, still matched and still launchable - anything that treats unknown as a failure is wrong. (4) Regions are recorded as the source states them; normalisation and any preference hierarchy are explicitly OUT of scope and belong to the item that consumes this. (5) GATE ON A COPY of Tom's instance: the baseline row set is unchanged (re-measure the 26,262 first) with region newly populated on arcade rows and unchanged elsewhere. ⚠️ RUN rematch_system_roms, NOT A BARE RESCAN. A rescan skips any file whose size and mtime are unchanged; its early-continue path only reconciles game identity and backfills game_id (scanner.rs) and never recomputes region, so a rescan-only gate populates nothing and either fails on correct code or gets weakened until it certifies nothing. Assert a non-zero number of files was actually considered, so a run that does nothing fails instead of passing.
nodes.title: Give every ROM a region where one can be known
nodes.why: The second half of choosing the right ROM. Region exists on both sides of the arcade problem (MAME set data for the file, LaunchBox alternates for the name) but only the console half reaches the app today. Approach varies by system by design: MAME has real data, console is parsed from filenames, and some systems will simply have nothing.

nodes.body: load_payload_map ships every available file and payload_roles_are_launchable requires exactly one 'launch' member, so 3,176 visible games (16%) are REFUSED as unlaunchable rather than mis-picked. The rank already exists in the tree; product v2 just does not call it.
nodes.done_looks_like: A game with several files is launchable, and the file it launches is chosen by a stated rule rather than alphabetically. (1) RE-MEASURE FIRST; these are 2026-08-27 sightings from rom_files LEFT JOIN rom_content_members grouped per game, mirroring load_payload_map + payload_roles_are_launchable: 20,130 visible non-windows games with available files, 15,900 launchable, 3,176 REFUSED for having more than one 'launch' member, 1,054 refused for having roles but no 'launch' member. (2) load_payload_map (build_sync.rs:504) emits exactly ONE launch member per game, so the 3,176 become launchable with NO change to payload_roles_are_launchable (build_sync.rs:140), runner.rs:146, or library_game_launchability. Prove the count moves: assert refused-for-multiple-launch is 0 after. (3) THE RANK IS LIFTED FROM THE ONE THAT EXISTS - RomResolverOps::resolve_best_for_games (db/operations.rs:2630), today called only by the retained v1 generator/exporter. Order: source priority, then region, then match_type/confidence, then a stable path tiebreak. There must be ONE preference in the tree afterwards, not two; assert the v1 generator path still resolves identically. (4) library_source_systems.priority is honoured. RomSourcesModal.tsx already tells the user 'Higher priority sources win when the same game is in both' and that is FALSE today - it must be true when this lands, or the copy changes. The table is empty in Tom's instance, so a test must set priorities rather than assume them. (5) DETERMINISM: the same library yields the same choice across runs. Region decides only ~979 of the 3,176; roughly 41% fall to the path tiebreak (amiga500 990, zxspectrum 580 - sightings; same title in Amiga/Favourites vs Amiga/Roms, or .z80 vs .tzx of one game). Those must be stable, never insertion-ordered - note asset_status.rom_path today uses 'ORDER BY available DESC, rom_file_id' (operations.rs:4741) and api/mod.rs:3418 uses LIMIT 1 with no ORDER BY at all. (6) NO schema change, NO migration, NO catalogue change, NO manifest schema bump, NO app-version coupling. If any becomes necessary, STOP and re-scope rather than absorbing it. (7) State and test what happens to the losing files - dropped from the manifest, or demoted to a non-launch role. Dropping is the default: a device should not carry duplicates it can never launch. (8) OUT OF SCOPE: the 1,054 games carrying only dependency/update/dlc roles and no 'launch' member (wii 363, gamecube 21, psx 21) - a producer-side defect, captured separately.
nodes.title: One launch file per game, so a multi-file game can actually start

nodes.body: The game detail panel shows one ROM string (games.rom_name) - no file list, path, region or count - so there is no way to see that a game has ten files, let alone pick one. This is THE override mechanism: shipped defaults and user choices are the same rows with different provenance, and the user always wins.
nodes.done_looks_like: The inspector shows which file a game launches and lets the user pick a different one, through the single mechanism that shipped defaults also use. (1) The game detail panel lists every available file for the game with enough to tell them apart - relative path, source, and region where known - marks which one is currently chosen, and lets the user choose another. It appears ONLY when the game has more than one file; a one-file game gets no UI and needs none (invisible for roughly 17,000 of Tom's games - re-measure). Today the panel shows a single string (LibraryDetailPanel.tsx:249) and get_system_roms is per-SYSTEM not per-game, so a new per-game read is part of this. (2) The choice PERSISTS and BEATS the automatic rule from RS-770. A game carrying an override launches the overridden file - assert through build_sync and the runner, not just the panel. (3) ONE MECHANISM, TWO ORIGINS: the store carries a provenance column so a shipped default override and a user override are the same kind of row, differing only in origin. THE USER ALWAYS WINS, and a shipped default must never overwrite a user choice - including on upgrade, re-provision or a catalogue refresh. Pin that with a test that ships a default onto a game the user has already overridden. (4) Provenance records WHERE THE DATA CAME FROM, not a concept in the model: no CoinOPS table, column, enum or string constant. (5) Clearing an override returns the game to the automatic rule, and the panel says which file the rule then picks. (6) An override naming a file that no longer exists must fail safe - the game stays launchable on the automatic rule, and the stale override is visible rather than silent. (7) This mechanism is system-agnostic. It serves arcade parent/clone overrides and console duplicates identically; nothing about it may be arcade-specific.
nodes.title: See which ROM a game uses, and choose a different one

nodes.body: A master launches in place from payload.src and never reconciles or stages; only a client uses payload.path. So the loopback starter instance -- the DEFAULT topology and the case CLAUDE.md says must stay the first test -- never exercises the build/reconcile path at all. Tom's proposal: the server creates a build too, the instance splits into server/ and client/, and on a loopback instance the client folder LINKS to the server's ROMs rather than copying them, while artwork is genuinely materialised.
nodes.done_looks_like: The master's own device materialises like any other device, so the default topology exercises the same path as a real client. (1) DECISIONS ALREADY SETTLED WITH TOM 2026-08-28 - do not reopen them: (a) NOT a server/ + client/ split of the instance; the minimum is a DEVICE ROOT DISJOINT FROM SCANNED SOURCES, because staging inside the mapped roms/ source would be re-indexed as new rom_files on the next scan - THE MAPPING IS THE SCAN. (b) NOT the names 'server' or 'client': 'server' is the banned user-facing word in VOCABULARY.md and client/ already means the viewer source directory; the vocabulary word is DEVICE. Avoid library/ too (legacy Library/ is a live compatibility path and APFS is case-insensitive). (c) A SAME-MACHINE DEVICE REFERENCES ROMS IN PLACE - it neither copies nor links them. A remote device copies, because it must. This removes the Windows question entirely: symlink creation there needs Developer Mode or elevation, which an app cannot grant itself, and hardlinks cannot cross volumes - and Tom's library is on a different volume, so his own instance would land in exactly that awkward case. No link, no privilege, no platform branch. (d) Materialise ONLY what must genuinely exist as a file on that device: a generated playlist, saves, per-game config. (2) The staging directory exists for EVERY device including the master's, so a per-game namespace is always available - that is what gives RS-775's generated .m3u a home with no special case. (3) runner.rs LOSES ITS ROLE FORK: the is_client branch at runner.rs:198 choosing between payload.path and payload.src collapses to one path. Assert the master and a client resolve a launch through the same code. (4) THE FREEZE EXEMPTION IS THE POLICY BIT, NOT A NEW ASYMMETRY: build_sync.rs:1950 already freezes revisions on 'any NON-master device', and referencing-in-place cannot honour the frozen 'byte-identical' promise - so referencing is legitimate exactly for the device already exempt. State that as one policy, not scattered conditionals. (5) WHAT THE CURRENT SHORTCUT BUYS MUST SURVIVE: zero duplication on loopback, instant authoring preview (boot_payload reads the head straight from the DB, build_sync.rs:2176), and a working first run with no reconcile machinery. Prove each still holds. (6) 'The server must create a build' is ALREADY effectively true - the master's viewer refuses without an association (runner.rs:187) and create_starter_build exists - so this changes what association DOES, not whether it is required. Say plainly what a fresh instance with no build now does. (7) LOOPBACK IS THE FIRST TEST CASE per CLAUDE.md, not an afterthought. (8) DEPENDS ON RS-777: this item does not solve addressing. A file outside the instance root must already be resolvable before the master's device can reference it.(9) WHAT BUILD THE MASTER'S DEVICE HOLDS - do not invent one, and do not assume it has content. create_starter_build (api/mod.rs:4976) already exists and already associates the master's device. ⚠️ RULED BY TOM 2026-08-28 AND TRACKED AS RS-779: the starter build STARTS EMPTY. It must no longer fall through to build_manifest_from_library (the whole library at the legacy grain). So this item must NOT assume the master's device holds any games, and must behave correctly when its build is empty - a master with an empty build is the NORMAL new-instance state, not a degenerate one. Do not author playlists, collections or themes to give yourself something to test with; use a fixture. State plainly in the delivery which grain the master's device is on. If making the master a real device turns out to REQUIRE an authored collection, that is a scope change - stop and say so rather than authoring one. (10) A build carries a theme. If the master's device needs one and none is set, say what it falls back to and test that path; do not let an unset theme become a launch failure.
nodes.title: Give the master's own device a real device root, and materialise by reference

nodes.body: create_starter_build calls save_build(name, None), which with no authored collection falls through to build_manifest_from_library -- the ENTIRE library at the legacy library grain. A build is a collection applied to a device; defaulting it to everything misrepresents the model and hands the user a build they never authored. Tom's ruling 2026-08-28: it starts empty.
nodes.done_looks_like: A new instance's starter build contains no games, and the user is told what to do about it. (1) create_starter_build (api/mod.rs:4976) produces an EMPTY build. It must stop falling through to build_manifest_from_library, which returns the whole library at the legacy grain -- on Tom's instance that is 20,130 games he never authored. (2) ⚠️ AN EMPTY BUILD MUST NOT BE A DEAD END. This is the point of the change, not a side effect: state and test what the admin UI and the viewer show for an associated build with zero games, and that there is an obvious route to adding something. StarterBuildAction.tsx and the first-run FinishStep.tsx currently offer this action with copy that implies the library comes with it -- that copy changes. FinishStep already handles an `empty: true` result for a zero-game library, so the empty path partly exists; make it the NORMAL path rather than the degenerate one. (3) EXISTING ASSOCIATIONS ARE UNTOUCHED. Tom's instance already holds a whole-library build; this changes what a NEW starter build contains, never what an existing one holds. Pin that. (4) src-tauri/tests/starter_build.rs asserts games are included (see the tests around lines 100-259). Those expectations change -- and EVERY changed expectation must be justified in the delivery as newly-correct rather than merely made green. A test expectation that moves to accommodate a build is where a real regression hides. (5) build_manifest_from_library is NOT necessarily deleted: save_build still takes an explicit systems filter and build_sync's own tests use it. Say exactly what remains, what calls it, and whether the legacy library grain is now reachable only deliberately. (6) THE VOCABULARY GETS CLEARER, so say it: a build is an authored collection applied to a device, and 'the whole library' was a fallback that made 'the master has a build' true in a weaker sense than the model intends. (7) Out of scope: authoring playlists, folders or themes; the master/client device-root work (RS-776); and anything about which files a build can serve (RS-777).
nodes.title: The starter build starts empty, not as the whole library

nodes.body: Define the canonical editable RetroArch bezel-pack contract, convert the CoinOPS daytime corpus into a development pack, and publish lean runtime packs.
nodes.done_looks_like: RS-782 delivers one canonical development-to-runtime bezel-pack path. (1) Managed pack metadata, user-owned overrides, treatments, variants, system defaults, exact game entries, and explicit shared mappings resolve deterministically. (2) Conventional entries remain RetroArch-ready PNG plus one overlay CFG or Slang preset; integrated vendor presets remain supported; general emulator settings are rejected. (3) Build/reconcile materialises a complete contained resource closure and launch remains read-only. (4) One logical shared bezel has one pack-wide RetroArch presentation even when mapped to releases in several systems; system-local user artwork still takes precedence. (5) The CoinOPS daytime development pack retains at most one accepted self-contained MAME layout and one canonical RetroArch presentation per logical bezel. Later occurrences extend provenance and supported-release mappings rather than adding layout copies. (6) Every inspected MAME source bundle is recorded as canonical-layout, mapped-to-existing, or staged with a machine-readable reason and complete contained files; there is no terminal skipped state. (7) Exact decoded-pixel identity is automatic. Differently named or resized artwork may identify automatically only at fanart visual-hash distance zero plus normalised RMSE no greater than 0.035; all weaker perceptual matches require explicit review. (8) Migration builds and verifies a fresh candidate without first rewriting the live pack and is idempotent under reordered input. (9) Publication writes a fresh distributable directory, excludes development, history, user content, filesystem metadata, and temporary files, emits a deterministic manifest, and passes pack validation. (10) Origin updates preserve user files and whole-stem revisions. (11) The disposable product-v2 harness exercises production resolution, materialisation, config chaining, and launch planning while launching only with an explicit flag. (12) Deterministic tests cover schema validation, shared cross-system resolution, fingerprint thresholds, MAME-layout uniqueness, staging completeness, publication exclusions, containment, snapshot idempotence, shader geometry/rotation, target refusal, and launch-time read-only behavior. (13) Static validation resolves each Slang reference chain to one full root and verifies all passes and textures. (14) A human visual gate is required before the migrated pack replaces the current live pack or RetroArch is launched.
nodes.title: Define editable RetroArch bezel packs and treatments
nodes.why: RetroStack needs portable system-level bezel choices that preserve user additions, pair artwork with an editorial display treatment, and do not create a second emulator-config path.

nodes.body: The library and the build-as-materialised are indistinguishable on disk today: a client's reconciled media lands at the same media/<system>/<kind>/<file> path as the master's library media, so on a loopback instance they are literally the same directory. RS-776 carved out one corner (the per-game ROM namespace under device/) and left everything else colliding, which is why the model reads as muddled -- half a distinction is worse than none.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every instance has one auto-managed device/ directory, and a client has nothing a user could mistake for something they should fill. (1) THE THREE DECISIONS ARE RULED (Tom, 2026-08-28) - build to them, do not reopen: uniform device/ on EVERY instance; client saves BESIDE device/ not inside it; a device downloads its own emulator binaries with no master relay. (2) A CLIENT IS THREE FOLDERS: retrostack/, device/, saves/. It gets NO library folders. Today create_tree gives a client 62 empty roms/<system>/ dirs plus bios/, media/, emulators/, themes/ and collection_assets/ (first_run.rs:1049-1062) while its own comment says a client "already is a device-only tree" - re-measure the 62 first, it is a sighting. Pin a test that a freshly created client tree contains exactly the three expected entries and no library folder. (3) ⚠️ HARD ORDERING CONSTRAINT: role-gating the client tree and fixing the R7 sentinel check MUST LAND TOGETHER. write_sentinel_config refuses to write unless roms/ exists (first_run.rs), so removing a client's roms/ without making that check role-aware fails every client create at its last step. Pin both directions: a client create succeeds without roms/, and a half-made tree still refuses the sentinel. (4) THE DEVICE TIER MOVES UNDER device/ ON BOTH ROLES: payload namespaces (already there), synced media, bios, emulators, runtimes, config/emulators, and the synced-build state. The library tier stays exactly where it is on a master - roms/, media/, backgrounds/, themes/, collection_assets/, the bios vault, the catalogue and the database - and gets NO grouping directory (library/ collides with legacy Library/ on a case-insensitive filesystem). (5) ONE MEANING PER PATH is the point: media/ currently means the curated library on a master and a sync cache on a client. After this, a name means one thing regardless of which machine you are looking at, and the code drops its role conditionals - materialisation_root() collapses to root/device everywhere. Assert master and client resolve through the same code with no role branch. (6) device/ IS DELETABLE WHOLE. Nothing in it is user-authored and nothing in it is irreplaceable; saves are outside precisely so this holds. Pin a test that deleting device/ and re-syncing restores a working device, and that saves survive it. (7) LOOPBACK IS THE FIRST TEST CASE (CLAUDE.md), not an afterthought. (8) START FRESH - Tom has ruled nothing in his current instance is worth preserving, so this item does NOT need to migrate an existing tree. Bootstrap must produce the new shape and a fresh scan must work end to end. State plainly what an existing instance would do if launched against this build, even if the answer is "re-bootstrap". (9) DO NOT BREAK what this batch just landed: RS-770's ungrouped-disc guard, RS-774's disc-set grouping, RS-775's generated playlists, RS-776's for_device_role policy, RS-777's source locator and route containment. (10) OUT OF SCOPE, each its own item: per-device emulator config and bezel generation from devices.capabilities (empty since migration 032); pruning (RS-784); and hardening /media, which currently serves the whole instance root including config.toml and the database.
nodes.title: Split the instance into the library and the build, with one testable rule

nodes.body: RE-SCOPED 2026-08-30. The original framing — 'device/ is documented deletable, so deleting it destroys every setting saved through the Emulators panel' — rested on an agent's ruling (RS-783's 'safe to delete whole') that Tom never made, and no product code deletes device/ (both remove_dir_all calls against it are in tests). The real exposure is narrower and LIVE: the panel writes user policy into [provision] of device/config/emulators/*.toml (settings.rs:210, set_binary_url mutates provision in place), and heal_product_mechanism rewrites that same file on every seed pass. Today [provision] survives only because nobody happened to list it in managed_paths — it is protected by omission, not by decision.
nodes.done_looks_like: What the Emulators panel writes is protected by an explicit, tested decision rather than by absence from a list. A test saves policy through the panel path, runs a seed pass, and asserts it reads back identical — with a positive control showing that a key the product DOES own is healed in the same pass, so the test cannot pass by the heal being inert. The boundary is stated where a reader will find it, since docs/LAUNCH_SYSTEM.md:128-130 currently explains the current behaviour as intended. NOT in scope: relocating the files, a database shadow copy (RS-438 settled one mechanism deliberately so hand edits and panel edits cannot disagree), or any deletion invariant.
nodes.title: The heal boundary is what protects panel settings, not the tier
nodes.why: Panel settings are policy the user typed into OUR UI, which is different from customisation made in an emulator's own UI: losing the latter is acceptable (re-seeding restores it), losing the former is our bug. The exposure is the heal, which runs on every seed pass, not a deletion nobody performs.

nodes.body: Add a declarative SEEDED preference tier beside enforced settings. Fresh devices receive seeded keys; unchanged declarations preserve the emulator/user's base file; changed top-down declarations push only added/changed/retired keys once, and Reset device preferences applies only that owned key set.
nodes.done_looks_like: retroarch.toml declares video_smooth only under [config.seed], names one safe seed_file, and no static retroarch.cfg/[setup].copy remains. A schema-2 receipt records prior resolved seed declarations: missing destination creates a complete base, missing receipt adopts any existing file byte-identically, a current receipt preserves bytes+mtime through provision/reconcile/launch, and a changed receipt edits only added/changed/retired keys while preserving unrelated lines, comments, order and line endings. Filename/removal transitions clean old declared keys; receipt publication follows all base writes; malformed/unsafe paths and active-emulator changes fail without writes; the RS-825 writer lock serializes Reset and automatic pushes. The Tauri/HTTP/UI Reset device preferences surface restores/removes only seeded keys, path/collision/concurrency/mutation tests pass, launch docs describe all three tiers, and cargo test --workspace plus the frontend build pass.
nodes.title: There is no declarative SEEDED tier — only enforced
nodes.why: The three-tier model (enforce / seed / untouch) is the settled design and half of it has no mechanism. Anything we enforce silently overrides the user's own UI, so the seed tier is what keeps taste out of that trap. Found by an independent review, 2026-08-29.

nodes.body: Replace the rotting managed-path allowlist with semantic receipts for every shipped emulator TOML and embedded setup source. A shipped product-contract change pushes the shipped surface once; unchanged releases never rewrite user edits; the instance's complete [provision] table is preserved unless the user explicitly resets.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every embedded emulator TOML has a semantic shipped-product receipt whose digest excludes only top-level [provision]. Missing files seed atomically; current receipts make startup, empty reconcile, provision, panel reads and launch byte-no-ops; an old/missing receipt upgrades the complete shipped product surface once, removes retired keys, preserves the instance's whole [provision] table, and publishes the receipt after the file. User-authored TOMLs are untouched; embedded setup sources use the same change trigger without a preserve table. A shared cross-process lock and Windows-safe atomic replace cover automatic pushes, panel URL edits and both Reset paths. Real runner and headless-server startup tests upgrade historical RetroArch and standalone fixtures before load, concurrent/failure tests pin ordering, explicit Reset restores full shipped bytes including [provision], docs state the first-upgrade cost, managed_paths is absent, and cargo test --workspace passes.
nodes.title: New product mechanism in a TOML never reaches upgraded instances
nodes.why: This is a class, not two bugs: every future addition of product mechanism to a shipped TOML has the same silent-on-upgrade failure unless someone remembers the heal list. The heal list should be derived from what is declared as mechanism, or a test should assert that an instance seeded from an OLD toml ends up with the shipped mechanism. Found 2026-08-29.

nodes.why: Some MAME games depend on external WAV sample archives for sound; non-merged ROM sets do not include them, so missing resources fail silently at runtime.

nodes.body: Inspect the exact pinned upstream version/source behind all 14 shipped emulator profiles and produce the authoritative managed/not-applicable matrix that later declaration, protocol and wiring work consumes.
nodes.done_looks_like: A versioned research artifact covers all 14 shipped top-level TOMLs and, for every save-producing profile/core, cites pinned first-party source for the ordinary-save path, native path lever, macOS/Windows differences, content/shared scope, file/tree shape, selectors, explicit includes/excludes, measured member-count/byte bounds, existing-path migration and managed/not-applicable verdict. It explicitly corrects MAME 0.252 to homepath/hiscore and excludes cfg, identifies Supermodel NVRAM versus save-state Saves/, resolves or records a falsifiable blocker for xemu's disk state and Xenia's mixed content tree, and distinguishes firmware/game installs/config/cache/states from saves. A checked-in small machine-readable evidence fixture (bulk mirrors outside Git) accounts for every profile exactly once and a validation test fails on omission, duplicate classification, missing evidence, unbounded managed unit or state/config/game-content inclusion.
nodes.title: Measure every shipped emulator's ordinary-save surface
nodes.why: Xenia content, xemu disk state, nested NAND trees, VMUs and memory cards cannot safely share a guessed flat-save rule; this evidence gate prevents config, firmware, DLC, states or whole disks entering sync by accident.

nodes.body: Add the typed save_sync schema, generated embedded manifest, strict validation and logical member resolver shared by reconciler, runner, saves service and server.
nodes.done_looks_like: EmulatorConfig parses exactly one managed/not_applicable save_sync classification per shipped TOML and build generation emits one typed embedded manifest consumed by reconciler, runner, saves service and server with no handwritten duplicate inventory. Managed units validate class=save, activation, content/shared scope, file/tree shape, normalized roots strictly beneath saves/, required include/exclude patterns and measured limits; not_applicable requires reason+evidence. A logical resolver maps (emulator_id, unit_id, game_id?, member_path) to an authorized local path only after lexical and canonical containment, no-symlink/reparse traversal, overlap, pattern and limit checks; clients cannot supply roots. Schema+request/response examples and error variants are documented; fixtures from RS-833 cover every profile; mutation/property tests prove omission, traversal, absolute path, link escape, undeclared unit/member, overlap, oversized member/count and state/config/game-content inclusion fail before filesystem mutation; format/lint and targeted/full Rust tests pass.
nodes.title: Define and generate the logical save-sync contract
nodes.why: Every later path, protocol and lifecycle leaf must compose on one authoritative declaration/identity/security contract; duplicating inventory or accepting raw client paths recreates the current hard-coded boundary in several places.

nodes.body: Implement schema-2 manifest/member PUT/DELETE handling, bounded history, tombstones and storage migration on the master using the shared logical save identity and resolver.
nodes.done_looks_like: A versioned master API accepts launch context and logical (emulator_id, unit_id, game_id?, member_path) identities, returns hashes/sizes/tombstones, and streams member bytes without accepting a client root or raw instance path. Server-side resolution uses RS-834's master's shipped declarations; content units require authoritative game_id and shared units reject one. Atomic PUT and DELETE rotate any live predecessor into bounded history before publishing bytes/tombstone; retention is deterministic and failures leave the live value/history unchanged. Existing RetroArch save/history data migrates idempotently to schema 2 or remains readable through an explicit compatibility adapter with removal criteria. Headless loopback/server tests cover flat, memory-card, nested-tree and MAME fixtures plus conflict hashes, deletion, restart and history restore; hostile identity/path/size/count requests cannot mutate live bytes/history; protocol docs include exact routes, request/response examples and errors; targeted/full Rust tests pass.
nodes.title: Replace raw save paths with a logical master save protocol
nodes.why: The current server authorizes a raw relative path against two hard-coded RetroArch roots and cannot represent shared units or deletions; the master must enforce shipped declarations rather than trusting client filesystem names.

nodes.body: Replace runner.rs's RetroArch stem scan with a background save-sync loop: the client's reconcile tick pulls a 'changes since cursor' feed from the master for its active build and applies changed members and tombstones off the launch path; launch reads local bytes with no network; clean exit checks changed members into a compare-safe schema-2 queue that drains in the same loop.
nodes.done_looks_like: The master exposes a cursor-based change feed over the RS-835 ledger (schema 2, enrolment-gated, bounded page) covering every unit of every game in a device's active build plus shared units, with per-launch manifest retained. The client's reconcile loop pulls it, downloads only members whose hash differs from the local baseline, applies tombstones only where the local file still matches, advances the cursor only after a page is fully applied, and never blocks on an unreachable master. Launch preparation selects active units from the authoritative game_id/system/emulator/core context, makes no network request, hashes nothing, and waits only for an in-flight download of this game's members; loopback master validates the same selection against its canonical saves/ bytes in place. Clean exit re-enumerates bounded members (stat before hash), uploads only hash changes plus deletions with base hashes, advances the baseline after acknowledgement and logs last-write-wins conflicts; forced/crashed exits make no check-in claim. A versioned pending-operation queue stages logical identity/action/hash/bytes, drains on the loop and after restart, and deletes an entry only if it is still the exact uploaded version; no v1 queue or history is migrated. Per-core RetroArch savefile_directory roots are rendered for every non-flat unit; the v1 route, get_save_set and the LEGACY_STATE_DIR exception are removed. Integration tests cover content/shared units, background pull of a change made on another device, offline create/change/delete, newer requeue during drain, master/client restart, missing master, partial download/upload, no-op hashes and a launch that makes zero requests; states/config/firmware/game content never sync; docs name the loop, crash and conflict policy; targeted/full Rust tests pass.
nodes.title: Integrate logical save checkout, check-in and offline recovery
nodes.why: A correct master protocol does not deliver user value until the authoritative LaunchPlan selects units and the client survives offline/restart races without resurrecting deletions or dropping a newer queued operation.

nodes.body: Add the final synthetic matrix and documentation that prove the contract, master protocol, runner lifecycle and per-emulator wiring compose across loopback and enrolled-client topologies.
nodes.done_looks_like: A synthetic headless matrix traverses production bootstrap/seed, server dispatch, reconcile, runner launch preparation and clean-exit completion for loopback master and enrolled client. It proves the background pull (a change made on another device reaches this one on a reconcile tick), the bounded in-flight-download wait at launch, the after-exit check-in, content and shared identity, tombstones, bounded history, the schema-2 offline queue and its compare-and-delete drain, client restart and master-restart recovery, stat-before-hash no-ops, conflict logging and device/ deletion/reprovision using RetroArch flat saves, one memory card, one nested tree, the RetroArch `mame` core's pair — `mame.nvram` (tree) and `mame.hiscore` (file) through RS-896's `device/bios/mame/hiscore` link — and at least one link/junction-wired emulator. Negative matrix cases prove traversal/link escape, oversize/count, undeclared profile/unit/member and every state/config/firmware/game-content exclusion leave master/client bytes, history and queue unchanged. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/LAUNCH_SYSTEM.md and API docs agree on canonical saves/, declarations, routes, lifecycle, crash/conflict policy, the explicit statement that no existing instance data is migrated, the Reset distinction, and exclusions; a fresh reviewer maps every RS-111 root-acceptance clause to evidence; frontend build, format/lint, targeted tests and cargo test --workspace pass. No production behaviour changes in this leaf: a matrix case that fails is raised as a Change Request against its producer leaf (RS-835, RS-836, RS-812, RS-894, RS-896 or RS-907) and fixed there.
nodes.title: Prove the cross-emulator save lifecycle end to end
nodes.why: Each component can pass in isolation while mismatched identities, paths, tombstones or exclusions fail at the seams; one fresh integration gate must exercise real production entry points after all producer leaves land.

nodes.body: Build a dedicated AI-reviewed offline archive/import pipeline for reusable widescreen fanart, square fanart, and logos; prove it against one explicitly scoped source folder.
nodes.done_looks_like: A dedicated tools/artwork-archive workflow is documented, indexed from tools/README.md, and covered by synthetic tests. It can scan one explicit source into SHA-256/pHash inventory plus labelled contact sheets, accept parallel AI-authored assessments for widescreen/square/logo assets, produce a non-mutating import plan, copy approved files into a new archive, maintain one pretty-printed filename-keyed index.json inside each asset-type directory, keep a bounded set of plain-JSON pre-update backups, verify the result, and return ranked candidates from stored work/series/genre/system associations. Semantic tags and ambiguous pHash matches cannot be accepted without AI review; exact/confirmed duplicates retain filename/hash evidence; widescreen alone requires subject focus; unassociated custom-looking art may be preserved but is not selected. The first real run successfully imports and verifies only /Volumes/Transfer/NEW START/General Nav Assets/Full Screen Artwork into /Volumes/Media/Retro Games Archive/Reusable Artwork Archive, leaves that source unchanged, and provides evidence that no existing large media/artwork archive was scanned or mutated.

During a DOS-launch-system scan (dos | win3x) a walked archive whose rel_path, size and mtime truncated to whole seconds all equal a manifest row's is resolved with the row's sha256 and no content hash is computed for it — a test proves it with a fixture archive whose real bytes hash differently from the manifest row (the resolution follows the manifest and the evidence carries a line naming the manifest path and the manifest file's own sha256); an archive whose size or mtime differs, or that has no row, is read in place as today (tests for each), and an mtime that differs only in sub-second precision still matches (test). ScanResult carries hashes_from_manifest and hashes_read, printed on the CLI's summary line. The rescan 'unchanged' rule (scanner.rs:2037-2047) and the materialiser's re-hash-and-refuse at launch (exo_launch.rs:4919-4924) are unchanged, and a test cites the latter by name for the wrong-manifest case. tools/game-database-v2/scripts/export_win3x_hash_manifest.py writes the TSV from the win3x protocols corpus's host-verified source_contracts (path relative to the eXoWin3x source root, size, mtime to the second, sha256), deterministic, 1,137 rows on the real corpus with its own sha256 printed, and a pytest on a synthetic corpus. nodes.body: Add a per-build preferred-emulator layer to the resolver chain (game override > collection override > BUILD PREFERENCE > declared TOML priority as the seed default), stored against the device's active build, exposed through invoke commands, and make provisioning, the client manifest and launch all derive from the resolved (emulator, core) so switching arcade between the mame core and standalone MAME, gamecube/wii between the dolphin core and Dolphin, dreamcast between the flycast core and Flycast, psx between swanstation and DuckStation, and ps2 between a pcsx2 core and PCSX2 is one setting per build, overridable per game.
nodes.done_looks_like: A device can carry a preferred (emulator, core) per system: `set_device_emulator_preference` writes one, `clear_device_emulator_preference` removes it, `device_emulator_preferences` lists them, and each round-trips over both Tauri invoke and `retrostack-server` HTTP. Resolution order is game override > collection override > device preference > declared TOML priority, and `EmulatorResolution.source` reports which of the four decided it. With a device preference of (`arcade`, `retroarch`, `mame`) set, `resolve_launch` for an arcade game returns emulator_id `retroarch` and core_name `mame`, on a device where `mame.toml` still declares `priority = 60`. With that same preference set, `provision_for_manifest` over a manifest containing an arcade game downloads the `mame` libretro core and does NOT install standalone MAME; with no preference set it does the opposite. Both assertions run offline against an injected fetcher. Setting, changing, or clearing a preference leaves `build_manifests.content_hash` for the device's build byte-identical: a preference never cuts a revision and never enters the manifest. A client receives its own device's preferences and the build's game and collection overrides in the `begin_reconcile` response, and materialises all three to `device/state/emulator_routes.json`; its provisioning and its launch resolve the full four-level chain from that file with no database query. An override set on the master for a game in the build resolves on an enrolled client at launch, and that emulator and core are provisioned on the client without an override launch having happened first. `effective_routes(root, store, manifest)` returns the build's effective set of (system, emulator, core, origin), including the extras overrides pull in: the device-level resolution of every system in the build, unioned with the (emulator, core) of every game override whose game is in the build and every collection override whose collection is in the build. Provisioning and `effective_emulator_routes` read this one function, and nothing else decides what provisioning installs; the manifest never reads it (it is build grain — see the byte-identical clause below). A game overridden to `retroarch` + `mame` inside a build whose arcade route is standalone MAME provisions BOTH: the standalone for the rest of arcade, and the libretro core for that game. A game overridden to `duckstation` in a build whose psx route is RetroArch provisions DuckStation, which no build provisions today. With no preference and no override, a build containing a system that a standalone wins does not download that system's RetroArch core; with a game in the build overridden to that core, it does. The manifest's emulator-dependent members are keyed on the union of every coherent route for the build's systems, not on any one device's resolved route, so two devices on one build with different preferences receive a byte-identical manifest. `effective_emulator_routes(device_id)` returns, for every system in that device's build, the resolved emulator_id, core_name, `origin` ∈ {"device","default"}, `stale_preference`, the count of games in that system carrying their own override, and the selectable alternatives. A preference naming an emulator that does not claim the system, or RetroArch with a core that does not claim the system, is rejected at write time with an error naming the system and the emulator; a preference that becomes incoherent later (the TOML changed) is ignored at read time, logged, reported with `stale_preference: true`, and never fails a launch. `cargo test --manifest-path=src-tauri/Cargo.toml --workspace` passes with 0 failed, and the server dispatch coverage test passes without `server/src/dispatch.rs` being hand-edited.

nodes.done_looks_like: Resolution order is game override > collection override > device preference > LIBRARY default > declared TOML priority, and EmulatorResolution.source reports which rung decided. nodes.body: Foundation + pure deletion: permit a {platform} segment in a declared unit root (expanded in unit_root/root_of, validated at build time, overlap rules compare unexpanded strings; no {app_root}); relax decl.rs/mod.rs/save_surface.rs so a root is a safe normalized instance-relative path no other unit claims, with canonical containment checked against the unit's OWN declared root and .sync/.history still refused; delete the migrate_* family and its call sites (RS-920 = remove; keep copy_bytes_readonly, adopt_home_saves, ensure_link for firmware); revert Cemu, Supermodel, Eden, Ryujinx, the mame.hiscore unit, standalone MAME (its two phantom roots) and Flycast-macOS to their native roots by deleting the symlink lever and redeclaring the root (spec §3); delete assert_no_save_bytes_in_device and the not-inside-device assertion; rewrite the three device-deletion round trips to assert what a user loses and what the master brings back; correct the docs the morning pass missed (ARCHITECTURE :202-204/:219-222, SAVE_SYNC_API :17-19/:79/:737-740, LAUNCH_SYSTEM :832-851, docs/emulators/{mame,rpcs3,pcsx2}.md, ten source comments) and the inventory (TARGET header, copy_then_verify rows → none|grandfathered).
nodes.done_looks_like: A declared unit root may carry a {platform} segment expanded by the resolver and validated at build time (an unknown token fails the build); the contract no longer requires a root under saves/ and canonical containment is checked against the unit's own declared root with .sync/.history still refused everywhere; the migrate_* family and all its call sites are gone and no test asserts a relocation; Cemu, Supermodel, Eden, Ryujinx, retroarch mame.hiscore, standalone mame and Flycast-macOS declare roots inside the emulator's own tree, their symlink levers are deleted, and every lever assertion proves the wiring matches the declaration; every declared root is still created at provision; the device-deletion tests assert what a user loses and what the master brings back, and no test, doc, source comment or inventory row says device/ may be deleted whole, is disposable or information-free; the inventory agrees with the shipped declarations field-for-field; the master's saves/ store, feed, loop, queue, preference layers and MAME provisioning are unchanged; cargo test --workspace passes on the submitted commit with the hash beside the totals. SETTLED FIRST (review BN5), in the delivery note and a test: the MASTER's canonical live bytes stay under saves/<emulator>/<unit>/ while only the device-side resolution moves — a unit therefore declares a canonical root (master, under saves/) and a device root (native), resolve_member takes the role, and the loopback and enrolled matrices assert both; if Tom prefers one root, the spec's 'master saves/ untouched' clause is withdrawn in writing instead. The platform is THREADED, not assumed (BN2): unit_root returns an owned expanded path, resolve_member and enumerate_unit take the platform of the device whose bytes they resolve, DeviceContext carries it, every call site (manifest.rs, store.rs, journal.rs, saves/mod.rs, sync.rs, device_config.rs) states what platform it passes, and a template reaching the filesystem unexpanded is a test failure. A unit may declare a PER-PLATFORM root where the platforms differ in shape (Eden, Flycast — BN3), with the overlap and case rules checked once per platform over the expanded set, proved by a test declaring an Eden-shaped and a Flycast-shaped pair; the Flycast unit is owned whole by this leaf. The {platform} token is validated at build time in decl.rs beside the path-safety checks and rejected anywhere but as a whole path component (BN4). Where a root widens to a directory the emulator also uses for other state, include/exclude and the ceilings are re-derived from what it now holds, and a test writes one excluded artefact into each widened root and proves enumeration ignores it (BN6). Eden's Windows root resolves against the app root and is asserted as path/text only, carried into the untested-at-runtime list (BN7). Profile/unit counts are derived from the shipped TOMLs, never literals or a base-commit diff (BN9). The doc sweep is proved by a repository-wide search over docs/, src-tauri/src/ and config/ for 'deleted whole', 'disposable', 'information-free', with RS-837's delivery note on the list (BN10).

nodes.body: Add a dependency view to scripts/gen_architecture_map.py: coupling between top-level Rust modules, and every mutual-dependency pair named.
nodes.done_looks_like: docs/generated/dependencies.md is produced by scripts/gen_architecture_map.py and lists, for every top-level Rust module, its line count, fan-out and fan-in, plus every mutual-dependency pair with the reference count in each direction. THE EDGE RULE IS PINNED IN THE FILE'S OWN HEADER AND IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: an edge counts BOTH a `use crate::x` import AND a fully-qualified inline `crate::x::...` path, in value and type position, excluding #[cfg(test)] blocks and */tests.rs files. This is load-bearing because RS-985's cycle ratchet is computed under this exact rule, and because the rule decides what an edge even is: of db's 12 references to rom_scanner exactly ONE is a `use` (operations.rs:4), so an import-only rule would report a single edge and deleting that one line would make a real coupling appear to vanish with no code moved. The view is a COUPLING REPORT, not a defect list — db's remaining rom_scanner references are types and pure functions, retained by design. Re-running on an unchanged tree leaves the file byte-identical and --check exits 0. docs/generated/README.md gains a row for this view in its table of views. --check cannot detect a missing row (the file stays self-consistent either way), so it is stated here explicitly. The workspace suite figure is measured ON THE LEAF'S OWN SUBMITTED COMMIT: run cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast before and after the change on that same commit, zero failed both times, and no test removed or renamed. 'Same as before' naming no commit is a sighting, not an invariant (tools/game-database-v2/docs/ACCEPTANCE_CONVENTION.md), and RS-978 is in flight and adds tests, so a rebase changes the count for an innocent reason.

nodes.body: Move four of db's nine filesystem sites above db (rediscover_exe's discovery call, AssetSourceOps::create's head, ValidationOps + AssetRefreshOps to library_inventory.rs) and pin the remaining five in an impl-qualified ratchet that only shrinks.
nodes.done_looks_like: db's filesystem footprint is an exact, impl-qualified RATCHET in src-tauri/tests/seam_contracts.rs that can only shrink — not a zero, because the spec keeps ensure_bootstrapped (which calls read_dir) and backfill_external (the external arm of the same DEADLOCK-SITE cluster) in db by design. Measured 2026-09-05 on df821ed: nine db functions touch the filesystem, not the four first named. This leaf removes FOUR of them from db with zero behaviour change: GameOps::rediscover_exe's pc_scanner::discover_exe call (the caller supplies the discovered value), AssetSourceOps::create's pre-insert head (exists/is_dir/canonicalize/probe_source — the SECOND create; six fns share the name, address it impl-qualified) moving above db with error precedence preserved and db keeping its own name guard, and ValidationOps + AssetRefreshOps moving VERBATIM with their assets_root to a new module src-tauri/src/library_inventory.rs carrying a //! header (name settled against docs/VOCABULARY.md: library_sources was rejected because it names a DB table of ROM roots neither struct touches). The retained list is exactly five, each with its reason in the test: LibrarySourceOps::ensure_builtin_source (create_dir_all + canonicalize, RS-693 D0c ordering), LibrarySourceOps::create (user-typed root validation), LibrarySourceFolderOps::ensure_bootstrapped (read_dir; deadlock cluster), LibrarySourceFolderOps::backfill_external (discover_source_folders_at behind the load-bearing DB guard; private; deadlock cluster), AssetSourceOps::ensure_builtin_source (canonicalize). THE TEST IS A CAPABILITY ASSERTION, NOT A STRING BAN: it scans src-tauri/src/db/ production code (outside #[cfg(test)] and */tests.rs) for filesystem calls (.exists/.is_dir/.is_file/.canonicalize/.metadata/File::open/read_dir/create_dir_all/WalkDir/std::fs and the two upward discovery calls), attributes each to Impl::fn, and FAILS on any site not in the list AND on any listed site that has disappeared (stale arm), and separately asserts no struct in db holds a Path-typed field (types, not field names). PROVEN TO BITE three ways, each recorded in the evidence: reintroduce one .exists() into db → named failure; remove one retained entry from the list → stale-arm failure; add a PathBuf field to a db struct → failure; all restored. No private db helper is widened to pub(crate) — if a move appears to need it, the leaf stops and reports. No command signature changes, so regen_dispatch.py is not run. docs/generated/command-surface.md is byte-identical before and after once its api:line column is stripped (modules.md changes and that is expected). Touched files are formatted with rustfmt --edition 2021 <file> only; never cargo fmt, never lib.rs. The workspace suite is measured ON THIS LEAF'S OWN SUBMITTED COMMIT: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast on parent df821ed and on that commit, zero failed both times, result lines grep-counted, DEFAULT TMPDIR; if artwork_acquisition's resave test alone fails it is re-run in isolation and both results reported (RS-988).
nodes.title: Take the filesystem out of the persistence layer
nodes.why: db has the highest fan-in in the repo — 16 modules — and genuinely walks the disk in three places and stat-s it in fourteen more, so the layer everything stands on cannot be tested without a filesystem.
