nodes.body: resave.rs:106 DEBOUNCER is a process-GLOBAL LazyLock<(Mutex<DebounceState>, Condvar)>, and mark_dirty() RESETS state.deadline to now+1500ms. All ~1550 lib tests share one process, so any other test calling mark_dirty — reachable from api/mod.rs, catalogue_provision.rs and artwork_acquisition.rs — pushes this test's deadline back. Its wait budget is a bare 5s literal, so roughly four interfering calls starve it.
nodes.done_looks_like: The test no longer synchronises on the process-global DEBOUNCER. Preferred fix: it drives the resave directly — as its own setup already does at the top via resave_all_collections — because the invariant under test is revision freezing, NOT the debounce; using the synchronous path for setup and the debounced path for the assertion is the inconsistency at the heart of this. If the debounced path must be exercised, the debouncer is injectable per-test rather than a static, and any remaining deadline is DERIVED from DEBOUNCE with stated headroom, never a bare literal. PROVEN by running the full workspace suite --no-fail-fast three times on the fix commit with the machine deliberately loaded, zero failures each time — running the test alone proves nothing here, since alone is exactly the condition with no interfering writer. Separately REPORT (fix or explicitly leave with a reason) the two other wall-clock waits in artwork_acquisition/tests.rs — wait_until at :412 and the bare thread::sleep(2s) at :547 — and whether any other test depends on the global DEBOUNCER.
nodes.title: Debounce wait in the artwork resave test has too thin a margin
nodes.why: Diagnosed as machine load; it is actually cross-test interference through shared global mutable state. Slower runs only raise the odds by widening the window in which another test can reset the deadline. Raising the timeout would hide it, not fix it. The DEBOUNCER's `pending` list also carries other tests' connections, so the worker resaves their databases too — a latent hazard wider than this one test.

nodes.body: Three goals in one pass over all ~1,851 test functions: (1) find what cannot fail — no assertion, is_ok()-only, doubles that model a shape the product lacks, assertions that do not pin the call site; (2) find what fails for the wrong reason — sleeps and wall-clock deadlines (76 across 21 files at last sighting); (3) make the suite faster — per-test timings, the provisioning-fixture tail, timing waits replaced by direct calls, any test compiled into more than one binary. Measure first (timings + counts as a checked-in artifact), classify KEEP/IMPROVE/CUT with reasons, act in file-sized batches through build-verify-merge.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every test function in the workspace is classified KEEP, IMPROVE or CUT with a one-line reason in a checked-in file (tools/test-review/classification.tsv), and the IMPROVE and CUT decisions are acted on. A CUT names the other test that asserts the same thing (Tom 2026-09-06: named replacement only; the one exception — a provably cannot-fail test — needs the classifier and the fresh reviewer both to sign it). An IMPROVE names the specific defect: an assertion that cannot fail, a wall-clock or timeout wait, a double that models a shape the product lacks, an assertion that does not pin the call site, or a dependency on a mutable process-global. Coverage percentage is never a justification. SPEED (Tom 2026-09-06): no single test over 10 s run alone and no test binary over 2 minutes on a quiet machine — measured per test with RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 --report-time on the stable binaries, before and after, as checked-in snapshots; the four PROVISION_LOCK-chain breaches are named and fixed or explicitly listed as blocked. Every wait removal is proven the RS-988 way: full workspace suite three times under load, zero failures. The enforcement layer (seam contracts, save_contract guards, ratchets) is KEEP by construction. Fixes that need a product change are LISTED for Tom, not done. The classification is resumable: a later pass starts where this one stopped.

nodes.done_looks_like: A PS3 title is identified from what it IS, not from its filename — scene releases ship packages named like 'msEhHsrOgiLqBwqwzaMgqgEgg...pkg', which no name tier can ever match. Specifically: (1) a .pkg on a ps3 source yields its title id from the header — embedded_id.rs already reads exactly this field for Vita (VITA_PKG_CONTENT_ID_OFFSET 0x30, size 0x30, the same 48-byte title_id PS3 uses), and the dispatch at ('psvita','pkg') simply has no ('ps3','pkg') sibling, so this is a new arm rather than a new reader; (2) a JB disc dump — a FOLDER holding PS3_DISC.SFB and PS3_GAME/ — is discovered at all, which extensions=['pkg','iso'] cannot express; (3) PARAM.SFO yields the human title and version where a title id alone is not enough. Invariants: no full-file read is introduced (a 5.7GB disc dump and a 1.8GB DLC package are both identified from bounded reads); a package that is an update, DLC or patch is not offered as a launchable game; and identity survives a filename nobody can parse.

```
grep -rhoE '"/(Users|Volumes)/[^"]+"' tools scripts .claude/skills \
  --include="*.py" --include="*.sh" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

Pattern to follow: `tools/retrostack_data_root.py` + each tool's `paths.py`. Note the existing separate convention for the *instance* root (`RETROSTACK_ROOT` -> RetroStackAssets/) vs the *tool data* root (`RETROSTACK_DATA_ROOT` -> retrostack-data/). The /Volumes/Transfer paths are external source media and probably want their own env var or a required CLI arg rather than a default.

DO NOT rewrite absolute paths inside `tools/*/reports/*.md` or `tools/game-database-v2/docs/` — those are provenance records of past runs and are accurate as written.

nodes.body:
Build v2's stage 70 to emit a game_reference.db shape-compatible with the contract the Rust scanner already reads, so consumers need no migration.

ITS INPUT SPEC NOW EXISTS: tools/game-database-v2/docs/STAGE70_READ_SET.md (RS-165, 2026-08-04) names every table and column the scanner reads, each traced to a file:line, independently re-derived by a gate that found NOTHING the scanner reads which the document omits. Seven tables are read, three are not. Read it before designing anything.

THREE OBLIGATIONS BEYOND THE COLUMN LIST. (1) Hash case: matcher.rs:224 lowercases the probe and matcher.rs:232 compares raw, so an export emitting anything but lowercase hex matches NOTHING, silently -- no error, no log line, and the scan still reports success. (2) Id stability: games.id and rom_entries.id are persisted into rom_files.release_id/rom_id and joined against a LATER catalogue, so an id must name the same release in the next export or not appear; nothing enforces this and schema_version is not read, making a renumbering export indistinguishable from a stable one. (3) INDEXES ARE PART OF THE CONTRACT: the hash-lookup argument holds only because the query is index-served; all sixteen indexes are declared in export_contract.INDEXES, and the exporter's ANALYZE (export_game_reference.py:411-416) is why the shipped file carries sqlite_stat1 (22 rows) and sqlite_stat4 (504). An export that emits every column and skips either satisfies the column list and is still not the file the app was tuned against.

THE appleii DRIFT IS THIS ITEM'S TO RESOLVE, AND IT RESOLVES BY DEFAULT (recorded here for RS-202, whose acceptance asks for it on a tracked item). The shipped v1 export files Apple II under 'appleii' (1,752 games) -- the ONLY one of its 58 platforms absent from the manifest's 84 keys, independently confirmed twice on 2026-08-04. v2 already emits 'apple2' (1,763 releases, run 75), so stage 70 ends the drift by existing. Change nothing upstream: test_linking_fixes.py:198 asserts 'appleii' is not a manifest key per the owner's ruling of 2026-07-28, and parity_dialect.PLATFORM_ALIASES declares the alias as a deliberate DISCLOSURE, warning that folding it moves six gate-verified numbers. Also measured: 27 manifest systems carry no catalogue rows at all, four of them optical (cd32, cdi, jaguarcd, neogeocd) -- so stage 70 should say what it does about a manifest system it has no data for, rather than leaving it indistinguishable from a spelling drift.

PRIORITY RAISED p4 -> p2 on 2026-08-04: this is the project's stated remaining goal, RS-371 (release_ref empty on every user install, p1) depends on it, and RS-274's six display fields have nothing to travel through until it exists.

BUILD 3 WAS GATED AFTER THIS ITEM WAS CLOSED, 2026-08-04 -- a process slip, recorded rather than tidied away. Verdict PASS WITH FINDINGS: the code was correct (no candidate dropped by a primary key in either new table, both callers reconcile against COUNT(*)), but 12 of 28 mutants survived because build 3 had received no mutation campaign at all. Fixed in 0930ce2: 14 build-3 mutants added, all killed; the 00000000 class of names now loses its filename while keeping its row and hash, taking genuine filename ambiguity from 559 pairs to 10; FILENAME_SHAPED_ALIAS_SOURCES now imports alias_shape.FILENAME_ALIAS_TYPES rather than redeclaring it. DESCOPED 2026-08-03 by Tom: the second half -- carrying v1's ~200-260 irreducible edges and 1,202 bespoke curated notes across as durable overrides -- is dropped from this item and the RS-189 crosswalk dependency with it. v1 is being replaced, not preserved. The previous acceptance was never updated when the body was descoped at 12:44 the same day: it still demanded COUNT(*) WHERE notes IS NOT NULL >= 1202, still routed a 200-260 edge residue into RS-180's override carrier, and still discussed the 12 fix_db_year corrections -- all of which the body dropped along with the v1 crosswalk. Nobody could have passed it as written.

THE DECISION, taken 2026-08-03 and not to be re-derived: derive sequel/prequel from IGDB COLLECTIONS ONLY, NOT FRANCHISES. A collection is a series; a franchise is a brand. Measured against works run 64: collections are 9,740 groups averaging 4.2 members with 33% same-year adjacent pairs; franchises are 2,453 groups whose largest hold 490, 475, 320, 284 and 279 works, with 53% of adjacent pairs sharing a year. Chaining 475 works into a linear spine by year produces 474 false assertions, and on franchises more than half the output would be exceptions rather than edges.

What must be true when this is done:
- v2_work_relationships gains sequel_to / prequel_to edges derived by year-adjacency WITHIN a collection, roughly 27,761 chain edges; same-year ties write an exception rather than a coin-flip, and the exception count is reported.
- Franchise groupings are NOT used as a sequel source, and PIPELINE_SPEC records why, so the next person does not re-derive it.
- No new edge type is added for `contains`: browser/db.py's INVERSES already renders included_in -> contains (works_build.py:2155).
- The relationship rows carry provenance -- which grouping and which rule produced them -- which needs the schema change RS-193 delivers.
- The old '< 500,000 rows' ceiling is dropped as an acceptance clause: year-adjacency yields ~48,700 edges against a 1.27M naive all-pairs space, so the ceiling proves nothing. Assert the SHAPE (a chain, not a clique) instead: a collection of N works yields at most N-1 edges.
- pytest and cargo test report 0 failed.

NOT already delivered: the existing 32,083 rows are five DIFFERENT types read off IGDB game_type plus bundle containment (included_in 26,728, expanded_from 2,093, remake_of 1,446, remaster_of 1,345, standalone_expansion_of 471). sequel_to, prequel_to and spinoff_of appear in neither the table nor the code.

nodes.body:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-03 against works run 64 / map run 65. THE WHOLE ITEM IS WORTH 329 RELEASE ROWS. If every one of the 1,197 title_norm+year duplicate groups were merged, 329 of 103,308 release rows would repoint (0.32%), and 620 of the groups (51.8%) carry no releases at all so are invisible to that layer. Only 235 of 1,197 have more than one member carrying releases.

EVERY CANDIDATE SIGNAL WAS TESTED AND FOUR OF FIVE ARE DEAD:
- Shared external id: across 637,992 distinct (source, uid) keys only 268 are shared by more than one igdb_id, and ALL 268 are source 20 (Amazon ASIN), which routinely covers bundles. IGDB evidently enforces uniqueness on every id that would be trustworthy. It fires on NEITHER of this item's two flagship examples.
- Shared cover image_id: ZERO of the 1,197 groups have two members sharing a cover.
- Slug stem: worse than useless. IGDB's --N suffix IS IGDB's statement that these are different records (double-dragon--21 is an LCD-vs-MSX distinction).
- Title+year: ~21% precision on a 40-group random sample (seed 7) -- 8 clear merges, 24 clear non-merges, 6 debatable -- statistically indistinguishable from the 64%-wrong already recorded for BARE title equality. Adding the year buys a 92% cut in candidate volume and NO measurable precision. Failure classes: Rambo III 1988 (Ocean computer game vs Sega light-gun game), Batman Returns 1992 (beat-em-up vs LCD vs a WRISTWATCH game), Wordle 2021 (clone vs the real one), Taisen Bomberman 24 vs 24 Plus (series entries 3 and 5 collapsed by a normalisation that ate 'Plus'). 58 of the 1,197 mix an LCD-only member (platform 411) with a non-LCD one and every sampled case was a different game.

THE ONE SIGNAL THAT WORKS: byte-identical summary of 40+ chars within a title+year group, applied PAIRWISE -- 62 clusters, 125 works, 63 surplus, 16 releases repointed. 25 hand-read and essentially all defensible; the only debatable class is console-vs-DS movie tie-ins, which 1870d7a already says to merge. PAIRWISE IS LOAD-BEARING: the Illusion (2022) group has four members of which only two share a summary and the other two are unrelated horror games, so a group-wide rule merges four strangers.

NOT BOUNDED: identical summary IGNORING title gives 1,480 clusters / 2,649 surplus -- a larger, orthogonal population worth 30 rows of hand-reading before anyone dismisses it.

CAVEAT: run 64 predates 1870d7a, 9abaa57 and 635f095, which change how works_build resolves ports, names and editions. 9abaa57's control reports the work COUNT stable at 321,435 but the duplicate POPULATION has not been re-measured. Re-measure the 1,197 after the next stage-50 run before building.
nodes.done_looks_like:
NARROWED 2026-08-03 to what the evidence supports. The deliverable is a CARRIER and a REPORT, not a merge campaign.

- A work-level merge verdict kind exists in curation/work_verdicts.jsonl, keyed on IGDB ids (never on a row id or run id -- those are regenerated), with a stage that applies it. This is what RS-177 and stage 70 actually need.
- A candidate report enumerates the duplicate groups with the evidence for each, ordered by community_rating_count, stating its cut-off as 'processed N at >=T votes; M below T not attempted'. Report-only: zero rows move.
- OPTIONALLY, as a demonstration that the carrier works, apply the identical-summary core: 62 clusters / 63 surplus works / 16 releases repointed, PAIRWISE not group-wide. Every repointed release named individually.
- DO NOT MERGE ON TITLE+YEAR. ~329 rows at roughly one-third precision, and a false merge is unrecoverable without a full rebuild. If a future pass wants more, the evidence bar is a NEW signal, not a lower threshold on this one.
- Re-measure the 1,197 groups against a post-2026-08-03 stage-50 run first and report the true figure.
- PIPELINE_SPEC records which signals were tested and rejected, with their measured precision, so nobody re-derives shared-external-id or shared-cover.
- pytest and cargo test report 0 failed.

nodes.body:
v2 has no schema_migrations table, no migrations directory, and 33 runtime _ensure_column() patches, so nothing records what schema the 6.4GB database is at and only column-adds can be evolved at all.

MORE WEIGHT, 2026-08-04 (RS-357's gate): the ad-hoc pattern now covers INDEXES and VIEWS too, not just columns -- _ensure_stg_igdb_id_index_widened and _ensure_views join _ensure_column and _ensure_release_alias_unique_widened. The gate verified that one is idempotent, reader-safe under WAL and self-healing if killed mid-DDL, so it is not a defect; but it measured the exclusive-write window on the first ensure_schema against the live file at 15-26 SECONDS (the commit's estimate of ~12.5s is optimistic), during which a concurrent writer gets 'database is locked' IMMEDIATELY -- because NO busy_timeout is set anywhere in v2. That is pre-existing and worth fixing on its own, but it is the cost of having no migration mechanism: every schema change becomes an unversioned first-open stall of unbounded length.
nodes.done_looks_like:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-03 against main b0a3709. Figures are EVIDENCE, not targets -- re-measure at dispatch.

Current: grep -c '_ensure_column(conn,' pipeline_v2/schema.py returns 34, not the 33 recorded. schema.py declares no schema_migrations table (0 references). v2_releases at run 62 is 164,696 -- THE OLD ACCEPTANCE ASSERTED 158,067, which was stale by 6,629 and would have failed a correct implementation.

What must be true:
- A schema_migrations table records what version the database is at, and a registry of migrations is applied in version order on open.
- The 34 runtime _ensure_column() patches are gone: grep -c '_ensure_column(conn,' returns 0. Today they mean only column-ADDS can be evolved at all, and nothing records what schema the 10.8GB file is at.
- Tests: a fresh :memory: database after ensure_schema has a schema_migrations row for every registered version; applying the registry twice is a no-op; a database missing a migrated column gains it.
- The live database is BASELINED rather than migrated from nothing -- it already has 35 of the 45 declared tables, so the mechanism must recognise an existing database as being at a known version instead of trying to build it from scratch. Baselining is a WRITE to the live file and needs the owner's sign-off; deliver the mechanism and the baseline procedure, and say plainly that it has not been run.
- Do NOT assert an absolute release count anywhere in this item's tests. That is what made the old acceptance wrong.
- pytest and cargo test report 0 failed.
nodes.title: Give v2 a schema migration mechanism
nodes.why: Every new source adds or alters tables. Adds already work (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, _ensure_column), but renames, drops, backfills, index changes and ordering have no path at all, and no database records which changes it has had.

nodes.body: 37% of releases carry no work. Mint one for each -- no vote threshold. Where the title matches nothing, mint clean. Where it collides with an existing work, mint anyway and record the candidate igdb_ids as a correction hint, since a duplicate work is correctable later while an absent game is invisible. Every release ends with a work; nothing is held back pending review. Deciding what enters the catalogue and deciding what deserves human attention are separate concerns -- the latter is RS-293.
nodes.done_looks_like: After the minting stage EVERY release carries a work -- assert matched + minted = total releases as an equality and report the arithmetic, since that reconciliation is what catches a rule with a gap in it; a release whose normalised title collides with one or more existing works is still minted, and the minted work records those candidates as external igdb_ids so a later correction is a one-line verdict rather than a fresh investigation; verdicts from the curation artifact apply BEFORE minting so a ruled release never gets a local work it then has to lose; no vote threshold appears anywhere in the pipeline; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Mint a work for every release that has none
nodes.why: A release with no work cannot be exported, and a narrow-but-correct identity beats absence; the manual layer widens it over time.

nodes.body: test_export_to_yaml panics because it opens a hardcoded January database at a legacy path whose game_id is TEXT; the exporter's i64 decoding is correct. See context.md premise check.
nodes.done_looks_like: `cargo test --manifest-path=src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --ignored` reports 6 passed, 0 failed (today: 5 passed, 1 failed, panicking at config/exporter.rs:402 with 'Invalid column type Text at index: 0, name: game_id'). GameRow.game_id stays i64 and commands/mod.rs:1126 still compiles. If the test is rebuilt on a temp migrated DB, `grep -c 'Library/Application Support' src-tauri/src/config/exporter.rs` returns 0 and the test passes without --ignored. If instead left red, the test carries #[ignore = "<reason>"] naming an existing Haven ref that owns it.
nodes.title: A Rust test has been failing in the --ignored suite and nothing tracks it
nodes.why: A permanently-red suite is a broken smoke alarm; it hid nothing this time only because the gate checked the baseline.

nodes.body:
Stage 55 matches IGDB by title only; two deterministic keys go unused. RESCOPED 2026-08-03 on measurement from RS-173, which found IGDB's own field rename broke half the premise.

STEAM: reachable and clean. RS-173 projects 153,574 steam ids into a new work-level v2_work_external_ids, joinable to releases through v2_release_work_map. IGDB's steam appids are 1:1 with IGDB games. This half is ready to build.

WIKIPEDIA: present but UNTYPED, and this is the part the item was wrong about. fetch_igdb.py:60 requests websites.category, but IGDB renamed the field and silently dropped it, so every staged websites entry carries only id and url -- category is None on all 122,828 sampled and there is no website_type either. 26,103 of 333,195 IGDB entries carry a Wikipedia URL (26,176 URLs) in stg_igdb_games.websites_json, projected by nothing, and selectable ONLY by URL host. There is no category join to make. Decide whether host-matching is good enough before building; do not assume the typed field exists.

Note the same rename would have bitten external_games (external_game_source, not category) -- nothing in the tree reads category today, so nothing is silently broken, but the next consumer written against IGDB docs will be.
nodes.done_looks_like: pytest tests -q reports >= 40 passed, 0 failed including a Wikipedia-URL-normalisation case and an ambiguous-article refusal case; and after a stage 55 rerun on a scratch DB: 'SELECT matched_via, COUNT(*) FROM v2_release_work_map GROUP BY 1' shows wikipedia_article > 5000 and steam_appid > 15000 as their own rows; the wikipedia_article count is <= 17600 -- the RELEASE-grain ceiling measured 2026-07-28, since 10224 unambiguous articles fan out to 16854-17579 releases (one work spans many platforms); do NOT compare it against 10224, which is the article count and which a correct build exceeds; the newest stage_55_match_release_work row in ingest_runs has stats_json containing matched_by_id and matched_by_id_pct; match_rate_pct >= 60.5 (measured projection with both ID routes: 62.1). If the steam_apps.json name-match route is present, grep must show an appdetails type=='game' gate in release_work_match.py -- otherwise the route must be absent.
nodes.title: Join IGDB on Wikipedia article and Steam appid before title matching
nodes.why: Wikipedia is the only identifier key with retro reach; Steam is windows-only and contributes nothing to the retro milestones.

nodes.body: stg_source_files registers 570 files (launchbox 2 + libretro 568) but not the 1.03 GB IGDB dump, so stage 01 cannot see the largest source.

nodes.body: There is no tools/game-database-v2/README.md and no documented way to run a full import, so every item in this track assumes context a newcomer does not have.

It states the nine shipped stages, that 45/60/70 do not exist, how to invoke pytest, and which of PIPELINE_SPEC.md vs PIPELINE_V2_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md wins where they disagree (per RS-46).
nodes.title: v2 has no entry point: write the README a newcomer starts from
nodes.why: Found grooming RS-161 2026-07-28: no README, no runbook, RETROSTACK_DATA_ROOT unset on this machine, paths.py points SCHEMA_DIR at a directory that does not exist, and sql/ and stages/ are empty — a newcomer fails before the first command.

nodes.done_looks_like: Either a title-ID source is adopted and `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v2_release_serials s JOIN v2_releases r ON r.id=s.release_id WHERE r.system_key='switch' AND s.id_type='nintendo_title_id'` returns a number comparable to the 6,069 switch releases; or a recorded decision states that Switch resolves by hash via GameTDB's 19,949 per-version crc/md5/sha1 records instead, with the cost of hashing multi-GB files accepted and stated.

nodes.body: Residue from RS-243. gameandwatch: 208 of 266 releases now match, leaving 58 plus three known-wrong matches (Baseball Vtech onto a Tomy Tutor work, Double Dragon onto MSX, Space Mission onto Arcadia 2001). The scummvm half is DONE -- RS-292 declared ScummVM a runtime in the manifest and exempted it from the platform gate, taking 304 of its 349 releases from 0 to matched. What remains here is Game and Watch alone.
nodes.done_looks_like:
CORRECTED 2026-08-03: the old acceptance said 'the ScummVM half is the substantive one', which contradicted the body and is no longer true. Two separable halves.

SCUMMVM -- verification, not work. c34b981 ('A runtime is not a platform') landed 2026-08-03 10:53 and config/systems_manifest.tsv carries runtime:true for scummvm, but stage 55 has not run since, so the live file still shows scummvm matched = 0 of 349, NOT the 304 the body quotes (that was a control run). Closing this half means confirming on the next full rebuild that scummvm matched rises from 0 to roughly 300+, with lost=0 on a per-release-id diff. No code change is expected; if one turns out to be needed, that is a finding worth stating.

GAME AND WATCH -- deterministic, 3 rows. Disable tier_5 for gameandwatch. Its manifest mapping already covers BOTH IGDB LCD platforms (307 and 411, systems_manifest.tsv:96), so the tier that exists to rescue releases IGDB's platform list omits has nothing left to rescue for this system. Exactly 3 gameandwatch releases match at tier_5 and all 3 are wrong: release 546847 Baseball (Vtech) -> igdb 297486 (Tomy Tutor only), 546895 Double Dragon -> igdb 281505 (MSX only), 547041 Space Mission -> igdb 281174 (Arcadia 2001 only). Verify each by id. Coverage falls 208 -> 205 and those three then mint a narrow-but-correct local work, which also routes them into the review queue -- note review_queue() (mint_works.py:659) pulls only MINTS, so a wrongly-MATCHED release cannot enter it; removing the match is what makes them reviewable.

DO NOT widen the platform gate for the other 58. 13 have a same-title work and matching them means reopening the gate RS-243 closed -- hand judgement only, and out of scope here. The other 45 have no IGDB title at all ('Coleco Galaxian', 'Invader from Space', 'Head to Head: Electronic Baseball'); minting is correct and they should be DECLARED not-a-defect rather than chased.

Measure: the tier_5 population for gameandwatch is provably those 3 rows and nothing else, so nothing can move the wrong way -- state that you checked the whole population, not a sample. pytest and cargo test report 0 failed.
nodes.title: Game and Watch releases still unmatched, and ScummVM releases have no platform at all
nodes.why: Reported by the RS-243 build and confirmed by its verifier, 2026-07-30. Both are out of scope for a platform-mapping item: one is a research question, the other a release-identity question.

nodes.body:
_review_candidates consults title_to_work_ids only, never alt_title_to_work_ids, so 'unmatched' means 'no PRIMARY-title candidate'. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-03 post-alt-names: 857 of the 45,970 unmatched rows have a work whose alternative name normalises to the release title (was 659). 512 carry at least 1 vote, 199 at least 5, 49 at least 20, 11 at least 50. The item's stated precision is exactly right: 0 of the 45,970 have a primary-title match.

VERDICT DETERMINISTIC, and it changes NO MATCH -- it moves 857 releases from unmatched/no_title_match to needs_review/title_collision. The one real consequence, which belongs in the acceptance: per the spec, title_collision mints surface at ANY vote count while no_title_match needs min_votes, so these 857 join the always-surfaced population. That is the intended effect, not a side effect. Sample read both ways -- right: Super Street Fighter II -> ...The New Challengers, Blazing Lazers -> Gunhed, Classic NES Series: Metroid -> Metroid; wrong: The Flintstones: BurgerTime in Bedrock -> BurgerTime Deluxe. Uncertain in both directions is the definition of review-worthy.
nodes.done_looks_like: Either those 659 releases get a needs_review row like the rest of the queue population -- they are the same shape, a real candidate blocked by the platform gate -- or the docstring on _classify_unmatched and the wording that says IGDB holds no such title are corrected to say PRIMARY title, and the 659 are recorded as a known exclusion. Decide which; do not leave both. If they join the queue, measure that the queue grows by about 659 and that coverage still does not move (byte-identical release_work_map dumps, per release id, not by count -- RS-225's inversion still applies: a rising match count here is a failure). Note this is 1.5 percent of unmatched, so it is a wording fix at least and a small queue extension at most. Whichever item picks up the 44,768 should carry this. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Alt-name matches never reach the review queue
nodes.why: Found by the RS-225 verifier, 2026-07-30. A defensible scope line -- the tier cascade already tries alt names inside the platform pool at tiers 3, 4 and 7 -- but the wording overstates it and RS-210 and RS-211 would inherit the gap silently.

nodes.body:
libretro DAT entries for prototypes, betas, promo videos and flashcart firmware carry Nintendo product codes borrowed from unrelated commercial titles, so serial matching attaches junk to real games. MEASURED 2026-08-03 at every layer: 22,490 accepted serial_exact edges -> 260 share no title token longer than 2 chars -> 34 ALSO carry a Proto/Beta/Demo/Video/Promo/firmware tag -> 12 contaminated link groups -> 185 candidates -> 22 releases, each carrying real ROM entries (Contra 4, Shantae, Shrek: Ogres & Dronkeys, GoldenEye: Rogue Agent, Bee Movie Game).

THE RULE IS A CONJUNCTION AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING. Suppress a serial_exact edge when the libretro side carries a Proto/Beta/Demo/Sample/Video/Promo/Kiosk/Debug/Alpha tag or is flashcart firmware AND the two titles share no token longer than 2 characters. Each condition ALONE is wrong: the tag alone breaks 332 edges, most of them right (Xenoblade Chronicles 3D (Beta) matching Xenoblade Chronicles 3D, the entire eShop (Video) corpus matching its own GameTDB records); low-overlap alone breaks 260, of which 226 are right and are exactly the tier's purpose (Japanese titles matching their English releases).

No counterexamples found in the 34 -- all are junk: Contra 4 (Proto) against Barbie in the 12 Dancing Princesses, SuperCard DSTWO against Fish Tycoon, Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (Video) against GoldenEye: Rogue Agent. VERDICT DETERMINISTIC; narrowest and best-evidenced of the five matching items.

Watch the join: v2_releases.source_link_group_id carries the documented #lb composite, so a naive join returns 0 releases. Use a prefix join.
nodes.done_looks_like: A prototype, beta, demo, video or flashcart-firmware DAT entry no longer joins a commercial release through a borrowed serial. THE HARM IS TRANSITIVE, so measure at group level not edge level: _generate_serial_edges skips same-source pairs, but a serial carried by N libretro rows plus one GameTDB row forms a star through the GameTDB hub and union-find merges all N+1 into one link group. Reproducer: nds serial AIPE, baseline 9 libretro candidates in 6 link groups, after RS-184 all 9 in ONE group of 14 containing Barbie in the 12 Dancing Princesses, Contra 4 (Proto), Crash Landed (Proto) x3, Nicktoons Android Invasion (Proto) x3, Shantae (Proto), Shrek Ogres and Dronkeys (Beta) x3 and SpongeBob Fists of Foam (Proto). dense_serial_cluster does NOT catch it -- its threshold is over 20. Population bound: 71 of 20,099 components (0.35 percent) contain a member sharing no title token with the core; 103 candidates absorbed, an UPPER bound since some are correct localisations. Three candidate fixes, narrowest first: (a) exclude Proto/Beta/Demo/Video-tagged and known loader-firmware libretro candidates from the SERIAL tier only, leaving them on title tiers; (b) drop dense_serial_cluster well below 20 for the cross-source case; (c) require a corroborating alias or title signal before a serial edge may join a component that already has 3 or more members. GUARD AGAINST OVER-CORRECTION: of the 97 low-overlap edges about 52 are RIGHT and are exactly what the tier exists for -- Made in Wario Gorgeous to WarioWare Gold, Lednikovyj period 3 to Ice Age Dawn of the Dinosaurs, Internado El to The Boarding School Black Lagoon. Hand-read what changes. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Prototypes and flashcart firmware borrow real product codes, so the serial tier merges them into the wrong release
nodes.why: Found by the RS-184 verifier 2026-07-30, which censused every edge rather than sampling. Not a parse defect: the raw codes are bare 4-character values read correctly on both sides, and the collision predates the commit. It only became visible once the tier fired.

nodes.body: Three defects found by the RS-212 verifier, none blocking but all in the way of trusting the instrument. N1: measure --read-only dies with 'no such table: v2_quality_spot_checks' on any database that has never run stage 60, which is exactly the standalone case the module docstring promises. N2: --read-only --verify silently ignores --verify and exits 0. N3: five rows per report store a count with numerator equal to denominator, so the printed rate is nonsense.
nodes.done_looks_like: The instrument is trustworthy pointed at a database it did not build. N1: _carry_forward_verdict (quality_assess.py:1649) returns None when v2_quality_spot_checks is absent rather than raising -- three lines, and it needs a test, because it is the first thing anyone pointing the tool at an unfamiliar database hits. Reproduce by cloning a database and dropping the two quality tables. N2: reject --read-only --verify with a message rather than swallowing the flag, since the verify path genuinely needs stored rows. N3: stage30_totals (4 dimensions) and system_without_igdb_platform are counts stored with numerator == denominator and value = float(count), so _fmt_rate renders 584,883 / 584,883 (584883.0 percent) and system:scummvm 349 / 349 (349.0 percent) -- quality_assess.py:1931 and :1221. Either give them a real denominator (stage30_totals against the run's candidate total, system_without_igdb_platform against total releases) or give counts a distinct storage and formatting path. THE TEST MUST CHANGE TOO: assert the denominator is meaningful, not merely non-NULL, or the same defect recurs. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: The quality report crashes on an unfamiliar database and prints percentages of 584883 percent
nodes.why: Three defects in the instrument, one of whose prescriptions was wrong: the item said refuse --read-only --verify because 'the verify path genuinely needs stored rows'. It does not -- the comparison is emitter-vs-independent-query and persistence has no bearing on it. Ruled 2026-08-03: verify rather than refuse.

nodes.body: _libretro_game_index (rom_spine.py:236-250) checks the 4-column key only after filtering to games that reached a release, so a one-sided collision is skipped silently and every ROM row under that key is attributed to the release-reaching game.
nodes.done_looks_like: A second staged libretro game sharing (ingest_run_id, dat_family, source_file, source_row_order) with an existing one raises RomSpineKeyCollision even when it reaches no release, pinned by a test for the one-sided case alongside the existing test_a_genuine_collision_on_the_full_key_raises; the key is checked over every staged game before the release filter; a full stage-41 run still yields v2_rom_entries = 290,229 with zero collisions raised on the real corpus; pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests/ -q reports 0 failed and at least 376 passed.
nodes.title: Widen the ROM spine collision guard to every staged game
nodes.why: That silent misattribution is the exact failure the guard exists to prevent, so the tripwire is one filter narrower than its own docstring claims.

nodes.body: 117 CRC32 values in the spine span more than one release. DOS is CRC32-only (4,225 releases, zero SHA1), so a scan of generic files resolves confidently to the wrong game -- QBASIC.EXE resolves to '!Bingo Granny!'.
nodes.done_looks_like: resolve_rom returns an ambiguous or unverified result rather than a single release when the only available tier is CRC32 and that CRC32 maps to more than one release; QBASIC.EXE and at least five other shared-CRC32 files from the 117 resolve as ambiguous rather than to a named game; a test pins the QBASIC.EXE case by hash; single-release CRC32 matches are unaffected and the DOS floor of 4,225 CRC32-reachable releases still holds; pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests/ -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Guard against CRC32-only matches on generic filenames
nodes.why: A confident wrong identification is worse for a validation product than no match, and DOS has no stronger hash to fall back on.

nodes.body: stg_source_files registers 576 files for launchbox, libretro and gametdb. discovery.py has no rule for igdb at all, so igdb_all_games.jsonl and its two drop sites are outside every file-level check. Separately discovery declares 10 libretro metadata-* kinds while libretro_ingest.METADATA_KINDS consumes 9 -- releasemonth is missing -- so 46 registered files are opened by nobody (417 registered minus 371 ingested). No ingest module reads stg_source_files; they all glob the filesystem independently.
nodes.done_looks_like: discovery.py registers the igdb dump so all four source families appear in stg_source_files, and a full discovery run registers more than 576 files with igdb present; either libretro_ingest consumes metadata-releasemonth or discovery stops declaring it, and after the change the count of registered-but-unconsumed files is 0 or is explicitly declared with a named reason; a test asserts every DiscoveryRule kind has a declared consumer, so adding a rule without a consumer fails rather than passing silently; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Discovery registers files nobody reads, and misses IGDB entirely
nodes.why: A registry that does not describe what is actually consumed cannot support any claim that nothing was silently dropped.

nodes.body: launchbox_metadata holds overview/genres/developer/publisher/max_players/cooperative at 83-100% coverage; game_reference.db exports none of it (games = id, work_id, name, platform, region, year, quality_tier). games.release_ref (lb-<LaunchBox id>, migration 031) is the join key.
nodes.done_looks_like: The v2 export carries the display fields the app needs -- overview, genres, developer, publisher, max_players, cooperative -- alongside identity, joined on the stable release ref; coverage per field is reported as measured figures against the v2 grain rather than inherited from v1's 83-100%; a game the app renders shows them end to end, named as a spot check. This is a REQUIREMENT ON STAGE 70 (RS-166), not a v1 export fix -- v1 is archived.
nodes.title: Display metadata never reaches the app: game_reference.db exports identity only
nodes.why: Blocks the detail overlay (RS-241 open question 4) and any metadata display. The data exists; only the export path is missing. Measured 2026-08-01.

nodes.body: The pipeline mints unconditionally (RS-194) and the queue is a view (RS-293), so nothing stops a database being exported while popular games still carry an unreviewed identity. Add a fifth gate to the parity harness: count unadjudicated queue rows at or above a vote threshold, and refuse the cutover while any remain. Backlog re-measured 2026-08-03 after RS-295: 3,183 rows at 10+ votes, 1,093 at 20+, 156 at 50+, 41 at 100+ (was 3,847 / 1,147 / 205 / 63 before RS-295 projected subordinate titles). Depends on RS-296: a gate that reads work coverage cannot be built on an instrument that understates it by 36 points.
nodes.done_looks_like: scripts/parity_report.py emits a fifth gate that counts queue rows with no verdict in the curation artifact at or above a configurable vote threshold, defaulting to 20; it returns PASS at zero, FAIL with the count and the top ten titles otherwise, and BLOCKED with a named reason if the curation artifact is absent or unreadable rather than silently passing; the threshold is a named constant reported in the output so a reader knows which line was applied; on the current generation it FAILS and names 1,147 at the default, which is the honest answer today; a test forces each of the three verdicts; the gate reads the same queue function as RS-293 rather than reimplementing the population, so the two cannot drift; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Cutover gate: the review backlog must be drained above the vote line
nodes.why: Minting gives every game an identity but not a correct one; the vote line is where a wrong identity would actually be noticed, so that is where readiness should be judged.

nodes.body: works_build resolves a port to the ABSOLUTE root of the parent chain, so a port of an expanded game skips past the work it belongs to. PSP Tekken: Dark Resurrection (igdb 24181, parent 1235, type 10) maps to Tekken 5; XCOM: Enemy Within lands on X-COM: UFO Defense (1994). Pass 4 unions port platforms onto that same wrong work, so work 1235 lists only Arcade and the PSP release cannot match despite 1235 already carrying the exact alias. 355 of 8147 ports and 125 of 3656 skip-type entries resolve differently under the two walks. RS-295 added _nearest_work_igdb_id for everything it introduced; this reconciles the pre-existing mapping and platform union onto the same rule.
nodes.done_looks_like:

Concretely: a verdict that names a SET of launchbox_ids can split a wrongly-combined source_link_group or join two wrongly-split ones, and it is applied at stage 40 -- before releases exist -- not replayed at 55. verdicts.py documents, per verdict kind, which stage applies it and which external key it uses; the existing split (alias at stage 50, attach/mint/reject at stage 56) is written down rather than implied. And the ordering hazard is handled: after a stage-40 split changes which release a launchbox_id lands on, downstream 55/56 verdicts keyed on that id are re-validated rather than silently retargeted -- the run reports how many verdicts changed target, and a target change is warned, never applied silently.

nodes.body: Steam is not a source today; the only Steam data v2 has is appids riding along on other sources -- LaunchBox extras_json (normalize.py:1957) and IGDB external_games (RS-173). The catalogue itself is unfetched, so three distinct things are unavailable at once. FETCH AUTHORISED by Tom 2026-08-03; this is the sign-off the standing no-refetch rule requires, and it covers this source only. Acquisition route matters: Valve's ISteamApps/GetAppList is DEAD (404) and IStoreService/GetAppList/v1 needs a paid-account key, but jsnli/steamappidlist mirrors Valve's own pre-split typing daily with no key (games_appid.json, 177,279 entries, DLC/software/video/hardware in separate files), and SteamSpy serves the whole catalogue at 1,000 rows per request -- about 178 calls, minutes not days. Per-appid appdetails polling is ~3 days at Valve's 200/5min and is NOT the bulk route; reserve it for appids that reached a release.
nodes.done_looks_like: THREE outputs, each measured rather than asserted. (1) SOURCE: the typed Steam app list is fetched, registered in stg_source_files with a sha256 through stage 01 discovery like any other source, and staged into its own stg_ table -- not read from a script at match time; the games list is used, so DLC, soundtracks, videos and hardware never enter, and the counts of each excluded class are reported. (2) ALIASES: Steam's canonical names reach works through works_build.apply_alternative_names as a new producer with source 'steam_name' -- no change to that function and none to stage 55, and subject to reject_colliding_names like any derived name; report applied/dropped by rejection reason, and confirm the invariant that every derived name still resolves to exactly one work. (3) THE GAP: state how many typed Steam games have no v2 work at all and how many have no release, as figures with the queries, broken down by whether IGDB knows the appid -- IGDB carries ~152,059 distinct appids against Steam's 177,279, so the headline is the size of that shortfall and what is in it. Field-level enrichment onto releases is OUT of scope and belongs to RS-47 (Stage 45); this item establishes the source, the aliases and the measurement. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

nodes.body: fetch_igdb.py:60 requests websites.category. IGDB renamed it and the API silently returns the entry WITHOUT the field rather than erroring, so all 122,828 staged website entries carry only id and url -- no category, no website_type. The same rename already happened to external_games (external_game_source), where the fetch script was updated but nothing reads the old name, so that one is harmless today. A source fetch that silently returns less than it asked for is the failure mode to guard, not the individual field: nothing in the pipeline notices a requested field arriving empty across 100% of rows. Found by RS-173 while projecting external_games. NO REFETCH is authorised by this item -- fixing the query is separate from re-running it, and re-running needs Tom's sign-off.

nodes.body:
SOURCE_FILE_CONSUMERS (pipeline_v2/parity_dialect.py) maps each registered (source_family, source_kind) to the stage that opens it, or to the sentinel UNCONSUMED. Parity gate 1 uses it to tell a parse defect (file opened, rows dropped) from a discovery defect (file opened by nobody).

Two kinds registered by a discovery rule appear in that map NOT AT ALL: ('launchbox','files') and ('libretro','core-headered'). parity.py:437 looks them up with .get((family, kind), UNCONSUMED), so a MISSING ENTRY IS SILENTLY REPORTED AS AN UNREAD FILE rather than raising. Both are in fact consumed -- RS-173 wired Files.xml into stage 10 and the three headered DATs into stage 11, and test_source_ingest_rs173.py asserts it.

Invisible today only because live discovery run 55 predates RS-173's rules: run 55 registered 576 files across 22 kinds, a current run registers 581 across 25, and the five-file difference is exactly Files.xml + three headered DATs + the IGDB dump. SO IT FIRES ON THE NEXT REBUILD, reporting two working sources as unread.

Found by the RS-192 builder 2026-08-03, deliberately left alone as out of scope -- attributing each kind to a stage is a judgement, not a mechanical fill-in. catchup_check.py does NOT catch this: it compares tables and stages, not per-kind consumption.

Also here, one line away: stage_contract.py's module docstring says 'twelve stages' and STAGE_OUTPUTS has 13 entries.
nodes.done_looks_like:
SOURCE_FILE_CONSUMERS names a stage for ('launchbox','files') and ('libretro','core-headered'), matching where RS-173 actually wired them (verify against the code, not against this sentence). The parity report run against a CURRENT discovery generation reports exactly one UNCONSUMED kind -- ('libretro','metadata-releasemonth') with its 46 files, which is deliberate and owned by RS-266 -- and reports neither of these two.

AND the silent default is closed: a registered (family, kind) with no entry must FAIL LOUDLY rather than defaulting to UNCONSUMED, since that default is what let this sit unnoticed. nodes.body:
Follow-up to RS-298, split out deliberately rather than folded in. RS-298 landed 244 repoints at roughly 8:1, and its whole wrong tail sits in ONE 13-row bucket. The gate found a separating rule at 90% precision: the NEW tier being tier_4 rejects 10 of the 19 primary_title->alt_name repoints, 9 of which are wrong.

IT IS PRINCIPLED, NOT FITTED TO THESE ROWS. tier_4 is the one cell in the cascade where BOTH names are derived (a release alias matched against a work's alternative name) AND the year is merely nearby rather than exact. Every other tier holds something exactly. The year relationship works and IS the tier: every year_delta=0 row is tier_3, every year_delta=1 row is tier_4, by construction. Other distinguishers measured and weaker: alias reach >= 3 releases (71%), alias is a single token (75%), alias <= 11 chars (50%), and the tier of the ABANDONED match (0% -- constant tier_6 across all 19).

MEASURED AS A THIRD ARM on the same clone (run 70): demoting a tier_4 alias win below tier_7 keeps coverage at 103,612 with 0 gained and 0 lost -- it demotes, it does not suppress. 119 rows corpus-wide (0.11%), 103 keep their match, 16 move: +10 corrected, -2 broken, 4 neutral. It breaks Parodius (GB) -> Parodius da! and The Cameron Files -> the correct Cameron Files.

WHY IT WAS NOT LANDED WITH RS-298, and this is the whole reason to wait: 4 of its 10 wins are junk-alias driven (start bat x2, fnf, talespin gg) and EVAPORATE once RS-309's refusal is regenerated -- the corpus still holds 358,217 aliases and start bat still reaches 88 releases, because RS-173 and RS-309 landed in code and stage 20/40 have not re-run. Landing it now would be tuning against a corpus about to change underneath it, and it is 5:1 rather than 10:0, so it costs two correct matches and deserves its own decision rather than riding along.

The 6 wins that are NOT junk-alias driven and survive the rebuild: Adventure Island II, Test Drive Le Mans x2, Nobunaga Iron Triangle, CosmicBreak Universal, Umineko. Those are legitimate aliases landing on a work's alt-name with a loose year, which is exactly the case the rule is about.

RE-MEASURE FIRST, AFTER A FULL REBUILD. This item must not be built against generation 62/64 -- that is the corpus the rule was measured on and the one about to be replaced. Re-run the three-arm comparison on a regenerated corpus and report the new +corrected / -broken / neutral split over the rows that remain. If the surviving wins no longer outnumber the losses by a margin worth two correct matches, CLOSE THIS AS NOT WORTH DOING and record why -- that is a valid outcome, not a failure.

If it is still worth doing: an alias win at tier_4 is demoted below tier_7 rather than suppressed, so coverage is provably unchanged (gained 0, lost 0, verified by byte-identical release_work_map dumps per release id, not by count). Every moved release named individually and judged, in both directions -- the two known casualties are Parodius (GB) -> Parodius da! and The Cameron Files, so state what happens to them. The ranking rule as amended is stated in PIPELINE_SPEC.

Do NOT reach for token overlap or any string-similarity filter. It was tested and rejected twice on the grounds that correct regional retitles have zero overlap -- Life Force -> Salamander, Denaris -> Katakis, Airwolf -> Blue Thunder.

nodes.body:
Title normalisation strips a trailing '+' (and 'Plus'), so two DIFFERENT games normalise to the same string. Normalised titles are the join key for the whole matching layer -- stage 30's title_exact evidence, stage 55's title and alt-name indexes, and every duplicate-work signal -- so a collapsed pair is invisible to all of them.

RE-MEASURED 2026-08-03 22:35 ON THE REBUILT GENERATION (releases run 75), and THE ORIGINAL REPRODUCERS DO NOT EXIST. The item was filed on 'Taisen Bomberman 24 vs 24 Plus' and 'Itsutsu no Neito vs Neito+', found during RS-180's duplicate analysis on the SUPERSEDED generation. Neither title is present on run 75 by any spelling. Do not go looking for them.

THE DEFECT IS REAL AND THE POPULATION IS SMALL AND CLEAN. 76 normalised titles collide only because a trailing + or Plus was eaten. The meaningful subset is 40 SAME-PLATFORM PAIRS, and every one sampled is a genuinely distinct game -- an enhanced re-release colliding with its original:

  Abduction Action!  2010  vs  Abduction Action! +  2014   xbox360
  Sorcery            1985  vs  Sorcery+             1986   amstradcpc
  Boulder Dash       1984  vs  Boulder Dash +       1987   c64
  Strangeloop        1985  vs  Strangeloop+         1986   amstradcpc
  Doors of Doom      1985  vs  Doors of Doom +      1986   amstradcpc
  Dead or Alive      1996  vs  Dead or Alive ++     1998   mame
  INV                1998  vs  INV+                 2004   atari2600
  Downfall           2011  vs  Downfall +           2014   jaguar
  Barbarian          1987  vs  Barbarian+           1987   amiga500
  Ace Combat: Assault Horizon Legacy 2011 vs Legacy+ 2015  3ds
  Slow Mole          2021  vs  Slow Mole+           2024   nes
  PICROSS S          2017  vs  PICROSS S+           2024   switch
  Hatsune Miku Logic Paint S 2021 vs ...Logic Paint S+ 2025 switch

NOTE THE NOISE, so it is not chased: the rest of the 76 is dominated by clusters like '2048', where many platform ports and author-disambiguated variants ('2048 (David Schmidt)') share a normalised title for reasons that have nothing to do with '+'. Only the same-platform pairs are the defect.

40 pairs is small enough to read every one by hand, which is what makes this tractable rather than a rewrite of the join key.
nodes.done_looks_like:
MEASURE FIRST, then decide -- this is a change to the join key of the entire matching layer, so its blast radius is the thing to establish before touching anything. Report: how many distinct title_norm values currently absorb a '+' or a trailing 'Plus'; how many v2_releases and v2_works those cover; and how many stage-30 edges and stage-55 matches currently rest on a normalisation that ate one.

If the population is small and the fix is clean, preserve the distinction -- normalisation stops discarding a trailing '+' / 'Plus', with the two known cases (Taisen Bomberman 24 vs 24 Plus, Itsutsu no Neito vs Itsutsu no Neito+) named individually before and after.

BUT TREAT COVERAGE LOSS AS THE RISK, not coverage gain. Preserving a character that was previously discarded can only make two strings LESS equal, so matches can be LOST. Measure gained/lost/repointed as three figures from two stage-55 runs on one clone, and JUDGE EVERY LOST MATCH INDIVIDUALLY -- a net-positive headline is not sufficient evidence. If the losses are real games that legitimately answer to both spellings, the answer may be an ALIAS rather than a normalisation change, and saying so is a valid outcome.

Whatever is decided is recorded in PIPELINE_SPEC next to the normalisation rules, with its measured cost, so the next person does not re-derive it. pytest and cargo test --workspace report 0 failed.
nodes.title: Title normalisation eats a trailing '+', folding distinct series entries together
nodes.why: A '+' is usually the whole difference between a game and its expanded re-release, and the matcher cannot see it.

nodes.body:
Found 2026-08-03 while projecting descriptions for RS-286, recorded rather than silently inherited.

normalize.py:1011 applies _clean_text to 'overview'. That helper collapses every run of whitespace -- correct for a title, wrong for prose. 82,156 of the 172,408 staged overviews contain a newline, so ROUGHLY HALF arrive at stage 40 as a single welded paragraph with every paragraph break gone.

Stage 40 does NOT compound it: RS-286 strips only the ends and leaves the middle alone, and a test holds it to that. So the fidelity returns the moment stage 20 stops discarding it -- nothing downstream needs to change.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the description exists so the app's front end can show it, and RS-274 carries it plus five more display fields into the export. A wall of text is a visibly worse product than the same text with its paragraphs, and this is the only point in the pipeline where the breaks still exist.

It also very likely affects any other prose field routed through the same helper -- check before assuming 'overview' is alone.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Prose fields keep their paragraph breaks through stage 20 while titles keep their current normalisation -- so the fix is a DISTINCTION between field kinds, not a change to _clean_text for everyone. Say which fields you classified as prose and why; check whether 'overview' is the only one routed through that helper.

Verify on a clone: of the 82,156 staged overviews containing a newline, the count still containing one after stage 20 goes from 0 to ~82,156, and a named example is shown before and after with its breaks intact. Confirm the ends are still trimmed and that no field currently normalised as a title changed at all -- a per-field diff, not a total.

BEWARE THE MATCHING LAYER. If any normalised prose value feeds a comparison key anywhere, preserving newlines changes that key. Check before changing, and if it does, report it rather than proceeding -- the same trap RS-337 exists for.

This needs a rebuild from stage 20 down to take effect on the live database, so state plainly that the code change alone does not fix the stored data. pytest and cargo test --workspace report 0 failed.
nodes.title: Stage 20 collapses newlines in prose, welding half the descriptions into one paragraph
