nodes.body: APPROVED 2026-08-04 by Tom: 'LaunchBox has dedicated entries with lots of reviews so we should add.' That signs off BOTH owner gates -- the targeted 'where game_type = 5' IGDB fetch, and admitting mods as work-creating. The recommendation's premise was wrong: the pipeline does not collapse mods, it never fetches them (igdb_request.py:115 excludes game_type 5, 1, 13, 14, so stg_igdb_games run 71 holds zero mod rows and stage 50's TYPE_MOD handling is dead code). Precedent for the classification change is RS-174, which settled the same question for bundles and standalone expansions. Two proposed structures already exist -- v2_work_relationships takes mod_of unchanged, and v2_works.game_type is work_type. The fetch is a targeted addition alongside the 333,195 staged entries, NOT a re-download; population size is unmeasurable in advance because the count query is itself an API call.
nodes.done_looks_like:
READ BOTH ARTIFACTS FIRST: 'recommendation.md' (spec) is the reviewing agent's proposal transcribed verbatim; 'assessment.md' (decision) carries the measured reason it cannot be built today and five corrections.

GATE 0 -- THE FETCH. Nothing here is buildable until IGDB is queried for game_type=5 and the owner has signed that off. It is a targeted addition, not a re-download: the existing paginated fetch takes a where clause, so mods collect alongside the 333,195 already-staged entries rather than replacing them. The mod population size CANNOT be measured first -- the count query is itself an API call, which is part of what is being approved.

GATE 1 -- THE OWNER'S WORK-CREATING TEST. works_build.py:44-50, recorded 2026-07-28: 'a type creates a work IF IT RUNS BY ITSELF WITH NO OTHER GAME NEEDED ... keeps out expansions, DLC and mods, which need a base game present.' The recommendation never engages with it. Do not quietly widen WORK_CREATING_TYPES. The assessment argues the test SURVIVES applied to the right object -- a patch needs the base, an applied romhack boots by itself, exactly like Sonic & Knuckles which the test already admits -- but that is the owner's test to confirm.

THEN: an IGDB game_type=5 entry creates its own work carrying its own igdb_id, title, ratings, dates, platforms and payload; a mod_of row lands in the EXISTING v2_work_relationships (no schema change -- work_id and related_work_id are both non-null FKs to v2_works, which is precisely why it could not hold mods while they had no work); v2_works.game_type carries 5 rather than a new work_type column; neither title becomes an alias of the other, and matching 'Pokemon Black Version' does not select Blaze Black. Spot check: LaunchBox 144821 (release 1198799, nds, 277 votes) maps to a Blaze Black work with the IGDB payload instead of minting a disconnected local work, and port grouping is unaffected.

OUT OF SCOPE -- ROM-LEVEL IDENTIFICATION. The recommendation's evidence order mixes grains. Items 2 and 5 are stage 55. Items 1, 3 and 4 identify a FILE ON A USER'S DISK, which is the Rust rom_scanner reading game_reference.db -- RS-165/RS-166, not this item. The catalogue can publish 'this hash is the verified base ROM'; it cannot publish 'this unknown hash is a modified base ROM'. Uncatalogued patches, translations and randomizer output stay release variants of the base work and mint nothing.
nodes.title: IGDB mods are excluded at fetch, so substantial romhacks can never carry IGDB identity
nodes.why: Seven Pokemon romhacks sit in the top ten of the review queue and Blaze Black is better attested in LaunchBox (277 votes) than the game it modifies (195).

nodes.body: SCOPE CHANGED 2026-08-04 after three independent analyses -- read the 'settled-design.md' decision artifact on this item BEFORE anything else; it carries the measured evidence and the reasoning for every clause. This item is NO LONGER a replacement of the join. Matching stays at work grain; entry grain becomes a narrow classed rule plus a review queue. Headline numbers, each verified by at least two agents with control arms reproducing live run 92 byte-for-byte: 229 gains, 168 disagreements, 182 losses under full replacement, ~210 new errors against ~210 correct gains. Depends on RS-387 (338 stale title_norms worth 62 matches) landing first, or its 62 will be misattributed to this work.
nodes.done_looks_like:
READ settled-design.md FIRST. Deliver in this order, and each step is separately valuable.

1. RS-387 LANDS FIRST -- it is a data repair worth +62 matches and -8/9 wrong ones, and leaving it undone corrupts the measurement of everything below.

2. THE PORT RULE. A release matches through a subordinate port entry when the work's OWN platforms (platforms_own_json, not the widened union) exclude the release's system and the entry's include it. 20 of 20 judged in that cell were entry-better. Verify Balloon Fight (lb 333, nes, 293 votes) and Ice Climber (lb 333's neighbour, 220) both reach their work at tier_1, and that the arcade Balloon Fight converges on the same work as the NES one.

3. THE EXPANSION EXCLUSION IS NOT OPTIONAL. expansion_of_work must NEVER be followed: it maps to the base game's work and destroys the identity of every distinctly-titled expansion. 16 of 17 judged were control-better. Name The Sims 3: Pets, Doom 3: Resurrection of Evil and Diablo: Hellfire individually and show each keeps its own work.

4. KEEP THE alternative_names PROJECTION (RS-295/303). It rescues the mirror channel -- title on the subordinate, platform on the root, 58 rows -- and removing it costs 58 losses for nothing.

5. THE QUEUE, INCLUDING TIES. Ties are Tom's addition and reach beyond entry grain: 794 shipped matches were decided with a tie present, 564 spanning MORE THAN ONE WORK, including Final Fantasy VII (psx, 681 votes), Pac-Man (mame, 417), Tetris (nes, 364) and Resident Evil 4 (ps2, 278) -- identity settled by an integer. Queue cross-work ties; a within-work tie is provenance only. Order by votes as the existing queues do. Carry the disagreement_class field (mapping_reason, ctrl_platform_ok, entry_platform_ok), which turns 168 judgements into about five.

6. RECORD THE MATCHED igdb_id on every match, whatever else is decided. 5,791 releases reach the same work through a different entry and 4,583 of those sit on a root that does not list their platform -- that is Balloon Fight's metadata loss at scale and it lands on RS-274 and stage 70.

GATE: coverage may not fall. Two stage-55 arms on ONE clone sharing identical starting bytes; gained/lost/repointed as three figures; EVERY loss judged individually. A net-positive headline is not sufficient -- RS-297 gained 94 while breaking 13. Note work_verdicts.jsonl cannot express a repoint today (mint_works_stage plans only from load_unmatched), and several queue rows want a work_merges.jsonl line instead because they are duplicate works.
nodes.title: Follow the IGDB entry for ports, keep the work for expansions, queue the rest
nodes.why: Measured three ways: replacing the join is roughly 1:1 on errors, but the port cell where the entry supplies a platform the work lacks was right 20 times out of 20.

nodes.body: Found by RS-337's builder, 2026-08-04, while verifying the trailing-'+' fix. Release 'Sorcery' carries 'Sorcery+ (Europe)' among its ALIASES -- TOSEC dumps of the '+' version filed under the base game -- so the two titles remain conflated even after normalisation stops eating the '+'. The defect is in alias derivation, not the join key. Contrast 'Bridge It' / 'Bridge It +', which has no such alias and separates cleanly under RS-337. This is the same species as RS-309 (filename-shaped aliases refused at derivation): an alias that is not a name the game is known by. Measure how many releases carry an alias that differs from the canonical title by a trailing '+' or ' plus', and how many stage-30 edges and stage-55 matches rest on one.
nodes.done_looks_like: MEASURE FIRST: how many releases carry an alias whose only difference from their canonical title is a trailing '+' / ' plus'; how many are same-platform; how many stage-30 title_exact and alias_title_exact edges and stage-55 matches currently rest on one. Then decide -- an alias that names a DIFFERENT product is refused at derivation, in the same place and by the same mechanism as RS-309's filename-shaped aliases, rather than filtered downstream. Sorcery / Sorcery+ separate, stated individually before and after. Coverage loss is the risk, not gain: report gained/lost/repointed as three figures from two stage-55 arms on one clone and judge every lost match individually. Closing this as not worth doing is a valid outcome if the population is trivial -- say so with the figure.
nodes.title: A release's alias set absorbs a DIFFERENT game's title when TOSEC files the '+' version under the base game
nodes.why: RS-337 fixed normalisation and its own headline case still did not separate, because the conflation was never in normalisation.

nodes.body: Found by RS-357's gate, 2026-08-04, and judged non-blocking for Part 1 -- but RS-360 is the first consumer and must not inherit it silently. v2_work_igdb_entry scopes to the latest COMPLETED stage-12 run. The two obvious alternatives are worse: joining on igdb_id alone double-projects (it broke six test_stage_contract.py tests immediately, which seed a second stage-12 generation by hand), and scoping on v2_works.igdb_run_id is a trap because the incremental UPSERT restamps ingest_run_id and deliberately not igdb_run_id, so a carried-over work names a staging run RS-159 has since deleted. Reachable in supported tooling via import_v2.py --skip-build-works. Mitigating: in the real runner path discard_superseded_generations deletes the old generation inside the stage-12 transaction, so those map rows dangle under ANY scoping and exact scoping would return zero rather than a refreshed payload -- not obviously better. The view discloses which generation it read (igdb_run_id) and the assertion docstring states the limitation.
nodes.done_looks_like: A stage-12 ingest that is not followed by stage 50 cannot leave v2_work_igdb_entry quietly serving a different generation's payload against an older mapping. Either the view refuses to project across a generation boundary, or something asserts on the mismatch OUTSIDE stage 50 -- today both assertions run only inside it, which is why the drift is silent. Reproduce the gate's construction first: on a clone insert one completed stage_12 run with 2 staged rows, do NOT re-run stage 50, and confirm the failure (view rows for run 77 collapse 333,099 -> 1, mapped-but-not-projected goes to 333,098, igdb 2735 returns the new dump's summary against the run-77 mapping). Then show the same construction is caught. Deciding the honest answer is 'return zero rows rather than the wrong payload' is a valid outcome -- say so with the reasoning.
nodes.title: A stage-12 ingest without a stage-50 re-run silently repoints every projected payload
nodes.why: RS-357's gate reproduced it on a clone: 333,099 view rows collapsed to 1 and igdb 2735 came back carrying a NEW dump's summary against its OLD mapping, with no assertion firing.

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04 while isolating RS-334's delta. release_work_match.py:397 calls normalize_title() on each work's alternative names AT MATCH TIME, using whatever is on disk -- so stage 55 is not the pure consumer of stored norms it reads as. A change to normalize.py therefore lands in stage 55 IMMEDIATELY, while canonical_title_norm and alias_norm on the stored rows still carry the old normalisation until stages 20/40/50 re-run. The measured cost of that half-applied state on RS-337's change was 6 matches, silently. CONSEQUENCE NOW LIVE: RS-337 merged as 0c16745, so the live database (releases 75 / works 77 / map 78) holds OLD-normalisation stored norms while the code on main normalises differently. Anyone running stage 55 against it before RS-361's rebuild gets a mixture. This is not a defect in RS-337's own measurement -- its arms re-derive the stored norms first -- it is a property of stage 55 nobody had written down.
nodes.done_looks_like: Either stage 55 stops deriving join keys at match time (alt-name norms are computed and stored by the stage that owns normalisation, and stage 55 reads them), or the mixed state is made impossible to enter silently -- a stage that finds stored norms disagreeing with the current normalize_title refuses, or says so loudly, rather than matching on a mixture. MEASURE FIRST: how many join keys stage 55 derives live versus reads from storage, and what else besides work alternative names is re-derived at line 397 and around it. Reproduce the 106,278-vs-106,284 gap on a clone by running stage 55 with normalize.py from before and after a normalisation change without re-running stages 20/40/50; that six-match gap is the regression test. Coverage loss is the risk if keys move to storage -- report gained/lost/repointed from two arms and judge every lost match individually. Note RS-361's rebuild clears the CURRENT mixed state but does not stop the next one.
nodes.title: Stage 55 re-normalises work alt names live, so a normalize change half-applies without a rebuild
nodes.why: RS-334's reconciliation found the control arm matching 106,278 instead of 106,284 on a branch whose only other change was to normalize.py.

nodes.body: Found by RS-165, confirmed to the digit by its gate, 2026-08-04. matcher.rs:306-310 falls back to rom_entries.filename with LIMIT 1 and NO ORDER BY. rom_entries has no unique constraint on filename (only game_filenames has PK (filename, platform)). Measured on the shipped game_reference.db: 12,907 duplicated (filename, platform) pairs covering 28,852 rows, of which 72 SPAN MORE THAN ONE game_id. For those 72 the identity a user gets is whichever row the planner happens to return -- and it may differ between two exports of identical data, or after an ANALYZE, without anything changing in the source.
nodes.done_looks_like: A filename that names more than one game does not silently resolve to an arbitrary one. Either the query orders deterministically so the same input always gives the same answer, or an ambiguous filename is refused and falls through to the next matcher tier -- decide which, and say why, because they differ: determinism makes it reproducible but still possibly wrong, refusal costs matches. Re-measure first (12,907 / 28,852 / 72 are 2026-08-04 sightings against the shipped export and will move when stage 70 replaces it). Name several of the 72 individually and say what a user would see today for each. Regression test seeds two games sharing a filename on one platform and asserts the outcome; it must fail if the ORDER BY or the refusal is removed. Note the same shape may exist on other LIMIT 1 paths -- matcher.rs:341-348's union arm 3 returns g.name while filtering gf.platform -- so check the neighbours before closing.
nodes.title: A ROM filename that names two games resolves to whichever row SQLite returns first
nodes.why: 72 filenames each name more than one game, and the query picks between them with LIMIT 1 and no ORDER BY.

nodes.body: Raised by RS-359's builder, 2026-08-04, which explicitly declined to fix it and recorded it in the code instead. FIGURES CORRECTED BY RS-359'S GATE, which recomputed them two independent ways (a controlled clone run and the live pre-change generation, agreeing exactly). remake_of, remaster_of, expanded_from and standalone_expansion_of resolve their target by walking to the ROOT of the IGDB parent chain. Where the chain has an intermediate work-creating entry the root is a false statement: 'Dear Esther remake_of Half-Life 2', 'Sigil remaster_of Doom'. MEASURED: 375 of the four types' 5,374 rows have root != nearest. 352 PREDATE mods. RS-359 added 23 new ones -- not the 19 first reported, which was the NET row-count change (23 appeared, 4 vanished). CRUCIALLY, THE 4 THAT MOVED WENT FROM CORRECT TO INCORRECT and are regressions rather than inherited defects: 'Dear Esther: Landmark Edition remaster_of Dear Esther' became 'remaster_of Half-Life 2', and the same shape hit The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, The Stanley Parable Demonstration and Ashes: Hard Reset. They are inert TODAY -- _same_family already returns True for every pair they can name, and v2_work_relationships is read by no export and no Rust -- which is why the gate judged shipping them acceptable once disclosed. RS-359 used _nearest_work for mod_of specifically, on evidence the gate confirmed exactly (959 of 9,729 mods resolve differently, and nearest was right in every sampled case: Dark Rising->FireRed not Red, Deus Ex: Revision->GOTY, Nightmare House 2->HL2 Episode Two). So the two walks now disagree by design, which is either the fix half-applied or a deliberate distinction, and nobody has ruled.
nodes.done_looks_like: A decision recorded either way, with evidence. If Pass 3 moves onto _nearest_work: the 375 rows are reported as a before/after list, EVERY ONE JUDGED INDIVIDUALLY in both directions -- a nearer target is not automatically the truer one, since an intermediate entry may be a bundle or a regional edition rather than the thing actually remade. Name Dear Esther, Sigil and several others explicitly. If the root walk is KEPT for these four: say why the mod case differs, so the disagreement between the two walks is a documented distinction rather than an accident, and correct the 19 rows RS-359 added or state why they are acceptable. RE-MEASURE FIRST -- 375/5,373/356/19 are 2026-08-04 sightings taken on a clone before the live rebuild (RS-361), and the rebuild moves them. Closing this as 'the root walk is correct for these types' is a valid outcome.
nodes.title: Four relationship types name the root of the chain when a nearer work is the truth
nodes.why: 375 of 5,373 rows say a game is a remake or expansion of something it is not, and 356 of them predate the change that surfaced it.

nodes.body: Found by RS-372's builder, 2026-08-04, while auditing the neighbours of the ambiguous-filename fallback. TWO PLACES in matcher.rs's ensure_name_cache and the pass that reads it. (1) The 'exact' map takes the FIRST row of an unordered three-arm UNION ALL, so which of several same-named rows wins is whatever SQLite returns. (2) The fuzzy pass breaks a score tie with max_by over a HashMap -- and Rust randomises HashMap iteration order PER PROCESS, so two runs of the same binary over the same data can disagree on a tie. That is worse than the RS-372 defect it was found beside: that one was arbitrary but at least stable for a given database, this one is not stable across restarts. Note RS-165's read-set document already flags the UNION ALL half as an assumption the schema does not promise; the HashMap half is new.
nodes.done_looks_like: The same ROM scanned twice against the same catalogue identifies as the same game, across process restarts. Establish a deterministic tie-break for both halves -- the UNION ALL's first-row-wins and the fuzzy pass's max_by -- and say what you chose and why, because the choice is a claim about which candidate is better and not merely which is first. REPRODUCE BEFORE FIXING: run the fuzzy pass twice in separate processes over a fixture with a genuine score tie and show the answers differ; that reproduction is the regression test, and it must fail without the fix. Beware that a test running both passes in ONE process may see the same iteration order and pass vacuously -- the acceptance is two processes. Consider whether refusing a tie is better than breaking it, as RS-372 concluded for its own case; a wrong answer stated confidently is worse than a fall-through.
nodes.title: A tie in the fuzzy name match resolves differently between two runs of the same binary
nodes.why: HashMap iteration order is randomised per process, so the same ROM against the same catalogue can identify as two different games.

nodes.body:
Found by RS-372 and confirmed in detail by its gate, 2026-08-04, when re-measuring turned a matcher question into an exporter one. TWO MECHANISMS, both in export_game_reference.py, both landing on the same symptom.

(1) TRUNCATION AT PUNCTUATION. The launchbox-names filename derivation truncates a title at its first '.', so 'Dr. Brain Thinking Games: IQ Adventure' is stored as 'Dr', 'Mr. Bree+' as 'Mr', every BIT.TRIP title as 'BIT'. The gate verified 262 of the 264 affected filenames are an exact PREFIX of their game's name (A.D <- A.D. 2044; F.E.A.R <- F.E.A.R. 2: Project Origin; Plants vs <- Plants vs. Zombies). The other 2 are titles that BEGIN with a full stop -- '.flow' and '.kkrieger' -- which strip to the EMPTY STRING. Counts: 72 ambiguous (filename, platform) pairs over 269 rows, 71 of them windows; Dr names 26 games, Mr 17, BIT 8, F.E.A.R 9. Exactly ONE of the 72 is a genuine source collision: tmd on nds, No-Intro's ROM name for five DSiWare titles.

(2) AN ARBITRARY PICK AT EXPORT TIME. export_game_reference.py:295-300 populates game_filenames with INSERT OR IGNORE ... SELECT DISTINCT and NO ORDER BY, while the table has PRIMARY KEY (filename, platform). So the PK silently DROPS 197 of the 269 game associations and keeps whichever row the master's join happened to emit first. The app then reports that pick at MatchType::Filename confidence with no ambiguity signal -- 'Dr' resolves to Dr. Brain Thinking Games: IQ Adventure, 'BIT' to BIT.TRIP BEAT, 'tmd' to Brain Age Express: Arts & Letters. RS-372's refusal guard cannot see any of this: match_by_filename tries game_filenames FIRST and returns early, and all 72 pairs exist there, so the rom_entries arm is never reached.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Stage 70's export does not manufacture an ambiguous filename, and does not resolve one silently when the source genuinely provides it. BOTH mechanisms addressed. For (1): no derived filename is a truncation of its title at punctuation, and none is empty. For (2): an ambiguous (filename, platform) either does not reach game_filenames at all, or reaches it in a form the app can recognise as ambiguous -- INSERT OR IGNORE with no ORDER BY must not be how the winner is chosen. VERIFY by re-running the gate's counts against the new export: 72 ambiguous pairs fall to approximately 1 (tmd/nds, which is real and must SURVIVE as a legitimate ambiguity for the matcher to refuse), 0 empty filenames, and 0 game associations dropped by a primary key. Name Dr, Mr, BIT, F.E.A.R, tmd and .flow individually before and after. INTERACTION: RS-372's refusal stays correct either way -- it exists for genuine collisions -- but it is currently SHADOWED by the game_filenames arm, so fixing (2) is what makes it reachable.

RESTATED AS INVARIANTS 2026-08-04, BECAUSE THE DEFECT CHANGED SHAPE. The verify clause above quotes v1-control figures ("72 ambiguous pairs fall to approximately 1") and those cannot be read literally against v2. Per ACCEPTANCE_CONVENTION a drifted figure is never auto-corrected, precisely because sometimes the defect changed shape -- and here it did, so the numbers are superseded rather than updated. Measured by the RS-166 planner:

MECHANISM (1) HAS NO SOURCE IN V2. v1's truncation victims came entirely from source='launchbox-names' -- game TITLES stored as filenames -- and v2 does not project LaunchBox titles into the ROM spine at all. So "no derived filename is a truncation of its title at punctuation" is satisfied by construction in v2, NOT by a fix. Do not claim credit for it, and DO assert it, because a later change that starts projecting titles would reintroduce the mechanism silently.

MECHANISM (2) IS LARGER, NOT SMALLER. 72 ambiguous pairs was the v1 control; against v2's larger DAT corpus it is 560 genuinely ambiguous pairs. The named cases (Dr -> 26 games, Mr -> 17, BIT -> 8, F.E.A.R -> 9, tmd -> 5, 1 empty) were re-confirmed on the CONTROL today and remain the right worked examples -- but "72 -> ~1" is not the target. The invariant is what matters: an ambiguous (filename, platform) either does not reach game_filenames, or reaches it in a form the app can recognise as ambiguous. INSERT OR IGNORE with no ORDER BY must not be how the winner is chosen, and no game association may be dropped by a primary key.

A THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME MECHANISM EXISTS, IN A DIFFERENT TABLE, AND IS CURRENTLY UNPOLICED. 91 SHA1 values name more than one release in v2 (54 in the v1 master). rom_hashes' primary key is (hash, hash_type), v1 fills it with INSERT OR IGNORE and no ORDER BY, and -- the part that matters -- REFERENTIAL_CHECKS["hash_multi_game"] CANNOT DETECT IT: the primary key guarantees one row per hash BEFORE the check runs, so the check is vacuous and has been sitting there looking like coverage. A 4,391-pair version of the same shape exists in game_serials. Stage 70 must pick deterministically or omit, and the vacuous check must be made capable of failing or removed -- a check that cannot fail is worse than no check.

RE-MEASURE ALL OF THE ABOVE before building: 560 / 91 / 4,391 are 2026-08-04 sightings taken against generations releases 103, works 105, map 106.
nodes.title: The export manufactures wrong filename-to-game answers, in two independent ways
nodes.why: The count drifted because the DEFECT changed shape: mechanism (1) has no source in v2 at all, mechanism (2) is 560 pairs not 72, and a third unpoliced instance exists in rom_hashes behind a check that cannot fail.

nodes.body: Read BOTH artifacts before starting: 'recommendation.md' (spec) is the reviewing agent's proposal transcribed from chat; 'assessment.md' (decision) verifies its premises, corrects one amendment, and records what RS-360 changes about it. Verdicts are replayed unconditionally each generation, so one that upstream has since fixed is reapplied blindly and can undo the improvement. The rule: evaluate each verdict against a PRE-CURATION baseline match and classify it needed / satisfied_upstream / conflict / structurally_stale, applying only 'needed'. VERIFIED PREMISES: mint_works_stage plans from load_unmatched() alone (mint_works.py:798, helper :327), so attach/mint/reject cannot reach a matched release and a verdict on one is silently inert rather than reported; and the corpus is effectively empty -- work_verdicts.jsonl holds ONE line against 22 in work_merges.jsonl. DO IT NOW BECAUSE IT IS FREE NOW: conditional semantics change what a verdict MEANS, from 'always do this' to 'do this while still needed', and applying that retroactively rewrites every verdict in the file. Today that is one verdict; after a review season it is hundreds.
nodes.done_looks_like:
READ recommendation.md AND assessment.md FIRST.

EVERY verdict is classified each generation against a baseline built WITHOUT release-level curated aliases: needed / satisfied_upstream / conflict / structurally_stale. Only 'needed' is applied. The classification, the baseline target, the verdict target and the reason are all persisted and reported -- a verdict that no longer applies is REPORTED, never deleted, because a dormant verdict is retained knowledge and reactivating it when upstream regresses is the point.

PER KIND, as the recommendation sets out: attach applies only while baseline is unresolved; alias is dry-run against an index built without curated aliases and applied only if still required; mint does not create a local duplicate when an IGDB-backed work now matches; reject reports a conflict rather than silently accepting or blindly rejecting; defer continues to apply nothing. Work merges and source-group verdicts keep their SEPARATE structural validation -- they are durable judgements, not queue repairs.

TIES ANNOTATE, THEY DO NOT RECLASSIFY (Tom's correction, 2026-08-04 -- an earlier draft proposed a fifth 'tie means needed' class and it was WRONG). A tie-decided baseline is still a match. If it equals the verdict's target it is satisfied_upstream; if it differs it is a conflict; those are exhaustive and both are already safe. What the tie earns is a PRIORITY SIGNAL: record whether the automatic side was decided by _pick_best's lowest-id tiebreak and sort conflicts on it, because 'these disagree and the automatic side was decided by an integer' is a far stronger candidate for the verdict being right. Scale: 794 shipped matches carry competing_count > 1 and 564 span more than one work.

SHARED PLUMBING: verdicts must be EVALUABLE against matched releases even though they are only APPLIED to unmatched ones. RS-360 needs the same capability for its repoint path -- build it there, consume it here, which is why this depends on RS-360 rather than racing it through mint_works.py.

VERIFY on a clone: a verdict whose target upstream now matches classifies satisfied_upstream and applies nothing; one that disagrees classifies conflict and does NOT override; a structurally stale one is skipped as today. Use the recommendation's own Phantasy Star IV and Blaze Black cases as the worked examples, both named individually. Do NOT expect the alias dry-run to mostly confirm -- RS-360 keeps the ~14,500-name derived alternative_names projection, so more aliases will retire as satisfied_upstream than the recommendation anticipates; that is a good outcome, not a defect rate.

THE REVIEWER-FACING HALF, WHICH IS NOT OPTIONAL. This change alters what a verdict MEANS, so it is not done until a person can tell. Three things:

(a) curation/README.md:7 currently says a judgement 'is re-applied on every run'. That becomes FALSE -- evaluated every run, applied only while needed. It is the one sentence telling a reviewer what a verdict means. Update it, and give the six-verdict table a column for what each kind does when the baseline ALREADY AGREES. The authoring act itself does not change: same JSON, same external keys, same append-never-edit. Say so explicitly, so a reviewer does not think their habits need revising.

(b) NAME THE SURFACE A PERSON READS. 'Persisted and reported' is not enough. Conflicts are work the pipeline generates FOR the human -- a second inbox, where today the loop is one-way (read queue, append line, done). Say where conflict rows appear and that a reviewer is expected to look. A conflict nobody reads is the silent-inertness defect this item exists to fix, moved one layer out.

(c) DISAMBIGUATE defer FROM satisfied_upstream. Both apply nothing; they differ only in queue membership (defer stays, satisfied leaves). State it, or the two states are indistinguishable to the reviewer.

AND THE TIE ANNOTATION NEEDS THE SAME PROSE. RS-360 will annotate queue rows with 'the automatic side was decided by a lowest-id tiebreak'. The classifier correction above stops a tie RECLASSIFYING a verdict, but the identical misreading is still available to a PERSON: a reviewer seeing that flag will reasonably read it as 'this match is wrong' and override matches that are fine -- Tom's own failure mode, arriving through the queue instead of through the code. The annotation must read as LOOK HARDER, not AS WRONG, and it must say so where the reviewer sees it, not only in this item.
nodes.title: A manual verdict should apply while it is still needed, not on every rebuild
nodes.why: An alias verdict SILENTLY overrides an already-matched release today -- no check, no exception row, no report (planner finding, 2026-08-04). The other four kinds are needed-only by accident; this one is the live defect, and it grows with every alias the reviewer writes.

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04. The RS-387 build surfaced this as a single anecdote -- work 'Inv' (igdb 100134) has no year and no platforms, so release 1098013 atari2600 'INV' cannot reach it even with correct normalisation -- and the orchestrator measured the class behind it: 53,020 of 331,150 generation-91 works have platforms_json null or empty. That is 16% of the works table. MATCH_TIER_CASCADE gates SIX of its seven tiers on platforms_json; only tier_5 is platform-blind. So a platformless work is reachable through exactly one tier, the weakest one, and a release whose correct work is platformless will usually mint a duplicate instead -- the matcher declines, stage 56 mints, and the catalogue grows a second record for a game it already held. Upstream of RS-360 rather than part of it: RS-360 decides which entry a release follows; this decides whether the right answer is reachable at all.
nodes.done_looks_like: MEASURE BEFORE DESIGNING -- 53,020 is a 2026-08-04 sighting and the SHAPE matters more than the count. Establish how many of the 53,020 are genuinely platformless upstream versus losing platforms in projection (IGDB entries carry platforms; a work built from a graph of entries may fail to union them), because those are different defects with different fixes. Then count how many releases currently mint a local work whose correct target is an existing platformless work -- that is the actual cost, and it should be counted, not estimated. VERIFY: the platformless count falls, and for a named sample of releases that previously minted, the release now reaches the existing work rather than a duplicate. Report gained and lost as two figures. DO NOT simply relax the platform gate to compensate: six tiers gate on it deliberately, and RS-360's analysis found the platform-blind tier_5 is where several of the worst mismatches already come from -- four Prince of Persia releases land on an SNES work through exactly that tier.
nodes.title: 53,020 works carry no platforms, so six of seven match tiers cannot reach them
nodes.why: MEASURED 2026-08-04: the platforms are absent UPSTREAM (52,973 of 333,195 raw IGDB records, 15.9%), not lost in projection -- the item's original 'defect we own' framing was wrong. Route around or accept; there is no projection bug to fix.

nodes.body: READ BOTH ARTIFACTS FIRST: 'recommendation.md' (spec) is the reviewing agent's proposal transcribed from chat; 'assessment.md' (decision) verifies every premise against the code and flags ONE PROPOSED REVERSAL OF A DOCUMENTED DECISION. Premises confirmed: v2_local_works (schema.py:1469-1497) carries only local_key/title/title_norm/release_year/mint_reason/candidate_igdb_ids_json/vote_count/member_count/provenance_json -- no type, no relationships, no alt names. v2_work_relationships (:1274-1286) has BOTH work_id and related_work_id as NOT NULL FKs to v2_works, so a local work cannot appear on either side -- the same obstruction mods hit before RS-359, where the cheap fix was to give mods real works rather than widen the table. v2_work_group_members.work_id (:1660-1690) FKs to v2_works alone. OWNER-ASSIGNED because point 3 contradicts a recorded schema decision: 'A work minted at stage 56 has no IGDB identity, so it cannot be in an IGDB collection; and a libretro franchise that reaches one keeps its claim at RELEASE level instead of inventing a work-level one.' The recommendation's argument is that the invariant was scoped to INFERENCE and a human assertion is different evidence -- defensible, not a naive flag flip, and not a builder's call.
nodes.done_looks_like:
SPLIT THIS -- four points, different urgency, different review questions.

READ assessment.md FIRST. It was REVISED after the owner asked how the existing Sonic & Knuckles represents itself, and the answer collapses most of the proposal.

IGDB ALREADY MODELS THE LOCK-ON CASE, AND WE COPY ITS SHAPE. 'Sonic the Hedgehog 3 & Knuckles' is its own IGDB work (igdb 11219, 1994), with BOTH cartridges pointing at it through a relationship type that already exists: Sonic the Hedgehog 3 --included_in--> it, and Sonic & Knuckles --included_in--> it (plus Sonic & Knuckles --standalone_expansion_of--> Sonic the Hedgehog 3). included_in is the pipeline's most common relationship at 26,920 rows. 'Knuckles the Echidna in Sonic the Hedgehog 2' is simply ABSENT from IGDB -- which is why it mints -- and must then be minted in the SAME shape its sibling already has: Sonic 2 (igdb 4438) --included_in--> [minted work], Sonic & Knuckles (igdb 9475) --included_in--> [minted work].

SO DO NOT ADD lock_on_combination_of. It would invent a vocabulary with no source, diverging from IGDB's own answer to the same question. game_subtype has lost its motivating example; it may still earn a place, it no longer has this one. The multi-target requirement is real but trivial -- two ordinary included_in rows, not a new concept and not a new cardinality.

POINT 4 FIRST AND ALONE -- it is an active regression. When mint_title replaces the LaunchBox title the original is LOST, so a curator renaming a work to something canonical REDUCES what the matcher finds next run. Preserve the original release title as an alias on the local work.

POINT 2 SECOND, AND IT IS NOW ONE NULLABLE COLUMN. v2_work_relationships.related_work_id is a NOT NULL FK to v2_works (schema.py:1274-1286), so nothing can point AT a local work. That is the entire gap the Sonic case needs. NOTE THE DIRECTION -- included_in runs constituent to combination, so the minted work is the TARGET, not the subject; the same is true of the 4 Fun in 1 compilation. An earlier orchestrator suggestion to give local works their own relationships table 'because the subject is always local' was WRONG IN BOTH EXAMPLES and is withdrawn. Caveat that stands: RS-375 shows this table has 375 known-wrong rows and NOTHING READS IT, so widening it is still the wrong order -- but the change is now one column rather than a two-id-kinds rework, and it has a concrete consumer in the curation queue.

POINT 1 (work type): if local works gain a type vocabulary, NAME THE IGDB ONE AT THE SAME TIME. The pipeline currently uses raw integers (WORK_CREATING_TYPES = {0,8,9,10,3,4}, plus 5 for mods after RS-359); symbolic names on one side only leaves two vocabularies for one concept. Note expanded_from ALREADY EXISTS and is what the recommendation's game_type 'expanded_game' means.

POINT 3 (group membership) IS THE OWNER'S DECISION AND HALF ALREADY EXISTS. v2_work_group_members already carries member_kind='release' for exactly the workless case -- 'a libretro franchise tag whose release stage 55 left workless; the claim is real and the work is not nameable, so the row says exactly that.' So franchise membership for a workless release IS ALREADY EXPRESSIBLE. The genuine gap is narrower: whether a curated local work carries ONE membership instead of N release-level ones, and can be the subject of the idx_v2_work_group_members_work read every consumer makes. ARGUE IT AS GRAIN AND ERGONOMICS, NOT EXPRESSIVENESS. The proposed reversal -- 'do not require a local work to have an IGDB identity merely to belong to a source-backed franchise' -- contradicts a recorded schema decision and is NOT a builder's call. It is also not a naive flag flip: the invariant was written against INFERENCE, and a human assertion is a different evidence class.

DEPENDS ON RS-388, DOES NOT RESTATE IT. The stale-verdict clause is exactly RS-388's needed/satisfied_upstream classification, and mint is one of the kinds Build 2 gates. No new mechanism.

VERIFY: a curated mint records its type and its relationships by STABLE ids (IGDB ids or local keys, never regenerated row ids), and both survive a full rebuild that regenerates every internal id -- the property work_verdicts.jsonl already demonstrates. Knuckles in Sonic 2 ends up with two included_in rows naming igdb 4438 and igdb 9475, matching the shape of igdb 11219. An automatic mint records type=unknown and invents NO relationships. Conflicting franchise evidence on a grouped mint produces a review exception rather than a silent pick.

ON THE TWO HELD VERDICTS -- USE 'defer', WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT IT IS FOR. An earlier draft of this item said 'hold the verdicts BUT capture the facts in the reason prose', which is incoherent: you cannot write a reason for a line you are not writing. The file already solves it. 'defer' is in VALID_VERDICTS and DELIBERATELY ABSENT from ACTIONABLE (verdicts.py:138-144); its documented behaviour is 'nothing; the row re-surfaces' (:39). So a defer line applies nothing, keeps the release in the queue, and carries a reason -- and because the file is append-only and last-line-wins on launchbox_id, a real mint line supersedes it later with no cleanup.

So: write defer NOW for '4 Fun in 1' and the Sonic lock-on game, with the reason naming igdb 4438 (Sonic the Hedgehog 2), igdb 9475 (Sonic & Knuckles) and igdb 11219 (Sonic the Hedgehog 3 & Knuckles, the precedent for the shape), and stating that it waits on this item. The knowledge is the scarce thing and it is currently only in a chat log; the schema is not scarce and can follow.
nodes.title: A curated local work cannot record its type, relationships or series
nodes.why: IGDB models the lock-on case ALREADY (igdb 11219 with two included_in parents); we cannot point at a minted work because related_work_id is NOT NULL to v2_works. The gap is one nullable column, not a new vocabulary.

nodes.body:
Found 2026-08-04 by the RS-388 Build 3 builder while writing the M33 mutation test; pinned as behaviour in a test docstring rather than fixed. Stage 50 calls load_verdicts with NO works_run_id -- it is mid-build of the very works those titles would resolve against -- so an alias line carrying target_title and no target_igdb_id is skipped there at 'missing_target' and its name NEVER ENTERS THE WORKS LAYER. Stage 55 can resolve it (it has a completed works generation to resolve against), so it classifies the verdict 'needed' -- correctly, and forever. The result is a live verdict that is reported as needed on every run and does nothing on every run. A reviewer has no signal that it is inert. curation/README.md's six-verdict table currently offers target_igdb_id and target_title as EQUALS for alias, which is false. NOTE the same table is already wrong in another way -- it is headed 'The six verdicts' over five rows, and VALID_VERDICTS now holds EIGHT (the two group verdicts were never documented, and repoint was added 2026-08-04).

⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-04 BY THE RS-388 BUILD 3 GATE -- THE MECHANISM WAS RIGHT AND THE CONSEQUENCE WAS WRONG. This item, and the builder's commit and pinned test, originally said a title-only alias is 'permanently needed and permanently INERT'. The first half is right; the second is FALSE, and the gate proved it by running the fixture through a stage the test does not: STAGE 56 ATTACHES IT. mint_works.py:795-797 calls load_verdicts WITH works_run_id, so the title resolves there, and mint_works.py:229 treats VERDICT_ALIAS as an attach for a still-unmatched release. The gate's probe asserted attached_by_verdict == 0 and failed on 1.

The live corpus corroborates and explains a figure nobody had accounted for: stage 56 on the 11-line file reports attached_by_verdict = 8, which is 3 attaches PLUS THE 5 ALIASES whose names never reached works run 105.

SO WHAT A TITLE-ONLY ALIAS LOSES IS THE ALIAS'S DEFINING PROPERTY, NOT ITS EFFECT. The name never enters the works layer, so it clears exactly the one queue row it names instead of the family of releases carrying that title. What becomes false is curation/README.md's 'One alias can clear many queue rows; an attach clears exactly one' -- NOT 'your verdict does nothing'. For a reviewer that is a different instruction: 'your line is inert' sends them to rewrite it, 'your line acts, but only on the release it names' tells them the truth.
nodes.done_looks_like:
EITHER stage 50 can resolve a title-only alias, OR the pipeline refuses to accept one and says why. DECIDE WHICH -- do not leave the third state, where it is accepted, reported as needed, and inert.

If resolving: stage 50 must resolve target_title against the works it is mid-build of, which is a change to that stage's ordering and is the reason this was not fixed in Build 3. Establish it can be done without a second pass before committing to it.

If refusing: a title-only alias becomes a parse-time or resolve-time skip with a counted reason, so the reviewer sees it rejected rather than silently pending. This is the cheaper answer and is probably right -- an alias that cannot reach the works layer is not a weaker alias, it is not an alias.

EITHER WAY curation/README.md must stop offering target_igdb_id and target_title as equals for the alias kind, and must fix the two other defects in that table: the heading says SIX over FIVE rows, and VALID_VERDICTS holds EIGHT (split_group and join_group are documented only in verdicts.py's module docstring; repoint was added 2026-08-04). Fold into RS-388 Build 4 if that lands first.

VERIFY: write a title-only alias against a release the matcher does not otherwise answer, run stage 50 then stage 55, and confirm the outcome is the one chosen -- the name is in the works layer and the release matches, OR the line is reported as refused with a reason. NOT 'needed' with no effect. RE-MEASURE against the generation you test on: works run 105 / map 106 as of 2026-08-04 14:13, and the live file holds 6 aliases, all of which carry target_igdb_id -- so the live population of this defect is currently ZERO and it is a trap waiting rather than a live wrong answer.
nodes.title: A target_title-only alias silently degrades to an attach
nodes.why: A title-only alias silently degrades to an attach: it acts on the one release it names instead of the family carrying that title, so the reviewer gets an alias's promise and an attach's reach.

nodes.body: Split out of RS-166 on 2026-08-04 by the owner's 'get export done, then bucket the tidy-up' direction. RS-166's acceptance demanded 'a game_metadata table exists, since the current export carries no metadata at all and 858 matched games show year=0, genre=0, players=0'. That clause is an ENHANCEMENT BEYOND THE VERIFIED READ SET, not a requirement for the file to load: docs/STAGE70_READ_SET.md traces what the Rust scanner reads, and it reads name/platform/region/year off the release-grain games table and nothing else. So a metadata table is worth having and is not what makes the export work. DEPENDS ON RS-46, which builds the stage-60 split that puts IGDB metadata at the right level (work vs release) with provenance -- that is where the metadata would come FROM, and it is unstarted.
nodes.done_looks_like:
RE-MEASURE FIRST: 858 is an undated sighting inherited from RS-166's acceptance and predates the 2026-08-04 rebuild (releases 103, works 105, map 106). The current figure may differ and the SHAPE matters more than the count -- establish how many matched games lack year, genre and players SEPARATELY rather than as one number, because they have different sources and different fixes.

Then: a metadata table exists in the export and the app can render a year, a genre and a player count for a matched game. VERIFY the count of matched games showing year=0 falls, named individually for a sample, and that nothing that previously rendered stops rendering.

MIND THE READ SET. docs/STAGE70_READ_SET.md is the authority on what the app actually reads, and today that is games.name/platform/region/year plus the ROM tables -- seven tables read, three not. Adding a table the app does not read repeats the game_works situation (128,403 rows carried for 'browsing that does not exist yet'). So either land this WITH the consumer that reads it, or say plainly in the item that it is being staged ahead of a consumer and why.

DEPENDS ON RS-46 for the source data. Do not synthesise metadata in the exporter to route around an unbuilt stage 60 -- that puts the level decision (work vs release) in the wrong place, which is the defect RS-46 exists to fix.

Ambiguity still wins: where the base title is shared by several releases (Firepower/'Fire Power', Project X, Mixed-Up Mother Goose 1988 vs 1991) the probe stays unmatched.

Numerals are OUT OF SCOPE: GTA 6 -> 'Grand Theft Auto VI' and Archon 2 -> 'Archon II: Adept' are the sequel gate's territory, not this rule's — do not add Roman/Arabic mapping here.

nodes.body: Half (a) — popularity as the tie-break inside a structural tie — is delivered by RS-686 (votes are the third rung of its evidence ladder; 'has any votes' is the discriminator). What remains here is the SHARED GATE (prove closure per system) and HALF (b): a sole candidate above a derived lower floor where the corpus is demonstrably closed. Depends on RS-686 landing first so the measurement is not confounded.
nodes.done_looks_like:
HALF (a) IS NOT HERE — RS-686 delivers popularity-as-tie-break (2026-08-25). This item is the shared gate plus half (b), unchanged in substance:

=== SHARED GATE: prove the corpus is closed before trusting it ===
Measure closure PER SYSTEM and report it (catalogue sizes were 2026-08-20 sightings; re-measure). For files that do not match, SAMPLE 20-30 and determine whether the game is genuinely absent from the catalogue or merely named differently — those look identical in a count and mean opposite things. Apply the rule only to systems where closure is demonstrated, and name the systems excluded.

=== HALF (b): the sole candidate above a lower floor ===
Where exactly one candidate clears a lower floor and no other candidate is anywhere near it, accept it even though it fails the absolute floor RS-686 leaves in place. Do NOT pick the threshold — DERIVE it from the A/B across the real corpora (RS-686's control-arm harness is the instrument): find the point at which the wrong-identity rate is zero and report the recovery there, with the tolerance accepted and why. Test whether corpus size should scale the floor before building on it. The structural ladder's Blocked/withheld states are HARD STOPS and stay so — a key with multiple owners is proven ambiguous, not weakly evidenced. Every changed identity is JUDGED INDIVIDUALLY; no file may change from one game to a different wrong game.
nodes.title: Break match ambiguity with popularity, and trust the closed corpus
nodes.why: RS-577 made the matcher refuse ambiguity rather than guess, which is safe but leaves files unmatched. Both halves recover matches without reintroducing the confident-wrong-identity failure, IF each is gated on measured evidence rather than assumed.

nodes.body: RS-589 blocked 1,421 stage-30 pairs, 1,457 stage-40 attachments and 362 stage-55 work links. Judging 30 of them individually found several classes the available evidence DOES resolve - they are correctly blocked under today's rules, but the rules are leaving information unused.

Each class below is either resolved by using the evidence, or explicitly declined with a reason. Re-measure the counts first - they are 2026-08-20 sightings.

(1) PUBLISHER resolves a tie the title cannot: NES Tetris (Nintendo vs Tengen) and Tetris (Atari vs Sega, where a raw qualifier also helps). Note the scanner side landed exactly this idea as RS-592 and it worked - the catalogue has publisher on ~90% of game_metadata rows.

nodes.body: roman_to_int refuses every one-character token in sequel.rs and match_evidence.py alike, so 'Ultima I', 'SoulCalibur V' and 'Sangokushi V' extract no number and carry zero sequel penalty against their own base title.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Re-measure first - every figure below is a 2026-08-20 sighting taken from game_reference.db (schema_version 6, exported 2026-08-04), not an invariant.

A single-character Roman token folds to a number when the evidence says it is a numeral, and does not when it is a brand letter. 590 of 164,696 catalogue titles end in a bare i/v/x/l token (x:286, i:175, v:118, l:11). Only 65 of those have their own base title present on the same platform, which is the entire population that can be wrongly merged today. Exactly ONE title has both a letter sibling and an arabic-equivalent sibling: 'Mega Man X' against 'Mega Man 10' on wii.

Establish the discriminator by measurement rather than assumption. Two candidates: (a) the RAW separator, since 'Rally-X', 'Quad-X' and "Bomb'X" join the letter with punctuation while 'Ultima I' and 'SoulCalibur V' use a space, and normalisation is what destroys that evidence - _numeric_penalty already receives left_raw/right_raw; (b) series corroboration in the corpus, where 'Ultima I' is a numeral because Ultima II and III exist on the platform. Report which one actually separates the 65, and say plainly if neither does.

These are tests. Must NOT fold: 'Rally-X', 'Quad-X', "Bomb'X", 'Revolution X'. Must NOT lose the penalty that keeps them apart: 'Mega Man X' must not become numerically identical to 'Mega Man 10'. Must fold: 'Ultima I' against 'Ultima' scores a sequel mismatch, likewise 'SoulCalibur V' and 'Sangokushi V'.

Both consumers stay equivalent - the cross-language corpus test added by RS-593 must still pass. Do NOT modify config/match_rules/sequel_vectors.json. Report how many scanner matches and how many stage-30 edges change.
nodes.title: Single-character Roman numerals are invisible to the sequel gate in both consumers
nodes.why: Surfaced 2026-08-20 by the adversarial pipeline review as a canonical-validation bypass; RS-593 closed the bypass by refusing single chars outright, which turned a wrong-fold into a blind spot rather than removing it.

nodes.body: The shipped catalogue carries no rating, no vote count and no play signal: quality_tier is NULL on all 164,696 games and game_metadata has only overview/genres/developer/publisher/max_players/cooperative. LaunchBox ratings and vote counts are ingested upstream and then dropped at export.
nodes.done_looks_like:
The exported game_reference.db carries a per-game popularity signal the scanner can read, and STAGE70_READ_SET.md documents it as v1 does the rest.

Re-measure first - 2026-08-20 sightings: 164,696 games, quality_tier NULL on 100%, game_metadata columns are overview/genres/developer/publisher/max_players/cooperative only.

Decide and RECORD what the signal is rather than assuming. LaunchBox carries a community rating and a vote count; those are two numbers with different failure modes, and a rating without a vote count is noise on a game three people rated. Say which you export and why. quality_tier already exists as a column and is computed by tools/game-database/scripts/compute_quality_tiers.py, which has never been run (RS-155) - decide whether to revive it or export the raw numbers and let the consumer band them. Prefer the raw numbers if the banding is contested, because a band is a decision the exporter cannot take back.

Report coverage: how many of the 164,696 games carry the signal, broken down by platform for at least megadrive, amiga500, nes, snes, psx, ps2. A signal present on 5% of a platform cannot break ties on that platform, and saying so is part of the deliverable.

Do NOT rebuild the v2 database. Do NOT overwrite the shipped catalogue - v2's exporter requires an explicit --output and refuses to overwrite, and that is deliberate.

nodes.body: The deployed game_reference.db was exported 2026-08-04. Eight matching and pipeline items have merged since. Regenerating would carry those improvements into the app, and would re-run the identity resolution that produced the ids the user's library references.
nodes.done_looks_like:
A decision is recorded: either the catalogue is regenerated and redeployed, or it is explicitly deferred with the reason and the trigger that would change the answer.

WHAT IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, measured 2026-08-20 - do not re-litigate these, verify them:

The v1-to-v2 identity transition ALREADY HAPPENED on this instance and broke nothing. The shipped game_reference.db is the v2 stage-70 export (schema_version 6, 2026-08-04, 436,686,848 bytes) and it sits in both the data root and /Users/tom/RetroStack/retrostack/. Of the instance's 859 matched games, all 859 resolve in it, and all 859 carry ids present in the FROZEN crosswalk pipeline_v2/data/legacy_release_ids.tsv.gz. NONE is a minted id.

That is what makes this decision smaller than it looks. Carried ids are stable by construction, because the crosswalk is a frozen file keyed on (launchbox_id, platform). The exposure of a regeneration is confined to whether the LaunchBox anchor and platform still agree for a given release after the pipeline fixes - not to the id scheme changing under the user.

WHAT THE DECISION NEEDS:

Run scripts/compare_reference_exports.py between the deployed export and a candidate one BEFORE shipping anything, and report the diff at three grains: how many games.id values move, how many of the instance's 859 move, and how many games gain or lose a match-relevant field. A regeneration that moves zero of the 859 is a different decision from one that moves forty.

Say what the regeneration BUYS. Merged since the 2026-08-04 export: ambiguity blocking at three seams (RS-589), segment containment and canonical Roman validation (RS-590/591/593), corroborated fragment recovery. Quantify the improvement rather than asserting it - if the shipped catalogue is materially as good, deferring is the right call and costs nothing.

Do NOT overwrite the deployed file. v2's exporter requires an explicit --output and refuses to overwrite an existing file; that guard is deliberate and stays.

This is Tom's call, not an AI one: it trades a known-good deployed catalogue against improvements whose size is not yet measured.

nodes.body: acceptance_probe.py reports a rule-1 violation - a bare count used as a target, unmet because the work has not been done - with the same DRIFTED verdict and the same 'no longer true' wording it uses for a sighting that has genuinely rotted.
nodes.done_looks_like:
The probe separates an acceptance that quotes a STALE FACT from one that states a GOAL not yet reached, and only the first is called drift.

READ tools/game-database-v2/docs/ACCEPTANCE_CONVENTION.md FIRST. It already draws the line this item is about, and the correction below was made after re-reading it - an earlier draft of this item claimed the convention was silent, which is wrong and would have sent someone to invent a rule that exists.

Rule 1 is "An acceptance states invariants. It never states a bare count as a target." Rule 5 adds that if you do write a floor, the parenthetical beside it is a sighting and belongs in the body. The doc's outcome table defines DRIFTED as "the comparison fails - the acceptance asks for something untrue".

So the probe is not simply broken. It is conflating two failures that need different responses:

(1) A recorded SIGHTING no longer matches reality. Response: re-measure, and consider whether the defect changed shape. This is the case the doc's RS-304 example is about and it must keep its DRIFTED verdict.

(2) The acceptance states a bare count as a TARGET, in violation of rule 1, and the target is not met because the work has not been done. Response: rewrite the acceptance as an invariant. Calling this "1 acceptance figure(s) no longer true" is wrong - it was never true and is not meant to be until the work lands.

Both examples are reproducible 2026-08-20 and both are also rule-1 violations, so fixing them is part of this item:

RS-183 records "returns >= 1,200 (12 today)". Current is 12, so the SIGHTING is exactly right, and the probe still prints "*DRIFTED RECORDED >=1,200 of 12 CURRENT 12" with the verdict "no longer true". After this item, correcting a sighting to match reality must silence the drift verdict for that figure.

RS-160 asserts that after the fix, COUNT(*) WHERE id_type='xbox_title_id' returns 0. It returns 2,743, which IS the defect, present and correct for a ready item.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING. CLAUDE.md instructs re-measuring an item's figures before building it and points at this script. A reader following the verdict on RS-160 would "correct" the recorded 0 to 2,743 - rewriting a target into a description of the bug, leaving an acceptance that its own defect satisfies. And because every un-started item carrying a numeric target reports DRIFTED, the verdict trains readers to ignore it, which costs the genuine case (1) its signal.

A rule-1 violation deserves its own outcome alongside HOLDS/DRIFTED/STALE/BROKEN/SKIPPED, naming the rule, rather than being folded into drift.

Test both shapes: an item whose sighting matches current reports no drift for that figure even when its target is far off; an item whose sighting has genuinely moved still reports DRIFTED. The first fails today.

Note the probe already reports honestly that it extracts only 68% of probe-shaped spans and prefers missing one to inventing one. Do not weaken that - a fabricated CURRENT reads as a passing check.
nodes.title: The acceptance probe cannot tell a stale fact from a goal not yet reached
nodes.why: Found 2026-08-20 while re-probing RS-183 before dispatch: after correcting its sighting from 11 to 12 so it matched current exactly, the probe still called that figure no longer true. Re-reading ACCEPTANCE_CONVENTION.md then showed the convention already forbids counts as targets, which reframed the item.

nodes.body: RS-596 measured the two resolvable classes: an exact publisher tiebreak makes 190 blocked decisions unique across the three seams, and a strict numeral-plus-year rule makes another 7. Both need a guard distinguishing positive agreement from an opponent that merely has no data.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Publisher and numeral+year are used as evidence at the seam that can act on them, each with a guard proving the evidence is POSITIVE rather than merely unopposed.

All figures below were measured 2026-08-20 by the RS-596 research pass against live generations (IGDB 99, normalize 101, match 102, releases 103, works 105, release-work 106). They are sightings. Re-measure at dispatch.

=== PUBLISHER: ceiling 190, honest number lower ===

Coverage is 148,602 of 164,696 game_metadata rows (90.23%). An exact normalized-publisher tiebreak mechanically makes 190 decisions unique: stage 30 six pairs, stage 40 fifty-six attachments, stage 55 one hundred and twenty-eight links. Nine Tetris links resolve, including the NES Nintendo/Tengen pair that motivated this.

THE CEILING IS NOT THE ANSWER. Only 69 of the 128 stage-55 wins have publisher data on EVERY competing work; the other 59 win partly because a rival lacks metadata. Absence is not disagreement, and a rule that treats it as disagreement will confidently pick a loser whose only fault is a gap in IGDB.

The demonstrated counterexample must be a test: the 2007 Windows Resident Evil 4 release, where Ubisoft uniquely selects BASE work 974 because IGDB records Ubisoft there and omits it from expanded work 145191 - even though 145191 is the specific PS2/PC edition the release actually is. The rule picks the wrong work, confidently, on complete-looking evidence.

So require positive evidence from all contenders, and evaluate against related-edition families (game_type/parent_game, version_parent) rather than treating them as unrelated rivals. Report the recovery under the guard, not the ceiling - if it lands near 69 rather than 128, that is the true figure and it is still worth having.

Note the ROM scanner shipped this same idea for Amiga (RS-592) and reasoned about the identical hazard in a comment at matcher.rs:1659 - "a correct candidate with no publisher is filtered out while a wrong candidate whose recorded publisher agrees can win uncontested". It judged the risk narrow at 90% coverage and accepted it. At stage 55 the absence-driven fraction is 59/128, which is not narrow, so do NOT simply mirror the scanner's trade-off here.

=== NUMERAL + YEAR: 7 recoveries, all clean ===

The strict rule - one contender uniquely agrees with both the numeral signature and the exact year, and the numeral actually discriminates - recovers 4 stage-30 pairs and 3 stage-40 attachments. Stage 55 recovers zero because it already applies its strongest year discrimination before declaring ambiguity.

The four stage-30 recoveries are Muscle Bomber (1993, no numeral, selects Saturday Night Slam Masters over 1994's Ring of Destruction: Slam Masters II) and three Game Boy Gallery 3 rows selecting Game & Watch Gallery 3. The TOSEC Australia row stays blocked because it records 1998, so its numeral says 3 while its year favours Gallery 2 - REFUSAL ON CONFLICTING EVIDENCE IS CORRECT AND MUST STAY. Pin it.

=== WHERE THESE GO ===

Both belong in stage-30 matching evidence and scoring. Neither belongs in works construction. Stage 40 should keep consuming its stored pair score rather than growing a separate publisher heuristic, so a stage-40 improvement must come from changing stage-30 evidence.

Do NOT rebuild the v2 database. Report how many decisions each rule changes at each seam, and judge changed decisions individually rather than counting them.
