nodes.body: The trailing four digits in a Retroplay .lha name are an SPS/IPF disk-image id, and LaunchBox Files.xml already carries the crosswalk locally: 1,449 distinct ids, 1,144 of them linked uniquely to a release. Used to intersect the candidate set rather than to assert identity, it resolves 25 of the 39 Amiga ambiguities still live after RS-592.
nodes.done_looks_like:
The Amiga matcher intersects its candidate set with the release an SPS/IPF disk-image ID identifies, and declines cleanly whenever that ID is absent, unknown, or maps to more than one release.

READ THE RS-594 ARTIFACT FIRST. Every figure here is a 2026-08-20 sighting - re-measure at dispatch.

=== IT IS NOT A WHDLOAD ID ===

The trailing four digits in AfterBurner_v1.0_Activision_0095.lha are an SPS/IPF DISK-IMAGE id, not a WHDLoad install id. That distinction is the whole basis of the rule: it identifies the source disk image the archive was built from, which is why it crosswalks to a release at all.

=== THE CROSSWALK IS ALREADY LOCAL - DO NOT FETCH ANYTHING ===

No new source is needed and none should be acquired. LaunchBox Files.xml already carries the Retroplay filenames, and the v2 database has them in stg_launchbox_files: 2,716 staged Amiga filename rows, 1,687 carrying an ID suffix, 1,449 distinct IDs, of which 1,150 link to releases - 1,144 uniquely and 6 to multiple. The three worked examples 0095, 0611 and 0156 already resolve to After Burner, Barbarian II and Turbo Trax.

The public Retroplay WHDLoad Database on GitHub is the upstream of the same data and is NOT required for this work. whdload.de's install list carries no structured SPS field at all.

=== THE SAFETY RULE IS THE ITEM ===

AN SPS ID IS NOT A PRIMARY KEY. An archive can acquire a different suffix when a newer package is built from a different source disk image - Barbarian II records SPS 0110 for v1.0 while the local v1.1 archive uses 0611. It is durable EVIDENCE, not identity.

Therefore: INTERSECT the existing candidate set with what the ID points at. Never treat an ID as an unconditional match, never let it add a candidate the name tiers did not produce, and never let it override an unambiguous match. Where the ID maps to several releases (6 of 1,150), or to none, the existing refusal stands unchanged. Each of those three refusals is a test, and each needs a positive control showing the rule WOULD have fired otherwise.

This is the same shape as the publisher tie-break (RS-592) and should sit beside it, not replace it: publisher reaches only 24 of 1,490 archives, this reaches far more.

=== EXPECTED YIELD ===

| Scope | Total | Carry an ID | Unique ID to a current release |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Current directory | 1,490 .lha | 943 | 757 |
| Still ambiguous after RS-592 | 39 | 26 | 25 |

So the target is 25 of the 39 live ambiguities. Note the original ledger of 43 has already drifted to 39 because RS-592 resolved four. Pure ID linkage (757) is the safer figure than exact full-filename linkage (762) - prefer it.

The one ID-bearing case that must still refuse is BlockOut_v1.2_0208.lha: the source row exists but the catalogue holds two Block Out releases and cannot safely choose. Pin it.

=== SCOPE ===

Report every changed identity individually, not as a count. No file may change from one game to a DIFFERENT game. Do not modify config/systems_manifest.tsv. Do not rebuild the v2 database - if the crosswalk needs to reach the scanner, state how it should be exported rather than reading the 10.9GB master at scan time.
nodes.title: SPS disk-image IDs in Amiga filenames resolve 25 of the 39 live ambiguities
nodes.why: RS-594 established the crosswalk exists and is already on disk, and corrected the identifier's nature: it is an SPS disk-image id, not a WHDLoad install id, and it can change between archive versions - so it is evidence, never a key.

nodes.body: 183 unattached ps2 serials name 69 distinct catalogue games that carry no serial at all - small enough to finish by hand, and the right first population for RS-210's review surface because the verdict-survives-rebuild property can actually be proven on it.
nodes.done_looks_like:
A human can adjudicate the serials automated matching refuses, and their verdicts survive a pipeline rebuild.

This is RS-210's first real population. Read RS-210's acceptance before designing - it already states the hard parts: exceptions clustered BY CAUSE rather than enumerated, an AI proposal that records the source values it saw, multi-hit cases refused rather than picked, and THE CORE TEST, that a recorded verdict survives an end-to-end re-run. A queue whose answers are thrown away by the next rebuild is worse than no queue, because someone will have spent an evening on it.

=== THE FIRST POPULATION: 69 GAMES ===

Sighting 2026-08-20, re-measure at dispatch. Of 3,458 unattached ps2 serials, 183 name a ps2 game that IS in the catalogue and has NO serial at all - 69 distinct games, median 2 serials each. Ape Escape 2 (9 serials, currently zero attached), Alone in the Dark (5), Area 51 (5), Arcana Heart, Clannad, Bomberman Jetters.

This population is chosen deliberately: small enough to finish in one sitting, real enough to prove the verdict-survives-rebuild property, and each decision is a genuine judgement rather than a mechanical one.

Do NOT widen it. The other two buckets have their own items: regional cross-linking is RS-606 and is mechanical, and the titles absent from the catalogue are a completeness problem, not a matching one.

=== THE INPUT ALREADY EXISTS ===

Do not build exception generation. The seams already refuse and record why: RS-589 taught stages 30, 40 and 55 to withhold tied links rather than pick the lowest id, and the stage-30 structural ladder records a terminal refusal with its rung. The queue's job is to surface what is already being written down.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

A verdict recorded against a cluster is still in force after a full pipeline re-run, and the count reconciles exactly. That is the test that matters; everything else is presentation.

An AI proposal shows the source values it saw - the DAT title, the serial, the candidate releases and why each was or was not chosen - so a human is checking evidence rather than trusting a verdict.

Where a serial could belong to several releases, the surface REFUSES and says so. It must not present a guess as a proposal.

Report how many of the 69 a human actually resolved and how long it took. If the answer is that most were obvious, that is a finding: it means the automated rule was too conservative and the right fix is upstream, not a queue.
nodes.title: Adjudicate the 69 PS2 games automated matching refuses, and make the verdicts stick
nodes.why: Tom proposed accepting a manual work queue 2026-08-20. Measuring it showed the genuinely manual part is far smaller than the 3,458 headline: most of the rest is mechanical regional cross-linking (RS-606) or titles the catalogue does not hold.

nodes.body: After serial-string normalisation the real ps2 gap is 1,919 serials across 1,310 titles, of which only 8 share a normalized title with any mapped candidate. These are not matching failures - there is no game record to attach a serial to.
nodes.done_looks_like:
It is established whether the titles in the ROM DATs that the catalogue does not hold are genuinely absent from LaunchBox, or present under a name nothing has connected - and the answer is acted on or explicitly declined.

=== THIS IS NOT A MATCHING PROBLEM ===

An independent review established it 2026-08-20 and the framing matters: after normalising serial strings, the real ps2 gap is 1,919 serials across 1,310 normalized titles, and only EIGHT of those share a normalized title with any mapped candidate. No amount of loosening the matcher reaches the rest. Two attempts to explain the gap as matching failures have now been wrong - do not make a third.

Re-measure at dispatch; these are sightings.

=== THE QUESTION ===

For a sample of 40 of the 1,310, determine which of these each one is:

(1) genuinely absent from LaunchBox, so nothing can attach a serial because there is no game record to attach it to;
(2) present in LaunchBox under a materially different name - a Japanese title against its Western release, a subtitle difference, a transliteration - which is a catalogue-linking question, not a fuzzy-matching one;
(3) not a distinct release at all - a demo, a sampler, a coverdisc, a bad DAT entry.

The sample suggested many are Japanese releases. Test that rather than assuming it: report the split by region and by source DAT.

=== WHAT TO DO WITH THE ANSWER ===

If (1) dominates, the honest conclusion is that the catalogue's coverage is bounded by LaunchBox's, and the options are to accept it, to add a source that carries those titles, or to mint releases from the DAT itself. Say which you recommend and why - minting releases from a ROM DAT changes what a release MEANS in this model, so it is a real decision, not a cleanup.

If (2) dominates, that is a cross-source linking problem and belongs with the alias work, not here.

Do NOT build a fix in this item. Establish the shape, report it, and let the decision be taken with the numbers in hand.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===

Do not rebuild the v2 database or run a full pipeline stage. Open databases with file:...?immutable=1 and filter in SQL - a review process was killed loading a whole result set from the 10.9GB file.
nodes.title: 1,310 ps2 DAT titles have no catalogue game at all, and no matcher will ever reach them
nodes.why: Two explanations of the unattached-serial gap have already been wrong, both mine: first that it was mostly regional variants, then that a looser ladder would reach it. An independent review refuted both, which leaves catalogue coverage as the actual question.

nodes.body: Sampling 40 of the 1,310 unattached ps2 titles: 28 are existing releases under localized, transliterated or subtitle-expanded names, 10 are not releases at all, and only 2 are genuinely absent. Blind DAT minting would create a duplicate or non-game entry for 38 of 40.
nodes.done_looks_like:
Localized, transliterated and subtitle-expanded source titles link to the LaunchBox release they already are, carrying the evidence for the link - and demos, magazine discs, trailers and utilities are excluded from becoming releases at all.

=== WHY THIS SHAPE, AND NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE ===

RS-608 sampled 40 of the 1,310 unattached ps2 titles. The result rules out minting releases from ROM DATs: doing that blindly would create a duplicate or a non-game entry for 38 OF THE 40.

  2/40   genuinely absent from LaunchBox
  28/40  present under a materially different name
  10/40  not distinct releases at all - magazine and cover discs, demos, a trailer, a setup utility

Worked examples of the 28, each a real release we already hold:
  Prince of Persia: Futatsu no Tamashii  ->  Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones
  Jin Samguk Mussang                     ->  Dynasty Warriors 2
  Sakura Daejeon V                       ->  Sakura Wars: So Long, My Love
  Suwanggi: Project Altered Beast        ->  Altered Beast
  Serie de Catastroficas Desdichas...    ->  Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events
  Petit Copter                           ->  Go Go Copter: Remote Control Helicopter

Only four of the 28 are mere spelling or punctuation differences. The other 24 are substantive localization, subtitle or transliteration links that no normalisation rung will ever reach - which is why this is NOT another fuzzy-matching item. Two attempts to explain this gap as a matching failure have already been refuted; do not make a third.

=== THE REGIONAL READ WAS ALSO WRONG ===

Japan-only titles are 19 of 40 - the largest block but not a majority, and Japan plus Korea is 22. More to the point, 13 of those 19 ALREADY have a LaunchBox counterpart under a Western name. The population is mostly games we hold, not games we lack.

=== SCOPE ===

Build explicit, provenance-carrying equivalence: a localized title and its serial link to an existing release, and the link RECORDS what justified it. A link a human cannot audit is worth little here, because the failure mode is a confident wrong equivalence.

Exclude the non-release class explicitly. Magazine and cover discs, demos, trailers and utilities must not become releases; Redump and the PCSX2 demo/tool lists already mark many of them, so establish whether that marking is usable rather than writing a title-pattern heuristic.

Serial corroboration is the strongest available evidence and several of the 28 were confirmed that way - a candidate whose serial already resolves to a release is strong evidence the titles are the same game. Prefer it over name similarity, and say what you do when the two disagree.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

Re-measure first; all figures are 2026-08-20 sightings. Source-vs-catalogue missing rates: psp 3,601 of 5,524 (65.2%, the worst by far), xbox 200 of 625 (32.0%), psx 1,849 of 10,585 (17.5%), ps2 1,919 of 11,629 (16.5%), ps3 748 of 5,186 (14.4%).

Report links made, links refused, and non-releases excluded, per platform. Judge every link individually in a sample of 30 - a wrong equivalence merges two real games and is worse than leaving both unlinked.

Do NOT mint releases from a DAT. That changes what a release MEANS in this model, from a catalogued game release to a dumped-disc record, and it is a product decision that has not been taken.

=== THE ALIAS MUST FEED BACK INTO THE DATABASE ===

Tom 2026-08-20: alias data we discover should feed the aliases in the db too. This is not
an add-on - it is what turns a one-off link into something both consumers learn from
permanently, and it is cheap because the table already exists and already ships.

game_names REACHES THE SCANNER. matcher.rs:1485 builds its name cache from games plus
game_names plus game_filenames, so an alias written here immediately improves FILE
matching, not just the pipeline internal link. A user whose disc is named after the
localized title gets a match that no normalisation rung would ever have produced.

The table is HALF POPULATED, and the missing half is precisely the transliterated forms
the DATs use. Measured 2026-08-20:

  Dynasty Warriors 2   has Shin Sangoku Musou            MISSING Jin Samguk Mussang
  Altered Beast        has the Hangul title in script    MISSING its romanisation Suwanggi
  Prince of Persia     has Prince of Persia I Due Troni  MISSING Futatsu no Tamashii

Altered Beast is the sharpest case: the catalogue holds the Korean title in Hangul while
the DAT writes the same name romanised, so the knowledge is present in a form nothing can
join on.

Coverage: 89,971 of 164,696 games carry any alias at all (54.6%); 74,725 have none.

RECORD THE PROVENANCE. name_type currently holds the single value alternate on all 297,360
rows, so the column exists and says nothing. An alias asserted by this work must be
distinguishable from one that came from a source, or the next person cannot tell a
derived equivalence from an attested name - and cannot revisit ours if the rule is later
found wrong.

An alias is only written where the link itself was accepted. A refused or ambiguous link
must NOT deposit an alias, or a wrong equivalence becomes permanent and self-reinforcing:
the bad alias would then justify the bad link on the next run.

Report how many aliases are added, and how many files in the real archive match through a
newly added alias that did not match before. That second number is the user-visible
benefit.

nodes.body: Tom, 2026-08-25: before any import, a proper analysis of how RetroStack would actually use these — archive structure per collection, the launcher mechanism (LaunchBox XML ApplicationPath → per-game .bat → DOSBox with the config in !DOSmetadata.zip; whatever eXoWin3x/9x do), whether each game is self-contained or depends on a shared machine image (CC Reloaded Win98 = content zip + FAT32 .sav differential + shared Windows 98 SE image), which bits a client copies, what runtime is needed on macOS/Windows (Win9x-era games do not run natively on modern Windows), and what the catalogue needs (LaunchBox's 'Windows 3.X' platform, 1,235 games, is ingested and dropped because the manifest has no windows3x system; 'windows9x' maps to nothing; eXoDOS holds ~1,450 DOS games LaunchBox lacks plus the 7,745 DOSBox configs and 10 curated playlists). Measurements from 2026-08-25 are in the artifact.
nodes.done_looks_like: An analysis artifact on this item, grounded in the share and the tools (no guesses), that answers for EACH of eXoDOS, eXoWin3x, eXoWin9x and the CC Reloaded Windows 98 set: (1) the archive structure and the exact identity key (measured: zip stem = launcher basename for eXoDOS, 7,666/7,666); (2) the launcher mechanism — what Setup installs, what the per-game .bat/.conf require (which DOSBox/ScummVM/machine emulator), and whether a game is self-contained or depends on a shared image (the Win98 set is content zip + FAT32 .sav differential + shared Windows 98 SE image); (3) what a RetroStack client copies for one game and what runtime it needs on macOS and on Windows, with the Win9x-era native-launch problem stated plainly and the candidate runtimes named; (4) what the catalogue needs first — the LaunchBox 'Windows 3.X' mapping (1,235 games dropped today), what windows9x means, and whether eXo is ingested as a source for the ~1,450 DOS games, configs, playlists, aliases and media; (5) the scanner profile each shape needs. Ends with a recommended order of work as candidate items (not created), each with its measured size, and names what it could not establish without running a game.
nodes.title: Deep dive: importing and launching the eXo collections (eXoDOS, eXoWin3x, eXoWin9x) and the CC Reloaded Windows 98 set
nodes.why: These collections are ~10,000 games on the share that RS-630 defers; the metadata question (eXo vs LaunchBox) was measured 2026-08-25 — descriptive fields are the same, the launch/curation data is unique — but nobody has established how a game from any of them becomes a launchable row on a client.

nodes.body: Pure-first product-v2 plan: prove representative eXoDOS packages, integrate DOSBox Pure, classify the corpora and treat Windows/specialist shapes as evidence-gated candidates or explicit deferrals.
nodes.done_looks_like: Five observable outcomes are evidenced: (1) at least two ordinary eXoDOS configuration families pass Tom-approved intended-gameplay, media, music/effects, input/flow, clean-exit and second-launch-state checks from immutable .dosz packages while source hashes remain unchanged; (2) product-v2 loopback and enrolled-client paths provision RetroArch plus dosbox_pure, reconcile stable-id packages and per-content options, preflight audio/BIOS dependencies and sync Pure writable state without treating it as immutable payload; (3) every current eXoDOS game and every recorded eXoWin3x/eXoWin9x source row appears exactly once as pure_validated, pure_structural_candidate, pure_deferred or pure_unsupported, with unclassified = 0 and a reason for every non-candidate; (4) Windows 3.x directory/boot-image and Windows 9x parent/difference probes publish PASS, FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN without requiring fallback runner implementation; (5) dated commands, hashes, reports, approved human receipts and product-v2 regression results are indexed from the parent log, with no unapproved launch and no source/live-instance mutation.
nodes.title: Import eXo collections through RetroArch DOSBox Pure first
nodes.why: RetroStack needs one controller-friendly RetroArch route that can package supported eXo games safely without making near-total compatibility or fallback runners a phase-one requirement.

nodes.body: Turn the parked archive inventory prototype into accepted dated source evidence for eXoDOS, eXoWin3x and eXoWin9x after the representative Pure recipe is proven.
nodes.done_looks_like: Starting from isolated commit 484f30748f69511bf749a72f143e7e0ad1fca334 or an equivalent clean implementation, tests reproduce and fix the independent verifier’s control-file cross-association, referrer-relative resolution, normalized Unicode/case collision, SET/%VAR% dependency, source-changed-during-verify and malformed-estimate failures; symlink escape and case-insensitive ZIP extension policy are explicit; two current-source runs emit byte-identical canonical JSON/TSV and a Markdown report enumerating every eXoDOS, eXoWin3x and eXoWin9x game and joining launch-relevant configs, scripts, runtimes, updates, shared assets and guest/machine images; totals reconcile per collection; source roots, versions, sizes, hashes, commands and bounded nested-archive estimates are recorded; source and live-instance hashes remain unchanged; no archive is extracted and no emulator/game process starts; a fresh verifier returns PASS and the artifacts are indexed from the parent log.
nodes.title: Pure corpus — repair and freeze the three eXo source inventories
nodes.why: Corpus classification needs exact source closure, but the isolated prototype’s join, relative-path, Unicode, BAT-variable and source-consistency failures must be fixed before its output is evidence.

nodes.body: Define and implement the product-v2 schema connecting content units, game launch intent, shared dependencies and immutable-seed/writable-state policies through manifest compatibility.
nodes.done_looks_like: The normalized launch-profile schema and at least one concrete example per collection are implemented and documented; any database migration is schema-only; manifest compatibility is versioned with round-trip tests, legacy-default behavior and explicit refusal of unsupported newer versions; profiles name payload roles, shared dependencies, host runner, arguments, prerequisite checks, immutable seeds and writable-state policy; all current manifest, reconcile and runner tests pass.
nodes.title: eXo foundation — versioned launch profile, dependency and state contract
nodes.why: DOS, Win3x and Win9x adapters must consume one versioned contract or each branch will invent incompatible packaging and state semantics.

nodes.body: Build the shared nested-archive inventory and isolated extraction engine with path and collision checks, atomic progress, exact eXo update ordering, provenance and content-addressed shared dependencies.
nodes.done_looks_like: One fixture from each collection materializes twice to byte-identical immutable content; nested archives and update overlays apply in declared order; traversal, symlink escape, case-fold collision and duplicate-target inputs are rejected; an interrupted extraction resumes or rolls back atomically after a free-space preflight; shared dependencies deduplicate by content; recorded source hashes remain unchanged; automated tests cover every invariant.
nodes.title: eXo foundation — safe resumable archive materializer
nodes.why: Users should not run eXo setup or manually unpack collections, and interruption or malicious archive paths must not corrupt source or client state.

nodes.body: Persist imported eXo content units/profiles, emit them in collection versions, reconcile their complete closure and make the runner compose or explicitly refuse the declared native launch path.
nodes.done_looks_like: Imported eXo records persist their content units and launch profiles; saved collection manifests carry the complete payload/dependency closure; reconcile transfers each required member exactly once; loopback and enrolled-client preflight either compose the declared launch plan or identify the exact missing prerequisite; the existing blanket PC refusal is removed only for valid profiles; legacy non-PC manifest, reconcile and runner tests still pass.
nodes.title: eXo foundation — connect known collections to manifest, reconcile and launch preflight
nodes.why: A standalone materializer is not product support until the live product-v2 library-to-device path carries and enforces its results.

nodes.body: Independent evidence gate for the shared source, contract, materializer and product-v2 integration foundation.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS only when the corpus snapshot is dated and hash-grounded; one fixture from each eXo collection materializes twice to byte-equivalent immutable content; traversal, collision, interruption, idempotence and update-order tests pass; manifest schema compatibility and explicit refusal tests pass; source hashes are unchanged; and the parent validation log links every command and evidence artifact.
nodes.title: Gate 1 — eXo package foundation evidence review
nodes.why: DOS and Windows runner work must not build on an undocumented or state-unsafe package contract.

nodes.body: Parse dosbox.txt, every config variant, BAT command and exception launcher into normalized launch profiles, with a machine-readable signature/unsupported report and no ignored construct.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every config referenced by the frozen eXoDOS index, every BAT command, dosbox.txt row, exception launcher and runtime selector yields exactly one normalized profile or one explicit unsupported record; totals reconcile with no ignored line or unknown token hidden; cycles=auto, MIDI-device and known Staging/ECE translations have fixtures; output ordering and hashes are deterministic; unknown constructs report the exact source path, line and token.
nodes.title: eXoDOS — translate and classify the complete config and launcher corpus
nodes.why: The runner adapter can only be trusted for source semantics the importer has explicitly recognized and routed.

nodes.body: Add native macOS, Windows and Linux DOSBox Staging provisioning/launch templates, translated config generation, shared SoundFont/MT-32 prerequisite resolution and device-local writable DOS state.
nodes.done_looks_like: A pinned standalone DOSBox Staging route is provisioned idempotently for macOS, Windows and Linux or the host is explicitly refused with a reason; generated config derives only from the normalized profile; SoundFont and MT-32 dependencies are resolved or named precisely; NE2000/networking remains disabled unless declared; all writes are confined to device-local state; fixture launch-plan and provisioning tests pass without changing source or immutable seed hashes.
nodes.title: eXoDOS — provision and launch standalone DOSBox Staging
nodes.why: Ordinary eXoDOS profiles need one reproducible standalone runner path that uses the product-v2 manifest and never writes into the source or immutable seed.

nodes.body: Generate deterministic fixtures for classic, ECE, Staging-native and specialist classes; exercise materialization, launch-plan composition, runtime logs, media/audio initialization, controlled exit and post-run state hashes.
nodes.done_looks_like: Fixtures cover classic DOSBox, evidenced ECE translation, Staging-native and specialist/unsupported families; Jazz Jackrabbit, DOOM and Tyrian regressions exercise materialization and launch composition; evidence records command, effective config, runtime log, media/audio initialization, controlled exit and before/after state hashes; the full frozen corpus passes structural routing; repeating the suite produces the same classification and evidence index.
nodes.title: eXoDOS — structural smoke suite and representative family evidence
nodes.why: The collection needs repeatable family evidence and full structural coverage without relying on a person to play thousands of titles.

nodes.body: With each launch explicitly approved, perform the bounded human checks for intended gameplay, continuous music/effects, input/flow and clean in-game exit on the representative DOS family matrix.
nodes.done_looks_like: For every predeclared representative launch that Tom explicitly approves, the receipt records intended program/gameplay, continuous music and effects, usable input/flow and in-game clean exit as PASS, FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN; no unapproved game is launched, no title-specific tuning is introduced, and the dated receipt is linked from the parent validation log.
nodes.title: eXoDOS — confirm representative perceptual equivalence
nodes.why: Audio quality and behavior equivalence cannot be established from logs or frames alone, but only a bounded family sample needs human observation.

nodes.body: Independent evidence gate for ordinary and specialist native DOS routing.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS only when every current eXoDOS game routes to an ordinary validated family or a named specialist, structural_only or unsupported class; representative classic, ECE and Staging-native probes have machine evidence plus Tom's bounded perceptual receipt; shared MIDI/firmware and writable-state checks pass; macOS is demonstrated; Windows and Linux provisioning routes or explicit refusals are documented; and the rolling parent log links the dated corpus report and commands.
nodes.title: Gate 2 — native eXoDOS family support review
nodes.why: Windows-family work may reuse DOSBox parsing only after the DOS translation and evidence boundary is explicit.

nodes.body: Re-measure every directory/boot-image, runtime/config and multimedia signature, then run bounded reversible probes to recommend standalone Staging, DOSBox-X or a declared specialist route per family.
nodes.done_looks_like: A dated matrix classifies every frozen eXoWin3x game by directory/boot-image shape, runtime/config signature and multimedia needs; bounded reversible probes compare plausible native runners; each family receives one evidence-backed runner recommendation or an explicit specialist/unsupported outcome; source totals reconcile and all probe commands, versions, hashes and observations are linked from the parent log.
nodes.title: eXoWin3x — classify families and select native runner mappings
nodes.why: The dominant source assignment is a Windows-only ECE build, and choosing a cross-platform replacement without evidence would hard-code an unproven architecture.

nodes.body: Implement the family mappings selected by the probe through the shared launch profile, including config translation, directory/boot-image mounts, client provisioning and isolated persistent state on macOS, Windows and Linux.
nodes.done_looks_like: The selected family mappings are implemented through normalized launch profiles for both directory and boot-image payloads; native runner provisioning succeeds idempotently on macOS, Windows and Linux or refuses an unsupported host explicitly; generated mounts/configs match the profile; persistent writes stay device-local; fixtures prove launch-plan composition and missing-prerequisite refusal; relevant product-v2 regression tests pass.
nodes.title: eXoWin3x — implement selected standalone adapters and writable state
nodes.why: Family research must become a repeatable product-v2 launch path rather than a standalone test-lab recipe.

nodes.body: Exercise directory and boot-image fixtures through materialization and composed native launch plans, capturing Windows startup, mounted media, MIDI/WAV initialization, controlled exit and post-run state boundaries.
nodes.done_looks_like: Representative evidence includes at least one directory and one boot-image family and captures Windows startup, intended executable, optical media, MIDI/WAV initialization, controlled exit and immutable-versus-writable state hashes; all frozen Win3x rows pass structural routing; repeated runs produce deterministic reports; commands and outputs are linked from the parent log.
nodes.title: eXoWin3x — structural smoke suite and representative multimedia evidence
nodes.why: Windows 3.x support needs repeatable evidence across both payload shapes before the whole family is routed.

nodes.body: With each launch explicitly approved, confirm intended Windows/game flow, mounted-CD behavior, MIDI/WAV audio, input and clean exit for the bounded directory and boot-image representative set.
nodes.done_looks_like: For every predeclared Win3x launch that Tom explicitly approves, the receipt records intended Windows/game flow, mounted-CD behavior, MIDI/WAV audio, input and clean exit as PASS, FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN; no unapproved game is launched, no title-specific tuning is introduced, and the dated receipt is linked from the parent validation log.
nodes.title: eXoWin3x — confirm representative perceptual equivalence
nodes.why: Machine evidence cannot by itself establish multimedia and gameplay equivalence, but human work remains bounded to the material family sample.

nodes.body: Independent evidence gate for Windows 3.x native runner selection and family support.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS only when all current eXoWin3x records route by measured directory/boot-image and runtime/config signature; the selected native mapping is supported by documented probes; representative directory and boot-image games have machine evidence plus Tom's bounded multimedia/gameplay receipt; state remains device-local; macOS is demonstrated; Windows and Linux routes or explicit refusals are documented; and the rolling parent log links the dated report and commands.
nodes.title: Gate 3 — native eXoWin3x family support review
nodes.why: Windows 3.x must close with an evidence-backed mapping rather than an assumed DOSBox-family conversion.

nodes.body: Re-measure every DOSBox-X parent family, play.conf image/CD/network/locale signature and 86Box Windows 98/ME machine profile, recording user-supplied OS, ROM-set and host-network prerequisites.
nodes.done_looks_like: A dated machine-readable report maps every frozen eXoWin9x game to its DOSBox-X parent or 86Box Windows 98/ME machine profile and records image/CD sets, network, locale, tuned CPU/output and all OS/ROM/host prerequisites; parent and image hashes are recorded; totals reconcile to the frozen source snapshot; no referenced config or source launcher is silently ignored.
nodes.title: eXoWin9x — freeze parent, machine-profile and prerequisite families
nodes.why: Layered state and runner adapters need an exact current parent/machine graph and cannot infer missing licensed or hardware assets at launch time.

nodes.body: Implement content-addressed guest parents, atomic child creation/recovery, per-game disk/config state, persistent versus ephemeral policies, backup/restore and manifest-safe separation of immutable and mutable files.
nodes.done_looks_like: Guest parents are content-addressed and verified immutable; child disk/config creation, interruption recovery and replacement are atomic; persistent and ephemeral policies are tested; backup and restore reproduce the prior child hash; a simulated crash cannot corrupt or promote a child into a parent; reconcile verification excludes declared mutable paths but validates every immutable member; traversal and collision tests pass; source and parent hashes never change.
nodes.title: eXoWin9x — immutable parent and writable child state service
nodes.why: Both DOSBox-X and 86Box can corrupt or erase user state if parent, child and per-game disks are treated as ordinary reconciled payloads.

nodes.body: Translate play.conf plus shared options into native DOSBox-X launch plans for every measured parent family, CD set, tuned CPU/output, locale and declared network capability, with client provisioning on three host operating systems.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every measured DOSBox-X parent family translates into a normalized launch plan including images, CD sets, tuned CPU/output, locale and declared network state; a pinned native DOSBox-X route provisions on macOS, Windows and Linux or refuses the host explicitly; networking is opt-in and never installs Npcap silently; fixture tests cover ordinary, tuned, locale, multi-CD and network-declared profiles with device-local child state.
nodes.title: eXoWin9x — standalone DOSBox-X adapter for parent-image families
nodes.why: The dominant Windows 9x population needs a native adapter over the shared state service rather than a reproduced Windows BAT chain.

nodes.body: Provision native 86Box, validate required machine ROMs, materialize the declared Windows 98/ME child disks and per-game machine configs, mount optical media and keep machine/game state inside the instance.
nodes.done_looks_like: Measured Windows 98 and ME machine profiles translate into normalized 86Box launch plans; native 86Box provisioning and exact machine-ROM preflight are implemented for macOS, Windows and Linux or explicitly refused; child disk, machine config and optical media are assembled without writing parents; missing licensed OS images or ROM assets produce precise actionable refusals; fixture and state-isolation tests pass.
nodes.title: eXoWin9x — standalone 86Box adapter for Windows 98 and ME machines
nodes.why: The full-machine tail declares hardware and OS profiles that cannot be treated as DOSBox-X config variants or silently migrated to another emulator.

nodes.body: Exercise fresh and second launches across ordinary, network, locale, tuned, 86Box Windows 98 and 86Box Windows ME fixtures, capturing parent/child hashes, CD mounts, state changes, crash recovery and controlled exit.
nodes.done_looks_like: Fresh and second launches cover ordinary DOSBox-X, tuned, locale, network-declared, 86Box Windows 98 and 86Box Windows ME fixtures; evidence records launch/exit logs, mounted media, crash recovery and before/after parent/child hashes; parents remain byte-identical while persistent or ephemeral state behaves exactly as declared; the frozen Win9x corpus passes structural routing and the repeatable report is linked from the parent log.
nodes.title: eXoWin9x — layered-image smoke suite and representative machine evidence
nodes.why: Image-backed support needs repeatable proof that shared parents remain immutable and each game's writes survive or reset exactly according to policy.

nodes.body: Run only the bounded approved Win9x matrix and record intended desktop/game flow, audio, input, controlled exit and second-launch persistence against the translated native routes.
nodes.done_looks_like: For every predeclared Win9x launch that Tom explicitly approves, the receipt records intended desktop/game flow, CD and music/effects behavior, usable input, controlled exit and expected save/state after a second launch as PASS, FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN; no unapproved game is launched, no title-specific tuning is introduced, and the dated receipt is linked from the parent validation log.
nodes.title: eXoWin9x — confirm representative perceptual and persistence behavior
nodes.why: Automated image and process evidence cannot establish that the intended Windows program, audio and interaction are perceptually correct.

nodes.body: Review corpus routing, immutable-parent evidence, DOSBox-X and 86Box adapter results, state behavior, explicit prerequisites and the bounded human validation receipt before whole-corpus reporting starts.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS only when every frozen eXoWin9x game routes to DOSBox-X, 86Box, specialist, structural_only or unsupported with no silent omission; immutable parent hashes survive fresh, second and crash-recovery runs; DOSBox-X and 86Box families have machine evidence plus Tom's bounded receipt; licensed/firmware/network prerequisites are explicit and networking remains opt-in; host routes or refusals and every command/report are linked from the parent log.
nodes.title: Gate 4 — native eXoWin9x family support review
nodes.why: The final corpus pass must not depend on a Windows image path until its parent/child boundary and representative behavior have independent evidence.

nodes.body: Run the measured eXoDOS, eXoWin3x and eXoWin9x importers and routers, reconcile every source game to one normalized profile and publish machine-readable classifications with provenance.
nodes.done_looks_like: Machine-readable outputs contain exactly one row for every game in each frozen eXoDOS, eXoWin3x and eXoWin9x snapshot; each row records normalized profile id, family signature, host runner routes, prerequisites and exactly one of validated_native, structural_only, specialist or unsupported with a reason and evidence links; per-collection totals reconcile, unclassified equals zero, and unchanged input produces byte-identical ordered output.
nodes.title: eXo corpus — publish deterministic three-collection classification outputs
nodes.why: Representative family success is insufficient unless every source row is routed or explicitly refused with no silent omissions.

nodes.body: Execute structural materialization, launch-plan composition, prerequisite refusal and immutable-versus-writable state assertions over every classified profile without interactively playing games.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every classified profile undergoes non-interactive materialization, launch-plan composition, prerequisite and host-refusal checks, and immutable/writable boundary assertions appropriate to its class; no game process is started; failures identify collection, game, profile and invariant; per-class totals reconcile with RS-724; repeated runs are deterministic and all commands/results are indexed in the parent log.
nodes.title: eXo corpus — automate launch-plan and state-boundary smoke coverage
nodes.why: Whole-corpus regressions need automated evidence beyond the smaller perceptual validation matrices.

nodes.body: Exercise saved revision, manifest, reconcile, provisioning and launch preflight for DOS, Windows 3.x and Windows 9x profiles in default loopback and a separate enrolled client topology.
nodes.done_looks_like: At least one DOS, Win3x and Win9x profile completes saved revision, manifest generation, reconcile, emulator provisioning and launch preflight in both default loopback and separate enrolled-client topologies; dependency files are transferred once, mutable state remains client-local, missing prerequisites refuse before process start, delta reconcile is idempotent, and product-v2 regression tests pass.
nodes.title: eXo corpus — prove product-v2 loopback and enrolled-client delivery
nodes.why: A valid native package is not a RetroStack feature until the production master/client path can deliver and compose it.

nodes.body: Synthesize per-collection and per-family counts, host routes, prerequisite requirements, representative behavioral evidence, specialist/unsupported reasons and deferred RetroArch work.
nodes.done_looks_like: A dated support matrix reports per collection and family: frozen population, validated_native, structural_only, specialist and unsupported counts; macOS/Windows/Linux runner routes or refusals; shared and licensed prerequisites; state policy; representative machine and human evidence; known limitations; and RetroArch/bezels/controller work explicitly deferred; every number links to machine output and sums to the frozen corpus.
nodes.title: eXo corpus — publish final native support matrix and limitations
nodes.why: Operators need a dated decision record that distinguishes proven native support from structural-only routing and future frontend enhancements.

nodes.body: Independently review source reconciliation, automated corpus evidence, product-v2 delivery, human receipts and the final support matrix against the parent acceptance.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS only when the three frozen source totals reconcile with unclassified = 0; automated materialization, launch-plan, prerequisite, state-boundary and product-v2 loopback/enrolled-client evidence passes; all bounded human receipts are present; every source, command, hash, result and decision is indexed in the append-only parent validation log; the final matrix distinguishes validated, structural, specialist and unsupported support; and the parent RS-696 acceptance is satisfied without claiming deferred RetroArch work.
nodes.title: Gate 5 — complete native eXo path acceptance review
nodes.why: The umbrella item should complete only when all five planned outcomes are evidenced and indexed, not when the last adapter happens to compile.

nodes.body: Consume the accepted eXo reference pack to classify every eXoDOS launch as a canonical Pure profile and lazy DOSZ recipe, explicitly deferring or refusing unsupported semantics instead of reparsing the source corpus or repacking it up front.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every eXoDOS row in the accepted versioned reference pack yields exactly one canonical on-demand DOSZ recipe or one pure_deferred/pure_unsupported record; profiles cover startup, mounts/discs/images, machine/CPU/memory/video/audio, stable-id per-content options, SoundFont/MT-32 prerequisites and Pure state key; all pack statements are consumed or report source path, line, token and reason, and sampled outputs trace back byte-for-byte to RS-762 source provenance; the dated 22-title specialist sighting is re-measured and each title is deliberately routed; no Staging, DOSBox-X, 86Box or custom runner is implemented; unchanged pack inputs produce byte-identical ordered JSON/TSV; actual DOSZ materialization is bounded to fixtures while every candidate recipe passes closure, path and collision checks; source hashes remain unchanged and no emulator/game process starts; tests and outputs are indexed from the parent log.
nodes.title: Pure corpus — translate every eXoDOS launch into an on-demand package recipe or refusal
nodes.why: RetroStack needs deterministic per-game launch intent and on-demand client packages, not a second fully unpacked copy of 7,666 games.

nodes.body: Validate every candidate recipe without gameplay and materialize representative DOSZ fixtures for each distinct supported structural family.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every eXoDOS classification undergoes non-interactive closure, canonical-package-plan, full-.opt, prerequisite and state-key validation; every supported structural family materializes at least one fixture whose ZIP integrity, member order, DOSBOX.BAT/conf startup and before/after immutable hashes pass; pure_deferred and pure_unsupported rows name the construct/capability and never compose a launch command; failures identify game, source path and invariant; totals reconcile exactly with RS-702 and RS-742 and unclassified equals zero; repeated runs are byte-identical; no emulator/game process starts; focused tests and the dated machine report are indexed from the parent log.
nodes.title: Pure corpus — run eXoDOS structural smoke and family evidence
nodes.why: A translated row is only credible when its closure, generated package/options, prerequisites and state boundary can be checked deterministically.

nodes.body: Independently verify current eXoDOS coverage, package recipes and structural family evidence without promoting candidates to gameplay-certified status.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS only when the accepted current eXoDOS total reconciles across inventory, translator and smoke report with unclassified = 0; every row has exactly one pure_validated, pure_structural_candidate, pure_deferred or pure_unsupported status; validated means only a represented family with an approved behavior receipt and unplayed rows remain candidates; every candidate passes closure, package-plan, full-.opt, prerequisite and state-key checks; every deferred/unsupported row names its source construct or capability, including each re-measured specialist-runtime title; deterministic rerun hashes match; no fallback runner was implemented; source hashes are unchanged and all evidence is indexed. Otherwise return FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN with the exact mismatch.
nodes.title: Gate 3 — complete eXoDOS Pure classification evidence
nodes.why: The Windows probes and final report need a trustworthy DOS baseline with every omission and specialist capability explicit.

nodes.body: Without launching, translate one ordinary eXoWin3x directory game and one of the measured boot-image games into the proven Pure package/profile/state contract.
nodes.done_looks_like: An isolated test root contains deterministic stable-id Pure packages and full content .opt files for 3-D Ultra Pinball or another documented directory representative and Sonic’s Schoolhouse or another documented boot-image representative; a dated selection note explains any substitution; package listings, startup path, images/media, Windows files, CPU/memory/video/audio options, prerequisites and state mode are recorded; dry-run Pure launch plans point only at the isolated copies; ZIP/image integrity and source/package hashes pass; unsupported source semantics produce a named pure_deferred or pure_unsupported record rather than being ignored; no emulator/game process starts; no source/live-instance file changes; evidence is indexed from the parent log.
nodes.title: Pure Windows probe — prepare Win3x directory and boot-image packages
nodes.why: Pure documents directory content and boot images, but the complete game-local Windows 3.x environment and its multimedia startup still require source-grounded translation evidence.

nodes.body: Without launching, determine whether one ordinary eXoWin9x DOSBox-X-family package can be represented by a local immutable OS base, per-game content disk and Pure per-content difference.
nodes.done_looks_like: A dated note selects one non-86Box game from the dominant ordinary Windows parent family and maps every required parent image, per-game VHD, optical image, Windows-file delta, registry/startup action and tuned option; the isolated test root contains or references only local read-only copies with SHA-256 and a full Pure content profile/.opt; a before-launch verifier proves the OS base and package are immutable and the declared difference/save targets are separate; the dry-run launch plan disables networking and names every guest-OS/audio/video prerequisite; if the eXo delta cannot be represented without installation or mutation, the title/family is pure_deferred or pure_unsupported with the exact failing semantic; all 29 measured 86Box titles remain explicitly deferred; no emulator, OS or game process starts and no source/live-instance file changes; evidence is indexed from the parent log.
nodes.title: Pure Windows probe — prepare one Win9x immutable-base and per-content difference
nodes.why: Pure has the right documented state primitive, but eXo’s shared parent plus D-drive Windows/registry delta is not identical and must be mapped or refused from evidence.

nodes.body: For each Windows sample the preparation evidence marks runnable, approve separately and record Windows/game flow, media, audio, input, exit and state; do not launch deferred samples.
nodes.done_looks_like: For each Win3x directory, Win3x boot-image or Win9x sample marked runnable, no launch occurs until Tom explicitly approves that individual run and the receipt records PASS, FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN for intended Windows/game flow, mounted media, music/effects, usable input, clean exit and expected second-launch state; any structurally deferred/unsupported sample is listed with “not launched” and its preparation reason; no title-specific tuning or networking is introduced; post-run hashes prove each immutable package/OS base and the source unchanged and show all differences under the isolated save/state/config tree; the receipt is indexed from the parent log.
nodes.title: Pure Windows probe — Tom validates only runnable prepared samples
nodes.why: Windows startup and multimedia behavior need human observation, while a structurally refused package should remain unlaunched.

nodes.body: Review the bounded Win3x and Win9x package/state probes and approved receipts, allowing an explicit deferred/unsupported conclusion.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS when the Win3x directory and boot-image samples and one ordinary Win9x parent/difference sample each have a complete deterministic preparation record and exactly one runnable, pure_deferred or pure_unsupported result; every runnable sample has Tom’s separately approved behavior/state receipt and every non-runnable sample is explicitly not launched; Win9x base/package hashes remain immutable across any run and differences are isolated; networking remains disabled; all 29 re-measured 86Box-family titles and Wing Commander IV DVD Edition have a deliberate phase status; no fallback runner is implemented; commands, hashes, receipts and limitations are indexed. PASS may therefore record zero supported Windows families if the evidence justifies it; otherwise return FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN with the exact missing evidence.
nodes.title: Gate 4 — DOSBox Pure Windows viability evidence
nodes.why: The Pure-first plan needs an evidence-backed Windows boundary, not a requirement to force guest Windows families through one core.

nodes.body: Combine the accepted source inventory, DOS corpus evidence and bounded Windows probes into one deterministic row-level Pure support dataset for all three collections.
nodes.done_looks_like: Canonical JSON and TSV contain exactly one row for every game in the accepted eXoDOS, eXoWin3x and eXoWin9x snapshots; each row records source identity/version, original runtime family, package/profile signature, prerequisites, representative evidence link and exactly one pure_validated, pure_structural_candidate, pure_deferred or pure_unsupported status plus reason code; only games represented by a full approved behavior family may be pure_validated and unplayed matching shapes remain candidates; Windows rows outside a demonstrated shape are deferred rather than guessed; the specialist DOS, Win3x boot-image and Win9x 86Box/ME populations are re-measured and explicitly represented; per-collection totals reconcile, duplicates are impossible, unclassified equals zero and unchanged input produces byte-identical ordered output; commands and hashes are indexed from the parent log.

nodes.body: Turn the row-level dataset into a dated per-collection/family report that says what RetroStack can launch through Pure, what remains a candidate and why games are deferred or unsupported.
nodes.done_looks_like: A dated Markdown report links the canonical JSON/TSV and reports, per collection and structural family, source total, pure_validated, pure_structural_candidate, pure_deferred and pure_unsupported counts; it states that family validation is not per-title certification; every count sums to the accepted inventory; reason-code tables name specialist hardware, source semantics, missing licensed prerequisites and demonstrated failures; macOS/Windows/Linux RetroArch/Core provisioning routes or refusals, package/state policy and SoundFont/MT-32/guest-OS prerequisites are explicit; the original Staging, DOSBox-X, custom DOSBox and 86Box assignments are preserved solely as future fallback evidence; bezels, shaders, controller profiles and title fixes remain separate; every claim links to dated machine or approved human evidence and the parent log indexes the report.

nodes.why: A machine classification needs a readable operational promise and must preserve the original runtime evidence for any future fallback phase.

nodes.body: Independently judge the complete Pure-first package, product delivery, corpus classification, Windows probe and support-report evidence against the revised parent acceptance.
nodes.done_looks_like: PASS only when Gate 1 proves at least two ordinary eXoDOS families through approved Pure launches; Gate 2 proves loopback and enrolled-client package/options/prerequisite/state delivery plus an approved viewer lifecycle; Gate 3 reconciles every current eXoDOS game with unclassified = 0; Gate 4 records complete Win3x/Win9x probe outcomes even if all are deferred; canonical all-collection JSON/TSV contains every accepted source row exactly once in one Pure status; the user-facing report sums every population and preserves fallback evidence without implementing it; source/live-instance immutability and the no-unapproved-launch rule hold; relevant product-v2 tests report zero failures; every command, hash, artifact and human receipt is indexed from the parent log. Otherwise return FAIL or NEEDS-HUMAN with the exact unmet clause.
nodes.title: Gate 5 — complete Pure-first eXo delivery acceptance
nodes.why: The umbrella should complete only when supported and unsupported scope is both operationally proven and fully accounted for.

R-E and R14 are declared equivalents with their reasons recorded.

nodes.body: The m3u half shipped in 9f905d4. A set with NO .m3u never becomes a Playlist content unit, so the new launch-contract arm never fires: each disc stays its own unit with its own launch member and the gate refuses the game. classify_optical must group sibling (Disc N) files into one unit.
nodes.done_looks_like: A multi-disc game with NO .m3u launches. THE M3U HALF IS ALREADY DONE AND MERGED (9f905d4) - do not rebuild it, do not touch the emulator TOMLs again, do not weaken RS-770's ungrouped-disc guard. (1) RE-MEASURE FIRST. 2026-08-27: 17 games are disc sets with no .m3u anywhere and are still refused because each disc is its own content unit carrying its own launch member, so payload_roles_are_launchable sees more than one. They are: The Daedalus Encounter (3do, 8 files - TWO rival 4-disc sets), Shenmue (dreamcast, 5 - four discs plus a Passport image), Gran Turismo 2 (psx, 4), Wing Commander III (3do, 4), Policenauts (saturn, 3), R4 Ridge Racer Type 4 (psx, 3), and eleven 2-disc games incl. Resident Evil 2 Dual Shock, Heart of Darkness, Night Trap, Skies of Arcadia, Black/Matrix AD, D, Shock Wave 2, Deep Fighter, Headhunter and Alone in the Dark (on both dreamcast and psx). (2) THE NAME PARSING ALREADY EXISTS AND MOSTLY WORKS - DO NOT BUILD A SECOND ONE. matcher.rs's strip_disc_tag / generate_disc_set_id already group sibling discs by stripped base name, and 12 of the 17 games ALREADY carry a correct rom_files.disc_set_id today (Policenauts' three discs are one set at the row level right now). The defect is that the CONTENT-UNIT layer ignores it: only an .m3u creates a Playlist unit, so without one the classifier emits a separate unit per disc, each carrying its own launch member, and payload_roles_are_launchable counts launch members rather than disc sets. The work is to make classify_optical produce ONE unit consistent with the disc_set_id the row layer already computes - reusing that parser, never a new one. This is exactly the two-rival-representations split RS-770's decision note warned about, surfacing as a bug. (3) The grouped unit behaves exactly like an m3u-owned one, so the launch-contract arm merged in 9f905d4 serves BOTH and there is ONE representation of a disc set, never two. Prove that by asserting a no-m3u set and an m3u set produce the same shape. (4) DO NOT write an .m3u into the library (CLAUDE.md: RetroStack never reorganises the source library) and DO NOT teach build_sync or payload_roles_are_launchable about disc sets (RS-770's decision note). (5) THE TWO HARD CASES MUST BE PINNED: The Daedalus Encounter holds two RIVAL 4-disc sets, so grouping must yield two units and RS-770's preference then picks one WHOLE set; Shenmue's Passport image is NOT a disc of the set and must not be grouped into it. A rule that swallows the Passport or merges the two Daedalus sets is wrong even if the game becomes launchable. (6) The 5 games held by RS-770's ungrouped-disc fail-safe (Shenmue, Skies of Arcadia, Alone in the Dark, Deep Fighter, Headhunter) must come OUT of that state because they now group properly - never by narrowing the guard. Assert the guard still fires for a set this rule does not group. (7) Takes effect on a rescan; gate on a rescan of a COPY of Tom's instance showing all 17 launchable, and assert a non-zero number of files was actually walked so a run that does nothing cannot pass. (8) Disc SWAPPING remains out of scope and does not exist in the tree; this gets the game booting on its first disc.
nodes.title: Multi-disc sets with no .m3u still cannot launch (17 games)

nodes.body: Once a disc set is one content unit, an emulator that reads m3u still needs an m3u to exist -- and 17 of Tom's sets have none. Reconcile already writes the discs into roms/<system>/<game_id>/ on the device; it writes the playlist there too, as a sibling. No master-side storage, no serving, no new durable path, and device-relative contents by construction.
nodes.done_looks_like: A multi-disc game whose emulator reads an .m3u gets one and can swap discs, and it is CREATED ON THE DEVICE AT RECONCILE TIME rather than stored on the master. (1) THE PLAYLIST IS GENERATED BY RECONCILE INTO THE PER-GAME STAGING DIRECTORY THE DISCS ALREADY LAND IN - reconcile writes root.join(want.path) and a grouped member's device path is roms/<system>/<game_id>/<name>, so the .m3u is written there as a sibling of its own discs. NO new top-level directory, NO OWN_TOP_LEVEL change, NO CLAUDE.md layout change, and NO master-side storage. (2) THIS IS NOT A LIBRARY WRITE, and the distinction must be stated in the code comment so nobody 'fixes' it later: <root>/roms/ is RetroStack's OWN managed staging area (it is in OWN_TOP_LEVEL and reconcile already writes reconciled ROMs into it on every sync). The rule 'RetroStack never reorganises the source library' protects the user's EXTERNAL source folders - Tom's archive at /Volumes/Media/Retro Games Archive/ROMs is library_sources row 16. Pin a test that generation writes nothing under any NON-BUILTIN library source root. (3) IT IS CREATED, NEVER FETCHED. It carries no ManifestFile.src and is not served over /media; reconcile refuses a fetched file with no serving path, and this file is not fetched at all. Do not add it to the payload as a normal member. (4) THE MANIFEST DECLARES THE INTENT, THE CLIENT DOES THE WRITING: the manifest says this game's payload wants a playlist (a role or flag on the existing manifest shape - no new transport, no new client concept), and reconcile materialises it. Loopback is the default topology and the master is its own client, so this path must work there first. (5) ONLY WHERE IT HELPS: only when the resolved emulator declares m3u (swanstation, flycast, mednafen_saturn, duckstation today) AND the set has no .m3u of its own. Dolphin and PCSX2 cannot read one - generating for them is waste and must not happen; assert it. A set that already ships its own .m3u keeps it and is never shadowed. (6) CONTENTS ARE THE DISC FILENAMES AS SIBLINGS ON THE DEVICE - which they are by construction, since they are written into the same directory. Assert against the actual staged filenames, not against source paths. (7) DISC ORDER IS DISC-NUMBER ORDER via matcher.rs parse_disc_number, never lexical or directory order. Pin it with a fixture whose lexical order DISAGREES with disc order (RS-774 uses disc 3 named 'Alpha', disc 1 named 'Zulu'); without that the test cannot tell the two orderings apart, which is exactly the hole review caught in RS-774. (8) IDEMPOTENT AND SELF-CLEANING: same set, same bytes; a disc added, removed or re-chosen rewrites it; a game that stops qualifying has its generated playlist removed rather than left behind. Reconcile already owns that directory, so this is its job. (9) GATE ON A COPY of Tom's instance: the qualifying sets among the 17 gain a playlist that resolves against their own staged discs, and assert a non-zero number of sets was processed so a run that generates nothing cannot pass. (10) THIS is where disc swapping arrives - say so, and say which of the 17 still boot disc 1 only because their emulator cannot read a playlist.
nodes.title: Generate the .m3u a disc set needs, on the device at reconcile time

nodes.body: reconcile never prunes: the only deletion in reconcile.rs is the .part temp cleanup (line 729). A device keeps every stale build's payload forever, growing without bound across build changes. Tom ruled 2026-08-28 that unneeded items should be removed. THE RISK IS NOT PRUNING, IT IS SCOPE: on a client today the build payload, hand-placed BIOS and saves all share one root.
nodes.done_looks_like: A device stops accumulating payload it no longer needs, and never loses anything the user placed by hand. (1) THE LICENCE TO PRUNE IS TOM'S RULE: a user never writes into the build folder, so everything there is regenerable and safe to remove. THAT RULE IS ALSO THE WHOLE RISK, because it only holds for the BUILD tier. ⚠️ On a client today there is no tier separation at all -- the staged payload, the user's hand-placed BIOS and their saves share one instance root. A prune scoped to "anything not in the manifest" WOULD DELETE THE USER'S BIOS, which VOCABULARY.md line 45 says is declared never shipped and which runner.rs:283's own comment calls the thing "only the user can fix". (2) SO PRUNING MUST BE SCOPED TO KNOWN BUILD-TIER PATHS, never to "whatever is not in the manifest". Either land the tier separation first (RS-783) or enumerate the build-tier paths explicitly and refuse to delete outside them. State which, and pin it with a test that a hand-placed BIOS file, a save, a state and an installed emulator all SURVIVE a build change that removes every game. That test is the point of the item. (3) PAYLOAD PRUNES EAGERLY, MEDIA LAZILY. Media paths are keyed by system + game rather than by build, so a game shared across a build switch verifies by size (reconcile.rs:694 AlreadyVerified) and costs nothing to keep; eager media pruning turns switching back into a re-download. Measure the trade rather than assuming it. (4) A MASTER HAS LITTLE TO PRUNE: since RS-776 it references ROMs in place rather than copying, so unbounded growth is a CLIENT problem specifically. Say what a master prunes, if anything. (5) FAIL SAFE AND VISIBLE: a prune that cannot identify a file's tier does nothing and says so. A partial prune must never leave a build unlaunchable -- assert launchability after pruning, not just that files went. (6) Re-measure before building: how much stale payload does a real device actually hold? The number decides whether this is urgent or housekeeping, and nobody has measured it.
nodes.title: Remove payload a build no longer needs, without deleting what the user placed

nodes.body: Emulator settings are a format! string in saves.rs: every setting is a Rust edit and none can depend on the device. Declare them per emulator in its TOML instead, rendered per device and layered through --appendconfig.
nodes.done_looks_like: Emulator settings are declared in TOML and rendered per device, with no Rust edit needed to add one. SCOPE IS THE MECHANISM, NOT THE VALUES (values are RS-794). Re-specified 2026-08-28 after two independent reviews; the spec artifact rs789-spec.md is authoritative and this restates its gates. (1) SCHEMA: each emulator TOML declares [config] (format + output dir), [config.settings] for the device level, [cores.<id>.config] and [systems.<key>.config]. System MUST be a level: genesis_plus_gx serves megadrive, mastersystem, gamegear, sg1000 and megacd. [cores.<id>.options] is NOT in this item -- RetroArch writes its own per-core .opt files and option keys in a .cfg do nothing (RS-795). (2) PLACEHOLDERS resolve per device and absolute: {bios} {saves} {states} {device} -- all four required, {saves} and {states} being distinct directories (saves.rs:20-21). {roms} is NOT in this item: no setting consumes it. {screen_width}/{screen_height} are declared but MUST fail loudly at render until RS-790 -- never emit the literal. The global intent layer admits only intents passing Test A (RetroStack already wires it for two or more emulators): self-contained install, firmware, saves, and fullscreen -- fullscreen being FLAG-shaped, delivered as a launch argument, and a RetroArch binding must NOT also emit video_fullscreen. Vsync and exit behaviour are candidates; screenshots is out. (3) RENDERING is one renderer per format; retroarch-cfg only, others rejected with a clear error. Idempotent and content-compared. Rendered AT LAUNCH and additionally on provision -- launch-time render is what heals a deleted device/ on a loopback master, where the tick is client-only and reconcile_and_provision refuses masters. The renderer MUST create the directory for every path-valued setting it writes, with its own test: RetroArch treats system_directory as unset when the path is missing and silently falls back to its own, which is the RS-783 firmware bug. (4) DELIVERY: the runner composes one --appendconfig argument least-specific-first, device|core|system|<build layers>, expanded into the template through a {config_chain} placeholder (to nothing when no layer exists). The | delimiter, ordered append and non-fatal missing files are verified at configuration.c:6373-6417. There is NO game rung in this item. DO NOT build on RetroArch's content-directory rung. Seed-if-missing is RETAINED. The template migration is KEY-LEVEL: a STANDING RULE, not a one-time migration -- it re-evaluates every seed pass. For a TOML that DECLARES a [config] block (retroarch alone today), args/working_dir/links self-heal to the shipped value via toml_edit: they are product mechanism and hand-editing them is unsupported by declaration. Replace the WHOLE args value for the platform, never a fragment within it -- fragment surgery on a platform-quoted command line yields a silently broken argv on a partial match. A TOML with NO [config] block must never have its args, working_dir or links touched: mame.toml and the other twelve are regression-tested for this exactly as emulator/settings.rs:202-257 rewrites [provision] keys, leaving every policy key untouched (the panel owns URLs/sources/claims; args, working_dir and links are product mechanism). Unconditional overwrite is FORBIDDEN: it un-ships RS-438, since emulator_settings seeds before reading (api/mod.rs:6524) so opening the Emulators tab would revert URLs saved through that same tab, and reconcile.rs:862 runs every client tick. provision_respects_an_existing_instance_config (reconcile.rs:~2765) must stay green, and a new test must show a panel-edited TOML getting {config_chain} while keeping its pinned binary_url. (5) BUILD EXTENSION POINT: a build may contribute extra layers at a defined chain position -- a PACK is self-contained, assets riding the manifest and materialising like firmware, config rendering on the device. Bezels motivated it; HD texture packs are the same mechanism. Defines the seam, NOT any pack format. (6) AUTHORING SAFETY: every setting key any shipped TOML declares is checked against .claude/skills/retroarch/references/settings.tsv, PLUS an enumerated list of constructed key families GENERATED from their call sites (input_player{N}_{mouse_index,joypad_index,analog_dpad_mode,device_reservation_type} at configuration.c:6538-6549; input_libretro_device_p{N} at :9703-9705). The family list MUST be generated from the call sites, never hand-copied -- the illustrative table in the spec was itself incomplete on first writing (network_remote_enable_user_p{N} at :6486, led{N}_map at :6569, input_remap_port_p{N} at :9711 were all missing). input_player4_analog_dpad_mode, input_libretro_device_p1 and led2_map must pass; an invented key must fail the build. (7) MIGRATION: the five settings ensure_retroarch_overlay writes today move into the TOML unchanged. The gate is PARSE equality -- the rendered file yields exactly the same key/value set as today's, same keys, same values, nothing added or lost. Byte equality is NOT achievable: today's file interleaves eleven comments between non-alphabetical settings. The function's directory-creation side effects must survive its retirement. The old retrostack.cfg is deleted ONLY once {config_chain} is live in the composed argv: while the active template lacks it the renderer keeps writing that file, because a stale --appendconfig pointing at a deleted file is non-fatal and silent (configuration.c:6404-6411) and would drop system_directory, both save dirs and config_save_on_exit at once. (8) EVIDENCE must include an argv assertion, not only a rendered-file assertion: the composed launch args contain the chain in rung order, AND a template lacking {config_chain} still yields the old single-file flag with retrostack.cfg present. (9) Full suite green, every 'test result:' line counted, 0 failed.
nodes.title: Per-device emulator configuration, declared in TOML

nodes.body: We write NO settings for any standalone emulator — the modules do portable markers and BIOS links only. Dolphin (1,807 games) and PCSX2 (1,727) are 80% of the 4,433 games RetroArch cannot run. Mirror each config reference the way libretro's was, then test whether RS-789's intent layer is genuinely expressible on a second emulator or only reads that way.
nodes.done_looks_like: Dolphin's and PCSX2's config references are mirrored the way libretro's was, so their claims are greppable rather than recalled; a renderer exists for each format; and each declares default settings through RS-789's mechanism with no second config path. ⚠️ Each renderer MERGES — it writes only the keys it owns and leaves the rest of the file exactly as found, the way emulator/settings.rs edits the TOMLs with toml_edit. A renderer that rewrites a whole Dolphin.ini would destroy the user's own edits on every launch, and a test must pin that it does not. Answers whether the intent layer is genuinely expressible on a second emulator or only reads that way — the question RS-789's spec said would validate it.
nodes.title: Mirror Dolphin and PCSX2 config references, then bind the intent layer to a second emulator

nodes.body: Settle the mirror-checked RetroArch plain-config values and ownership tier. Product-mechanism keys are enforced; video_smooth=false is the chosen seeded preference; generated input defaults and core options are explicitly excluded.
nodes.done_looks_like: The delivered mirror/evidence set names every selected plain RetroArch config key, value and ownership tier: mechanism keys render through the enforced declaration path; video_smooth=false is selected as seeded preference and remains in the static seed only until RS-820 gives it a declarative home. Generated input_player*_analog_dpad_mode defaults are absent so the emulator UI is not made inert; core options are absent and remain RS-795 work. The delivery cites the pinned settings table/generated families and records the implementation commit; no claim is made that RS-820's declarative seed mechanism is already present.
nodes.title: Which RetroArch settings, and their values
nodes.why: This item selected and evidenced values; RS-820 owns the missing declarative seeded mechanism. Correcting the acceptance prevents a done research/value decision from claiming future implementation.

nodes.body: libretro hosts per-core system-file bundles at https://buildbot.libretro.com/assets/system/<Name>.zip — the URL behind RetroArch's 'Core System Files Downloader' menu. We ship the ppsspp and bluemsx cores; PPSSPP.zip and blueMSX.zip exist there and nothing in provision_retroarch fetches either. Neither core works properly without its assets.
nodes.done_looks_like: Provisioning fetches each shipped core's system-file bundle from buildbot.libretro.com/assets/system/<Name>.zip and unpacks it into the system directory, declared per core in retroarch.toml rather than hard-coded. ppsspp and bluemsx receive theirs. Nothing requires opening RetroArch's Core System Files Downloader menu. A test asserts a core declaring a bundle gets it and one declaring none is untouched.
nodes.title: Two shipped cores need system files provisioning never fetches
nodes.why: Found 2026-08-28 while answering how dolphin-libretro gets its Sys folder. The same mechanism is the answer for any future core needing support files (Dolphin.zip, LRPS2.zip), so this is one URL template plus unzip into system_directory, declarable per core in retroarch.toml — the same shape as the existing core download. ⚠️ pcee2 has NO bundle, so its REQUIRED pcsx2/resources has no automatic source; LRPS2 needs only the user's BIOS because cheats/ and cheats_ws/ self-create and its widescreen patches are embedded.

nodes.body: RPCS3 applies per-game settings automatically from a config database keyed by title_id: cfg_mode::database_config OR ::custom (the default) triggers get_database_config(title_id) at boot, and System.cpp's own comment names the no-gui case as why the lookup happens there. The data is ONE document at https://api.rpcs3.net/config/?api=v1 — measured 2026-08-28: 297 KB, 2,138 games, each entry a ready-to-use RPCS3 YAML fragment (e.g. 'Core:\n  Libraries Control:\n    - libvdec.sprx:lle'). Fetch once to <settings dir>/config_database.dat; there is nothing per-game to fetch.
nodes.done_looks_like: On a fresh macOS instance, RPCS3 holds a current config_database.dat at <config dir>/GuiConfigs/, fetched during provisioning from https://api.rpcs3.net/config/?api=v1 — because deploy-mac.sh does not bake it in and the in-app downloader is GUI-parented. Per-game settings then apply at boot without anyone opening RPCS3. Do NOT pin the byte count or game count in a test; both drifted within a day of measurement.
nodes.title: Provision RPCS3's per-game config database, because only the Windows build ships it
nodes.why: ⚠️ .ci/deploy-windows.sh bakes config_database.dat into the build; deploy-mac.sh and deploy-linux.sh do NOT. So on macOS the database arrives only via config_database.cpp's runtime downloader, which is Qt/GUI-parented — and RetroStack never opens RPCS3's GUI. Without this, PS3 games on macOS get no database config at all. Same shape as the core system-files fetch (RS-804), so probably the same code path. Bonus: holding the file lets us READ which games have a known-good config. Re-scope RS-157: the API carries settings with no explanation, while the wiki harvest's remaining value is the NOTES saying why.

nodes.body: Create the portable/ directory beside the RPCS3 binary so its config root moves inside device/, relocate dev_hdd0 via the VFS config so installed games survive an emulator update, and install .pkg files with a separate --headless invocation.
nodes.done_looks_like: RPCS3 launches with its config root inside device/: a portable/ directory exists beside the binary (fs::get_config_dir returns it — Utilities/File.cpp:2240-2244), and on macOS that is device/runtimes/macos/rpcs3/portable/ because get_executable_path returns the app bundle. dev_hdd0 is relocated via the VFS config so replacing the emulator does not destroy installed games. A .pkg installs from the command line with a SEPARATE --headless invocation, never --no-gui (which refuses: 'Cannot perform installation in no-gui mode!', rpcs3.cpp:1156-1159), and reports per-package success so a batch can be trusted. Nothing requires opening RPCS3's GUI.
nodes.title: Put RPCS3 in a deterministic layout we control
nodes.why: RPCS3 is the one standalone module doing no portable setup, so today its config, dev_hdd0 and installed games all land in ~/Library/Application Support, outside the instance and unreachable by us.

nodes.body: A per-device settings surface, populated during client setup on the machine, carrying internal render scale for the emulators that accept one.
nodes.done_looks_like: A client setup run on the machine asks for internal render scale and persists it per device, not per build, so the same collection can run at different scales on different hardware. The value reaches the emulators that accept one through RS-789's declared-settings mechanism, with no second config path. The surface is general enough for the routing policy (RS-801) to use rather than build its own.
nodes.title: Ask for render scale at client setup
nodes.why: Settled 2026-08-28: render scale belongs to the machine, not the collection, so one library plays well on a Mac Mini and a desktop without separate builds. No per-device surface exists; the routing policy work wants the same one, so it is built once here.

nodes.body: Only one may be declared: two cores claiming ps2 would make system_cores['ps2'] depend on HashMap iteration order in EmulatorConfigStore::add_configs. Declaring one IS the choice.
