nodes.title: Choose the PS2 core: LRPS2 or PCEE2
nodes.why: Narrowed 2026-08-29. The GameCube/Wii half is settled in code — [cores.dolphin] is declared and dolphin.toml carries priority = 60, so the route exists for a per-game override while standalone Dolphin stays the default. Only the PS2 core remains open. LRPS2: native arm64 recompilers (verified on ARM Linux, not macOS), an LRPS2.zip system-files bundle, options in a header. nodes.body: Pass --config at the base retroarch.cfg that [setup].copy already places in the device directory and that nothing currently reads, so RetroArch stops reading the user's own config and the seed tier has somewhere to write.
nodes.done_looks_like: RetroArch launches against a base config inside device/, not the user's own, so the never-touch-their-config promise is structural rather than restraint. The base config is seeded once and never re-imposed, matching how mame.toml seeds cfg/default.cfg. A user's change made in RetroArch's own menu PERSISTS — which means config_save_on_exit is reconsidered, since it exists only to protect a file we would no longer be borrowing. The --appendconfig chain still applies its mechanism keys on top. A test asserts the launch argv names a config inside device/ and that a user-writable base config exists there.
nodes.title: Give RetroArch its own base config so seeded settings have a home
nodes.why: Today the launch passes no -c, so RetroArch reads the user's personal retroarch.cfg and we only layer over it — which is the sole reason config_save_on_exit is forced false. That leaves nowhere to seed shaders or look-and-feel, and makes every enforced key silently override what the user set in RetroArch's own menu.

nodes.body: apply_setup's copy step skips when dest.exists(), which FOLLOWS a symlink. So if device/emulators/retroarch/retroarch.cfg is a link to ~/.config/retroarch/retroarch.cfg, the seed is skipped, RetroArch is handed that path via --config, and writes through the link into the user's own file — with config_save_on_exit now true. ⚠️ ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED 2026-08-29: refusing at SEED time is cosmetic. The old code already skips a symlinked destination, so warning-and-skipping changes nothing observable and a mutation restoring the old branch leaves the test green. The enforcement point is LAUNCH, where resolve_launch hands the path to RetroArch: verify the base is a regular file whose canonical path is inside device/, and refuse the launch otherwise. That is the moment harm would occur and the only place a test can catch it.
nodes.done_looks_like: A launch refuses, with a message naming the file, when the base config the template selects is not a regular file resolving inside device/ — a symlink out to the user's own config being the case that matters. The test must be killed by a mutation that removes the check: assert the launch ERRORS, not that the user's file is unchanged, because the pre-fix code also leaves it unchanged (it skips) and such a test passes either way. A positive control shows a normal device-owned base still launches.
nodes.title: A symlinked base config escapes the never-touch-their-config promise
nodes.why: RS-813's stated goal was making the promise STRUCTURAL rather than a matter of restraint, and a symlink defeats it structurally. Found by an independent review, 2026-08-29.

nodes.body: Same method over the identification half of rom_scanner; the walking/probing half is its own leaf.
nodes.done_looks_like: Method (shared by every classification leaf, from the plan §3.2 and Tom's decisions): every row in this batch (the P0 `batch` column decides membership) leaves `unreviewed` with a verdict and a one-line reason; an IMPROVE names exactly one checklist defect from the plan's table: D1 cannot fail (assertion true on every outcome — is_ok() alone, asserting the value just constructed, a constant); D2 wall-clock (a sleep so a side effect can happen, a deadline that is the assertion, a budget that fires under load); D3 shape-fake (a double returns a shape the product type cannot produce or omits a refusal path the product has); D4 call site unpinned (commenting out the production call leaves the test green — backed by doing exactly that and running the file's tests; a measurement, not an opinion); D5 pins a moment (a literal cross-file count, git show <base>:, today's date, a figure another merge will move — an #[ignore]d test without its resource and recipe is coded D5); D6 unfalsified guard (never broken-and-restored, or a control that passes on its own allowlist); D7 shared global without serialiser (reads or resets a process-global static without holding the matching lock — the RS-988 class); D8 slow with a cheaper instrument (over the per-test limit and a shared or smaller fixture exists or can); D9 guard made unfalsifiable by its fix (the only reachable false branch is gone; the assertion survives for a new reason);  a CUT names the other test that asserts the same thing and carries two signatures, classifier and a fresh reviewer, or is a provably cannot-fail test both signed (Tom 2026-09-06: named replacement only); an IMPROVE whose fix needs a product change is written as verdict `IMPROVE-blocked` with the product change in `reason` (RS-1013 renders the list for Tom). nodes.body: Both clear flags destroy v2_release_work_map (and v2_release_work_exceptions) by necessity. Combined with --skip-match-release-work, or any run ending before stage 55, the map stays empty and nothing says so. The catalogue then reports zero release-to-work matches with no error.

Reproduce first: import_v2.py --clear-works --skip-match-release-work on a populated scratch database currently exits 0 with v2_release_work_map at 0 rows and no message. Cover BOTH sides, since --clear-releases has the identical shape. A warning at exit is enough; do not make it an error, because clearing without rebuilding is legitimate mid-recovery. While there, fix the related wording defect (nit 2): the help string, the docstring on clear_releases_with_work_map, and PIPELINE_SPEC all say these flags clear v2_release_work_map, but clear_release_work_map walks all of RELEASE_WORK_TABLES and also empties v2_release_work_exceptions. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.

nodes.body:
RESCOPED 2026-08-03 after measurement. The proposed fix -- give title_exact precedence over alias_title_exact -- is mostly WRONG. Measured across all 361,174 accepted title/alias edges: 349 candidates have a title_exact edge losing to a higher-scoring alias_title_exact edge pointing elsewhere, and the current answers are overwhelmingly defensible because the alias IS the regional retitle (Crime Fighters 2 -> vendetta, Gradius -> nemesis, Same! Same! Same! -> fire shark, Jungle King -> jungle hunt, Oni - The Ninja Master -> metamoqester). Giving title_exact precedence moves these onto duplicate LaunchBox records of the same game. THE FIX SET AND THE DO-NOT-BREAK SET ARE THE SAME SET -- that is the whack-a-mole signature, not a tuning problem.

The named 18-row Masterchess reproducer COULD NOT BE RE-VERIFIED: LaunchBox holds no zxspectrum record titled Masterchess, and every accepted edge on those ROMs is alias_title_exact to CHESS. Three publishers' chess games attach to one LaunchBox row -- a source-coverage problem, not a scoring-precedence one. Re-derive before building anything.

What survives is a DETECTOR: both edge types present, pointing at different LaunchBox ids, within 0.03. Fires on 349 rows -- a worklist a human can clear, not a rule to encode.
nodes.done_looks_like: The 349 rows are surfaced as a review worklist alongside the other attachment questions, ordered by vote count like the rest of the queue, with both candidate LaunchBox records and both edge scores shown so a human can choose; no change to _score_edge or _attach_candidate precedence; the Masterchess reproducer is either re-derived against current data or struck from the record. Explicitly NOT in scope: making title_exact outrank alias_title_exact.
nodes.title: Which LaunchBox record a ROM attaches to: a worklist, not a scoring fix
nodes.why: Found by the RS-187 verifier 2026-07-30, which classified all 456 moved rows rather than sampling. The mechanism is pre-existing; RS-187 fed a new signal into that weighting rather than changing it, so it surfaced the flaw instead of causing it.

nodes.body: RS-171 repointed rom_ceiling's hash:sha1 and hash:crc32 at the spine. The loss is narrower than first filed: because CRC32 is on 100 percent of staged libretro ROM rows (0 of 399,794 NULL), spine-derived hash:crc32 must equal map-derived dimension='' -- both 64,532 -- so losing a libretro release from the spine now breaks a subset relation inside the same run. That contradiction test did not exist before and is load-bearing. What nothing cross-checks is the sha1 COLUMN itself: a projection that wrote entries correctly but nulled sha1 would move hash:sha1 while hash:crc32, dimension='' and rom_spine all sat still.
nodes.done_looks_like: A stage-60 metric compares spine SHA1 entries against staged SHA1-bearing rows that reach a release -- 227,898 libretro spine entries against the staged population, both computed for the same generation -- so nulling or corrupting the sha1 column moves a stored metric; a test proves it by nulling sha1 on a scratch spine and asserting the metric moves; the existing hash:crc32 vs dimension='' equality at 64,532 still holds and dimension='', any_rom_source, source_type:* and the 68 system:* rows remain spine-independent; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Restore the instrument's ability to catch wrong hash values
nodes.why: The old staging recomputation would have contradicted a nulled sha1 column; the new one cannot, and that was a conscious trade rather than a considered design.

nodes.body: quality_tier is NULL on 100% of releases everywhere and compute_quality_tiers.py has never been run. That script is v1's, and v1 is being dropped, so the capability now belongs to nothing. Tiers are what let the app say 'these 1.4% are the games worth shipping' and separate them from the ~52% that are demos, betas and shovelware. Decide where they compute in v2 -- a stage 60 concern or an export-time one -- and on what evidence, given v2 carries IGDB total_rating/total_rating_count on works and LaunchBox community_rating_count on releases, which v1 did not have. Raised 2026-08-03 when the v1 items were archived, so the intent is not lost with them.
nodes.done_looks_like: A tier lands on the v2 grain that actually carries the evidence, stated and justified (work or release, not both); the distribution across tiers is reported as measured figures rather than inherited from v1's 1.4/46/52 split; the rule is written into PIPELINE_SPEC; a release with no rating evidence gets an explicit unrated tier rather than being silently binned as junk; pytest reports 0 failed.

nodes.body: Surfaced by RS-297's review of its 94 gained matches, both from IGDB's own parent_game_id rather than from anything v2 does: 'The Flintstones: BurgerTime in Bedrock' resolves to 'BurgerTime Deluxe', and 'The 7th Guest Remake' to 'The 7th Guest VR'. Also from its repointed set: Lunar Lander x3 move onto igdb 9129 'Moonlander', a type-8 remake under a different title, and the C64 'Spelunky64' demake moves onto Spelunky (2012) when it is a demake of Spelunky Classic (2008). The question is whether IGDB's parent edges need a sanity filter before v2 inherits them -- a remake with a DIFFERENT title is a weaker claim than one with the same title.
nodes.done_looks_like: A measured answer to how often an IGDB parent edge links entries whose titles share no normalised token, with the distribution by game_type; a recommendation on whether v2 should refuse or flag such edges, with the false-positive cost of doing so stated; the four named cases resolved either way. Research item -- the output is a decision and its evidence, not code.

nodes.body: Raised by RS-297's builder while rejecting a shortcut, and worth keeping. platforms_json is rendered by the browser as the work's platform list -- a claim about the world -- while stage 55 also uses it as a hard filter on six of its seven tiers. Those two jobs disagree the moment we want the gate to be more generous than the fact: unioning a port's platforms onto BOTH the nearest work and the root would have satisfied RS-297's 'loses none' clause literally, at the cost of Tekken 5 displaying PSP forever. If a generous gate is ever wanted, the honest shape is a SECOND column -- platform_gate_json, the union over the subtree -- kept apart from the displayed platforms_json, so the widened set never becomes a displayed claim. Not needed today; RS-297 chose the truthful narrow list and RS-303 recovers the losses by name instead.
nodes.done_looks_like: A decision recorded either way. If adopted: platform_gate_json is populated as the subtree union, stage 55 gates on it, the browser and any export keep reading platforms_json, and the two are shown to differ on a named work. If rejected: the reason is written into PIPELINE_SPEC next to the union so the next person does not re-derive it. Design item -- the output is the decision and its evidence.
nodes.title: A work's platform list is displayed, so it cannot double as a generous match gate
nodes.why: The moment a displayed fact is also a filter, someone widens it for matching and quietly publishes a lie.

nodes.body: Found by the RS-296 gate, all pre-existing and none blocking that merge. (a) quality_report.py has ZERO pytest coverage while being the only reader of the quality metrics -- RS-296 added ~110 lines to it untested, and one mutation (stripping the mint arm from the independent --verify total) survives the suite for that reason alone, though --verify itself catches it. (b) 'measure --read-only --verify' silently IGNORES --verify: cmd_measure returns inside the read-only branch before reaching it, so the invocation that is safe against the live database is the one that cannot verify. nodes.body: Found by the RS-204/250/307 batch, pre-existing and untouched. test_import_runner.py's SKIP_EVERYTHING_ELSE constant omits --skip-gametdb and --skip-quality-assess, so seven tests run the real data-sources/gametdb/ ingest on every suite run -- against conftest's own stated rule that nothing in the suite opens the real data. Read-only and harmless today, but it means the suite's runtime and its result both depend on a corpus outside the repo: a developer without the data root gets failures that say nothing about their change, and a corpus that shifts changes what the suite proves. The batch's two new tests use a stricter skip list and are hermetic; the seven are not.

nodes.body: Found by RS-198's gate, 2026-08-04. TWO INSTANCES OF ONE SHAPE. (1) config/systems.txt is GENERATED from the manifest and carries 74 keys against the manifest's 84 -- missing fds, satellaview, virtualboy, pokemini, vic20, plus4, cdtv, x68000, pc98, odyssey2. Last regenerated 2026-07-28 (015f9d6); scripts/sync_systems_txt.py has not run since ten keys were added. Blast radius is small today -- only bootstrap.sh and bootstrap.ps1 read it, and only as a fallback when the manifest is absent -- which is exactly why nobody noticed. (2) NOTHING MECHANICALLY TIES the two flag-key registries: MANIFEST_FLAG_KEYS at seed.rs:25 and the tuple at system_mapping.py:23 are kept in step by a prose comment in each pointing at the other. Rust hard-fails on an unknown key, Python silently ignores one, so a third flag added to the Python side only would make Rust refuse to seed a manifest Python accepts. RS-198 added 'disc' to both correctly; the next one has no guard. Pre-existing in both cases -- RS-198 did not cause either.
nodes.done_looks_like: A derivative of the manifest cannot silently fall behind it. For systems.txt: either it is regenerated and something fails when it is stale -- a test comparing its key set to the manifest's is the cheap version -- or it is deleted and the bootstrap scripts read the manifest directly, which is better if the fallback has no remaining reason to exist; establish which and say why. For the flag registries: a single declaration both consumers derive from, or a test that fails when they diverge; adding a hypothetical third flag to one side only must go red. RE-MEASURE FIRST (74 vs 84 is a 2026-08-04 sighting). Note the two halves can be delivered independently and either alone is worth having.
nodes.title: The manifest's derivatives can drift from it silently, and one already has
nodes.why: config/systems.txt is ten keys behind the manifest, and nothing would have said so.

nodes.body: Found by RS-361's rebuild, 2026-08-04. After the rebuild v2_works holds 331,150 rows at run 91 plus TWO at run 77: igdb 287961 'M_Day' and 255574 'Paranoia: The Game Edition'. Both are game_type 11 ports whose parent is a MOD (277686 and 165050). Before the mods dump existed those parents were absent, so each port could find no root and became its own work; now the parent exists, each port maps onto the mod work instead (port_of_work -> 2394676 and 2305188). The two old rows are entirely unreferenced -- 0 map rows, 0 relationships, 0 external ids, 0 release-work rows -- but stage 50 SKIPS rather than deletes, so they linger. Harmless while v2_works is counted with a run filter, which is exactly what catchup_check warns about; the risk is a future query that forgets the filter and silently counts a superseded generation. Other stages already discard their superseded generations via discard_superseded_generations (RS-159); stage 50 does not.
nodes.done_looks_like: A work row whose generation has been superseded does not survive the stage that superseded it -- stage 50 discards its own superseded generation the way RS-159's runner does for the stages that already do, rather than skipping and leaving orphans. Verify on a clone by reproducing the exact condition: a port whose parent is absent becomes its own work, then the parent is staged and the port re-maps, and the old work row must be gone rather than merely unreferenced. Name M_Day (igdb 287961) and Paranoia: The Game Edition (igdb 255574) individually before and after. Confirm catchup_check stops reporting v2_works as multi-generation. RE-MEASURE FIRST -- 'two rows' is a 2026-08-04 sighting on generation 91 and the number depends on which parents were absent last time. If the honest answer is that skipping is deliberate and the fix is to make every reader filter by run, say so with the reasoning; that is a valid outcome.

nodes.body: Found by RS-381's gate, 2026-08-04, recorded rather than self-fixed because it touches the sweep's delete condition. referencing_columns reads PRAGMA foreign_key_list over every table, and its docstring argues that a hand-kept list 'would go quietly short'. THE PRAGMA GOES SHORT TOO: v2_quality_spot_checks.work_id (600 non-null) and v2_release_work_exceptions.work_id (19,666 rows) both hold v2_works.id with NO DECLARED FK. The second matters -- it is stage 55's other table, holding the previous generation at exactly the moment the sweep runs, which is the same argument that justifies the whole predicate. PRAGMA foreign_key_check is blind to undeclared references by construction, so the gate's clean run against the live clone proves nothing about these two. MEASURED EXPOSURE TODAY IS ZERO WORKS: nothing reads previous-generation exception rows (mint_works scopes to the current stage-55 run, quality_assess never touches work_id), and v2_quality_spot_checks already carries 200 dangling work_ids of 600, so it is already a snapshot by design. Inert -- but the safety property is asserted only by proxy, which is the species every gate this week has been finding.
nodes.done_looks_like: The set of columns holding v2_works.id is either TRUE by derivation or asserted, rather than believed. Two routes, and the gate laid both out. (a) Add FOREIGN KEY (work_id) REFERENCES v2_works(id) to v2_release_work_exceptions so the derivation becomes true -- needs a table rebuild, and v2_quality_spot_checks must stay OUT since it dangles deliberately. (b) Keep the derivation and narrow the docstring to what it actually guarantees, DECLARED keys, plus a test asserting no undeclared column matching *work_id exists outside a named allowlist, so the next one is caught where it is added. Prefer (b) unless the rebuild is wanted anyway; (a) makes one column true and leaves the general hazard. VERIFY by adding a third undeclared work_id column to a fixture and confirming whichever route you took catches it. RE-MEASURE the 600/19,666/200 first -- 2026-08-04 sightings on generation 91. Also fold in three MINOR notes from the same gate: the DDL declares FOREIGN KEY (igdb_run_id) REFERENCES ingest_runs(id) but ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN cannot carry it, so fresh and migrated databases diverge (benign, verified by PRAGMA); the backfill docstring claims 'one indexed scan' when there is no index on igdb_run_id and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN says SCAN (0.017s, harmless, but the claim is wrong); and the _table_exists/_column_exists guards in the backfill are unreachable from ensure_schema.
nodes.title: The foreign-key derivation goes short in exactly the way the hand-written list would have
nodes.why: Two columns hold v2_works.id with no declared key, so the PRAGMA that replaced a hand-kept list cannot see them either.

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04 by the RS-387 build and independently confirmed by the orchestrator against the live DB. v2_works.igdb_run_id names run 71 on 321,421 of 331,150 generation-91 works, while stg_igdb_games holds only run 85. The 9,729 rows that DO carry 85 are exactly the mods RS-359 minted -- so the only works with truthful IGDB provenance are the ones written fresh after that change, and every carried-over work still points at a staging generation that no longer exists. Same root cause as RS-387 (stage 50's ON CONFLICT restamps some columns and not others), but this is PROVENANCE, not a join key: nothing matches on it, so RS-387's re-derivation deliberately left it alone. It is also PINNED BY A TEST -- test_stage_contract.py::test_incremental_rerun_does_not_rewrite_content_columns exists to stop exactly this kind of rewrite -- so changing it means changing a deliberate contract, not fixing an oversight.
nodes.done_looks_like: A DECISION FIRST, then code. Either igdb_run_id means 'the staging generation this row's IGDB content came from' (and must be restamped when that content is re-read, which requires amending the stage-contract test and saying why), or it means 'the generation that first created this row' (and the column is misnamed -- rename it and document that it is creation provenance, not content provenance). Do not restamp it silently: the pinning test is deliberate and predates this finding. VERIFY: whichever reading is chosen, a query answers 'which staging generation is this work's IGDB data from' correctly for all 331,150 rows, and the stage-contract test either still passes or has been amended with its reasoning recorded. RE-MEASURE FIRST: 321,421 / 9,729 / run 71 vs 85 are 2026-08-04 sightings on generation 91.

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04 by the RS-360 Build B builder while judging its own repoints. The port cell tests whether the ENTRY'S work fails to list the release's platform -- it cannot test the control's, because for the 84 gains there is no control work to test. The plan called that choice forced and it is. But the claim the rule then makes is 'the entry's work does not describe this release', not 'the work does not', and those come apart: in 28 of 79 repoints the control's own IGDB record ALREADY listed the release's platform, so the rule displaced a work that fit. Contra (nes, 732 votes) is in this class and is correct -- the control was the Famicom-only record. Romance of the Three Kingdoms IV: Wall of Fire (saturn 18, psx 24) and Sonic Adventure (ps3 13, xbox360 23) are in it and are WRONG: control carried the exact title and already listed the platform. So the class is not uniformly bad and cannot simply be excluded -- it needs a second discriminator. Measured alongside: a random sample of 20 sub-50-vote repoints ran 14 entry-better / 5 control-better / 1 unclear, against 20 of 20 entry-better at >=50 votes. The design's evidence was gathered where the control had NO answer, which is why it did not see this.
nodes.done_looks_like: A discriminator that separates the Contra case from the Sonic Adventure case, or a recorded decision that the residue is accepted and handled by review instead. EITHER IS A VALID OUTCOME -- the owner has already accepted a reviewable residue once (2026-08-04, choosing to ship the port rule minus alias-tier repoints), so do not assume code is required. What is required is that the choice is made on measurement rather than inherited by default. VERIFY: the >=50-vote band stays 20 of 20 entry-better; the sub-50 error rate is re-measured on a fresh sample and REPORTED AS A FIGURE whether or not it moved; Contra, Bubble Bobble and Pro Wrestling still repoint; Romance of the Three Kingdoms IV and Sonic Adventure do not. RE-MEASURE FIRST -- 28/79, 84 gains and the 14/5/1 sample are 2026-08-04 sightings taken against a clone at generations 89/91/92, before Build B merged and before any rebuild.

nodes.body: Container created 2026-08-04 at the owner's direction: get the export done, then bucket the tidy-up. Everything here is real and none of it blocks stage 70 -- the export reads release-grain data (games, rom_entries, rom_hashes, game_filenames, game_names, libretro_thumbnails) and reads the works layer NOT AT ALL, so every works-layer improvement in this bucket is parallel to it rather than upstream of it. Members fall into four kinds: (a) the reviewer's surface -- queues, conflict reporting, the README and a CLI, which is what makes curation ergonomic rather than possible; (b) curation expressiveness -- what a reviewer can record about a work they minted; (c) known-wrong data with no live consumer; (d) guards and vocabularies that work but drift. NOTE RS-383 is deliberately NOT here: it is a defect in the export stage 70 replaces, so it belongs to RS-166 as a do-not-reimplement constraint.

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04 by the RS-388 Build 3 gate, while verifying a DIFFERENT claim that turned out to be fabricated. work_merge.py:189-199 publishes work_merges_applied = len(self.merges) -- the count of resolved LINES IN THE FILE -- while what stage 50 actually did is tracked separately as work_merge_map_rows_created and work_merges_survivor_missing. So the key says 'applied' and means 'loaded'. This is EXACTLY the misnomer RS-388 Build 3 fixed in the sibling class: VerdictFile.as_stats published verdicts_applied = len(self.verdicts) and was renamed verdicts_loaded on the reasoning that A CLASS THAT READS A FILE CANNOT KNOW WHAT A STAGE DID WITH IT. That reasoning applies here unchanged and this class was not touched. NOTE HOW IT WAS FOUND: Build 3's docstring justified keeping a group-level key by citing 'GroupOutcome.as_stats' -- a class and a key that HAVE NEVER EXISTED (one grep hit, in that sentence; git log -S returns only the commit that added it). The gate went looking for the contrast the docstring named, could not find it, and found the real sibling instead. A genuine defect was sitting behind a fabricated reference.
nodes.done_looks_like: work_merges_applied either means what a stage applied, or is renamed to say what it counts. PREFER THE RENAME, matching verdicts_loaded -- a class constructed from a file genuinely cannot know what a stage did with it, and stage 50 already publishes the honest figures separately (work_merge_map_rows_created, work_merges_survivor_missing). VERIFY: no key named *_applied is emitted by a class whose only input is a parsed file; grep the repo for other instances of the same shape before assuming these two were the only pair. MIND THE HISTORY DISCONTINUITY -- the RS-388 rename already created one in ingest_runs.stats_json (run 107 recorded verdicts_applied, later runs record verdicts_loaded), and nothing reads those keys programmatically, but a human comparing runs across the change sees a key vanish. Say so in the commit rather than leaving it to be discovered. SMALL: this is a rename plus its tests, and the RS-388 precedent measured the blast radius at two test assertions with no Rust, no docs and no scripts. Re-measure that for this key rather than assuming it matches.
nodes.title: MergeFile.as_stats reports work_merges_applied as the line count, not what stage 50 did
nodes.why: One of two sibling classes was corrected and the other was not, so the codebase now states two different things about the same word in two files.

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04 while correcting a fabricated docstring reference in RS-388 Build 3, and confirmed independently by the orchestrator. verdicts.py declares split_group and join_group in VALID_VERDICTS, parses them, and builds a GroupPlan (verdicts.py:832) that emits group_verdicts_applied. But apply_group_verdicts HAS NO PRODUCTION CALLER: the only non-test reference in the whole repo is docs/PIPELINE_SPEC.md:762, which describes it as though it runs ('verdicts.apply_group_verdicts re-partitions the mapping'). GroupPlan.as_stats is likewise reached only from tests/test_verdicts.py:1037. So a reviewer can write a split_group or join_group line, the loader will accept it, the stats will count it, and NO STAGE WILL EVER ACT ON IT. This is the same silent-inertness RS-388 exists to remove -- and unlike the title-only alias (RS-408, which turned out to degrade to an attach rather than do nothing), this one genuinely does nothing at all. It is also why a docstring justifying a stats-key rename by saying group_verdicts_applied 'counts group verdicts the stage actually acted on' was false twice over: the class name was invented AND no stage acts on them.
nodes.done_looks_like:
EITHER a stage applies group verdicts, OR the pipeline refuses them at parse time with a counted reason and the spec stops saying they run. DO NOT LEAVE THE THIRD STATE -- accepted, counted, inert -- which is exactly the defect RS-388 was built to remove.

DECIDE ON EVIDENCE OF DEMAND: check whether curation/work_verdicts.jsonl has ever carried a split_group or join_group line, and whether the review queue produces a case that wants one. If nothing has ever needed them, refusing is the honest answer and is cheap; building an applier for a kind nobody writes repeats the game_works situation (128,403 rows carried for 'browsing that does not exist yet').

VERIFY whichever is chosen: a group verdict written into the file either changes the source-link partition and says so in the stats, or is reported as refused with a reason -- not silently counted. And docs/PIPELINE_SPEC.md:762 agrees with the code either way.

CHECK THE SIBLING WHILE THERE: RS-411 covers MergeFile.as_stats publishing work_merges_applied as a line count. Same file-versus-stage confusion, one table over. They may be worth doing together since both are about a stats key claiming a stage acted.
nodes.title: Group verdicts are documented, loaded and never applied by any stage
nodes.why: Two of the eight verdict kinds are accepted, counted and never applied, and the pipeline spec states they run.

nodes.body: A raw PS2 .bin carries a readable SYSTEM.CNF serial (verified 2026-08-20: 'Dynamite Deka (Japan).bin' -> SLPM-62717) but config/systems_manifest.tsv does not admit .bin for ps2, so the scanner never sees it.
nodes.done_looks_like:
A raw PS2 .bin is discovered, classified, matched by its embedded SYSTEM.CNF serial, and launched, without any .bin belonging to a .cue set being counted as a game of its own.

Re-measure first. 2026-08-20 sightings: config/systems_manifest.tsv currently gives ps2 [".chd",".iso",".cso"], while psx already gives [".chd",".cue",".bin",".iso",".pbp"] and megadrive gives [".md",".bin",".gen",".zip",".7z"]. "Dynamite Deka (Japan).bin" reads SLPM-62717 from SYSTEM.CNF.

THE PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTS - inherit it rather than inventing a second mechanism. psx has admitted .bin beside .cue for some time, and rom_scanner/classification.rs already resolves a .cue to its referenced .bin and emits ONE finding whose launch_rel_path is the .cue (see the Game.cue and Disc 1.cue tests around classification.rs:907 and :866, and the broken-cue case at :933). Establish by test that ps2 gets that same behaviour, and that a BARE .bin with no .cue beside it is still discovered rather than suppressed by the pairing logic - that bare case is the entire point of the item.

These are the tests: a ps2 .cue plus its .bin yields exactly one game, launching the .cue; a bare ps2 .bin yields exactly one game and matches on its embedded serial; a multi-track .cue set yields one game, not one per track.

THE MANIFEST HAS TWO CONSUMERS. config/systems_manifest.tsv is parsed by Python AND by Rust with different rules, so this change must be gated against cargo test as well as the Python suite. Say explicitly which consumers you exercised.

State whether admitting .bin changes what the ps2 hash tier does. RS-579 established that container formats whose own hash can never equal a Redump raw-image hash should not be hashed at all; a raw .bin is NOT a container, so it may legitimately hash - confirm which side of that line it falls on rather than assuming.

nodes.body: 1,978 v1 slugs are absent from the current catalogue and 1,803 of them still exist under the same LaunchBox id with a new catalogue id. The frozen crosswalk could map them, but it is not shipped to instances, so backfill-release-ref leaves those rows NULL.
nodes.done_looks_like:
A library matched against an older catalogue can still publish its identities, or the limit is recorded as accepted with the reason.

THE SHAPE, measured 2026-08-20 during the RS-371 review - re-measure at dispatch. The current catalogue holds 144,854 carried v1 slugs and 19,842 minted lb- ids. 1,978 mappable v1 slugs are absent from it, and 1,803 OF THOSE STILL EXIST under the same LaunchBox id with a new catalogue id. A user whose library was scanned against the older v1 catalogue therefore has release_id values that resolve to nothing today: backfill-release-ref leaves them NULL and, as of RS-371, tells them plainly that their library was matched against an older catalogue and that --master may help.

That message is honest but it points at a file a user does not have. The recovery path exists in principle: old slug -> launchbox_id -> current release, using the FROZEN crosswalk at pipeline_v2/data/legacy_release_ids.tsv.gz (146,832 rows keyed on launchbox_id and platform). It is frozen precisely because it is a historical fact about what v1 shipped and what users have on disk.

THE DESIGN QUESTION, which is the actual work: the crosswalk is not shipped to instances today. Decide whether it should be - as its own file, folded into the catalogue export, or not at all. Each has a cost. Folding it into game_reference.db grows a 436MB file that every instance syncs; shipping it separately adds a second artifact the deploy must keep in step with the catalogue; not shipping it accepts that these users stay unpublished.

Do NOT assume the recovery is worth shipping. Measure the population that would actually benefit first: this affects only libraries matched before the 2026-08-04 export, so on THIS instance the number is ZERO - all 859 games resolve. If the only affected population is hypothetical, recording the limit and keeping the honest warning may be the right answer, and saying so plainly closes this.

If it IS built: a recovered id must be published only where the crosswalk maps the old slug to exactly one current release. Where it maps to none or several, the row stays NULL and keeps its release_id. Pin both refusals with positive controls.
nodes.title: Libraries matched against the older catalogue cannot publish 1,803 recoverable identities
nodes.why: Split out of RS-371 on 2026-08-20 rather than built: the recovery needs the frozen crosswalk to reach an instance, which is a shipping decision about a 436MB artifact, not a detail of the backfill.

nodes.body: LaunchBox knows the regional titles and the pipeline ingests them, but stage 70 drops them: game_names.region is NULL on all 296,968 exported rows. Cheap and additive - but NOTHING in the app can display an alternate name today, so this is groundwork, not a feature.
nodes.done_looks_like: The shipped game_reference.db carries region on alternate names, and a name_type that distinguishes a proper regional title from a filename-shaped string. GROUNDWORK ONLY - nothing in the app can display an alternate name today, so this ships data and no feature. (1) A STAGE-70 EXPORTER CHANGE ONLY. v2_release_aliases (the table stage 70 reads) has NO region column; region is joined back from stg_launchbox_alt_names on (games.launchbox_id, alternate_name). Measured 2026-08-27: 62,401 of 296,968 exported game_names rows join at all and 39,837 (13.4%) gain a non-empty region; the other 79% are libretro-sourced aliases with no region to give. No upstream re-run, no Stage 40 change. Re-measure - these are sightings. (2) name_type = 'regional' where a region is present; rows without one keep 'alternate'. ⚠️ 'derived_equivalence' MUST SURVIVE UNTOUCHED - src-tauri/tests/release_equivalence_scanner.rs:24 asserts it on a curated PS2 row (Jin Samguk Mussang (Korea)). (3) THE ROW COUNT MUST NOT CHANGE. A new game_names row is a new first-wins match candidate, which is the regression _project_game_names exists to prevent. Assert the count before and after. (4) NO SCHEMA BUMP: game_names.region and name_type are ALREADY declared columns of the schema-8 export contract. Assert the export still declares schema_version 8 and that catalogue_schema.rs MAX_SUPPORTED_CATALOGUE_SCHEMA_VERSION is untouched. If any part of this adds a COLUMN it becomes schema 9, check_supported() hard-refuses it, and the Rust ceiling plus an app rebuild and redeploy join the item - at which point STOP and re-scope. (5) PURELY ADDITIVE, VERIFIED: ensure_name_cache (matcher.rs:2394-2445) selects gn.name only, with no WHERE on name_type and no region; the provenance rank is a SQL literal per UNION arm, i.e. which TABLE, not what name_type says. Still prove no match moves - with rematch_system_roms, NOT a rescan (a rescan skips any file whose size and mtime are unchanged, so the matcher never runs and the assertion passes whatever the export did). Assert the matched count and the matched SET are identical and that a non-zero number of files was considered. (6) SPOT-CHECKED CASES, asserted by name AND region: Bare Knuckle -> Japan (megadrive), Green Beret -> World (mame), Buster Bros. -> North America (mame), Flying Shark -> Europe (mame). (7) REGIONS ARE NOT NORMALISED HERE. Record the distinct values; the vocabularies genuinely differ and a consumer will need an explicit crosswalk, not a string compare - LaunchBox says both 'North America' (2,446) and 'United States' (563) where rom_files says 'USA'; 'United Kingdom' vs 'UK'; rom_files has 'Taiwan', LaunchBox has only 'China'/'Hong Kong'. (8) OUT OF SCOPE: clone_of (it would add a column, hence schema 9, for data nothing reads); and the display side, whose honest reach is 215 games with a wholly different name out of 25,081 matched files, and which needs a consumer that does not exist.
nodes.title: Export regional alternate names as groundwork (stage 70 only, no schema bump)
nodes.why: Measured 2026-08-27. LaunchBox knows Bare Knuckle is Japan, Green Beret is World, Buster Bros. is North America - for console AND arcade (Rush'n Attack/mame carries Green Beret). Everything we spent the session working around - CoinOPS naming disagreements, arcade titles, regional variants - is answerable from data we already ingest and drop at the last step. nodes.body: MAME organises games as a parent set plus clones. Parent-default is 99.8% decisive on ambiguous held families and agrees with human curation 712 of 773 times; the ~61 disagreements ship as default-origin overrides through RS-771's mechanism. Explicitly NOT a region rule.
nodes.done_looks_like: Arcade games launch the parent set unless a shipped override says otherwise, and the user can override either. (1) The arcade rule is PARENT BY DEFAULT. Re-measure the sightings: of Tom's held arcade sets, 3,199 families have more than one held file and the parent is held in 3,194 of them (99.8%); the 5 exceptions are atom, bbcm, ibm5170, punirune, sltpcycl - BBC Micro, IBM PC and slot machines, i.e. not arcade at all. (2) The ~61 measured disagreements ship as DEFAULT-ORIGIN override rows through RS-771's mechanism - not a second mechanism, not an arcade-specific table. A user override of a shipped default wins and survives upgrade. (3) NO REGION RULE, and do not reintroduce one. Measured 2026-08-27 against 773 families where a human deliberately picked one file: as a preference over parent-default, Europe rescues 0 of the 61 parent-default misses and BREAKS 10 of the 712 it gets right; North America and Japan are far worse. Only 185 of 18,744 held arcade sets carry region 'Europe' at all. The residue is editorial - renames (pacman/puckman, gaiden/shadoww, slyspy/secretag) and 2-player boards chosen over 4-player (gauntlet, simpsons, tmnt) - which region cannot see. (4) The 61 are recorded with provenance as harvested data, NOT as a CoinOPS concept in the model. (5) HONESTY ABOUT THE GROUND TRUTH: the 61 come from one build's curation, not objective truth. Each override row must be individually inspectable and individually removable, so a disagreement is a one-row edit rather than an argument with a dataset. (6) BLOCKED UNTIL ARCADE IS ACTUALLY IMPORTED: Tom's instance holds ZERO mame/arcade/fbneo rows today because classify_arcade is gated to system_key=='neogeo' (scanner.rs:283). Any figure here is a projection off the share until that changes - re-measure against rom_files, not a filesystem walk.

nodes.body: Write //! headers for rom_scanner/scanner.rs and matcher.rs. 7,103 PRODUCTION lines between them (scanner 3,099, matcher 4,004) — the files are 20,730 total but 72% and 57% of them are tests.
nodes.done_looks_like: src-tauri/src/rom_scanner/scanner.rs and matcher.rs each carry a //! header meeting the CLAUDE.md convention: what the module owns, what it deliberately refuses, an invariant it holds, and what it hands off to — each saying something the signatures do not, and neither restating the module name. Both files today carry `//` prose (scanner.rs:1, matcher.rs:1), which is the exact trap CLAUDE.md names: it is invisible to every tool that looks for docs. FALSIFIABILITY IS REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL: at least one claim per header is pinned by a NAMED test — an existing one where it already exists (tests/source_folders.rs already pins 'the mapping is the scan' for scanner.rs), a new one in seam_contracts.rs otherwise — and a new test is PROVEN TO BITE by breaking it deliberately and restoring it. If RS-985's header-coverage ratchet has landed, both files are removed from its list in the same change, or its stale-entry arm fails. Without this the whole leaf is satisfiable by four confident wrong sentences that pass cargo check — and matcher.rs is the module the 'fuzzy tier is off limits' rule governs, so a wrong 'refuses' line there becomes a published claim other agents act on. docs/generated/modules.md shows a purpose for both modules (assert the two entries, NOT a coverage delta — the percentage moves whenever any module is added). Note save_contract/tests.rs:2117 walks src-tauri/src for banned phrases within a +/-2 line window, so the two new //! blocks are inside the scanned set. The workspace suite figure is measured ON THE LEAF'S OWN SUBMITTED COMMIT: run cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast before and after the change on that same commit, zero failed both times, and no test removed or renamed. 'Same as before' naming no commit is a sighting, not an invariant (tools/game-database-v2/docs/ACCEPTANCE_CONVENTION.md), and RS-978 is in flight and adds tests, so a rebase changes the count for an innocent reason.

DROPPED 2026-08-03 after measurement (scoping analysis). The headline reproducer NO LONGER REPRODUCES: windows Final Fantasy VIII (2000) sits correctly on the 1999 original and FF VIII Remastered (2019) on the Remastered work -- the release layer now carries them as two distinct releases. The 11 became 723 releases sitting on an original where a remaster shares the platform, and only ONE survives scrutiny: Sid Meier's Pirates!: Live the Life (xbox 2004 -> the 1987 work at tier_7). Its cause is not remaster preference -- the correct 2004 work exists but IGDB lists no Xbox for it, so the platform gate blocks it while RS-234's port-widening gave Xbox to the 1987 work, which wins at year-blind tier_7. A platform-gate plus year-blind-tier failure wearing a remaster costume.

Two candidate rules were built and both fail on titles that were read: a year rule (<=1y to remaster, >=2y to original) gives 28 rows about a third wrong INCLUDING the highest-vote row (FF XV: Windows Edition -> FF XV: Pocket Edition); a platform-nativity rule gives 53 rows about 95 percent wrong (Resident Evil 4 (2005) -> the 2023 remake, FF VII (1998) -> FF VII Remake). The blocker is structural: a 2016 release of a 1982 game is equally likely to be a re-release or a remaster and nothing in the data separates them -- Classic NES Series, Famicom Mini, ARCADE GAME SERIES, SEGA AGES all misfire. Rejected-rule evidence is in the scoping artifacts.

The 11 known cases resolve correctly: windows 'Final Fantasy VIII' attaches to the Remastered work, xbox "Sid Meier's Pirates! Live the Life" to the modern work rather than the 1987 original. Re-measure the 11 first — the count is against RS-234's output and will move if anything upstream lands. No release that correctly matches an original today is moved onto a remaster it should not have. python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Stage 55 can prefer an original over its own remaster once ports widen platforms
nodes.why: Measured 2026-07-28 while planning RS-234. It is a real regression that fix introduces, small and worth shipping against 2,133 gains, but it should not stay unfixed or unrecorded.

nodes.body: The RS-181 harness reports v2's libretro SHA1 arm identifying fewer releases than v1 on core consoles (psx -184 on a denominator that moved +32, snes -114, xbox360 -108, gba -73; about 500 across seven systems). That was filed as a v2 regression. It cannot be, because nothing establishes v1 as correct. Measured on v1: match_type is NULL on ALL 134,468 matched rom_entries, so v1 records no provenance for any match. By match_score, of the releases v1 counts as identified, 10,226 rest on 0.95-0.99, 3,070 on 0.85-0.94, and 1,419 on scores BELOW 0.85 -- under v1's own documented fuzzy floor. For psx specifically: 3,489 exact, 1,170 at 0.95-0.99, 87 fuzzy, 52 sub-threshold. So part or all of the gap may be v2 correctly declining matches v1 made wrongly.
nodes.done_looks_like: A judged sample settles the direction rather than an argument: at least 40 psx cases where v1 resolves a release and v2 does not, each hand-checked and recorded as v2-wrong (a real regression), v1-wrong (v2 correctly declined), or unresolvable, with the counts stated; the same for at least 20 snes cases; the verdicts are stored where they can be re-read rather than living in a report, which is what v2_quality_spot_checks.human_verdict exists for and it is currently NULL on all 200 rows; whichever direction the evidence points is written into PIPELINE_SPEC.md with its sample size; if v2 is genuinely losing matches, the cause is named and the fixable part fixed with the RS-181 harness re-run to show the numerator rising; RS-181's report 5 gains a line stating that v1's arm counts fuzzy and sub-threshold matches equally with exact ones, and naming the 1,419 sub-0.85 releases, so the comparison is never read as like-for-like accuracy; python -m pytest tools/game-database-v2/tests -q reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: Compare v1 and v2 on match ACCURACY, not match count
nodes.why: A count of matches is not a measure of quality, and choosing v2 over v1 on a number that treats a fuzzy name guess as equal to a hash would repeat the RS-171 error at a larger scale.

nodes.body: Found while building RS-297, out of its scope, left alone deliberately. The port_chain branch writes a map row and then the ordinary port pass writes a second for the same igdb_id, both pointing at the same work -- which is why v2_work_igdb_map holds 8,190 port rows for 8,147 ports. Its name also misdescribes it: 42 of the 43 are ports whose parent_game_id names an entry IGDB never staged, making them their own root; exactly one is a type-11 entry with no parent. No production reader consults mapping_reason today, so this is a correctness-of-record issue rather than a live defect -- but the map is about to become the join everything else uses.
nodes.done_looks_like: One map row per igdb_id, proven by a uniqueness assertion in the stage rather than a count that happens to be right; the port row count equals the port count; mapping_reason names what actually happened, with the 42 missing-parent cases distinguished from the 1 true chain case; pytest reports 0 failed.
nodes.title: port_chain writes two map rows per port and is named for the rare case
nodes.why: A table that double-counts is a table every future measurement has to know a special case about.

nodes.body: Wire MAME 0.252's source-evidenced ordinary play state—at minimum NVRAM and first-party hiscores—to declared canonical roots below saves/mame/. Exclude cfg/input, states, ROMs and reconstructible support data; reach upgraded instances and preserve clean-exit flushing.
nodes.done_looks_like: The RS-111 evidence row enumerates included/excluded MAME 0.252 write paths and corrects hi/ to homepath/hiscore. Shipped declarations and production wiring route effective NVRAM and hiscore writes to bounded units under saves/mame/ for fresh and upgraded instances, using MAME-native options or a justified computed link/junction. Synthetic fixtures survive device/ deletion/reprovision and pass checkout/check-in/tombstone coverage; cfg, states, ROMs and undeclared files never enumerate. macOS wrapper and Windows direct-launch tests address the real MAME process on stop, the delivery maps evidence to implementation/tests, and targeted plus full Rust tests pass without GUI or personal installs.
nodes.title: MAME's nvram and hiscores are play state with nowhere to sync from
nodes.why: MAME NVRAM and hiscores are accumulated play state that the RetroArch-only service cannot reach. The prior hi/ and device-tier rescope was wrong: MAME 0.252's first-party plugin uses homepath/hiscore, and durable bytes belong under saves/ by the canonical product-v2 architecture.

nodes.body: Noticed by RS-359's builder while adding mod_of, 2026-08-04, and deliberately left alone rather than widened silently. browser/db.py INVERSES is missing expanded_from and standalone_expansion_of, so the browser renders their reverse direction as the fallback 'target_of_<type>' string instead of a readable inverse. Pre-existing; RS-359 added only mod_of, which is what it was entitled to touch. Small and self-contained -- the kind of thing worth doing while something else is being gated.
nodes.done_looks_like: Every relationship type in v2_work_relationships has an entry in browser/db.py INVERSES, and the browser renders no 'target_of_' string for any of them. Derive the check from the relationship types the pipeline can actually emit rather than from a hand-written list, so a type added later fails the test instead of rendering as a fallback -- that is the difference between fixing two rows and fixing the class. Name the inverse wording chosen for each and confirm it reads as a sentence in the direction shown.
nodes.title: The browser renders two relationship types as target_of_ because INVERSES never learned them
nodes.why: A reader sees 'target_of_expanded_from' where the sentence should read the other way round.

nodes.body: Found by RS-199's gate, 2026-08-04, which verified the chain by READING it end to end and could not assert it. api/mod.rs:1667 copies outcome.failures into ScanLibrarySourcesResult.failed_systems and formats each as '{system} (source {id}): {err}'. The gate mutated that to return Vec::new() and NOTHING WENT RED -- five lines of pure shaping inside an async fn needing AppState, with no test either side and no frontend suite. The rest of the chain is sound and was traced hop by hop (scanner.rs -> api/mod.rs -> commands/mod.rs:645 -> api.ts:172 -> types.ts:122 -> RomSourcesModal.tsx:108-116 -> ToastHost.tsx:49, mounted at App.tsx:598), with exactly one caller at each end. The gate declined to fix it because making it testable means extracting a formatter from production code on the scan-failure path, over its fix boundary.
nodes.done_looks_like: Returning an empty failure list from api::scan_library_sources turns the suite red. The gate's suggested shape, worth following unless something better presents: give SystemScanFailure a describe() -> String carrying the '{system} (source {id}): {err}' formatting, unit-test THAT, and leave api/mod.rs a .map(SystemScanFailure::describe) -- which moves the logic somewhere testable rather than adding a test that mirrors it. Verify by applying the gate's exact mutation (failed_systems: Vec::new()) and confirming it now fails. While there, consider whether the same shape exists on other async fns in api/mod.rs that transform a result for the UI -- one untested shaping hop is a bug, several is a pattern.
nodes.title: Nothing asserts the scan's failure list survives the five lines that shape it for the UI
nodes.why: RS-199 exists so a failed system reaches a human, and the one hop that could drop it is the one hop no test covers.

nodes.body: Ship the RetroStack master, client, admin and viewer across macOS, Windows and Linux/handheld, with loopback and enrolled-client topologies verified.
nodes.title: Platform & Device Support
nodes.why: The v2 runtime is currently macOS-first; widening it requires shared-core portability plus platform-specific packaging, provisioning, input and launch work.

nodes.body: Remove macOS assumptions from the shared core, HTTP server, browser/Tauri admin, viewer, reconcile, provisioning and runner.
nodes.title: Platform Fundamentals (cross-platform)
nodes.why: Product v2 shares one Rust core and web viewer across roles, so platform-neutral foundations now live below every master/client shell rather than in the generator.

nodes.body: Windows master, streaming-host and client verification, defects, packaging and runner support.
nodes.title: Windows Platform Support
nodes.why: Windows code paths exist, and the accepted model makes Windows a first-class master/streaming-host platform; they have not been verified end to end.

nodes.body: Linux master/client support plus the ROCKNIX handheld client on AYN Odin 3.
nodes.title: Linux & Handheld Support
nodes.why: Linux is both a viable master/streaming host and the route to the motivating handheld client; the old export-target framing retired with product v1.

nodes.body: Make Linux a first-class platform across instance identity, shared Rust core, retrostack-server, viewer shell, reconcile, provisioning and runner.
nodes.done_looks_like: The core and retrostack-server build on x86_64 Linux; an instance reports platform=linux without a macOS fallback; a Linux client can enrol, reconcile its associated collection, provision or resolve an emulator, open the viewer and launch a game; no v2 platform match silently defaults to macOS.
nodes.title: Third platform through the stack
nodes.why: Platform detection still contains macOS fallbacks; under product v2 that would misidentify a Linux instance and poison server, provisioning and runner decisions.

nodes.body: Generate settings.conf, launcher .conf files and the launch script from per-platform templates instead of two inline hardcoded strings.
nodes.done_looks_like: settings.conf emits the correct launcherFolder and renderer for the target platform; the launch script comes from a per-platform template with no osascript off macOS; a macOS and a Windows build each produce paths that resolve on that platform.
nodes.title: Platform-aware settings.conf and launch-script generation
nodes.why: generate_global_settings() takes no platform parameter and hardcodes launcherFolder = launchers.apple, so Windows builds emit the macOS launcher folder today.

nodes.body: Expose renderer, decode, motion and logging choices as per-device viewer/runner preferences instead of RetroFE build-profile fields.
nodes.done_looks_like: Supported clients select platform-correct viewer rendering and video decode defaults; device preferences can override the supported settings; release clients do not emit debug logging; no product-v2 path writes RetroFE renderer settings.
nodes.title: Per-device viewer render and video preferences
nodes.why: HardwareVideoAccel is hardcoded false and SDLRenderDriver is never emitted, so every platform runs software decode against a Windows-oriented default renderer.

nodes.body: Produce content-addressed, viewer-ready video variants for collection manifests while leaving source media untouched.
nodes.done_looks_like: Saving a collection selects a normalised derived variant at configured resolution/bitrate for client delivery; source assets remain untouched; reconcile deduplicates the variant by hash; the measured MAME corpus shrinks materially while playback remains visually equivalent at theme size.
nodes.title: Media optimisation pipeline for build-bound video
nodes.why: MAME snaps are 1080p at 6.4Mbps (~25MB average across 987 files, ~24GB) against 640x480 console snaps, so decode cost and build size vary wildly for no visible gain.

nodes.body: Populate Linux emulator definitions and let client reconcile resolve system-provided emulators as well as downloadable ones.
nodes.done_looks_like: Emulator TOMLs carry Linux platform blocks; an enrolled Linux client can satisfy a manifest requirement from an on-device binary without downloading; an unsupported platform/emulator pair is reported as a provisioning gap without aborting unrelated reconcile work.
nodes.title: Emulator TOML platform coverage and system-provided provisioning
nodes.why: PlatformConfigs already exposes a linux field that no TOML populates, and provisioning assumes a macOS/Windows download-URL pair, which is wrong for ROCKNIX where emulators ship with the OS.

nodes.body: Build retrostack-server and the viewer runtime for Linux targets, and replace the macOS-only music hotkey helper with a platform-neutral or explicitly platform-scoped design.
nodes.done_looks_like: retrostack-server and the viewer run on x86_64 and aarch64 Linux clients; music control works on each supported platform or is explicitly unavailable with a visible reason; nothing is staged into a generated RetroFE build.
nodes.title: Viewer server, music and global-hotkey portability
nodes.why: The shared server/viewer code is portable Rust and web code, while deployed packaging and the Swift CGEventTap helper remain macOS-shaped.

nodes.body: Extend bootstrap and deploy scripts to each supported platform and add CI that produces a verified build per target.
nodes.title: Bootstrap, deploy and CI per platform
nodes.why: deploy.sh and postprocess_macos_app.sh are macOS-shaped and there is no CI, so non-macOS regressions stay invisible until someone runs a build by hand.

nodes.body: On a real Windows machine, install or bootstrap RetroStack, run a master or enrol a client, associate and reconcile a collection, open the first-party viewer and launch one game.
nodes.done_looks_like: A real Windows instance completes the chosen master/client flow, reconciles a saved collection, opens the RetroStack viewer and launches at least one game through the local runner; every defect encountered is captured as a Haven item.
nodes.title: End-to-end Windows v2 verification
nodes.why: Windows is required as a master/streaming-host platform, but the v2 transport, packaging, reconcile and runner path has not been exercised there end to end.

nodes.body: Fix defects found by Windows v2 verification: filesystem semantics, path separators, packaging, provisioning, input and local launch.
nodes.title: Windows defect fixes
nodes.why: The shared core and server contain Windows paths that remain unexercised; generator launcher-folder defects are no longer the target.

nodes.body: Produce a distributable Windows artifact containing the admin shell, retrostack-server, first-party viewer and required runtime assets.
nodes.title: Windows packaging and distribution
nodes.why: Windows users need an installable master/client app; bundling a generated RetroFE runtime is no longer the product target.

nodes.body: Build RetroFE for Linux and confirm it renders a themed collection with video snaps — this decides whether the Linux branch is viable at all.
nodes.done_looks_like: RetroFE built for aarch64 Linux launches a themed collection at 1080p with video snaps playing, or a documented verdict that it cannot with the specific blocking reason.
nodes.title: SPIKE: RetroFE on Linux (aarch64 and x86_64)
nodes.why: Everything else in the Linux branch is plumbing we control; RetroFE rendering on OpenGL/Freedreno is the one genuinely external unknown, so it should be de-risked before any hardware is bought.

nodes.body: Run a working RetroStack master/client loopback instance on conventional x86_64 Linux, including the first-party viewer and one local launch.
nodes.done_looks_like: On x86_64 Linux, retrostack-server serves admin and viewer, the loopback master owns an associated collection, reconcile reaches current, and the local runner starts one game and returns to the viewer.
nodes.title: Linux desktop target (x86_64)
nodes.why: Proves the platform abstraction on a normal distro before taking on an immutable handheld OS.

nodes.body: Deliver a ROCKNIX client for its immutable rootfs and /storage layout: discover/enrol with a master, reconcile one collection, use system emulators and launch from the first-party viewer.
nodes.title: ROCKNIX / AYN Odin 3 handheld target
nodes.why: ROCKNIX on Odin 3 is the motivating handheld; product v2 makes it an enrolled client rather than an exported RetroFE folder.

nodes.body: Verify and enable GPU decode on Linux, including whether ROCKNIX's GStreamer ships the V4L2 elements needed on the Odin.
nodes.title: Hardware video decode on Linux
nodes.why: RetroFE documents HardwareVideoAccel as Windows-oriented, so the Linux decode path needs empirical confirmation rather than assumption.

nodes.body: Adapt controller mapping, exit hotkeys and theme scaling for a 1080p handheld screen alongside ROCKNIX conventions.
nodes.title: Handheld UX: controls, hotkeys and small-screen theming
nodes.why: ROCKNIX owns global hotkeys and controller autoconfiguration, and CoinOPS themes are designed for large displays.

nodes.body: Code audit of platform handling, video/GPU findings and ROCKNIX/Odin 3 research backing the RS-1 phase.
nodes.title: Platform & device support — audit and findings
nodes.why: Scoping the device-support stream surfaced concrete file-level findings that would otherwise be lost to chat history.

nodes.body: Port the windows-games GPTK bundling mechanism to Linux by swapping D3DMetal/Rosetta for DXVK-VKD3D/FEX and reusing ROCKNIX's provisioned Proton runtime.
nodes.title: PC-game launching through Proton on Linux targets
nodes.why: The Mac launcher mechanism at ~/Local_Projects/windows-games already makes portable Windows game folders launchable; the same three-layer translation exists on Linux and is more mature on the graphics side.

nodes.body: Verdict: RetroFE is well-designed but unfinished; keep it, fix the tooling, carry a small leaf patch set. Rebuild not warranted.
nodes.title: RetroFE frontend — capability assessment & fork strategy
nodes.why: Jul-2026 source audit of the CoinOPS RetroFE fork + competitive benchmark, prompted by 'should we rebuild the frontend?'

nodes.body: Carry a small, upstreamable patch set on the CoinOPS RetroFE fork — not a feature suite.
nodes.title: RetroFE fork
nodes.why: RS-22 assessment concluded: keep RetroFE, fix tooling, patch the leaves. Rebuild not warranted.

nodes.body: Fork from origin/current (NOT master), make CMake canonical on macOS, enable ASan+UBSan, add a golden smoke test, publish a release RetroStack can provision.
nodes.done_looks_like: A fork builds from clean on Apple Silicon via CMake; a debug preset runs with ASan+UBSan; a scripted-input smoke test exits 0 with no ASan report; a tagged release artifact exists and RetroStack can download it.
nodes.title: Stage 0: buildable RetroFE fork on macOS + safety net
nodes.why: No feature is safe to attempt first: 0 tests, 0 asserts, 99 new vs 58 delete, and the macOS packaging workflow has run exactly once.

nodes.body: Sort, group and jump by any metadata field in the first-party viewer; define the binding and navigation semantics for the current engine.
nodes.done_looks_like: A field RetroStack invents (e.g. qualityTier) can be sorted by, used as a *-playlist grouping key, and jumped through with shoulder buttons; collections.<x>.list.sortType starts working as the canary; hand-curated playlists whose filename collides with a field name keep their file order.
nodes.title: Viewer sort, group and jump by any metadata field
nodes.why: The need survived the RetroFE fork plan, but it is now a viewer-engine design and implementation task rather than a generated-metadata patch.

nodes.body: Restore the gutted _<collection>:<item> parse in updateLastPlayedPlaylist, and make it MERGE foreign entries instead of pruning — mirroring saveFavorites.
nodes.done_looks_like: With globalFavLast=true, launching games across three different systems yields a Favorites/playlists/lastplayed.txt containing entries from all three in _<collection>:<item> form, surviving repeated launches; the merged Favorites collection renders them.
nodes.title: Patch: global last-played stops eating itself
nodes.why: With globalFavLast on, every launch rebuilds the global lastplayed.txt from only the current collection and writes the pruned list back — destroying cross-system history. It is a data-loss bug, not an enhancement, so it is the most upstreamable patch in the set.

nodes.body: Non-blocking video unload; O(n^2)->O(n) collection load; texture-cache call site + cap; default.conf override order; %ITEM_INFO_<key>% launcher variable; timeSpent as a sortable field.
nodes.done_looks_like: Scrolling a video-backed list shows no periodic stall; a large collection re-entered repeatedly loads without growing cost; VRAM does not climb unbounded with the texture cache on; a per-game info value overrides default.conf; a launcher can substitute an arbitrary info field.
nodes.title: Patch set: leaf performance and dead-config fixes
nodes.why: Each is under ~40 lines, additive, leaf-level and individually upstreamable; together they remove the scroll stutter and several silently-dead config paths.

nodes.body: On-device search in the viewer via on-screen keyboard. Migrated from the RetroFE fork plan; letter-skip exists, search is the next navigation affordance.
nodes.title: On-device search via on-screen keyboard (phase 1)
nodes.why: The only capability in the whole catalogue the generator genuinely cannot fake. PARKED: at 1,160 curated games, letter-jump may be sufficient — revisit only after the generator-side QoL work lands.

nodes.body: columns attribute + stride parameter on ScrollingList::scroll (provably identity at stride 1, so existing themes are untouched). ~200 C++ LOC plus a boxart-only grid layout.
nodes.title: Conveyor grid: 2D boxart navigation
nodes.why: A custom menu already RENDERS a grid; it navigates in reading order because scroll() rotates by one. PARKED: needs a boxart pipeline and a new layout, and video previews must be off (blocking unload stalls a row scroll).

nodes.body: Box-art detail view via existing GAMEINFO states; rich metadata display via info/<name>.conf; Continue-playing row; genre/decade/curated playlists; multi-user via separate collections dirs; merged Favorites collection.
nodes.done_looks_like: A generated build shows a game detail view, per-game quality tier/player count/region from generated info files, a Continue-playing row, and at least three curated non-genre playlists — with no change to the RetroFE binary.
nodes.title: Generator-side frontend QoL — no fork required
nodes.why: Roughly 70% of the perceived QoL needs zero C++ — ReloadableText/ReloadableMedia already fall through to getInfo. Do this BEFORE any fork work, because it changes which fork features still look necessary.

nodes.body: launcherFolder/layoutFolder/fontFolder/mediaFolder are written to settings.conf and read by nothing in RetroFE — the light-build media redirect is a no-op today (real key is baseMediaPath). launcherFolder = launchers.apple is hardcoded regardless of target platform (src-tauri/src/generator/mod.rs:1755).
nodes.done_looks_like: Light builds actually redirect media via baseMediaPath and it is verified on device; the four dead keys are removed; launcherFolder is derived from the target platform, not hardcoded; a Windows build emits launchers.windows.
nodes.title: Generator emits dead settings.conf keys + hardcodes launchers.apple
nodes.why: Found during the Jul-2026 RetroFE source audit (RS-22). A format that never complains plus tooling that never validates produces silent wrongness — this is that diagnosis in miniature.

nodes.body: favorites.txt, lastplayed.txt, playCount.txt and timeSpent are user-owned mutable state that RetroFE writes on-device. A redeploy that overwrites collections/ destroys the player's history.
nodes.done_looks_like: Deploying a rebuilt profile over an instance that has accumulated favourites and play history preserves all four; a test proves history survives at least two consecutive redeploys.
nodes.title: Redeploy must merge user state, not overwrite it
nodes.why: RS-22 audit: these four are the only genuinely live on-device state RetroFE owns. Delta-deploy currently has no merge rule for them.

nodes.body: vSync defaults false; SDLRenderDriver ships direct3d (=D3D9) and the hint is inside #ifdef WIN32 so it is dead code on macOS/Linux; HardwareVideoAccel=false and is NOT a safe blind true (it flips appsink caps I420->NV12, and the __APPLE__ branch enables nothing); boxart should be <=512px because decode is synchronous on the render thread.
nodes.done_looks_like: Generated settings.conf sets vSync=true; direct3d11 on Windows only; HardwareVideoAccel set from a tested per-platform profile rather than a blanket flag; the asset pipeline caps boxart at 512px.
nodes.title: Fix the shipped RetroFE defaults per platform
nodes.why: RS-22 audit: hardware acceleration is on by default and cannot be accidentally disabled, but the shipped defaults leave real performance on the table. All one-liners in generated config.

nodes.body: (1) Does <reloadableVideo selectedOffset="1" alpha="0"/> actually preroll the next item's video? (2) Measured highlight->first-video-frame latency, and load time for the largest realistic collection on target hardware.
nodes.done_looks_like: A written answer with measured numbers for both, obtained by running a real build — not by reading source. If selectedOffset prerolls, the idiom is encoded in the theme template.
nodes.title: SPIKE: measure the two numbers the frontend decision rests on

nodes.body: RetroFE silently ignores unknown attributes and hard-fails on almost nothing, so wrongness is invisible. nodes.body: A layer stays a rectangle until it declares points; then its box is derived from the bounding box so fit is unchanged and nothing without a shape is affected. Polygon, ellipse and curved edges compile to one internal primitive (clip-path polygon/ellipse/path). Per-edge: soft (one gradient mask each, intersected) and stroke (SVG sibling, since a stroke on the clipped element loses its outer half). Per-layer: shadow, applied to a wrapper holding artwork+stroke so it traces the outside of the stroke. Engine derives gradient angles, stop positions, inward normals and Bezier controls; a theme writes only numbers.

nodes.done_looks_like: Config rows carry a backend scope (generic | proton | d3dmetal | winlator). Generic rows — required runtimes, DLL overrides, Windows version, launch target and args — resolve for all three backends; backend-specific rows resolve only for their own and never leak (a DXVK-version row must not reach a D3DMetal launch). Coverage is reportable as the share of PC releases carrying at least one generic row. The 237 lines of hand-validated fixes in ~/Local_Projects/windows-games/lib/quirks.sh are ingested as a first-party source with provenance.
nodes.title: Wine/Proton/CrossOver per-game config as a catalogue source
nodes.why: PC titles are a primary content type on every client, and the same game needs different fixes per backend — CrossOver/D3DMetal on Mac, Winlator on Android, umu/Proton on Linux.

nodes.body: Model game capability (takes a lightgun / wheel / trackball) separately from peripheral profile (how to configure emulator E for device P), and join them to emit config for every capable game in a library.
nodes.done_looks_like: Capability lives on the release in the catalogue (seeded from MAME -listxml, RS-347); peripheral profiles are a small curated set keyed on (emulator, device class), not on any game. Enabling a device emits correct config for every capable game in the instance library without per-game input, and games lacking the capability are untouched. The binding survives a reboot: device enumeration order is not stable (Windows reshuffles mouse indexes, so lightguns stop working between boots; Linux and Android have the same hazard), so a device is identified by something durable rather than by index. Reportable as: how many games in this library become playable with device P.
nodes.title: Peripheral profiles: make a lightgun or wheel a switch you flick
nodes.why: Owner's ask 2026-08-03: owning a Sinden lightgun or a Logitech wheel should be one switch, not per-game setup — and the capability half is reference data the catalogue can hold for all known games.

nodes.body: stg_source_files carries path/size/mtime/sha256 but no source URL, fetch timestamp or upstream version token. Record provenance for ALL sources. Change-detection effort scales with how fast a source moves: fast (ProtonDB, WineHQ, Steam, IGDB), slow-but-versioned (config packs tracking MAME releases, MAME itself), closed (retired-console DATs).
nodes.done_looks_like: Every Stage 0 fetch records the request URL, fetch time, and whatever version token the source exposes (HTTP ETag/Last-Modified, git commit SHA, MediaWiki revid, API updated-at), stored against the resulting file alongside its sha256. Given only the database, any corpus file can be traced to the exact request that produced it. Each source also carries a re-fetchability status, so a withdrawn or paywalled source (WarpedPolygon's MAME packs were public on the LaunchBox forums and GitHub, now Patreon-only) is visibly irreplaceable rather than silently assumed reconstructible — that status is what backup policy keys off. A staleness check is answerable without re-downloading the payload where the source exposes a token; sources exposing none are recorded as such. Honours RS-206: this enables targeted re-fetch, it does not mandate incremental fetch where measurement rejected it.
nodes.title: Record fetch provenance, not just file provenance — URL, time and upstream revision per source
nodes.why: Owner 2026-08-03: config sources must be recreatable from files or re-scrapable, and change detection needs a version token to compare against; the RS-346/347/348 scrape sources make this acute.

nodes.body: A hotkey mid-game pauses the emulator and draws a RetroStack overlay on top — controller layout for this game, save states, game info, music control, exit. The BigBox pause screen is the reference.
nodes.done_looks_like: A configured hotkey during play suspends the running emulator and presents a RetroStack overlay above it; dismissing resumes the same session with no state loss. The overlay shows the control layout for the running game where one exists. Exit-to-frontend from the overlay terminates the emulator cleanly, so emulator-written state (NVRAM, cfg, saves) is flushed — see RS-350. Platform asymmetry is recorded rather than assumed: on desktop the emulator process can be genuinely suspended; on Android the emulator can only be backgrounded, so the Android behaviour is defined explicitly instead of degrading silently.
nodes.title: Custom pause overlay: interrupt a running game with RetroStack's own menu
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-03: the feature he most values in BigBox, and the natural home for per-game controller layouts — you forget which button is punch mid-fight, not at the menu. Never captured before today.

nodes.body: Config packs encode mappings for one physical layout (WarpedPolygon is XInput-only). Resolve an abstract control requirement — buttons, joystick ways, analogue axes — against the target device's layout and the runner's format, rather than shipping someone else's pad.
nodes.done_looks_like: A game's control requirement is held abstractly (from MAME -listxml per RS-347, or from an imported pack) and emitted per (target device, runner) — MAME cfg XML, RetroArch remap, or an emulator's own format. An imported XInput pack retargets to a different physical layout without hand-editing. Where no pack covers a game, a sensible mapping is derived from the requirement rather than falling back to emulator defaults. Feeds RS-348: the same resolution answers a lightgun or wheel as well as a pad.
nodes.title: Generate controller mappings for the target device, don't only inherit them
nodes.why: Tom 2026-08-03: discussed repeatedly but never filed. Odin 3, RP4, arcade stick and a Mac pad have different physical arrangements, and MAME cfg vs RetroArch remap are different formats for the same game.

nodes.body: 16 of 856 library games carry >1 available ROM (e.g. Aero Blasters (Japan) + Air Buster (USA)); ManifestFile has no type field, so RS-339 would transfer every variant and the runner can't tell which to launch. nodes.body: RS-286 shipped 154,273 LaunchBox overviews; sampling shows they are near-entirely copied from MobyGames, Wikipedia, Giant Bomb and publisher copy. Source descriptions from Wikipedia instead, joined IGDB id -> Wikidata P5794 -> sitelink.

Wikipedia text is a separable, attributed field so CC BY-SA share-alike cannot reach RetroStack's own prose. LaunchBox-sourced overviews are no longer emitted to any export. The same fetch also lands review scores and period awards from the publication-keyed {{Video game reviews}} template, and regional release dates. The tail with no article is explicitly decided — generated from structured facts, or left empty — not left carrying LaunchBox text by default.
