nodes.body: Hobbyist tier ($9.99/mo, non-commercial, 720 req/hour). Use on top games and to fill IGDB gaps — not a bulk spine and not a replacement for LaunchBox as the release source.
nodes.done_looks_like: MobyGames is registered as a Stage 0 source with provenance (RS-349) and ingested within the 720/hour non-commercial limit. Its fields resolve through release_build.py's existing per-source confidence weighting rather than displacing LaunchBox — disagreement rate against LaunchBox is measured and recorded, so precedence is set by evidence. product_codes land where RS-67's identifier tier can use them. BLOCKING PREREQUISITE: the redistribution licence is read and recorded before any paid subscription — the API docs and subscribe page cover access tiers only and say nothing about shipping the data inside a distributed application. Bronze ($99.99/mo) is the documented upgrade path if RetroStack ever charges.

nodes.why: Owner decision 2026-08-03. Their distinct value is staff credits, a faceted attribute taxonomy, product_codes at release grain, a second rating source, and 25 years of indexed contemporaneous magazine reviews — the era IGDB's aggregated_rating is empty for.

nodes.body: The loopback master IS a client, so the runner's first slice needs no network: wire select→launch→exit→back-to-shelf for megadrive/RetroArch on the machine the viewer is on. Scope: a launch composer that resolves the emulator TOML platform templates against the INSTANCE layout (they currently template against {build}, the generator-era output dir); a launch_game command on the invoke surface; viewer launch action (Enter/pad placeholder key); process lifecycle (emulator fullscreen over the viewer, exit returns). RetroArch may be hand-installed this slice — detection with a clear missing-emulator message is in, downloading it is RS-363's.
nodes.done_looks_like: On the master, from the booted build's shelf, the launch action on a megadrive game starts it in RetroArch full-screen; quitting the emulator returns to the viewer on the same game; a game whose emulator/core is missing gets a clear in-viewer message naming what's missing (not a silent nothing); launch composition (TOML template → command line against the instance layout, game-intrinsic core choice) is covered by cargo tests; the launch is recorded so play history has something to read later. This closes the M1/M3 vertical: library → save → boot → play.

nodes.body: Tom 2026-08-04, right after the first real plays: saves currently land in the USER'S RetroArch dirs (~/) because no config override is passed — they must be instance content. Scope: (1) an --appendconfig overlay pins savefile/savestate directories into {root}/saves/retroarch/{saves,states} without touching the user's own RetroArch; (2) master authority — a client checks OUT the game's saves before launch (get_save_set + /media fetch) and checks IN changed files after exit (device-gated PUT), per the vision's checkout/checkin model; (3) the master rotates an overwritten save into saves/.history/ instead of clobbering (the cheap seed of full save history); conflict UI and per-profile saves stay with RS-321.

nodes.body: Found 2026-08-04 while running RS-166 Build 2's acceptance. v2_release_aliases carries aliases that belong to OTHER games: release 'Ferias Frustradas do Pica-Pau' carries 'Prince of Persia (USA).md'; 'Hit the Ice' carries 'Shinobi III - Return of the Ninja Master (USA) (Genesis Mini).md'; 'Beyond Oasis' carries 'Davis Cup World Tour (USA, Europe).md'. All three traced to alias_sources_json ['libretro_game:libretro_rom_name'] with evidence_count 1. MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING: 65,492 of 716,882 aliases (9.1%) share no token with their release title, 35,860 of them from libretro_rom_name -- but that figure is an UPPER BOUND on contamination, not a measurement of it, because a legitimate retitle shares no token either ('Beyond Oasis' / 'La Historia de Thor' is correct). Someone has to separate the two.
nodes.title: Some release aliases belong to a different game, and game_names would ship them
nodes.why: Stage 70 Build 3 projects these into game_names, which feeds the fuzzy match tier; a contaminated alias makes the scanner answer the wrong game by name.

nodes.body:
Found by the RS-166 Build 2 gate, 2026-08-04, and MEASURED by the re-gate the same day: THEORETICAL, NOT URGENT. Of 144,854 carried ids, only 31 (0.02%) have an exported name differing from their own anchor's LaunchBox name, and all 31 are collapsed double spaces ('Ultima(tm)  Underworld I'). The anchor wins in practice, so a regrouping has essentially no title to move.

THE MECHANISM, kept because it is real even if currently inert: legacy_ids names LaunchBox DatabaseID stability as its residual risk; this is the other half. release_build.py takes canonical_system from the GROUP anchor and canonical_title is group-derived, so a stage-30 regrouping can move an anchor onto a different game AT THE SAME PLATFORM. The platform-agreement guard cannot see that -- the platform still agrees -- so stage 70 would carry the v1 id onto a row that now describes a different game. That is id REUSE, which STAGE70_READ_SET.md classes as unrecoverable, as against retirement which merely orphans rows.

CHEAP FIX IF IT EVER MOVES: scripts/build_legacy_crosswalk.py already opens the shipped v1 export, so carrying the v1 'name' into the frozen crosswalk would let the exporter compare titles and report divergence. Re-measure the 31 before acting -- it is a 2026-08-04 sighting.
nodes.title: The carried v1 id can silently name a different game if stage 30 regroups
nodes.why: An id that names a different game re-points a user's existing library silently, and nothing in the export or the app reports it.

nodes.body:
Found by the RS-166 Build 2 gate, 2026-08-04. The build plan's Arm 4 -- export from two different pipeline generations and assert the games.id sets are equal but for declared additions and retirements -- CANNOT BE RUN BY ANYONE TODAY. v2_releases holds only run 103 and v2_rom_entries only run 104; stage 40 restamps rather than appends, and the rom spine is cleared and rebuilt every run. Determinism has been verified WITHIN one generation only (two exports of run 103 are digest-identical per table but for schema_version.created_at, confirmed twice).

Arm 4 is the only test that would catch the failure mode legacy_ids exists to prevent, and it is currently unrunnable.

A ROUTE EXISTS, found by the re-gate: the GROUPING history survives even though the releases do not -- v2_source_links and v2_match_evidence each hold 3 generations. An Arm-4-shaped test could be built on those rather than on retained releases. The alternatives are capturing an id manifest beside each export to diff against later, or an explicit decision that within-generation determinism plus the frozen crosswalk is sufficient evidence.
nodes.title: Stage 70 cannot be proved id-stable across generations, because only one exists
nodes.why: The plan names this as the one check nothing else substitutes for, and it was recorded as cheap because two generations 'already exist'; they do not.

nodes.body:
Named by the RS-166 Build 3 filter analysis, 2026-08-04, as its largest unmeasured risk, and accepted deliberately by the owner when choosing the 297,360-row cut.

THE METHOD AND ITS BLIND SPOT. Contamination was detected by asking whether a filename-shaped alias is some OTHER release's rom_name on the same platform -- the ROM spine being an independent record of which files each release has. That found 10.19% contamination on libretro_rom_name, 0 false positives in 15 hand-checked. But the spine is LIBRETRO-DERIVED, so the method is structurally blind to a wrong launchbox_alt_name: there is no independent record to check it against. The 0.00% and 0.39% figures for non-libretro sources are ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE, not evidence of absence.

WHY IT MATTERS: the shipped filter emits roughly 330,000 of its 297,360 rows from exactly those unmeasured sources. A contaminated launchbox_alt_name would put a wrong title into the fuzzy cache, and matcher.rs:341-372 takes the first row it sees with no ORDER BY, so it can displace a correct match rather than merely adding a candidate -- the failure mode that disqualified the unfiltered option (F-22 Interceptor resolving to Bubsy).

WHAT WOULD ANSWER IT: a second independent record for launchbox-sourced aliases. Options not yet evaluated -- cross-check against IGDB alternative_names for the same work; check whether an alt_name is another release's canonical_title on the same platform; or sample and hand-check, which is what established the libretro rate.

RELATED: RS-423 is the upstream fix for the contamination itself. This item is about the part nobody has measured yet.
nodes.title: game_names contamination is unmeasured outside the libretro sources
nodes.why: The chosen filter's residual risk sits entirely in the sources the detection method cannot see, so nobody can currently say how large it is.

nodes.body: Every debounced resave re-hashes every media file of every game per tree-authored collection (resave.rs -> build_manifest_from_collection -> assemble_media/assemble_roster_media). Was <=5 files/game; RS-535 ph.2 adds up to 9 more roster types. Add a (path,size,mtime)->sha1 cache before a large published library meets the 1.5s debounce. Related sharp edges from the same review: a resave during a long publish can hash a file mid-copy and ship a torn sha1 (self-heals next resave); create_asset_type has no reserved-name check, so a user type named 'poster' or 'video' would collide with the legacy manifest kinds.
nodes.done_looks_like: A repeated auto-resave of an unchanged library re-hashes nothing (cache keyed path+size+mtime); a changed file re-hashes; create_asset_type refuses names that collide with legacy manifest kinds.
nodes.title: Auto-resave media hashing is unmemoised and now unbounded
nodes.why: e8m2-reviewer finding 11 (2026-08-11): per-save hashing cost now scales with the published library

nodes.body: Classification already separates base/update/DLC for Switch (title-ID low bits), PS3 (pkg flags + folder semantics) and Wii U, but update/DLC findings are dropped after classification: not persisted, not delivered in builds, not installed at launch. Pairing is mechanical for Switch (shared title-ID prefix) and PS3 (shared TITLE_ID); PS3 RAPs already group in the direct-PSN case as the model to follow.
nodes.done_looks_like: Update/DLC findings pair to their base game when the base is present in the same source: Switch by shared title-ID prefix, PS3 by TITLE_ID, Wii U by title-ID namespace; paired content persists with the base unit (rom_content_units members or attached rows preserving class), is carried in build manifests with roles intact, and is delivered to the device by reconcile alongside the base; an update/DLC with no base present remains a visible non-launchable finding exactly as today; PS3 RAP grouping is unchanged; fixtures pin the pairing per platform and a manifest-composition test proves the paired members travel; runner-side automatic installation is explicitly OUT of scope and captured as a follow-up item if not built; full Rust suite, tsc and vite green.

nodes.body: Measured 2026-08-20: 0 serial-tier hits in the name-only bench. CORRECTED after reading try_match_by_serial: it already normalises case/hyphens both sides, so PS3 SFO/pkg serials DO match in production (the bench's PS3 path lacked the catalogue closure). The real gap is Switch/Wii: scanner emits 16-hex title IDs (0100…, TMD), catalogue stores GameTDB short codes (A224A, D2AJ) — needs title-ID columns carried through the pipeline (RS-160/RS-183/RS-201).
nodes.title: The serial match tier is format-dead: scanner IDs and catalogue serials never speak the same dialect
nodes.why: Match-rate bench: 91.2% overall on names alone; the serial tier that should carry Switch/Wii/PS3 contributes nothing today.

nodes.body: Tom's direction 2026-08-20: any system with serial identifiers should regex the serial out of the file/folder name at the names tier — wbfs/GC bracket IDs ([RMCE01]), PS2/PSP/Vita SLUS/ULUS/PCSE tokens, PS3 BLES/NPUB in folder names, Switch 0100-hex (done), Wii U 0005-hex (done). Declare the per-system pattern beside the scanner profile so the hierarchy's names tier feeds try_match_by_serial before any content read.
nodes.done_looks_like: A per-system serial pattern is declared beside the scanner profile (config, not code constants); at the names tier the classifier emits serial identifiers extracted from file and per-game-folder names for at least wii/gamecube (bracketed id6 like [RMCE01]), ps2/psp/psvita (SLUS/SLES/ULUS/UCUS/PCSE tokens) and ps3 (BLES/BLUS/NPUB/NPEB); extracted serials feed try_match_by_serial before any content read; garbage-content fixtures whose names carry serials classify and match under NamesFirst while Thorough behaviour is unchanged; systems without a declared pattern behave exactly as today; a scratch-instance bench against the live archive records the wii serial-tier hit count as evidence (baseline 0, sighting 2026-08-20; catalogue wii serials are id6-shaped so bracketed wbfs ids should hit); full Rust suite, tsc and vite green.
nodes.title: Extract serials from filenames and per-game folders, per system
nodes.why: Match bench 2026-08-20: Wii at 35.6% name-only while its filenames literally carry serials; complements RS-201's header reads as the tier above them.

nodes.body: game_serials carries one dialect per source (GameTDB short codes A224A/D2AJ, hyphenated PS3); the scanner emits others (16-hex switch/wii title IDs). Stage 70 should export every known variant per release. SUPERSEDES RS-569. Blocked on a spec pass: read RS-160 (validity), RS-183 (recovery), RS-201 (title-ID matching) and re-measure their figures before building — catalogue-v2 work follows its own gates.
nodes.title: Export serial variants per release so every dialect matches
nodes.why: Match bench 2026-08-20: 0 serial hits for switch/wii despite 14k+ serial rows for those platforms; overlaps RS-160 (validity), RS-183 (recovery), RS-201 (title-ID matching) and needs reading their specs first.

nodes.body: amiga500 matched 78.7% name-only; the catalogue holds both LaunchBox and TOSEC name forms (32,504 filenames), so misses are variant drift — crack-group/version tags ([cr CSL], v1.2) and per-disk entries. Approach: strip TOSEC bracket/paren blocks in a platform-aware normaliser, and group Disk N of M sets into one launch unit (m3u-style) so a 3,540-unit count stops double-counting disks.
nodes.done_looks_like: A platform-aware normaliser for the Amiga family (amiga500, amiga1200, cd32, cdtv) folds WHDLoad names (title split at the _v<version> slave marker, CamelCase split, trailing _Amiga platform stamp), GameBase spaced names, and bare TOSEC version/revision suffixes onto catalogue titles — applied identically to the catalogue-alias side and the probe side — without touching any other platform's normalisation (pinned with literal expected strings); Disk N of M sets (TOSEC parens and underscore infix forms, including an untagged boot disk joining its _DiskN siblings) group into one launch unit with every disk a member, same-directory same-extension only, of-M totals agreeing, name-only so preview and scan agree; fixtures pin: WHDLoad stem matching its TOSEC catalogue entry exact-tier, two-disk set one launchable unit with both members, untagged boot disk folding, lone disk file unchanged, no cross-folder/extension/total merges, WHDLoad 2Disk qualifiers not treated as disk tokens, Darts 501-style titles surviving; a scratch-instance bench against the live archive records units and name-only match rate as evidence (re-measured baseline 3,540 / 78.7%; plan-validated expectation ~3,531 / ~95.4% with the exact-tier share rising from 92 to ~2,666 — judge by correctness and exact-tier share, not the raw headline); full Rust suite, tsc and vite green.
nodes.title: Amiga matching: TOSEC-aware normalisation and disk-set grouping
nodes.why: Match bench 2026-08-20; Amiga is the largest single system in the archive (3,540 units) and second-worst match rate.

nodes.body: Groups the 2026-08-20 match-quality work: serial extraction from names (RS-570), Amiga normalisation and disk grouping (RS-572), update/DLC pairing through persist/manifest/reconcile (RS-568). RS-571 (serial variant export) stays out pending its spec pass against RS-160/183/201.
nodes.title: Serial-first matching and update pairing

nodes.body: RS-570 declares bracketed:6 only — a 4-char bracketed group is too loose to extract safely — so the catalogue's 4,453 four-char wii serials (vs 3,394 six-char) can never hit from names. Candidate approaches: id4->id6 derivation (id6 = id4 + maker code), or content-tier reads for ambiguous cases per the query-cost hierarchy.

nodes.body: matcher.rs:1756 (publisher, RS-592) and the RS-602 SPS tier both return MatchType::Normalized with the name candidate's confidence, and scanner.rs:1284 persists only those two fields.
nodes.title: A tie broken by publisher or disk-id evidence is persisted as an ordinary name match
nodes.why: Found by the RS-602 review 2026-08-21: an auditor asking why a file matched cannot tell whether normalized text, a publisher token or a four-digit disk id decided it — and those tiers exist precisely because the text alone was ambiguous.

nodes.body: game_reference.db game_names carries 2,249 amiga500 names with a [NNNN] SPS tag, every one a unique owner — the table matcher.rs already loads. The LaunchBox Files.xml join reaches only 1,150 ids and mis-attributes several.
nodes.title: The Amiga SPS disk id is already in the shipped catalogue as a TOSEC name tag
nodes.why: Measured 2026-08-21 while reviewing RS-602: the tag settled After Burner 0095/0947, Bad Dudes 0098 and Knightmare 0966, disagreeing with the Files.xml bridge and being right each time. It needs no re-export, so it does not depend on RS-599.

nodes.body: matcher.rs:1481 does not select name_type; every game_names row becomes the same GameNameAlias at :1492 and participates identically in structural and fuzzy matching. RS-609 ships name_type='derived_equivalence' that no consumer reads.
nodes.title: The scanner's name cache ignores name_type, so a derived alias competes like a catalogue name
nodes.why: Found by the RS-609 review 2026-08-21: the whole point of provenance on an equivalence is that a wrong one should be distinguishable from a publisher-attested name at match time, and today it is not.

nodes.body: RS-609 ships 30 hand-authored PS2 links against 1,310 unattached titles. The PCSX2 demos/tools inventory holds 1,581 serials intersecting 687 missing candidates, all computable; no acquisition, parser or intersection generator exists.
nodes.title: A proposal generator would turn curated equivalences from a seed into coverage
nodes.why: The RS-609 review judged it plainly: computationally the overlay scales, the feed does not — the next 300 links cost 300 manual reviews unless a generator proposes them for human judgement.

nodes.body: No emulator TOML declares m3u, yet classification.rs:486 makes the M3U the launch member. But RetroStack ALREADY has its own disc-set model: matcher.rs:2361 generate_disc_set_id derives {system}:{base title} from the (Disc N) tag and stores it with disc_number on every rom_files row.
nodes.title: An M3U launch unit is unlaunchable on every system
nodes.why: Reframed 2026-08-21 after Tom asked whether m3u is even required: it is not. disc_set_id is populated and reaches nothing - it appears once outside the scanner, in src/lib/types.ts:1150 - so the disc-set model exists and was never wired to launch. The fix is to make disc sets first-class at launch, not to teach the runner about m3u; m3u is the right answer only for RetroArch, which supports playlists natively.

nodes.body: resolve_source_system_folders maps 42 of 44 archive folders, ps2 <- 'Playstation 2' included, via display names plus without_vendor_prefix which strips sony/nintendo/sega/commodore/sinclair. My original count only compared exact keys and the 'folder' alias key, and my confirming test used retrostack-cli scan, which by design reads ONLY the builtin source (cli.rs:554).
nodes.title: REFUTED: the archive folders do resolve; the CLI scan just ignores non-builtin sources
nodes.why: Refuted 2026-08-21 by running the real resolver against the archive. Two bad measurements in a row nearly bought 17 unnecessary manifest edits. The real gap is that the multi-source path (api::scan_library_sources) has no CLI entry point, so nothing on the command line can scan a registered archive.

nodes.body: Amiga, Genesis, Nintendo Wii and Playstation 3 keep their files one level below the system folder (PS3: Disc Games / PSN Games / DLC / GAME UPDATES). A folder alias alone therefore finds zero files in each.
nodes.title: Nested archive layouts discover nothing even with a correct system folder
nodes.why: Measured 2026-08-21. discovery.rs:101 deliberately refuses to follow a symlinked system folder, so a user cannot work around it by aliasing; the fix has to be a deeper source root or discovery that descends. Split from RS-615 because it is a code change, not a manifest entry.

nodes.body: The manifest key is cd32, not amigacd32, and the resolver maps 'Amiga CD32' -> cd32 correctly. My original check looked for the wrong key name.
nodes.title: REFUTED: Amiga CD32 resolves as cd32
nodes.why: Refuted 2026-08-21 alongside RS-615. Catalogue coverage for cd32 is still worth checking before judging the 183 files, but there is no mapping gap.

nodes.body: Two layers. SCOPE: load_payload_map (build_sync.rs:341, and :970 for the collection path) runs before the systems filter (:432) / node selection (:1014), hashing every available rom_file whose hash is blank, regardless of what enters the manifest. PERSISTENCE: the measured hash is never written back to rom_files.file_hash - the only cache is MEDIA_HASH_CACHE, an in-memory static, so every fresh process re-pays. The module doc at :15 already states the intent: 'when a SELECTED payload has a blank integrity hash'.
nodes.title: Build manifest hashes the whole library, not the build
nodes.why: Library is everything the master has; a build is the curated subset for a device (VOCABULARY.md:51,56). Hashing belongs to the build. Today a one-system build on an instance with the SMB archive registered reads 3703 GB, and pays it again on every restart

nodes.body: Startup maintenance begins during Tauri setup, but App.tsx creates its permanent 'Matching ROMs...' toast and subscribes to retrostack://startup_task later, in onMount. Tauri does not replay events. A fast terminal path -- no reference DB with an empty asset refresh, the already-running skip, or a database-open failure -- emits both stage results before the listener exists, so nothing ever settles the toast. PRE-EXISTING: at merge-base 9646783 the toast is created at App.tsx:216 and the listener registered at App.tsx:456, both inside the onMount at :156, and the old finishStartup at :424 required both flags. nodes.why: Every test on this path constructs the listener before delivering events, so no suite can see a race that is entirely about which exists first.

nodes.body: The acquisition lock is held on the inode, so deleting steam-artwork.lock while a run holds it lets a second run create and lock a fresh inode. Two runs then delete each other's .steam.part files, and a crash can leave an available=1 row with no file. Same caveat on a network filesystem where advisory locks are acknowledged but not coordinated. Recorded in a comment at steam.rs's try_lock; nothing in the app removes the file.
nodes.title: Steam artwork lock is defeated by unlinking the lock file
nodes.why: Found by the RS-632 independent review; advisory locking cannot close it, so it needs a different mechanism rather than a patch.

nodes.body: write_atomically now syncs the parent directory after the rename, so a power loss cannot lose the directory entry while the database says the asset is present. Nothing tests it: the failure needs a filesystem crash between two syscalls, which the suite cannot stage. Would need a fault-injection layer or a VM-level crash test to cover.
nodes.title: The Steam cache rename is not covered by a durability test
nodes.why: Stated honestly in the RS-632 commit rather than covered by a test that would not fail; capturing so it is not mistaken for tested behaviour later.

nodes.body: The Stage 0 IGDB query requested 'age_ratings.category, age_ratings.rating' (IGDB_INVESTIGATION.md:299), but the 1GB raw dump at data-sources/igdb-dumps/igdb_all_games.jsonl carries age_ratings as identity only: [{"id": 123634}, ...]. Every neighbouring expanded field worked -- genres, themes, keywords, platforms, game_modes and involved_companies all came back with names. So this is not an ingest defect; the dump itself is unexpanded. Most likely the sub-field names were wrong for the API version: IGDB renamed age_ratings.category to organization and rating to rating_category, and both now reference separate endpoints rather than being enums. Consequence: age_ratings_json is populated on 72,784 stg_igdb_games entries and is entirely unusable, so IGDB contributes nothing to age ratings today.

nodes.body: RetroArch reads core options from its own per-core .opt files and writes them itself; option keys in a .cfg do nothing. Needs runloop.c / core_option_manager.c mirrored or a real RetroArch probed before it can be specified.
nodes.done_looks_like: RetroArch reads core options from a file inside device/ that RetroStack writes: core_options_path is declared in retroarch.toml's [config.settings] and rendered through RS-789's mechanism, global_core_options is set so each core gets its own .opt (note the polarity — runloop.c:1597 passes !global_core_options as per_core_options), and a writer emits the global core-options file in RetroArch's flat key = "value" format. THE CORE PROPERTY: option defaults are SEEDED, not enforced — RetroArch hands the global file in as src_path only when a core's .opt does not yet exist (runloop.c:1322-1327, core_option_manager.c:834-836), so a user's later change in RetroArch's own menu lands in their per-core .opt and PERSISTS. A test must pin that: seed, simulate a user-modified .opt, re-run, and assert the user's value survived — with a positive control showing a missing .opt does get seeded. Deciding WHICH options is not this item.
nodes.title: Core options: a delivery mechanism RS-789 does not provide
nodes.why: Core options are not settings and RS-789 cannot deliver them — but the PATH to the file RetroArch reads them from is an ordinary setting, so the existing chain reaches them. Answered from source 2026-08-29 (see the core-options-delivery.md artifact); no probe needed.

nodes.body: Emulator resolution is per-game override, then per-collection, then a system default computed from TOML priority alone (resolver.rs:68-90, :198-213). There is no user layer at all, and the choice a user actually needs is not 'which emulator' but 'which routing policy' — the answer can differ per game within one system.
nodes.title: Route games between emulators by a user-chosen policy, not a fixed emulator
nodes.why: Owner, 2026-08-28: the system should hold the intelligence about which games support widescreen, and the user chooses routing at a top level. Three modes per system: ALL to the native emulator (widescreen where supported, no bezels); ALL to RetroArch (bezels everywhere); or SPLIT — widescreen titles to native, the rest to RetroArch with a bezel. The owner used the emulator as a proxy for a PRESENTATION PROFILE precisely to avoid authoring per-game bezel overrides, so a plain 'pick an emulator per system' dropdown would be the wrong build. Needs the widescreen capability flag (its own item) and a resolver rung that reads policy + capability. ⚠️ The all-to-RetroArch mode cannot deliver its widescreen half today: every core's widescreen switch is a CORE OPTION (pcsx2_widescreen_hint, flycast_widescreen_cheats, dolphin_widescreen), which RS-795 has no delivery mechanism for.

nodes.body: is_core_installed is a bare path.exists() (emulator/retroarch.rs:148-151) and provisioning skips any core already present, while core_url_template_* points at nightly/.../latest/. So a core is frozen at whatever nightly was current the first time THAT device provisioned, is never updated, and nothing anywhere records which build it is.

nodes.why: Owner decided 2026-08-28: arcade sets are kept current against the rolling libretro MAME core, and RetroStack does not get into ROM downloading. That position is workable only if a set/core mismatch is diagnosable — today two devices provisioned a month apart run different MAME cores silently, and a wrong-checksum refusal names no cause. Recording the build (Last-Modified plus fetch date) is not an updater and not ROM downloading.

nodes.body: Land a per-game 'supports widescreen' flag in the catalogue, joined on keys we already hold. Getting it wrong is visible, not silent — a 16:9 game framed in a 4:3 bezel. Join keys measured in the shipped catalogue: ps2 9,598 well-formed serials (99%), gamecube/wii GameIDs held in both 4- and 6-char forms, dreamcast 81% and weakest. Widescreen looks like the MINORITY case (~144 of thousands of GC/Wii titles), so the exception set is small and enumerable.

nodes.body: Second pass over the emulator download and configuration path: each emulator that carries a real library installs correctly, is put in a deterministic (portable) layout, and gets a declared set of default settings — with widescreen on by default via the safe per-game mechanism, and internal render scale exposed as a per-device option.
nodes.done_looks_like: Each of the six in-scope emulators (RetroArch, Dolphin, PCSX2/LRPS2, Flycast, RPCS3, MAME) installs into a deterministic layout inside device/, receives whatever support files it needs without anyone opening its GUI, and launches with declared default settings rendered through RS-789's mechanism — no second config path. Widescreen is on by default via each emulator's per-game patch/native mechanism and NEVER its geometry hack. Internal render scale is a per-device option. Every value is checked against a mirrored config reference for that emulator, not recalled. RPCS3 specifically is in portable mode, holds a current config_database.dat, and can install .pkg files headlessly. See spec.md for the scope boundary, the six constraints, and the five parts — E (widescreen under RetroArch) is gated on RS-795/RS-796 and must not share a leaf with the standalone half.

nodes.why: Tom, 2026-08-28. RS-789 built the mechanism for declaring settings and proved it on RetroArch; today 13 of 14 emulators have NO settings written for them at all, RPCS3 does no portable setup so its config and installs land in user directories we do not control, and two shipped cores (ppsspp, bluemsx) never receive the system files they need. The capability exists and nothing uses it.

nodes.body: materialise_launch_payload resolves a Copy device's every ROM to materialisation_root().join(payload.path), and materialisation_root ignores its argument and always returns <root>/device (reconcile.rs:348-351, :662-668). So a client can only play bytes laid out in RetroStack's own layout under its device tier. Only a master can reference source bytes in place, by resolving source://<id>/... against a library source root.
nodes.title: A client cannot reference ROMs it does not own a copy of
nodes.why: Tom, 2026-08-28: 'that's still a major limitation'. A client cannot keep its application on internal storage and read an existing, differently-organised ROM collection from an attached disk — it must own a materialised copy. Putting the whole client instance root on the external disk works today and is the current answer, but it is not the same thing. ⚠️ materialisation_root's unused parameter is the seam: making that root configurable would serve this AND master-side export to a disk, and launch follows for free because it calls the same function. Interacts with RS-783's rule that device/ is deletable whole.

nodes.body: ensure_config_database_with_fetcher returns Ok(false) the moment the file exists, so config_database.dat is installed once at provision and only ever refreshed by rebuilding device/. RS-805's acceptance asked for a CURRENT database.
nodes.title: RPCS3's config database is fetched once and never refreshes
nodes.why: Upstream adds per-game configs continuously; a database frozen at first provision silently stops covering new titles, and nothing reports it. Found while gating RS-805, 2026-08-29.

nodes.body: config_save_on_exit=true flushes live settings state to the file --config names. Appended values are indistinguishable from base ones: config_append_file merges them into the same conf object (configuration.c:6404), and the OVERRIDES_ACTIVE guard (runloop.c:4561) covers config/<core>/ overrides, not --appendconfig. ⚠️ UPGRADED FROM INFERENCE TO OBSERVED 2026-08-29: config_save_file IS in the mirror at configuration.c:8374 — it writes live settings state over a re-read of the existing file (8407), and its refusal guard at 8411 covers only OVERRIDES_ACTIVE. So the enforced chain's keys, absolute {bios}/{saves}/{states} paths included, ARE written into the seed file on exit. The trap is not the pollution: removing an enforced setting later would not revert it, because the stale value is already in the base and takes effect the moment the chain stops overriding it.
nodes.title: Enforced RetroArch settings may bake themselves into the seed config on exit
nodes.why: The trap is not the pollution, it is that REMOVING an enforced setting later would not revert it -- the stale value would already be sitting in the base config, and would silently take effect the moment the chain stopped overriding it. Also makes 'reset to defaults = re-run the seed' untrue, since the seed file is no longer pristine. Found while gating RS-813, 2026-08-29.

nodes.body: Shipped 84e6800: src-tauri/src/emulator/pkg.rs extracts retail PS3 packages (AES-128-CTR, published key, install dir from offset 55). Verified byte-identical to RPCS3's own install on Geometry Wars 3 base+v1.03 (1251 files, 0 differences) and Bejeweled 3 listed correctly from our install alone. REMAINING: .rap licences are not written (16-byte copy to dev_hdd0/home/<user>/exdata/), and nothing calls the extractor - it is not wired into reconcile/provisioning.
nodes.done_looks_like: PS3 packages install without RPCS3's GUI: retail .pkg extracted to dev_hdd0/game/<install_dir> and .rap licences copied flat into dev_hdd0/home/<user>/exdata/. VERIFIED byte-identical to RPCS3's own install on real retail packages (base 1107 files, base+update 1251, DLC-into-existing-subtree 201, all zero differences). REMAINING: (1) not wired into reconcile/provisioning - nothing calls it; (2) content_type unread, so a THEME or LICENSE-type package goes to game/ instead of theme/ or exdata/; (3) performance unfit for background use - 57 MB/s, per-16-byte AES block plus a GenericArray copy, whole-file buffering, and no target-feature=+aes so the M1's hardware AES is unused.
nodes.title: Extract PS3 .pkg files directly, because RPCS3's installer needs a human
nodes.why: RPCS3's --installpkg needs a gui_application with a main window and shows an unsuppressable modal, so it cannot run during a client's background reconcile and is unusable on a handheld with no keyboard. Tom, 2026-08-29.

nodes.body: Measured 2026-08-29 on an M1 Max: 3.1GB of Borderlands 2 DLC took 54s release, ~20 min debug (57 MB/s). Three causes, in order: the aes crate falls back to constant-time software AES because nothing sets target-feature=+aes; decrypt_in_place does one encrypt_block plus a GenericArray::clone_from_slice per SIXTEEN BYTES (~194M of each for that payload); and read_decrypted buffers each file whole in memory (546MB RSS observed on a 182MB file).
nodes.title: PKG extraction is too slow and too memory-hungry for a background reconcile
nodes.why: A client reconciling a large PSN library does this unattended, possibly on a handheld. Correctness is proven; throughput is not fit for purpose. Fix is a streaming loop with a fixed buffer, batched block encryption, and hardware AES - no second language needed.

nodes.body: PARKED by Tom 2026-08-30: current model is fine for now, but there is tension between allowing local edits and forcing remote official edits. Today ARCHITECTURE.md:16 is explicit that mutating library and collection operations belong to the master, and the only client-to-master writes are begin_reconcile and the saves check-in. Two distinct things sit behind 'edit the build from a client': (a) OPERATING THE MASTER REMOTELY - point the admin UI at the master's server, edit there, reconcile down; needs no new write direction and already fits the architecture; (b) EDITING LOCALLY AND SYNCING UP - a genuine new capability and the expensive one, because revisions freeze once synced so a local edit must cut a master revision, and a concurrent master edit puts us in the merge that push-wins exists to avoid. Also: 'remove a game' is two intents that look identical in a UI - 'not in my collection' (RetroStack-level, propagates everywhere) versus 'free the space on this handheld' (device-level, touches nobody else). The second is probably what a handheld user wants most and needs no new write direction at all: device-local eviction, not a collection edit.
nodes.title: Local edits on a client versus master-only official edits
nodes.why: Real tension, deliberately deferred rather than forgotten. Captured so the next person does not re-derive the distinction or build the expensive half by accident.

nodes.body: Retain LaunchBox thumbnail mappings outside generated catalogues, reuse and resume independent scraping, and support selected platform batches with coverage reporting.
nodes.done_looks_like: The standalone LaunchBox mapper reads Metadata.xml and either one supplied platform URL or a validated platform-list file, without opening a generated catalogue database. It atomically publishes data-sources/launchbox/launchbox_thumbnail_map.tsv and retains bounded acquisition progress separately. An unchanged completed run makes zero listing requests, including with unresolved games; matching-relevant XML changes rematch saved cards first and fetch only affected selected platforms when changed records remain unresolved. Explicit refresh discovers remote-only changes. Interrupted runs, including refreshes and multi-platform runs, resume validated completed pages without re-fetching them; corrupt or incompatible checkpoints and detected pagination drift cannot publish invalid mappings. Existing ID pairs remain immutable, same-pair thumbnail names may refresh, and unselected mappings survive. A conflicting ID pair or any pre-publication fetch, parse, validation, or write failure preserves the previous TSV byte-for-byte for the entire invocation; a crash after replacement recovers publication state without repeating completed requests. An exclusive process lock prevents a second updater from fetching or writing and releases on process exit; concurrent catalogue readers see a complete old or new TSV. Per-platform reports identify mapped, missing and ambiguous XML IDs, listing-only and retained-outside-XML records, additions, refreshes, and requested/reused pages with published versus pending results distinguished. Partial or absent mapping input is valid; malformed nonempty input fails visibly. A fresh complete catalogue build imports exactly the retained TSV or zero rows when absent/empty, performs no network requests, and needs no acquisition state; schema-9 export reproduces eligible launchbox_preview candidates. Removing generated databases preserves source mappings. Existing library-cover and saved-collection runtime behaviour remains unchanged. Focused fixture tests verify these invariants and both independent code reviews named in the spec have no unresolved correctness findings.

nodes.body: Extend retained bulk mappings with released-only, budgeted detail lookup and fan-art fallback, then reuse existing work joins in the library downloader.
nodes.done_looks_like: Bulk acquisition retains unambiguous XML-ID/website-ID pairs independently of covers and imports legacy TSV mappings without requests or lost pairs. Both observed LaunchBox CDN hosts survive retained-source ingestion, coordinated export/pack contracts and runtime URL construction; schema-9 compatibility remains. A zero-network detail worklist separates covered, eligible Released, excluded release types, missing/ambiguous identity, confirmed no-cover and retryable failures. Detail execution requires an explicit HTTP-attempt budget, never exceeds it, requests only eligible or explicitly selected unambiguous IDs, prefers standard front then tagged fanart front, and never substitutes screenshots/logos/3D boxes. Positive and no-cover results are retained; unchanged completed work makes zero requests, bounded runs resume after interruption, and source publication preserves RS-971 atomicity/locking guarantees. A clean synthetic catalogue rebuild needs only retained source and no network/acquisition state. Library box-front acquisition preserves local and own-release precedence, then uses direct candidates from exact nonempty shared work IDs in installed packs, same platform before other platforms, then existing Steam fallback; unrelated works and collection full-media selection remain unaffected. CDN-aware candidate fingerprints, donor provenance, duplicate-locator suppression and an explicit retry path for existing no_candidate jobs are tested without retry storms or overwriting local media. Synthetic parser, budget, resume, migration, export/pack and runtime integration tests pass; full Python/Rust results are recorded with any unrelated baseline failures evidenced. Source/schema checkpoint and final independent reviews have no unresolved correctness findings; canonical workflow and recovery documentation is updated. No all-platform acquisition, production catalogue cutover or deployment is required.

nodes.body: Extend the generated map with dependency, frontend and data-model views, then use the dependency view to prove the db layer stops walking the filesystem.
nodes.done_looks_like: 1) docs/generated/ carries a dependency view, a frontend inventory and a data-model view, each regenerating deterministically (gen_architecture_map.py --check exits 0 on an unchanged tree), and README.md carries a row for each. 2) The dependency view names every mutual-dependency pair between top-level Rust modules under an edge rule pinned in its own header, and is read as a coupling report, not a defect list. 3) db's filesystem footprint is an exact, impl-qualified RATCHET in seam_contracts.rs that only shrinks (Tom's ruling 2026-09-05, recorded on RS-981: nine sites were found, not four, and the spec's own STAYS list includes ensure_bootstrapped which reads the disk, so a zero was unsatisfiable): four sites left db (rediscover_exe's discovery call, AssetSourceOps::create's pre-insert head, ValidationOps and AssetRefreshOps to library_inventory.rs), five remain listed with reasons, the test fails on a new site AND a stale entry and asserts no db struct holds a Path-typed field — a CAPABILITY assertion proven to bite three ways. db's remaining references to rom_scanner TYPES and PURE functions are deliberately retained; db <-> rom_scanner stays a mutual pair by design. 4) The frontend inventory lists every TypeScript module nothing imports. 5) rom_scanner/scanner.rs and matcher.rs each carry a //! header per the CLAUDE.md convention, with at least one claim per header pinned by a named test. 6) The architecture is ratcheted: the mutual-dependency pairs and the header-less modules are checked-in lists that fail on a new entry AND on a stale one, both arms proven; the map fails a test when STRUCTURALLY stale (command set, module set, edges, header flags), never when only line counts move; every parser errors rather than emitting a smaller map; the api:line column is gone from command-surface.md. 7) Across every code move: the workspace suite, run on the leaf's own submitted commit with --no-fail-fast under the default TMPDIR, reports zero failures before and after; and command-surface.md's command set, Tauri column and HTTP column are identical before and after — compared with the api:line column stripped until RS-986 removed it.
nodes.title: See the structure, then fix the two places it is wrong
nodes.why: Nobody can see how the codebase fits together: the map shipped by RS-972 is an inventory with no dependency, frontend or data-model view, and the persistence layer 16 modules stand on is calling filesystem discovery with nothing able to detect it. Split five ways: the dependency view first because it is the instrument that measures the db extraction; the two other views and the extraction serialise behind it because all three edit scripts/gen_architecture_map.py and concurrent writers to one file are a known hazard here; the scanner headers are independent comprehension work.

nodes.body: Define plain-language capability chunks and their supporting tools, with current implementation and missing connections explained per system/emulator.
nodes.done_looks_like: The dashboard design defines a capability map covering identification and catalogue tools, library curation, emulator installation and prerequisites, default and game-specific configuration, controls, presentation, collection/device updates, save sync and wider vision. Each capability card states intended behaviour, scoped current capability, supporting tools, missing connections and dated evidence; unknown implementation and unverified behaviour are distinguishable. A source-grounded Dolphin per-game configuration example demonstrates the model. Coverage is secondary and no automatic manual game-verification queue is introduced. The final design records the chosen UI location, refresh behaviour and reviewable example overview/detail views before implementation is made ready.

nodes.body: Apply the agreed presentation tweaks: findings first, source links, curated task entry points and qualified detection wording.
nodes.done_looks_like: Generated reports lead with summaries and findings before extraction rules; commands, callers and module rows link to existing source files; the index offers curated entry points for common product tasks; detection wording does not imply proof of absence. Generation is deterministic and existing seam contracts pass with the linked table format.

nodes.body: Bounded reviewed module labels in the generated map and one direct dependency guard, implemented and independently reviewed by agents.
nodes.done_looks_like: The module map displays reviewed production/shared/compatibility assertions for the seven files named in spec.md, while absent declarations stay unclassified without inheritance. Source headers preserve their ownership explanation and cite their basis; malformed or duplicate role declarations fail with the file named. The existing structural check detects map/source role disagreement, including removed declarations. A fixed source-reference guard rejects detected direct production dependencies from build_sync, reconcile, runner or collection_tree to generator and names the source/site; changing a label does not disable it, and absent named modules fail. Negative controls prove these checks fail for violations and pass after restoration, with test/comment-only references excluded. Existing API/edge/header checks and measured command/edge sets remain intact. Independent review confirms each pilot's implementation/caller evidence and the documented limits; Python fixtures, seam tests, generation freshness/determinism and diff checks pass. No runtime behaviour, capability retirement, broad classification policy or catalogue cutover changes.
